exact_row.title: Unital star algebra and positive normalized state

items.title: Unital star algebra and positive normalized state
items.design_state: Fully authored draft with complete local argument; independent review remains pending.
items.statement:
A **unital complex star algebra** is a complex vector space $A$ with a complex-bilinear associative product $(a,b)\mapsto ab$, a specified unit $1_A$, and a conjugate-linear map $a\mapsto a^*$ such that, for all $a,b\in A$,

$$ (ab)^*=b^*a^*,\qquad (a^*)^*=a,\qquad 1_A^*=1_A. $$

A **positive normalized state** on $A$ is a complex-linear functional $\omega:A\to\mathbb C$ such that $\omega(1_A)=1$ and $\omega(a^*a)$ is a real nonnegative number for every $a\in A$. This is an algebraic definition: no norm, topology, boundedness condition, or completion is part of the data.
items.strategy: Definition with explicit algebraic operations and state conditions; no proof supplied.

references.title: Konrad Schmüdgen, An Invitation to Unbounded Representations of *-Algebras on Hilbert Space, Graduate Texts in Mathematics 285, Springer Nature (2020), §2.4, Definition 2.32
references.locator: §2.4, printed pp. 20–21: positivity and normalized states on a unital complex *-algebra.

references.title: Christopher J. Fewster and Kasia Rejzner, Algebraic Quantum Field Theory—an introduction, lecture notes, arXiv:1904.04051v2 (2019), §§2.2–2.3
references.locator: §2.2, Definition 2, and §2.3, algebraic state conventions.

items.title: Positive-state Cauchy–Schwarz and left radical
items.design_state: Fully authored draft with complete local argument; independent review remains pending.
items.statement:
Let $A$ be a unital complex star algebra and let $\omega$ be a positive normalized state on $A$ ([[def-qft-involutive-algebra-state]]). Define $q(a):=\omega(a^*a)$ and $N_\omega:=\{a\in A:q(a)=0\}$. Then

$$|\omega(b^*a)|^2\le q(a)q(b)\qquad(a,b\in A).$$

The form $(a,b)_\omega:=\omega(b^*a)$ is Hermitian and positive semidefinite, $N_\omega$ is its radical and a complex linear subspace, and $N_\omega$ is a left ideal: $c a\in N_\omega$ whenever $a\in N_\omega$ and $c\in A$.
items.strategy:
**Proof technique:** direct.

1.1 Put $X:=\omega(a^*b)$ and $Y:=\omega(b^*a)$. Positivity makes both $q(a+b)=q(a)+X+Y+q(b)$ and $q(a+ib)=q(a)+iX-iY+q(b)$ real; their imaginary parts give $\operatorname{Im}(X+Y)=0$ and $\operatorname{Re}(X-Y)=0$, hence $Y=\overline X$. Thus $(a,b)_\omega=\omega(b^*a)$ is Hermitian. [given, F1, algebra]

2.1 Suppose $q(b)>0$. For every $z\in\mathbb C$, positivity and the star-algebra laws give $0\le q(a+zb)=q(a)+zX+\overline z\,\overline X+|z|^2q(b)$. Taking $z=-\overline X/q(b)$ yields $0\le q(a)-|X|^2/q(b)$, so $|\omega(b^*a)|^2=|Y|^2=|X|^2\le q(a)q(b)$. [given, F1, step 1.1, algebra]

3.1 Suppose $q(b)=0$. If $X\ne0$, taking $z=-t\overline X$ for real $t>q(a)/(2|X|^2)$ makes $q(a+zb)=q(a)-2t|X|^2<0$, contradicting positivity. Hence $X=Y=0$, so the same Cauchy–Schwarz inequality holds when $q(b)=0$; if instead $q(a)=0$ and $q(b)>0$, step 2.1 forces $Y=0$ as well. [given, F1, step 1.1, step 2.1, algebra]

4.1 If $a\in N_\omega$, steps 2.1 and 3.1 give $(a,b)_\omega=0$ for every $b\in A$; conversely $(a,a)_\omega=0$ means $a\in N_\omega$. Thus $N_\omega$ is exactly the radical and is a linear subspace. For $c\in A$, set $d:=c^*ca$. Applying Cauchy–Schwarz to $a,d$ gives $|\omega(d^*a)|^2\le q(a)q(d)=0$, while $d^*a=a^*c^*ca=(ca)^*(ca)$; therefore $ca\in N_\omega$. [F1, step 2.1, step 3.1, algebra] ∎

references.title: Konrad Schmüdgen, An Invitation to Unbounded Representations of *-Algebras on Hilbert Space, Graduate Texts in Mathematics 285, Springer Nature (2020), §2.4 Proposition 2.33 and §4.4 Lemma 4.35
references.locator: §2.4, printed pp. 20–21, Hermiticity and Cauchy–Schwarz; §4.4, printed p. 78, null left ideal and quotient pairing.

references.title: Christopher J. Fewster and Kasia Rejzner, Algebraic Quantum Field Theory—an introduction, lecture notes, arXiv:1904.04051v2 (2019), §2.3
references.locator: §2.3, state positivity, Cauchy–Schwarz and the null left ideal used in the GNS construction.

items.title: GNS Hilbert reconstruction with invariant operator domain
items.design_state: Fully authored draft with complete local argument; independent review remains pending.
items.statement:
Let $A$ be a complex vector space with a complex-bilinear associative product, unit $1_A$, and conjugate-linear involution satisfying $(ab)^*=b^*a^*$, $(a^*)^*=a$ and $1_A^*=1_A$. Let $\omega:A\to\mathbb C$ be complex-linear with $\omega(1_A)=1$ and real nonnegative $\omega(a^*a)$ for every $a\in A$. Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$: every countable family of nonempty sets has a choice function. Put $N_\omega:=\{a\in A:\omega(a^*a)=0\}$ and $\mathcal D_\omega:=A/N_\omega$, with

$$([a],[b])_\omega:=\omega(b^*a),$$

using the first-variable-linear convention. Let $H_\omega$ be the Hilbert completion of this inner-product space, and identify $\mathcal D_\omega$ with its canonical dense image in $H_\omega$. For each $a\in A$ define left multiplication on the common domain $\mathcal D_\omega$ by $\pi_\omega(a)[b]:=[ab]$. Then $\pi_\omega$ is a unital algebra representation of $A$ on the invariant dense domain $\mathcal D_\omega$, and

$$\mathcal D_\omega\subseteq D(\pi_\omega(a)^*),\qquad \pi_\omega(a)^*|_{\mathcal D_\omega}=\pi_\omega(a^*).$$

Each $\pi_\omega(a)$ is closable, meaning that the closure of its graph in $H_\omega\times H_\omega$ is the graph of an operator. The vector $\Omega_\omega:=[1_A]$ is a unit cyclic vector, $\pi_\omega(A)\Omega_\omega=\mathcal D_\omega$, and $\omega(a)=(\pi_\omega(a)\Omega_\omega,\Omega_\omega)$. For uniqueness, let $K$ be a Hilbert space, $\mathcal D'\subseteq K$ a dense linear subspace invariant under every operator $\rho(a)$, and $\rho:A\to\operatorname{End}(\mathcal D')$ a unital algebra representation satisfying $(\rho(a)x,y)=(x,\rho(a^*)y)$ for all $a\in A$ and $x,y\in\mathcal D'$. If $\Omega'\in\mathcal D'$, $\mathcal D'=\rho(A)\Omega'$, and $\omega(a)=(\rho(a)\Omega',\Omega')$, then there is a unique unitary $V:H_\omega\to K$ with $V\Omega_\omega=\Omega'$ and $V\pi_\omega(a)x=\rho(a)Vx$ for all $a\in A$ and $x\in\mathcal D_\omega$. This theorem supplies neither a C*-norm nor essential self-adjointness of $\pi_\omega(a)$ when $a=a^*$.
items.strategy:
**Proof technique:** direct.

1.1 By [F1], $N_\omega$ is a subspace and every element of it pairs to zero with every element of $A$. Thus $([a],[b])_\omega=\omega(b^*a)$ is independent of both representatives; it is Hermitian and nonnegative, and $([a],[a])_\omega=0$ holds exactly when $a\in N_\omega$, so the quotient pairing is positive definite. [F1, given]

1.2 For $a,b\in A$, replacing $b$ by $b+n$ with $n\in N_\omega$ changes $ab$ by $an\in N_\omega$ because $N_\omega$ is a left ideal by [F1]; hence $\pi_\omega(a)[b]=[ab]$ is well defined. Bilinearity, associativity and $1_A$ give $\pi_\omega(a+b)=\pi_\omega(a)+\pi_\omega(b)$, $\pi_\omega(\lambda a)=\lambda\pi_\omega(a)$, $\pi_\omega(ab)=\pi_\omega(a)\pi_\omega(b)$ and $\pi_\omega(1_A)=I_{\mathcal D_\omega}$, and left multiplication keeps $\mathcal D_\omega$ invariant. [F1, given, algebra]

2.1 Apply [F2] to the quotient inner-product space $\mathcal D_\omega$; under the stated Countable Choice assumption this gives the Hilbert completion $H_\omega$ and a dense isometric embedding of $\mathcal D_\omega$, which we identify with its image. This is the only completion invoked. [F2, given, step 1.1]

2.2 For $a,b,c\in A$, the quotient form gives $(\pi_\omega(a)[b],[c])_\omega=\omega(c^*ab)=([b],\pi_\omega(a^*)[c])_\omega$. By the definition of the Hilbert-space adjoint, this identity for all $[b]\in\mathcal D_\omega$ shows $[c]\in D(\pi_\omega(a)^*)$ and $\pi_\omega(a)^*[c]=\pi_\omega(a^*)[c]$. [step 1.1, step 1.2, algebra]

2.3 Since $([1_A],[1_A])_\omega=\omega(1_A)=1$, $\Omega_\omega$ is a unit vector. Also $\pi_\omega(a)\Omega_\omega=[a]$ for every $a\in A$, so its algebraic orbit is exactly $\mathcal D_\omega$ and is dense. Finally $(\pi_\omega(a)\Omega_\omega,\Omega_\omega)_\omega=([a],[1_A])_\omega=\omega(a)$, recovering the state. [given, step 1.1, step 1.2]

2.4 Let $(H',\mathcal D',\rho,\Omega')$ be another algebraically cyclic *-representation of $A$ with common invariant dense domain $\mathcal D'=\rho(A)\Omega'$, $\rho(a^*)=\rho(a)^*|_{\mathcal D'}$, and $\omega(a)=(\rho(a)\Omega',\Omega')$. Define $U[a]:=\rho(a)\Omega'$. If $[a]=[0]$, then $\|\rho(a)\Omega'\|^2=\omega(a^*a)=0$, so $U$ is well defined; and for $a,b\in A$, $(U[a],U[b])=\omega(b^*a)=([a],[b])_\omega$ by the representation's adjoint identity. Thus $U$ is an isometry from $\mathcal D_\omega$ onto the dense subspace $\mathcal D'$. [given, F1, step 1.1, step 1.2]

3.1 Suppose $x_n\in\mathcal D_\omega$, $x_n\to0$ in $H_\omega$, and $\pi_\omega(a)x_n\to y$ in $H_\omega$. For each $z\in\mathcal D_\omega$, step 2.2 gives $(y,z)_\omega=\lim_n(\pi_\omega(a)x_n,z)_\omega=\lim_n(x_n,\pi_\omega(a^*)z)_\omega=0$. Density forces $y=0$. Therefore the closed graph relation of $\pi_\omega(a)$ contains no two distinct outputs over one input: their difference would be a nonzero pair $(0,y)$. The graph closure is a graph, so $\pi_\omega(a)$ is closable. In particular, if $a=a^*$ then $\pi_\omega(a)$ is symmetric on $\mathcal D_\omega$; this does not prove essential self-adjointness. [step 2.2, given]

4.1 The isometry extends uniquely from the dense domain to a unitary $\overline U:H_\omega\to H'$ because its range $\mathcal D'$ is dense. It sends $\Omega_\omega$ to $\Omega'$ and, for $[b]\in\mathcal D_\omega$, $\overline U\pi_\omega(a)[b]=\rho(ab)\Omega'=\rho(a)\overline U[b]$; hence it intertwines the representations on the common domains. Uniqueness follows because every vector of $\mathcal D_\omega$ has the form $\pi_\omega(a)\Omega_\omega$. [step 2.3, step 2.4, step 1.2] ∎

references.locator: §2.4, printed pp. 20–21; §4.4, printed pp. 78–81, especially Lemma 4.35, Proposition 4.36 and Theorem 4.38.

items.title: State-preserving symmetries implemented unitarily
items.design_state: Fully authored draft with complete local argument; independent review remains pending.
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, the hypothesis of [[thm-qft-algebraic-gns-domain]]. Let $G$ be a topological group with identity $e$. Let $A$ be a unital complex star algebra with positive normalized state $\omega$, and let $\alpha:G\to\operatorname{Aut}^*(A)$ be a group action: each $\alpha_g$ is a bijective complex-linear map preserving product, unit and involution, with $\alpha_e=\mathrm{id}$ and $\alpha_g\alpha_h=\alpha_{gh}$. Suppose $\omega(\alpha_g(a))=\omega(a)$ for all $g\in G$ and $a\in A$. Also suppose that, for every $a,b\in A$, the coefficient function $g\mapsto\omega(b^*\alpha_g(a))$ is continuous at $e$.

Use the GNS representation from [[thm-qft-algebraic-gns-domain]], with common dense domain $\mathcal D_\omega$ and cyclic vector $\Omega_\omega$. Then $U_g[a]:=[\alpha_g(a)]$ extends to a strongly continuous unitary representation $U:G\to\mathcal U(H_\omega)$, fixes $\Omega_\omega$, and satisfies

$$U_g\pi_\omega(a)U_g^{-1}|_{\mathcal D_\omega}=\pi_\omega(\alpha_g(a))\qquad(a\in A,g\in G).$$

Here strongly continuous means that $g\mapsto U_g\xi$ is norm-continuous for every $\xi\in H_\omega$. No differentiability, generator domain or spectral theorem follows from these hypotheses alone.
items.strategy:
**Proof technique:** direct.

1.1 If $n\in N_\omega$, then $\omega((\alpha_g n)^*\alpha_g n)=\omega(\alpha_g(n^*n))=\omega(n^*n)=0$, so $\alpha_g(N_\omega)\subseteq N_\omega$. Applying the same argument to $g^{-1}$ gives equality. For $a,b\in A$, $([\alpha_g(a)],[\alpha_g(b)])_\omega=\omega(\alpha_g(b^*a))=\omega(b^*a)$, so $[a]\mapsto[\alpha_g(a)]$ is an isometry on $\mathcal D_\omega$ with inverse induced by $\alpha_{g^{-1}}$; it extends uniquely to a unitary $U_g$ on $H_\omega$. The action law gives $U_gU_h=U_{gh}$, and $U_g\Omega_\omega=\Omega_\omega$. [F1, A1, given]

2.1 For $[b]\in\mathcal D_\omega$, $U_g\pi_\omega(a)U_g^{-1}[b]=U_g[a\alpha_{g^{-1}}(b)]=[\alpha_g(a)b]=\pi_\omega(\alpha_g(a))[b]$, using the representation rule and multiplicativity of $\alpha_g$. This is the claimed covariance identity on the common domain. [F1, A1, step 1.1]

2.2 For $a\in A$, state invariance and the quotient inner product give $\|U_g[a]-[a]\|^2=2\omega(a^*a)-\omega(a^*\alpha_g(a))-\omega((\alpha_g(a))^*a)$. The first cross term tends to $\omega(a^*a)$ as $g\to e$ by [A2]. For the second, invariance gives $\omega((\alpha_g(a))^*a)=\omega(\alpha_{g^{-1}}((\alpha_g(a))^*a))=\omega(a^*\alpha_{g^{-1}}(a))$, which also tends to $\omega(a^*a)$ by [A2] and continuity of inversion. Thus $U_g[a]\to[a]$ for every $[a]\in\mathcal D_\omega$. [F1, A1, A2, step 1.1, algebra]

3.1 Let $\xi\in H_\omega$ and $\varepsilon>0$. Choose $y\in\mathcal D_\omega$ with $\|\xi-y\|<\varepsilon/3$. Since each $U_g$ is unitary, $\|U_g\xi-\xi\|\le2\|\xi-y\|+\|U_gy-y\|$; step 2.2 makes the last term less than $\varepsilon/3$ for $g$ sufficiently near $e$. Hence every orbit is continuous at $e$. For any $g_0\in G$, $\|U_g\xi-U_{g_0}\xi\|=\|U_{g_0^{-1}g}\xi-\xi\|$, so continuity of multiplication transfers continuity to $g_0$. The unitary representation is strongly continuous on all of $G$. [step 1.1, step 2.2, given, algebra] ∎

items.title: Positive Weyl state without a continuous field generator
items.design_state: Fully authored draft with complete local argument; independent review remains pending.
items.statement: Assume Countable Choice, the hypothesis used to form the Hilbert completion in [[thm-qft-algebraic-gns-domain]]. The claim that positivity and the Weyl relations alone make every GNS one-parameter unitary group $t\mapsto\pi(W(tv))$ strongly continuous for every $v\ne0$ is false, even for the algebraic Weyl algebra of the standard symplectic plane.
items.strategy:
**Proof technique:** direct.

1.1 Bilinearity of $\sigma$ gives $\sigma(f,g)+\sigma(f+g,h)=\sigma(g,h)+\sigma(f,g+h)$, so the phase factors in $(W(f)W(g))W(h)$ and $W(f)(W(g)W(h))$ agree. Also $(W(f)W(g))^*=e^{i\sigma(f,g)/2}W(-f-g)=W(-g)W(-f)$ by alternation, and $W(0)$ is a two-sided unit. Thus the displayed operations define a unital complex star algebra. [given, A1, algebra]

1.2 For $a=\sum_{f\in F}c_fW(f)$ with finite support $F\subset S$, the Weyl relation gives $a^*a=\sum_{f,g\in F}\overline{c_f}c_g e^{i\sigma(f,g)/2}W(g-f)$. Only the terms $g=f$ contribute to $\omega(a^*a)$, and $\sigma(f,f)=0$, so $\omega(a^*a)=\sum_{f\in F}|c_f|^2\ge0$; also $\omega(W(0))=1$. Hence $\omega$ is a positive normalized state. [given, A1, algebra]

2.1 By [F1], its GNS quotient has dense span of the classes $[W(f)]$. For $f,g\in S$, $([W(f)],[W(g)])_\omega=\omega(W(g)^*W(f))$ is $1$ if $f=g$ and $0$ otherwise; these classes are an orthonormal family with dense span. Left multiplication satisfies $\pi(W(h))[W(f)]=e^{-i\sigma(h,f)/2}[W(h+f)]$, so it permutes this orthonormal family with unit-modulus phases and extends to a unitary on the Hilbert completion, with inverse $\pi(W(-h))$. [F1, given, step 1.2]

3.1 Fix $v\in S\setminus\{0\}$ and put $U(t):=\pi(W(tv))$ for $t\in\mathbb R$. Since $\sigma(tv,sv)=ts\sigma(v,v)=0$, the Weyl relation gives $U(t)U(s)=U(t+s)$ and $U(0)=I$. For every $t\ne0$, $U(t)\Omega=[W(tv)]$ is orthogonal to $\Omega=[W(0)]$, and both are unit vectors; thus $\|U(t)\Omega-\Omega\|=\sqrt2$. This orbit is not continuous at $0$, so $U$ is not strongly continuous. [A1, step 2.1, algebra]

4.1 Suppose a dense linear subspace $E$ had a norm derivative $\lim_{t\to0}(U(t)\xi-\xi)/t$ for every $\xi\in E$. Each such orbit would be continuous at $0$. For any $x\in H_\omega$ and $\varepsilon>0$, choose $\xi\in E$ with $\|x-\xi\|<\varepsilon/3$; unitarity gives $\|U(t)x-x\|\le2\|x-\xi\|+\|U(t)\xi-\xi\|$, so continuity on $E$ would imply continuity at $0$ for every $x$, contradicting step 3.1 at $x=\Omega$. Therefore no dense domain supports a norm-differentiable generator for this unitary group. The example is purely algebraic and asserts no physical preparation or relativistic vacuum. [step 3.1, algebra] ∎

items.title: Positive tempered moments on the tensor test algebra
items.statement:
Use the Schwartz spaces and their seminorm topologies of
[[def-schwartz-space-and-its-seminorms]] and
[[def-schwartz-topology-and-convergence]]. Put
$S:=\mathcal S(\mathbb R^4;\mathbb C)$ and
$S_n:=\mathcal S(\mathbb R^{4n};\mathbb C)$ for $n\ge1$, and set
$S_0:=\mathbb C$. A tempered distribution in $S_n'$ means a continuous
complex-linear functional on $S_n$
as in [[def-tempered-distribution]]; its pairing with a test is bilinear.

For complex vector spaces $S$, let $S^{\otimes_{\rm alg} n}$ be the algebraic
tensor product, characterized by multilinear maps out of $S^n$, with
$S^{\otimes_{\rm alg}0}:=\mathbb C1$. Define the algebraic tensor test algebra
$$T(S):=\bigoplus_{n\ge0}^{\rm alg}S^{\otimes_{\rm alg}n},$$
where the direct sum consists of finite-support sequences. Its multiplication
is concatenation of tensor factors, extended bilinearly, and its unit is $1$
in degree zero. Its conjugate-linear involution is specified on elementary
tensors by
$$(f_1\otimes\cdots\otimes f_n)^*:=\overline{f_n}\otimes\cdots\otimes\overline{f_1},\qquad (c1)^*=\overline c1.$$

For $f_j\in S$, the elementary tensor is evaluated against a distribution by
the test function
$$J_n(f_1\otimes\cdots\otimes f_n)(x_1,\ldots,x_n):=\prod_{j=1}^n f_j(x_j).$$
This is in $S_n$: for multi-indices split into four-coordinate blocks
$(\alpha_j,\beta_j)$, its Schwartz seminorm is
$$p_{(\alpha_j)_j,(\beta_j)_j}(J_n(f_1\otimes\cdots\otimes f_n))=\prod_{j=1}^n p_{\alpha_j\beta_j}(f_j).$$
Thus $J_n$ is multilinear and continuous, and the displayed formula extends
linearly to the algebraic tensor product.
In degree zero set $J_0(c1):=c$.

By these definitions concatenation is associative with the degree-zero unit,
and reversal together with complex conjugation is an involution satisfying
$(ab)^*=b^*a^*$; thus $T(S)$ is a unital complex star algebra.

A **positive tempered moment family** is a sequence consisting of $W_0=1$
and $W_n\in S_n'$ for each $n\ge1$ such that the multilinear maps
$$f_1,\ldots,f_n\longmapsto\langle W_n,J_n(f_1\otimes\cdots\otimes f_n)\rangle$$
extend, degree by degree and then over finite sums, to a complex-linear
functional $\omega:T(S)\to\mathbb C$ satisfying
$$\omega(1)=1,\qquad \omega(a^*a)\in[0,\infty)\quad(a\in T(S)).$$
Equivalently, the family supplies an actually positive normalized functional
on this algebra. Positivity is a hypothesis on the distributions; formal
coefficient families do not qualify merely because they obey algebraic
identities. No topology on $T(S)$, norm completion, C*-algebra, or existence
claim for an interacting field is part of this definition.
items.strategy: Definition of the algebraic tensor test data, positive functional, and exact topology conventions; no existence claim.

items.title: Weak operator-valued tempered distribution on a common domain
items.statement:
Let $S=\mathcal S(\mathbb R^4;\mathbb C)$ with its Schwartz topology, let $H$
be a complex Hilbert space, and let $D\subseteq H$ be a dense complex linear
subspace. Use the inner product linear in its first argument and conjugate-linear
in its second, as in [[def-real-and-complex-inner-product-space]]. A **weak
operator-valued tempered distribution on the common domain $D$** is a
complex-linear map
$$\Phi:S\longrightarrow\operatorname{Lin}(D),$$
where $\operatorname{Lin}(D)$ is the vector space of linear maps $D\to D$,
such that for every $u,v\in D$ the scalar map
$$f\longmapsto (\Phi(f)u,v)_H$$
is a continuous complex-linear functional on $S$, hence an element of
$S'=\mathcal S'(\mathbb R^4)$ by [[def-tempered-distribution]]. In particular,
every smeared map preserves the same domain $D$. This definition is weak in
the matrix-coefficient sense; it does not define point values $\Phi(x)$,
operators on all of $H$, or self-adjoint closures.
items.strategy: Definition by a common dense domain and continuous linear matrix coefficients.

items.title: Proper-orthochronous Poincaré action and test pullback
items.statement:
Fix coordinates $x=(x^0,\mathbf x)\in\mathbb R^4$ and the Minkowski matrix
$$\eta:=\operatorname{diag}(1,-1,-1,-1).$$
The proper-orthochronous Lorentz group is
$$SO^+(1,3):=\{\Lambda\in GL_4(\mathbb R):\Lambda^{\mathsf T}\eta\Lambda=\eta,\ \det\Lambda=1,\ \Lambda^0{}_0\ge1\},$$
with its subspace topology from real $4\times4$ matrices. The proper-orthochronous
Poincaré group is the semidirect product
$$P^\uparrow_+:=SO^+(1,3)\ltimes\mathbb R^4,$$
with multiplication $(\Lambda,a)(\Gamma,b)=(\Lambda\Gamma,a+\Lambda b)$,
identity $e=(I,0)$, and affine action $gx=\Lambda x+a$. Its topology is the
product topology on the matrix and translation coordinates.

For $f\in S:=\mathcal S(\mathbb R^4;\mathbb C)$ define the pointwise pullback
formula, viewed initially as a smooth function,
$$T_gf(x):=f(g^{-1}x)=f(\Lambda^{-1}(x-a)).$$
On smooth functions this formula obeys $T_gT_h=T_{gh}$ and $T_ef=f$, by the
group law. This definition specifies the formula and conventions; it does not
assert that $T_gf$ belongs to $S$. Translations have the convention
$T_{(I,z)}f(x)=f(x-z)$.

With this signature, $p\cdot z:=p^0z^0-\mathbf p\cdot\mathbf z$,
$\overline V_+:=\{p\in\mathbb R^4:p^0\ge|\mathbf p|\}$ is the closed forward
cone, and $x-y$ is spacelike exactly when
$(x^0-y^0)^2-|\mathbf x-\mathbf y|^2<0$.
items.strategy: Definition fixing the Lorentz signature, group topology, affine action, and pullback convention.

items.title: Minkowski Fourier transform and forward-cone support convention
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ ([[def-countable-choice]]), as
required by the Fourier transform suppliers. With $p\cdot z$ from
[[def-qft-poincare-test-action]], for $\psi\in\mathcal S(\mathbb R^4)$ set
$$\mathcal F_M\psi(z):=\int_{\mathbb R^4}e^{-ip\cdot z}\psi(p)\,d^4p.$$
To see that this is a continuous automorphism of Schwartz space, write
$\mathcal F_{2\pi}$ for the Euclidean transform
$\mathcal F_{2\pi}\psi(x)=\int e^{-2\pi i x\cdot p}\psi(p)\,d^4p$,
as in [[def-fourier-transform-of-a-tempered-distribution]].
For $u,v\in\mathbb R^4$, write $u\cdot_{\mathrm E}v:=\sum_{\mu=0}^3u^\mu v^\mu$.
Since $p\cdot z=(\eta z)\cdot_{\mathrm E}p$, the same defining integral gives
$$\mathcal F_M\psi(z)=(\mathcal F_{2\pi}\psi)(\eta z/(2\pi)).$$
The map $z\mapsto\eta z/(2\pi)$ is an invertible real-linear substitution,
so output composition with it is a continuous automorphism of Schwartz space
by [[lem-invertible-linear-substitutions-preserve-schwartz-space]], and
$\mathcal F_{2\pi}$ is a topological automorphism by
[[cor-fourier-transform-is-a-topological-automorphism-of-schwartz-space]].

For $D\in\mathcal S'(\mathbb R^4)$ define its Minkowski Fourier transform by
bilinear transposition,
$$\langle\widehat D_M,\psi\rangle:=\langle D,\mathcal F_M\psi\rangle\qquad(\psi\in\mathcal S(\mathbb R^4)).$$
For a closed set $C\subseteq\mathbb R^4$, the statement
$\operatorname{supp}\widehat D_M\subseteq C$ means
$\langle\widehat D_M,\psi\rangle=0$ for every compactly supported smooth
$\psi$ whose support is disjoint from $C$; the inclusion
$C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^4)\hookrightarrow\mathcal S(\mathbb R^4)$ is
[[lem-test-function-inclusion-in-schwartz-space-is-continuous]]. In particular,
the forward-cone condition means $C=\overline V_+$ with the definition in
[[def-qft-poincare-test-action]]. No joint self-adjoint energy-momentum
generators are included in this convention.
items.strategy: Definition by the stated Minkowski phase and bilinear transposition; the Schwartz automorphism relation is displayed.

items.title: Proper-orthochronous Poincaré pullbacks act continuously on Schwartz space
items.statement:
For every $g\in P^\uparrow_+$, the pullback $T_gf(x)=f(g^{-1}x)$ of
[[def-qft-poincare-test-action]] maps $S=\mathcal S(\mathbb R^4;\mathbb C)$
continuously to itself. For each fixed $f\in S$, the map
$g\mapsto T_gf$ from $P^\uparrow_+$ to $S$ is continuous. Consequently,
$\alpha_g(f_1\otimes\cdots\otimes f_n):=T_gf_1\otimes\cdots\otimes T_gf_n$
extends algebraically to a unital star-automorphism of the algebraic tensor
test algebra [[def-qft-positive-tempered-moments]], and
$\alpha_g\alpha_h=\alpha_{gh}$. No topology on the algebraic direct sum is
asserted.
items.strategy: Direct Schwartz-seminorm estimates for affine pullbacks and continuity in the group parameter.

references.locator: PDF pp. 12–17: proper-orthochronous Poincaré pullback on test functions in the Wightman framework.

items.title: Tested positive moments reconstruct closable smeared fields
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ ([[def-countable-choice]]) and let
$(W_n)_{n\ge0}$ be a positive tempered moment family on $T(S)$ as in
[[def-qft-positive-tempered-moments]]. Write $\omega$ for its linear extension,
and let $P^\uparrow_+$, $T_g$, and $\alpha_g$ be the group and pullbacks of
[[def-qft-poincare-test-action]] and
[[lem-qft-poincare-pullback-continuity-on-schwartz]]. Let
$(H_\omega,D_\omega,\pi_\omega,\Omega_\omega)$ be the GNS construction of
[[thm-qft-algebraic-gns-domain]] for this functional, with the first-variable-
linear Hilbert pairing.

For $f\in S$, put $X(f):=f$ in degree one and
$\Phi(f):=\pi_\omega(X(f))|_{D_\omega}$. Then $D_\omega$ is a common invariant
dense domain, every $\Phi(f)$ is closable with
$\Phi(\overline f)=\Phi(f)^*|_{D_\omega}$, and $\Phi$ is a weak
operator-valued tempered distribution in the exact sense of
[[def-qft-weak-operator-valued-tempered-distribution]]. Its vacuum moments are
exactly the input:
$$\bigl(\Phi(f_1)\cdots\Phi(f_n)\Omega_\omega,\Omega_\omega\bigr)=\langle W_n,J_n(f_1\otimes\cdots\otimes f_n)\rangle.$$

The following additional conclusions are conditional on additional moment
identities.

1. If $\omega\circ\alpha_g=\omega$ for every $g\in P^\uparrow_+$, then there
is a strongly continuous unitary representation $g\mapsto U_g$ on
$H_\omega$ fixing $\Omega_\omega$ and satisfying
$$U_g\Phi(f)U_g^{-1}|_{D_\omega}=\Phi(T_gf)\qquad(g\in P^\uparrow_+,\ f\in S).$$

2. Let $f,h\in\mathcal D(\mathbb R^4)=C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^4;\mathbb C)$ be
the complex test functions of [[def-test-function-space-d-of-an-open-set]],
viewed as elements of $S$ under the canonical inclusion of
[[lem-test-function-inclusion-in-schwartz-space-is-continuous]]. In this
definition, $\operatorname{supp}f$ and $\operatorname{supp}h$ are the closures
in $\mathbb R^4$ of their nonzero sets and hence compact. If these supports
are spacelike separated, meaning $(x^0-y^0)^2-|\mathbf x-\mathbf y|^2<0$ for every
$x\in\operatorname{supp}f$, $y\in\operatorname{supp}h$, and
$$\omega\bigl(b^*[X(f),X(h)]a\bigr)=0\qquad(a,b\in T(S)),$$
then $[\Phi(f),\Phi(h)]=0$ on $D_\omega$. More generally, any polynomial
relation $r\in T(S)$ satisfying $\omega(b^*ra)=0$ for all $a,b\in T(S)$ is
represented by $\pi_\omega(r)=0$ on $D_\omega$; tested field equations are
instances of this statement when their required identities are assumed.

3. For translations $\tau_z=(I,z)$ define
$$D_{b,a}(z):=\omega\bigl(b^*\alpha_{\tau_z}(a)\bigr)\qquad(a,b\in T(S)).$$
If $\omega$ is translation-invariant, each $D_{b,a}$ is a bounded continuous
function and hence a regular tempered distribution; applying the
symmetry-implementation lemma to the translation subgroup gives strongly
continuous unitaries $U_{\tau_z}$. If, in addition,
$\operatorname{supp}\widehat{D}_{b,a,M}\subseteq\overline V_+$ for every $a,b$,
with the Fourier convention of
[[def-qft-minkowski-fourier-transform]], then the reconstructed translation
matrix coefficients
$$z\longmapsto\bigl(U_{\tau_z}\pi_\omega(a)\Omega_\omega,\pi_\omega(b)\Omega_\omega\bigr)$$
have precisely the same Fourier support. This is a matrix-coefficient
spectrum condition; it does not assert joint self-adjoint energy-momentum
generators or their joint spectral measure.

This theorem reconstructs a weak field only from supplied, actually positive
continuous moments. It does not construct an unspecified positive functional,
complete a formal perturbation series, or establish the full Wightman
reconstruction theorem with assumptions not listed here.
items.strategy: Direct conditional GNS reconstruction, matrix-coefficient continuity, and support transfer under the displayed moment identities.

items.title: Radial Yukawa source power fails the homogeneous equation
items.statement:
For every $\mu\ge0$, the function
$$u_\mu(x):=\frac{e^{-\mu|x|}}{|x|^2}\qquad(x\in\mathbb R^3\setminus\{0\})$$
solves the homogeneous screened equation
$$(\Delta-\mu^2)u_\mu=0$$
at every point of $\mathbb R^3\setminus\{0\}$, where
$\Delta:=\partial_1^2+\partial_2^2+\partial_3^2$ is the Euclidean Laplacian.
The cited source uses the same off-origin Yukawa radial expression up to a
constant factor; no distributional statement at the origin is included here.
items.strategy: Explicit radial differentiation for r>0; no distributional normalization claim at the singular origin.

items.title: Finite bounded Kraus instrument
items.reference: Local A-page prerequisite added for lem-qft-finite-instrument-normalization; design source research/plan-quantum-field-theory-track.md L84 and QFT C5.
items.design_state: local-definition-prerequisite; complete explicit definition
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $H$ be a nonzero complex Hilbert space with inner product linear in its first argument ([[def-hilbert-space]], [[def-real-and-complex-inner-product-space]]). Write $\mathcal B(H)$ for the bounded linear operators on $H$ ([[def-space-of-bounded-linear-operators]]); for $M\in\mathcal B(H)$, $M^*$ is its Hilbert adjoint, characterized by $\langle Mx,y\rangle=\langle x,M^*y\rangle$ ([[def-hilbert-space-adjoint]]).

Under this same $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ hypothesis, [[thm-hilbert-adjoint-properties]] gives $M^*\in\mathcal B(H)$ and $\|M^*\|=\|M\|$.

A **finite bounded Kraus instrument datum** on $H$ consists of an integer $m\ge1$, integers $q_a\ge0$ for $a=1,\ldots,m$, and bounded operators $M_{a,r}\in\mathcal B(H)$ for $r=1,\ldots,q_a$. It is **normalized** when

$$\sum_{a=1}^{m}\sum_{r=1}^{q_a}M_{a,r}^*M_{a,r}=I_H.$$

Empty inner sums are zero. For each outcome $a$, define its outcome operator and operation by

$$E_a:=\sum_{r=1}^{q_a}M_{a,r}^*M_{a,r},\qquad \mathcal J_a(X):=\sum_{r=1}^{q_a}M_{a,r}XM_{a,r}^*\quad(X\in\mathcal B(H)).$$

These formulas take values in $\mathcal B(H)$: the adjoint theorem above makes each $M_{a,r}^*$ bounded, and $\|M_{a,r}XM_{a,r}^*x\|\le\|M_{a,r}\|\,\|X\|\,\|M_{a,r}^*\|\,\|x\|=\|M_{a,r}\|^2\,\|X\|\,\|x\|$; the sums are finite. This definition specifies only the displayed finite Kraus form; it is not a representation theorem for arbitrary instruments and does not assert that an apparatus realizes these data.

references.title: J. Watrous, The Theory of Quantum Information (Cambridge University Press, 2018; author-hosted pre-publication manuscript), §2.3.1 pp. 100–102 and §2.3.2 pp. 111–113
R. B. Griffiths, Notes on Quantum Information Theory, version 30 Jan. 2004, §7 pp. 1–3, equations (7.2)–(7.9)

items.title: Finite bounded instruments normalize measurement probabilities
items.design_state: reserved-QFT-MC03; complete conditional argument
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $H$ carry a normalized finite bounded Kraus instrument datum as defined in [[def-qft-finite-bounded-kraus-instrument]], and let $\rho$ be a density operator on $H$: a self-adjoint positive trace-class operator with $\operatorname{tr}\rho=1$ ([[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]], [[def-trace-class-operator]], [[def-trace-of-a-trace-class-operator]], [[def-self-adjoint-positive-unitary-and-normal-operator]]). For each outcome $a$, put $p_a:=\operatorname{tr}(\mathcal J_a(\rho))$. Then each $E_a$ is an effect ($E_a\ge0$ and $I_H-E_a\ge0$), each $\mathcal J_a(\rho)$ is positive trace class, and

$$p_a=\operatorname{tr}(\mathcal J_a(\rho))=\operatorname{tr}(\rho E_a)\in[0,1],\qquad \sum_{a=1}^{m}p_a=1.$$

The nonselective output $\sum_a\mathcal J_a(\rho)$ is a density operator. If $p_a>0$, the normalized conditional state $\rho_a:=\mathcal J_a(\rho)/p_a$ is a density operator; when $p_a=0$, this normalized update is undefined. For a unit vector $\psi\in H$, the rank-one density operator $\rho=T_{\psi,\psi}$ has outcome probability $p_a=\sum_{r=1}^{q_a}\|M_{a,r}\psi\|^2$. These are conditional mathematical identities; they do not assert that an apparatus realizes the instrument or supply a physical measurement postulate.
items.strategy: Define the finite bounded Kraus data explicitly, use the trace-norm density expansion and bounded trace cyclicity to prove outcome positivity and normalization, then normalize each positive-trace conditional update.

items.title: Every formal coefficient exists while convergence radius vanishes
items.design_state: reserved-QFT-MC03 B-leaf counterexample; complete local argument
items.statement:
Define $\mathbb C\llbracket g\rrbracket$ to be the set of coefficient sequences $(a_n)_{n\ge0}$, written $\sum_{n\ge0}a_ng^n$, with coefficientwise equality and addition and Cauchy multiplication: the coefficient of $g^n$ in a product is $\sum_{k=0}^na_kb_{n-k}$, a finite sum. Formal membership makes no numerical convergence assertion. For numerical evaluation use $g^0:=1$ for every $g$, including $g=0$; numerical convergence means convergence of the partial sums in $\mathbb C$. In the extended nonnegative reals $[0,+\infty]$, the numerical radius of a coefficient sequence is

$$R:=\sup\{r\in[0,+\infty): \sum_{n\ge0}a_ng^n\text{ converges for every }g\in\mathbb C\text{ with }|g|<r\},$$

where the supremum is taken in the extended order, so $R=+\infty$ when the set is unbounded. The claim to refute is that every element of $\mathbb C\llbracket g\rrbracket$ has $R>0$.

For $n\in\mathbb N_0$, define $n!:=\prod_{k=1}^{n}k$, with the empty product $0!:=1$; thus $(n+1)!=(n+1)n!$. View these integer products as coefficients in $\mathbb C$ through the canonical embedding $\mathbb Z\hookrightarrow\mathbb C$.
items.strategy: Use the coefficient sequence n! to define a formal series, then show its numerical terms fail the necessary term test for every nonzero complex coupling.

items.title: Schwartz/distribution spaces and Hilbert Fock conventions
items.statement:
For an integer $d\ge1$, let $\mathcal S(\mathbb R^d)$ be the complex Schwartz space with seminorms
$p_{\alpha\beta}(f)=\sup_{x\in\mathbb R^d}|x^\alpha\partial^\beta f(x)|$
for all multi-indices $\alpha,\beta$; this is exactly
[[def-schwartz-space-and-its-seminorms]]. Let
$\mathcal D(\mathbb R^d)=C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^d;\mathbb C)$ with the support convention of
[[def-test-function-space-d-of-an-open-set]] and the locally convex LF topology of
[[def-test-function-topology]]. The tempered-distribution space $\mathcal S'(\mathbb R^d)$
is the space of continuous complex-linear functionals on this topological
$\mathcal S(\mathbb R^d)$, paired bilinearly with test functions, as in
[[def-tempered-distribution]].

For every complex Hilbert space $H$, use the second-variable-linear pairing
$\langle u,v\rangle_2:=(v,u)_1$, where $(\cdot,\cdot)_1$ is the first-variable-linear
Hilbert pairing of [[def-real-and-complex-inner-product-space]]. Thus
$\langle u,v\rangle_2$ is linear in $v$ and conjugate-linear in $u$.
For each tensor product, use the same norm completion as
[[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]], but equip it with the
second-variable-linear pairing obtained by conjugating that supplier's
first-variable-linear pairing. This leaves the norm and completion unchanged;
on elementary tensors it gives the product of the second-variable pairings.
Let $H^{\widehat\otimes n}$ be the iterated Hilbert tensor completion, with
$H^{\widehat\otimes0}:=\mathbb C$; the tensor inner product is the product of
the factor pairings. Identify parenthesizations by the isometry fixing
elementary tensors: the product pairing is the same on their dense span,
so the map and its inverse extend to the completions. For $n\ge1$, let
$P_{s,n}=n!^{-1}\sum_{\pi\in S_n}U_\pi$ and
$P_{a,n}=n!^{-1}\sum_{\pi\in S_n}\operatorname{sgn}(\pi)U_\pi$, using the
permutation action and the orthogonal projections of
[[lem-nrqm-composites-permutation-sector-projections]]. Define
$H_s^{(n)}=\operatorname{ran}P_{s,n}$ and
$H_a^{(n)}=\operatorname{ran}P_{a,n}$, with
$H_s^{(0)}=H_a^{(0)}=\mathbb C$. These are the symmetric and antisymmetric
$n$-particle sectors.

The bosonic and fermionic Fock Hilbert spaces are the square-summable direct
sums
$\mathcal F_s(H)=\{(\Psi_n)_{n\ge0}:\Psi_n\in H_s^{(n)},\
\sum_n\|\Psi_n\|^2<\infty\}$ and
$\mathcal F_a(H)=\{(\Psi_n)_{n\ge0}:\Psi_n\in H_a^{(n)},\
\sum_n\|\Psi_n\|^2<\infty\}$, with the componentwise inner product.
Their vacuum is $\Omega=(1,0,0,\ldots)$. The finite-particle subspace
$\mathcal D_{\rm fin}$ consists of sequences with only finitely many nonzero
components.

For $h\in H$, the map $C_h:H\to\mathbb C$, $C_h(v)=\langle h,v\rangle_2$, is linear and bounded:
$|C_h(v)|=|(v,h)_1|\le\|h\|\,\|v\|$ by
[[thm-cauchy-schwarz-for-real-and-complex-inner-product-spaces]].
For any Hilbert space $K$, identify $\mathbb C\widehat\otimes K$ with $K$
by $J_K(z\otimes v)=zv$. Every algebraic tensor is $1\otimes w$;
the tensor norm is then $\|w\|$, so $J_K$ extends to a surjective isometry
on the completion (with inverse $w\mapsto1\otimes w$).
Throughout the following formulas, $C_h\otimes I^{\otimes(n-1)}$ means
$J_{H^{\widehat\otimes(n-1)}}\circ(C_h\widehat\otimes I)$, with
$I$ the identity on $H^{\widehat\otimes(n-1)}$.
The bounded tensor-map supplier therefore applies and gives norm at most
$\|h\|$. This includes $n=1$, where $H^{\widehat\otimes0}=\mathbb C$.
Contraction commutes with permutations of the remaining $n-1$ factors,
so it takes symmetric or antisymmetric tensors to the corresponding
$(n-1)$-particle sector (and to $\mathbb C$ for $n=1$).

For $n\ge0$, bosonic creation on sector $n$ is
$a_n^\dagger(h)\Psi_n=\sqrt{n+1}P_{s,n+1}(h\otimes\Psi_n)$; for $n\ge1$,
bosonic annihilation is
$a_n(h)\Psi_n=\sqrt n(C_h\otimes I^{\otimes(n-1)})\Psi_n$, where
$C_h$ is the bounded functional above, its tensor extension is supplied by
[[lem-nrqm-composites-bounded-tensor-maps]], and $a(h)\Omega=0$. Define fermionic creation
by $c_n^\dagger(h)\Psi_n=\sqrt{n+1}P_{a,n+1}(h\otimes\Psi_n)$; for $n\ge1$,
fermionic annihilation is the corresponding first-factor contraction
$c_n(h)\Psi_n=\sqrt n(C_h\otimes I^{\otimes(n-1)})\Psi_n$, and
$c(h)\Omega=0$. The annihilation maps are conjugate-linear in $h$; the
creation maps are linear in $h$. These formulas define sector maps on the
finite-particle subspace; their maximal closed domains and operator relations are proved in
[[lem-qft-fock-ccr-car]]. No physical statistics assignment or spin–statistics
theorem is part of these mathematical definitions.

items.title: Hermite functions form a graph core for position multiplication
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice [[def-countable-choice]]. Let
$H=L^2(\mathbb R,dx;\mathbb C)$ with its first-variable-linear integral pairing,
and let $Qf(x)=xf(x)$ on
$D(Q)=\{f\in H:xf\in H\}$. Let $(g_n)_{n\ge0}$ be the Hermite functions of
[[thm-nrqm-oscillator-hermite-recurrence]]. Then $Q$ is self-adjoint on $D(Q)$,
and the finite linear span of the $g_n$ is a core for $Q$: it is dense in
$D(Q)$ for the graph norm
$\|f\|_Q=(\|f\|_2^2+\|Qf\|_2^2)^{1/2}$.

items.title: Tensor products of sigma-finite L2 spaces
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice [[def-countable-choice]]. Let
$(X,\mathcal A,\mu)$ and $(Y,\mathcal B,\nu)$ be sigma-finite measure spaces,
let $\overline{\mu\times\nu}$ be their completed product measure, and put
$H_X=L^2(X,\mu;\mathbb C)$ and $H_Y=L^2(Y,\nu;\mathbb C)$ with the
second-variable-linear pairing fixed in
[[def-qft-fock-and-test-spaces]]. There is a unique unitary

$$T:H_X\widehat\otimes H_Y\longrightarrow L^2(X\times Y,\overline{\mu\times\nu};\mathbb C)$$

whose value on each elementary tensor is
$T(f\otimes g)(x,y)=f(x)g(y)$ almost everywhere. In particular, the Hilbert
tensor completion is identified with the full product $L^2$ space, not only
with the closure of a chosen class of product functions.

items.title: Bosonic and fermionic Fock operators with exact domains
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice [[def-countable-choice]] and let $H$ be a complex
Hilbert space with the second-variable-linear convention of
[[def-qft-fock-and-test-spaces]]. On $\mathcal D_{\rm fin}$ define the bosonic
creation and annihilation maps $a^\dagger(h)$ and $a(h)$ and the fermionic maps
$c^\dagger(h)$ and $c(h)$ as in
[[def-qft-fock-and-test-spaces]]. Write $a_n(h)$ and $a_n^\dagger(h)$ for
their restrictions to the $n$th bosonic sector. For bosons set

$$D(a(h))=\{\Psi\in\mathcal F_s(H):\sum_{n\ge1}\|a_n(h)\Psi_n\|^2<\infty\},\qquad D(a^\dagger(h))=\{\Psi\in\mathcal F_s(H):\sum_{n\ge0}\|a_n^\dagger(h)\Psi_n\|^2<\infty\}.$$

Then $\mathcal F_s(H)$ and $\mathcal F_a(H)$ are Hilbert spaces,
$\mathcal D_{\rm fin}$ is dense, and it is a graph core for both maximal
bosonic sector maps. The bosonic operators on their displayed domains are
closed and mutually adjoint, and on $\mathcal D_{\rm fin}$ satisfy

$$[a(h),a^\dagger(k)]=\langle h,k\rangle_2I,\qquad [a(h),a(k)]=[a^\dagger(h),a^\dagger(k)]=0.$$

The fermionic $c(h)$ and $c^\dagger(h)$ extend to bounded operators on the
whole Fock space, with norms $\|h\|$, and satisfy on the whole space

$$\{c(h),c^\dagger(k)\}=\langle h,k\rangle_2I,\qquad \{c(h),c(k)\}=\{c^\dagger(h),c^\dagger(k)\}=0.$$

This is a mathematical construction of the two Fock representations; it does
not assign particle statistics to a physical species.

items.title: One-mode factorization of symmetric Fock space
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice [[def-countable-choice]]. Let $H$ be a complex
Hilbert space, let $e\in H$ have norm one, and put
$K=e^\perp=\{v\in H:\langle e,v\rangle_2=0\}$. For
$\psi_m\in K_s^{(m)}$ and $k,m\ge0$, write
$|k\rangle:=e^{\otimes k}\in(\mathbb Ce)_s^{(k)}$ (with $|0\rangle=1$),
and define

$$J_{k,m}(|k\rangle\otimes\psi_m) =\sqrt{\binom{k+m}{k}}\, P_{s,k+m}(e^{\otimes k}\otimes\psi_m).$$

The map $J_{k,m}$ extends over the sector Hilbert tensor products and the
orthogonal direct sums to a unitary

$$J:\mathcal F_s(\mathbb Ce)\widehat\otimes\mathcal F_s(K) \longrightarrow\mathcal F_s(H).$$

Under this unitary, bosonic creation and annihilation by $e$ act on the first
factor as the one-mode ladder maps
$|k\rangle\mapsto\sqrt{k+1}|k+1\rangle$ and
$|k\rangle\mapsto\sqrt{k}|k-1\rangle$, respectively, tensored with the
identity on $\mathcal F_s(K)$, on finite-particle vectors.

items.title: Second-quantized multipliers, joint spectral measure and exact domains
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice [[def-countable-choice]]. Let
$(X,\mathcal A,\mu)$ be a sigma-finite measure space and let
$\boldsymbol\omega=(\omega_1,\ldots,\omega_d):X\to\mathbb R^d$ be a
finite-valued measurable map, where $d\ge1$. Put
$H=L^2(X,\mu;\mathbb C)$ with the second-variable-linear pairing of
[[def-qft-fock-and-test-spaces]], and form the bosonic Fock space
$\mathcal F_s(H)$. For $n\ge1$, identify $H_s^{(n)}$ with the symmetric
subspace of $L^2(X^n,\overline{\mu^{\times n}};\mathbb C)$ by iterating
[[lem-qft-l2-product-tensor-identification]]. Set $X^0=\{\star\}$,
$s_0(\star)=0$, and for $n\ge1$ set
$$s_n(x_1,\ldots,x_n)=\sum_{r=1}^n\boldsymbol\omega(x_r)\in\mathbb R^d.$$
For $1\le j\le d$, define $H_j$ by multiplication by the $j$th coordinate
$s_{n,j}$ on sector $n$, with exact domain
$$D(H_j)=\left\{\Psi=(\Psi_n): \sum_{n\ge1}\int_{X^n}|s_{n,j}|^2|\Psi_n|^2\,d\overline{\mu^{\times n}}<\infty\right\}.$$
Each $H_j$ is self-adjoint, and $\mathcal D_{\rm fin}\cap D(H_j)$ is a
graph core. The joint projection-valued measure
[[def-projection-valued-measure]] on $\mathbb R^d$ is
$$(E(B)\Psi)_n=\mathbf1_{s_n^{-1}(B)}\Psi_n\quad(n\ge1),\qquad (E(B)\Psi)_0=\mathbf1_B(0)\Psi_0.$$
For $\theta\in\mathbb R^d$, let $H_\theta$ be multiplication on sector $n$
by $\theta\cdot s_n$, with its maximal square-integrability domain. Then
$$U_\theta(t)\Psi:=\bigl(e^{it\theta\cdot s_n}\Psi_n\bigr)_{n\ge0}$$
is a strongly continuous unitary group on all of Fock space, and its norm
derivative at zero exists exactly for $\Psi\in D(H_\theta)$, where it is
$iH_\theta\Psi$. The zero-particle sector is the vacuum eigenvector at joint
value $0$.

items.title: Self-adjoint Segal fields and explicit Weyl unitaries
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice [[def-countable-choice]]. Let $H$ be a separable
complex Hilbert space with the second-variable-linear convention of
[[def-qft-fock-and-test-spaces]], and let $\mathcal F_s(H)$ and
$\mathcal D_{\rm fin}$ be its bosonic Fock space and finite-particle domain.
For $h\in H$ define on $\mathcal D_{\rm fin}$ the Segal field
$$\phi_0(h):=2^{-1/2}\bigl(a^\dagger(h)+a(h)\bigr).$$
For $h\ne0$, this symmetric operator is essentially self-adjoint; write
$\Phi(h)=\overline{\phi_0(h)}$. If $r=\|h\|$, $e=h/r$, $K=e^\perp$,
$G=\mathcal F_s(K)$, choose a countable orthonormal basis $(u_j)$ of $G$
whose vectors are finite-particle, and use the one-mode splitting of
[[lem-qft-fock-one-mode-splitting]] followed by the Hermite unitary
$|n\rangle\mapsto g_n$ into $L^2(\mathbb R,dx;\mathbb C)$ with pairing
$\langle f,g\rangle_2=\int\overline f g$ to write a vector as
$(f_j)_{j\in J}\in\ell^2(J;L^2(\mathbb R,dx;\mathbb C))$. Then the exact domain and
action are
$$D(\Phi(h))=\left\{(f_j):\sum_{j\in J}\int_{\mathbb R}(1+r^2x^2)|f_j(x)|^2\,dx<\infty\right\},\qquad (\Phi(h)f)_j(x)=rx f_j(x).$$
For $h=0$, $\phi_0(0)$ closes to the zero operator on all of $\mathcal F_s(H)$.

Define $\epsilon(z)=\bigoplus_{n\ge0}z^{\otimes n}/\sqrt{n!}$ for $z\in H$.
There are unitaries $W(h)$ determined on these total exponential vectors by
$$W(h)\epsilon(z)=\exp\!\left(-\frac{\|h\|^2}{4} +\frac{i}{\sqrt2}\langle h,z\rangle_2\right) \epsilon\!\left(z+\frac{i h}{\sqrt2}\right).$$
They obey
$$W(h)W(k)=\exp\!\left(-\frac{i}{2}\operatorname{Im}\langle h,k\rangle_2\right)W(h+k),\qquad \langle\Omega,W(h)\Omega\rangle_2=e^{-\|h\|^2/4},$$
and $h\mapsto W(h)$ is strongly continuous. For every $h$, the one-parameter
group $t\mapsto W(th)$ has norm derivative at zero exactly on
$D(\Phi(h))$, with derivative $i\Phi(h)$ (for $h=0$ this is the zero
generator). Thus the displayed bounded Weyl operators have precisely the
closed Segal fields as their generators; no point-field or measurement claim
is included.

items.title: One-mode CCR/CAR and a vector outside the number-operator domain
items.statement:
Let $H=\mathbb Ce$ with $\|e\|=1$, and write $|n\rangle=e^{\otimes n}$
for its normalized bosonic $n$-particle vector, including $|0\rangle=\Omega$.
On the one-mode fermionic Fock space write $|1\rangle=c^\dagger(e)\Omega$.
The one-mode bosonic and fermionic operators satisfy the CCR and CAR on their
stated domains. The bosonic number operator from
[[lem-qft-second-quantized-spectrum]] is
$N|n\rangle=n|n\rangle$ with
$$D(N)=\left\{(c_n)_{n\ge0}:\sum_{n\ge0}n^2|c_n|^2<\infty\right\}.$$
The Fock vector
$$\Psi=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}(n+1)^{-3/2}|n\rangle$$
belongs to $D(a(e))\cap D(a^\dagger(e))$ but not to $D(N)$.

exact_row.title: Scalar future mass-shell measure and test restriction

items.title: Scalar future mass shell, invariant measure and test restriction
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice [[def-countable-choice]]. Here
$\mathscr S(\mathbb R^4)$ is the Schwartz space of smooth complex functions
whose coordinate-weighted derivatives are all bounded, as defined in
[[def-schwartz-space-and-its-seminorms]].
Fix an oriented, time-oriented affine Minkowski space and an inertial coordinate
chart as in [[def-sr-affine-minkowski-model]] and
[[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]]. Use coordinates
$x=(x^0,\mathbf x)$ and metric $\eta=\mathrm{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$, matching the
$(-+++)$ convention of the SR suppliers. Some QFT sources use its negative
$(+---)$; the Lorentz group is unchanged, and the phase is fixed explicitly
below.
Coordinates $x$ have length units, momenta have inverse-length units, and the
Fourier phase below is dimensionless. A parameter $\mu\ge0$ has inverse-length
units and is only a mathematical shell parameter; it is not identified with a
physical rest mass. For $\mathbf k\in\mathbb R^3$, set
$$\omega_\mu(\mathbf k)=\sqrt{|\mathbf k|^2+\mu^2},\qquad p_\mu(\mathbf k)=(\omega_\mu(\mathbf k),\mathbf k).$$
The future mass shell is
$$H_\mu^+=\{(p^0,\mathbf p): (p^0)^2-|\mathbf p|^2=\mu^2,\ p^0>0\}.$$
When $\mu=0$, its apex is omitted; thus $\mathbf k\ne0$ in the massless
parameterization. The scalar shell pairing is
$$p\circ x:=p^0x^0-\mathbf p\cdot\mathbf x=-\eta(p,x).$$
Define the measure and one-particle Hilbert space by
$$d\nu_\mu(p_\mu(\mathbf k))= \frac{d^3\mathbf k}{(2\pi)^3\,2\omega_\mu(\mathbf k)},\qquad H_\mu=L^2(H_\mu^+,d\nu_\mu;\mathbb C),$$
where the omitted massless apex has measure zero. For $f\in\mathscr S(\mathbb
R^4)$ define its pointwise shell Fourier restriction by
$$K_\mu f(p)=\int_{\mathbb R^4}f(x)e^{ip\circ x}\,d^4x.$$
The Fourier convention is exactly the displayed integral, with no prefactor.
If $\widehat f(\xi^0,\boldsymbol\xi)=
\int f(x)e^{-2\pi i(x^0\xi^0+\mathbf x\cdot\boldsymbol\xi)}\,d^4x$ denotes
the standard transform in
[[cor-fourier-transform-is-a-topological-automorphism-of-schwartz-space]],
then
$$\mathcal F_+f(p^0,\mathbf p):=\int f(x)e^{i(p^0x^0-\mathbf p\cdot\mathbf x)}\,d^4x =\widehat f\!\left(-\frac{p^0}{2\pi},\frac{\mathbf p}{2\pi}\right).$$
Its inverse is
$$f(x)=(2\pi)^{-4}\int_{\mathbb R^4} \mathcal F_+f(p^0,\mathbf p)e^{-i(p^0x^0-\mathbf p\cdot\mathbf x)} \,dp^0\,d^3\mathbf p.$$
Thus this convention is a time reflection and rescaling of the cited
Schwartz automorphism and has the stated reciprocal normalization.
The proper orthochronous Lorentz group consists of linear maps preserving
$\eta$, orientation and the chosen future cone. A Poincare map is
$x\mapsto a+\Lambda x$ with $a\in\mathbb R^4$ and $\Lambda$ in that group.

This is a mathematical free scalar one-particle construction. It adopts the
chosen coordinates, measure and Fourier convention; it asserts no experimental
observation, physical mass identification or measurement outcome.

items.title: Local finiteness and Lorentz invariance of the scalar shell measure
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice. For every $\mu\ge0$, the measure $d\nu_\mu$ of
[[def-qft-scalar-mass-shell]] is locally finite and sigma-finite on $H_\mu^+$.
For every proper orthochronous Lorentz transformation $\Lambda$ and every
nonnegative Borel function $g$ on $H_\mu^+$,
$$\int_{H_\mu^+}g(\Lambda^{-1}p)\,d\nu_\mu(p) =\int_{H_\mu^+}g(p)\,d\nu_\mu(p).$$
The claim applies off the omitted apex when $\mu=0$.

items.title: Density of Schwartz test restrictions in the scalar shell space
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice [[def-countable-choice]]. For every $\mu\ge0$, the
space $H_\mu=L^2(H_\mu^+,d\nu_\mu)$ of
[[def-qft-scalar-mass-shell]] is separable, and
$$\{K_\mu f:f\in\mathscr S(\mathbb R^4)\}$$
is dense in $H_\mu$. If $\mu>0$, the range contains every function in
$C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^3)$; if $\mu=0$, it contains every function in
$C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^3\setminus\{0\})$.

references.title: Richard B. Melrose, MIT OpenCourseWare 18.155 Differential Analysis, Fall 2004, lecture notes, section 9
references.locator: Complete five-page official MIT OCW PDF, printed pages 58–62; Theorem 9.1 proves the Fourier transform isomorphism on Schwartz space and gives its inverse.

items.title: Continuity and Klein–Gordon annihilation of scalar shell restriction
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice [[def-countable-choice]]. For every $\mu\ge0$, the
pointwise restriction
$$K_\mu f(p)=\int_{\mathbb R^4}f(x)e^{ip\circ x}\,d^4x$$
of [[def-qft-scalar-mass-shell]] maps $\mathscr S(\mathbb R^4)$ continuously
and linearly into $H_\mu$. It also annihilates the Klein–Gordon test operator:
$$K_\mu\bigl((\partial_0^2-\Delta+\mu^2)f\bigr)=0 \qquad(f\in\mathscr S(\mathbb R^4)).$$
The coordinates are the fixed length coordinates of that definition and
$\mu$ has inverse-length units.

items.title: Unitary lift to bosonic Fock space
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice [[def-countable-choice]]. Let $H$ and $K$ be complex
Hilbert spaces and let $U:H\to K$ be unitary. The sector maps
$U^{\otimes n}$ restrict to unitaries $U_s^{(n)}:H_s^{(n)}\to K_s^{(n)}$;
their direct sum
$$\Gamma_s(U)=\bigoplus_{n=0}^\infty U_s^{(n)}$$
is unitary, maps vacuum to vacuum, and maps the finite-particle domain
$\mathcal D_{\rm fin}(H)$ onto $\mathcal D_{\rm fin}(K)$. It intertwines the
creation and annihilation maps:
$$\Gamma_s(U)a_H^\dagger(h)\Gamma_s(U)^{-1}=a_K^\dagger(Uh),\qquad \Gamma_s(U)a_H(h)\Gamma_s(U)^{-1}=a_K(Uh)$$
on the finite-particle domain. If $g\mapsto U_g$ is a strongly continuous
family of unitaries, then $g\mapsto\Gamma_s(U_g)$ is strongly continuous.

references.locator: Author-hosted HTML text of chapter 2, section 2.4, multiparticle Fock states; the complete lecture-note set is also listed as a 155-page PDF. The arbitrary-unitary lift and continuity claim are proved from the exact tensor-sector definitions on this page.

items.title: Strongly continuous scalar one-particle Poincare action
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice [[def-countable-choice]]. Use the proper
orthochronous Poincare group
$G=\mathbb R^4\rtimes SO^+(1,3)$ in the coordinates of
[[def-qft-scalar-mass-shell]]. For $g=(a,\Lambda)\in G$, define
$$f_g(x)=f(\Lambda^{-1}(x-a)),\qquad [U_\mu(g)h](p)=e^{ip\circ a}h(\Lambda^{-1}p).$$
Then $f_g\in\mathscr S(\mathbb R^4)$, $U_\mu(g)$ is a well-defined unitary
on $H_\mu$, $g\mapsto U_\mu(g)$ is a strongly continuous representation, and
$$K_\mu f_g=U_\mu(g)K_\mu f \qquad(f\in\mathscr S(\mathbb R^4)).$$
The group product convention is
$(a,\Lambda)(b,\Gamma)=(a+\Lambda b,\Lambda\Gamma)$.

items.title: Smeared free scalar field and its Poincare representation
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice [[def-countable-choice]], let $\mu\ge0$, let
$H_\mu$ and $K_\mu$ be as in [[def-qft-scalar-mass-shell]], and form
$\mathcal F_s(H_\mu)$ with vacuum $\Omega$ and finite-particle domain
$\mathcal D_{\rm fin}$. For $f\in\mathscr S(\mathbb R^4)$ define on
$\mathcal D_{\rm fin}$
$$\Phi_\mu(f)=a(K_\mu\overline f)+a^\dagger(K_\mu f).$$
This is a complex-linear map of test functions into operators
$\mathcal D_{\rm fin}\to\mathcal D_{\rm fin}$. For real $f$ it is symmetric
and equals $\sqrt2\,\Phi_{\rm Segal}(K_\mu f)|_{\mathcal D_{\rm fin}}$, where the Segal field of
[[lem-qft-segal-weyl-domain]] is
$\Phi_{\rm Segal}(h)=\overline{(a^\dagger(h)+a(h))/\sqrt2}$.
Thus its Weyl unitary is
$W_\mu(f):=W_{\rm Segal}(\sqrt2 K_\mu f)$ and, for real $f,g$,
$$W_\mu(f)W_\mu(g)= e^{-i\,\operatorname{Im}\langle K_\mu f,K_\mu g\rangle_2}W_\mu(f+g).$$
For every real $f$ the vacuum Weyl expectation is
$$\langle\Omega,W_\mu(f)\Omega\rangle_2 =e^{-\|K_\mu f\|_2^2/2}.$$
Here the inner product is second-variable-linear as fixed in
[[def-qft-fock-and-test-spaces]]. The vacuum has zero one-point function and
two-point function
$$\langle\Omega,\Phi_\mu(f)\Phi_\mu(g)\Omega\rangle_2 =\langle K_\mu\overline f,K_\mu g\rangle_2,$$
which obeys $\langle\Omega,\Phi_\mu(\overline f)\Phi_\mu(f)\Omega\rangle_2=\|K_\mu f\|_2^2\ge0$ for every complex test $f$ (ordinary diagonal positivity holds for real tests); higher vacuum moments of ordered real smeared
fields obey the CCR pairing recursion and hence the free-field Wick pairing
rule. The field is a weak operator-valued tempered distribution on $\mathcal D_{\rm fin}$: every matrix coefficient $f\mapsto\langle\Psi,\Phi_\mu(f)\Theta\rangle_2$ for $\Psi,\Theta\in\mathcal D_{\rm fin}$ is a continuous complex-linear functional on Schwartz space. Its adjoint satisfies $\Phi_\mu(f)^*|_{\mathcal D_{\rm fin}}=\Phi_\mu(\overline f)$, and its normalized vacuum defines a positive state on the finite polynomial $*$-algebra generated by these fields.

The relative-coordinate two-point tempered distribution is
$$W_\mu(z)=\int_{H_\mu^+}e^{-ip\circ z}\,d\nu_\mu(p),$$
understood by pairing with Schwartz tests. Its translation-invariant bidistribution is the shell integral of $e^{-ip\circ x}e^{ip\circ y}$; on product tests it is the displayed vacuum covariance.

For $g=(a,\Lambda)$, let $f_g$ and $U_\mu(g)$ be the affine test pullback
and one-particle action of [[lem-qft-scalar-poincare-action]]. Their Fock
lifts implement the same covariance for $\Phi_\mu$ on $\mathcal D_{\rm fin}$
and for the bounded Weyl operators.

For translations, the joint spectral measure on Fock space is the
second-quantized multiplier measure with one-particle vector
$(\omega_\mu(\mathbf k),-\mathbf k)$. Its support is contained in the closed
future cone $\{(E,\mathbf P):E\ge|\mathbf P|\}$; the vacuum is an eigenvector
at $(0,\mathbf0)$. These are conditional mathematical model deductions.
No point field, empirical observation or measurement claim is made.

items.title: Causal support of the scalar commutator distribution
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice. For $\mu\ge0$, define the tempered distribution
$$\Delta_\mu(t,\mathbf x)= \int_{\mathbb R^3}\frac{d^3\mathbf k}{(2\pi)^3} \frac{\sin(\omega_\mu(\mathbf k)t)}{\omega_\mu(\mathbf k)} e^{i\mathbf k\cdot\mathbf x},$$
with the massless integrand defined off $\mathbf k=0$; its $1/|\mathbf k|$
behavior is locally integrable in three dimensions. Then
$$\operatorname{supp}\Delta_\mu \subseteq\{(t,\mathbf x):t^2-|\mathbf x|^2\ge0\},$$
the closed causal cone for the $(-+++)$ metric. For real compactly supported
smooth $f,g$, put
$$\Delta_\mu(f,g)= \int_{\mathbb R^4}\!\int_{\mathbb R^4} f(x)g(y)\Delta_\mu(x-y)\,d^4x\,d^4y.$$
On $\mathcal D_{\rm fin}$ the smeared fields of
[[lem-qft-smeared-free-scalar]] satisfy
$$[\Phi_\mu(f),\Phi_\mu(g)]=-i\Delta_\mu(f,g)I.$$
Consequently spacelike-separated supports give commuting fields.

items.title: Isotony and spacelike commutativity of scalar local Weyl algebras
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice [[def-countable-choice]].
Let $O\subseteq\mathbb R^4$ be open. For real
$f\in C_c^\infty(O)$ define
$$W_\mu(f):=W_{\rm Segal}(\sqrt2K_\mu f),$$
where the Segal normalization is exactly
$\Phi_{\rm Segal}(h)=(a^\dagger(h)+a(h))/\sqrt2$ on the finite-particle
domain, as in [[lem-qft-segal-weyl-domain]]. This scale makes the self-adjoint generator
of $t\mapsto W_\mu(tf)$ equal to the closure $\overline{\Phi_\mu(f)}$,
whose restriction to $\mathcal D_{\rm fin}$ is the real scalar field
$\Phi_\mu(f)=a(K_\mu f)+a^\dagger(K_\mu f)$ of
[[lem-qft-smeared-free-scalar]]. Define the unital norm-closed operator
algebra
$$\mathfrak A_\mu(O)= \overline{\operatorname{alg}}^{\|\cdot\|} \{I,W_\mu(f),W_\mu(f)^*:f\in C_c^\infty(O;\mathbb R)\}.$$
Then $O_1\subseteq O_2$ implies
$\mathfrak A_\mu(O_1)\subseteq\mathfrak A_\mu(O_2)$. If every difference
$x-y$, with $x\in O_1$ and $y\in O_2$, is spacelike, then every element of
$\mathfrak A_\mu(O_1)$ commutes with every element of
$\mathfrak A_\mu(O_2)$. These are algebraic properties of the constructed
representation; they are not empirical signaling or measurement claims.

items.title: Positive vacuum correlation for spacelike-separated massless tests
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice. In the massless model $\mu=0$, there are nonnegative
real test functions
$f,g\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^4)$ with spacelike-separated supports for which
$$\langle\Omega,\Phi_0(f)\Omega\rangle_2 =\langle\Omega,\Phi_0(g)\Omega\rangle_2=0,\qquad \langle\Omega,\Phi_0(f)\Phi_0(g)\Omega\rangle_2>0.$$
The corresponding local Weyl operators commute by
[[lem-qft-scalar-local-weyl-algebra]]. The nonzero correlation is a
mathematical vacuum expectation in the specified representation; it is not a
measurement or a signaling effect.

items.title: Exact massless scalar on a conformally flat external metric
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ of [[def-countable-choice]]. On $M=\mathbb R^4$ with global coordinates $x=(x^0,x^1,x^2,x^3)$, set $\eta_{ab}=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$, orient $M$ by $o=dx^0\wedge dx^1\wedge dx^2\wedge dx^3$, and use $\partial_0$ to select the standard future cone. Coordinates have length units, derivatives have inverse-length units, and the Fourier phase and conformal factor are dimensionless, consistent with [[def-qft-scalar-mass-shell]]. Thus $\Box_\eta$, $\Box_g$, $R_g$, and $P_g$ have inverse-length-squared units. Let $\Omega\in C^\infty(\mathbb R^4;(0,\infty))$ be real and dimensionless, and define the prescribed external Lorentzian metric $g_{ab}=\Omega^2\eta_{ab}$. No field equation for $g$ is assumed. Write $d\mathrm{vol}_g=\Omega^4d^4x$ for its positive integration density and $\Box_\eta=\eta^{ab}\partial_a\partial_b$. Let $R_g$ be the scalar curvature with the convention of [[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]], which is also used by [[thm-emg-conformal-einstein-transformation]], and define
$$\Box_g h:=\Omega^{-4}\partial_a\!\left(\Omega^2\eta^{ab}\partial_bh\right),\qquad P_g:=\Box_g-\frac16R_g.$$
The test space is $\mathcal D=C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^4;\mathbb C)$ with the LF test-function topology of [[def-test-function-topology]]. Let $\Phi_0$ be the massless Minkowski Fock field and let $\varpi_0\in\mathcal D_{\rm fin}$ be its normalized vacuum vector, written $|0\rangle$ in Dirac notation. The common dense invariant domain and field convention are those of [[lem-qft-smeared-free-scalar]] and [[lem-qft-scalar-causal-commutator]]. For $f\in\mathcal D$, define the curved-background smeared field by
$$\Phi_g(f):=\Phi_0(\Omega^3f).$$

Then, with all equalities understood on $\mathcal D_{\rm fin}$ or as distributional equalities as appropriate:

1. The exact curvature and scalar wave identities are
$$R_g=-6\Omega^{-3}\Box_\eta\Omega,\qquad P_g(\Omega^{-1}u)=\Omega^{-3}\Box_\eta u\quad(u\in C^\infty(\mathbb R^4;\mathbb C)).$$

2. The map $f\mapsto\Phi_g(f)$ is a weak operator-valued distribution on $\mathcal D_{\rm fin}$, meaning that for every $\chi,\psi\in\mathcal D_{\rm fin}$ the map $f\mapsto\langle\chi,\Phi_g(f)\psi\rangle_2$ is a continuous complex-linear functional on $\mathcal D$ with its test-function topology. It satisfies $\Phi_g(P_gf)=0$ for every $f\in\mathcal D$. The normalized Minkowski vacuum defines a positive state on the finite polynomial $*$-algebra generated by the real-test fields.

3. If $\operatorname{supp}f$ and $\operatorname{supp}h$ are spacelike separated (every pair of points in the two supports has positive $\eta$-squared separation), then $[\Phi_g(f),\Phi_g(h)]=0$ on $\mathcal D_{\rm fin}$.

4. The two-point distribution relative to $d\mathrm{vol}_g(x)d\mathrm{vol}_g(y)$ is
$$W_g(x,y)=\Omega(x)^{-1}\Omega(y)^{-1}W_0(x,y),$$
where $W_0$ is the massless Minkowski Fock-vacuum two-point distribution from [[lem-qft-smeared-free-scalar]], relative to $d^4x\,d^4y$ and paired bilinearly as $W_0(f,h)=\langle\varpi_0,\Phi_0(f)\Phi_0(h)\varpi_0\rangle_2$. On compact tests, $P_g$ is formally symmetric for $d\mathrm{vol}_g$.

This is a selected free-field representation obtained from one Minkowski Fock vacuum. It asserts no uniqueness of a curved-spacetime state, generic Hadamard-state existence, thermal-state result, renormalized stress-tensor transformation, massive or minimally coupled result, Einstein equation, or backreaction claim. The metric is prescribed background data, not a dynamical solution.

items.title: Constant conformal factor verifies field and volume normalization
items.statement: Take the theorem's external metric with a constant conformal factor $\Omega=b>0$, so $g=b^2\eta$. The scalar field is smeared by $\Phi_g(f)=\Phi_0(b^3f)$ relative to $d\mathrm{vol}_g=b^4d^4x$. In particular, $R_g=0$ and $P_g=b^{-2}\Box_\eta$. Relative to $d\mathrm{vol}_g(x)d\mathrm{vol}_g(y)$, the two-point kernel is $W_g(x,y)=b^{-2}W_0(x,y)$, so its double smearing is $b^6$ times the flat covariance. This example checks the constant-factor normalization only; it asserts no preferred state for a general curved metric.

items.title: Quantum field quantities and compatible SI normalizations
items.design_state: planned local unit and domain definition; complete SI consistency argument, model conventions, and scope boundaries authored
items.physical_scope: A unit and domain dictionary for selected quantum-field model data in four-dimensional Minkowski length coordinates. It declares engineering normalizations and conventions only; it constructs no field representation, QED dynamics, continuum limit, apparatus, or empirical result.
items.statement:
Fix the oriented, time-oriented affine Minkowski spacetime and an inertial
chart of [[def-sr-affine-minkowski-model]] and
[[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]]. Use signature
$\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$, length coordinates
$x^0=ct$ and $x^i$ in metres, and coordinate time $t$ in seconds as in
[[def-sr-si-units-and-coordinate-conventions]]. Greek spacetime indices run
from $0$ to $3$; spatial indices run from $1$ to $3$ and are contracted with
the Euclidean spatial metric. The coordinates $x^a$ have unit metre and
$\partial_a:=\partial/\partial x^a$ has unit $\mathrm m^{-1}$.

The positive constants $c$, $h$ and $e_{\rm SI}$ have the exact SI defining
values; write $\hbar:=h/(2\pi)$. The magnetic constant $\mu_0>0$ has SI unit
$\mathrm{N\,A^{-2}}$ and is experimentally determined under the current SI;
no exact numerical value or current estimate for it is adopted. Put
$\varepsilon_0=(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}$ when that symbol is used. These are SI
normalization inputs, not empirical claims about a selected QFT model.

For a species with rest mass $m_{\rm rest,SI}>0$ in kilograms define its
inverse-length mass parameter

$$\mu:=\frac{m_{\rm rest,SI}c}{\hbar}\quad[\mathrm m^{-1}].$$

For a spatial wave vector $\mathbf k\in\mathbb R^3$, with each component in
$\mathrm m^{-1}$ and the Euclidean norm, define
$\omega_\mu(\mathbf k):=\sqrt{|\mathbf k|^2+\mu^2}\in\mathbb R_{>0}$, with
unit $\mathrm m^{-1}$. Here $\omega_\mu$ is the temporal wave number, not the
SI angular frequency; the corresponding SI angular frequency is
$c\omega_\mu$. Energy and momentum are $E=\hbar c\omega_\mu$ in joules and
$\mathbf p=\hbar\mathbf k$ in $\mathrm{kg\,m\,s^{-1}}$. With
$p=(\omega_\mu(\mathbf k),\mathbf k)\in\mathbb R^4$ and
$x=(x^0,\mathbf x)\in\mathbb R^4$, the phase convention is

$$p\mathbin{\circ}x:=\omega_\mu(\mathbf k)x^0-\mathbf k\cdot\mathbf x=-\eta(p,x).$$

For a selected local action represented on a chart region
$\mathcal U\subseteq\mathbb R^4$ by
$$\frac{S}{\hbar}=\int_{\mathcal U}\mathcal L_{\mathrm{nat}}(x)\,d^4x,\quad d^4x:=dx^0dx^1dx^2dx^3,$$
the natural Lagrangian density $\mathcal L_{\mathrm{nat}}$ has unit
$\mathrm m^{-4}$. Since $x^0=ct$, the corresponding SI Lagrangian density is
$\mathcal L_{\mathrm{SI}}:=\hbar c\,\mathcal L_{\mathrm{nat}}$ and has unit
$\mathrm{J\,m^{-3}}$. This unit conversion alone does not identify a
Lagrangian density with the model's Hamiltonian energy density.

For canonical engineering dimensions in this four-dimensional normalization,
use the formal field symbols $\phi_{\rm n}$ and $\psi_{\rm n}$ in the selected
scalar and Dirac kinetic terms, assigning them length degrees $-1$ and
$-3/2$, respectively. These are the dimensions fixed by those free kinetic
terms, not exact scaling dimensions of interacting fields: anomalous
dimensions, when present, are separate quantities. These symbols do not
assert pointwise field maps or operator fields; a model supplies its field
space and regularity. Let $A^\mu_{\rm SI}=(\varphi/c,\mathbf A)$ and
$F^{\mu\nu}_{\rm SI}$ use the component convention of
[[def-em-electromagnetic-tensor]], namely
$F_{0i}=-E_i/c$ and $F_{ij}=\epsilon_{ijk}B_k$, with
$F_{\mu\nu}=\partial_\mu A_\nu-\partial_\nu A_\mu$ only when a potential is
supplied. Define the normalized photon potential and field strength by

$$a^\mu:=\frac{A^\mu_{\rm SI}}{\sqrt{\mu_0\hbar c}},\qquad f^{\mu\nu}:=\frac{F^{\mu\nu}_{\rm SI}}{\sqrt{\mu_0\hbar c}}.$$

They have length degrees $-1$ and $-2$, respectively. The EM supplier is used
only for SI units and tensor components: no classical Maxwell equation,
Lorentz-force law, or classical-to-quantum identification is adopted here.

For any separately declared SI charge parameter $q_{\rm SI}$ in coulombs put

$$q_{\rm n}:=q_{\rm SI}\sqrt{\frac{\mu_0c}{\hbar}}.$$

It is dimensionless. For the positive exact SI elementary charge use
$e_{\rm n}:=e_{\rm SI}\sqrt{\mu_0c/\hbar}$ and define the rationalized
dimensionless coupling $\alpha:=e_{\rm n}^2/(4\pi)$. Since $\mu_0$ is
measured, these formulas do not assign an exact numerical value to
$e_{\rm n}$ or $\alpha$. If the model uses minimal coupling, its convention is
$D_\mu=\partial_\mu-iq_{\rm n}a_\mu$; for an electron with
$q_{\rm SI}=-e_{\rm SI}$ this reads $D_\mu=\partial_\mu+ie_{\rm n}a_\mu$.
Bare, renormalized-at-scale, and measured effective charges are separately
labelled model parameters; applying the conversion to one label does not
identify it with either of the others or specify a running law.

In a supplied four-component spinor representation, let
$\gamma^a\in\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb C}(\mathbb C^4)$, $a=0,1,2,3$, be
dimensionless linear maps satisfying
$\{\gamma^a,\gamma^b\}:=\gamma^a\gamma^b+\gamma^b\gamma^a
=-2\eta^{ab}I_4$, where $I_4$ is the identity map. Set $\beta:=\gamma^0$
and $\alpha^i:=\beta\gamma^i$; then $\beta^2=I_4$ and
$\gamma^i=\beta\alpha^i$. For a supplied four-component spinor $\psi$ write
$\bar\psi:=\psi^\dagger\beta$. The effective Clifford metric is $-\eta$.
A supplied free Dirac model may use
$(i\gamma^a\partial_a-\mu)\psi=0$ for its model-supplied spinor field
$\psi$; that model supplies its field domain and regularity. The phase and
Clifford choices are conventions; this item proves no representation or field
equation.

For the autonomous evolution convention, assume Countable Choice
[[def-countable-choice]]: every sequence of nonempty sets has a choice
function. Let a selected model supply a complex Hilbert space $\mathscr H$
as in [[def-hilbert-space]] and a time-independent complex-linear Hamiltonian
$H:D(H)\to\mathscr H$ with a specified dense linear domain
$D(H)\subseteq\mathscr H$ and SI energy
unit joules. Require self-adjointness as in
[[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]]: $H=H^*$,
including equality of domains and values. Here $y\in D(H^*)$ precisely when
there is a $z\in\mathscr H$ such that
$\langle Hx,y\rangle=\langle x,z\rangle$ for every $x\in D(H)$, and
$H^*y=z$; density makes $z$ unique.

The published mathematical supplier
[[lem-nrqm-controlled-dynamics-cc-arbitrary-hilbert-spectral-calculus]]
then supplies the spectral measure $E_H$ on the Borel subsets of
$\mathbb R$. This is a normalized projection-valued measure as in
[[def-projection-valued-measure]]: its values are bounded orthogonal
projections, $E_H(\mathbb R)=I$, $E_H(B\cap C)=E_H(B)E_H(C)$, and it is
countably additive in norm on every vector. For $\xi\in\mathscr H$ put
$\nu_\xi(B):=\langle E_H(B)\xi,\xi\rangle$, a finite positive measure.
The spectral integral of $\lambda$ represents $H$, on exactly the domain
$D(H)=\{\xi\in\mathscr H:\int_{\mathbb R}\lambda^2\,d\nu_\xi(\lambda)<\infty\}$.
For real $t$ in seconds define the autonomous evolution by bounded Borel
functional calculus,
$$U(t):=\exp(-itH/\hbar):=\int_{\mathbb R}e^{-it\lambda/\hbar}\,dE_H(\lambda).$$
The spectral variable $\lambda$ carries unit joule. This exponential is a
bounded operator on all of $\mathscr H$, even when $H$ is unbounded; it
does not mean an operator power series on arbitrary vectors. The supplier
gives a strongly continuous unitary group: $U(0)=I$,
$U(t+s)=U(t)U(s)$ and $\|U(t)\xi-U(t_0)\xi\|\to0$ as $t\to t_0$ for
each $\xi\in\mathscr H$. A model may restrict it to a declared
$I\subseteq\mathbb R$. Each $U(t)$ is a surjective complex-linear map
satisfying $\langle U(t)\xi,U(t)\zeta\rangle=\langle\xi,\zeta\rangle$
for all $\xi,\zeta\in\mathscr H$; write $U(t)^*:=U(t)^{-1}$. The exponent
is dimensionless because $\hbar$ has unit $\mathrm{J\,s}$. For any
model-supplied complex-linear operator $O:D(O)\to\mathscr H$, with specified
linear domain $D(O)\subseteq\mathscr H$, define its Heisenberg conjugate by
$$O_H(t):=U(t)^*O\,U(t),\quad D(O_H(t)):=\{\xi\in\mathscr H:U(t)\xi\in D(O)\}.$$
The model supplies the Hamiltonian and operator domains; the spectral supplier
justifies this evolution only for those data and hypotheses. This dictionary
constructs no model-specific Hamiltonian or field representation and does not
adopt a physical dynamics law. Where a free-field
module uses an inner product linear in its second variable, convert to the
repository's first-variable-linear pairing by
$\langle u,v\rangle_{\rm FF}=(v,u)_{\rm root}$.

For precision about domains, let $\mathcal H$ be a complex Hilbert space with
inner product linear in its first variable and let
$\mathscr D\subseteq\mathcal H$ be a dense complex linear subspace. A **weak operator-valued distribution
on the common domain $\mathscr D$** means a complex-linear assignment
$g\mapsto\Phi(g)$ for $g\in\mathcal D(\mathbb R^4)$, where each
$\Phi(g):\mathscr D\to\mathcal H$ is linear and, for every
$u,v\in\mathscr D$, the scalar map
$g\mapsto\langle\Phi(g)u,v\rangle$ is a continuous complex-linear functional
on the test-function space with the topology of
[[def-test-function-topology]], hence a distribution as in [[def-distribution]].
This definition gives no pointwise field $\Phi(x)$ and no product
$\Phi(x)\Phi(x)$; a product or extension needs a separate construction. It
asserts only matrix-element continuity and the stated linear maps; all further
operator properties, locality, local observable algebras, graded locality,
and gauge-specific potential behavior must be supplied by a constructed
model. Test-function units can be chosen so a specified smeared observable is
dimensionless; there is no universal test-function unit asserted here.

Primitive data for a selected model include its species and rest masses,
declared charge parameters, regulator geometry, couplings, state and any
constructed measurement data. Vacuum-subtracted Hamiltonians, regulator
eigenvalues, distributions, correlations and outcome probabilities are
derived only when their constructions supply the required domains and
well-definedness. This dictionary neither constructs an interacting
four-dimensional QED Hilbert space nor asserts pointwise field products,
scattering, an LSZ limit, asymptotic completeness, or removal of a regulator.

items.title: Physical interpretation of a supplied constructed quantum model
items.design_state: planned adopted model-conditional Born interpretation; exact finite-instrument hypotheses and absence of continuum/empirical claims stated
items.physical_scope: Adopts state, finite instrument and actual constructed unitary dynamics only; supplies no missing continuum representation or convergence.
items.statement:
Adopt the following physical reading only for an explicitly selected model
whose mathematical data have actually been constructed. Let $\mathscr H$ be a
nonzero complex Hilbert space, let $\rho_t$ be the model's density operator at
a time $t$ at which a measurement is made, and let
$\{M_{a,r}:r=1,\ldots,q_a\}_{a=1}^m$ be a supplied normalized finite bounded
Kraus instrument on $\mathscr H$ in the exact sense of
[[def-qft-finite-bounded-kraus-instrument]]. Assume the Axiom of Countable
Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ when using the normalization result of
[[lem-qft-finite-instrument-normalization]]. Its hypotheses include that
$\rho_t$ is a density operator and that the instrument really satisfies
$\sum_{a,r}M_{a,r}^*M_{a,r}=I_{\mathscr H}$; the supplier's result is a draft
with a complete conditional proof, not an independent approval or an
apparatus-realization theorem.

Put

$$E_a:=\sum_rM_{a,r}^*M_{a,r},\qquad \mathcal J_a(X):=\sum_rM_{a,r}XM_{a,r}^*.$$

As the **Born interpretation postulate** for this selected model, read

$$p_a(t):=\operatorname{tr}(\mathcal J_a(\rho_t)) =\operatorname{tr}(\rho_tE_a)$$

as the model probability for outcome $a$. The mathematical supplier proves
$p_a(t)\in[0,1]$ and $\sum_{a=1}^mp_a(t)=1$ under the hypotheses just
listed. When $p_a(t)>0$, adopt
$\mathcal J_a(\rho_t)/p_a(t)$ as the model's conditional state after outcome
$a$; at zero probability no normalized update is assigned. These are
model-level probability assignments, not observations.

If the selected construction supplies a self-adjoint observable in the sense
of [[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]] and its
spectral projection-valued measure as in
[[def-projection-valued-measure]], a declared finite Borel partition may be
used only after its projections have been constructed and verified as a
finite projective instrument. In that case the projections are the single
Kraus operators for their outcomes. A supplied bounded effect is read as an
outcome effect only as part of a supplied normalized instrument; this item
does not construct square roots, a spectral measure, or an instrument from an
arbitrary formal observable.

If a selected construction supplies a self-adjoint Hamiltonian
$\widehat H:D(\widehat H)\subseteq\mathscr H\to\mathscr H$ in the sense of
[[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]], and an evolution
family $U(t):\mathscr H\to\mathscr H$ whose maps are surjective
complex-linear and preserve the Hilbert inner product, as specified in
[[def-qft-framework-units]], for $t\in I\subseteq\mathbb R$ (with $t$ in
seconds), adopt the Schrödinger convention
$U(t)=\exp(-it\widehat H/\hbar)$ and
$\rho_t=U(t)\rho_0U(t)^*$ when that construction establishes that $\rho_t$
is a density operator. The unitary convention and SI dimensions are those of
[[def-qft-framework-units]], where $U(t)^*:=U(t)^{-1}$ and $\widehat H$ has
unit joules. For any supplied complex-linear operator
$O:D(O)\to\mathscr H$ with specified linear domain $D(O)\subseteq\mathscr H$,
define its Heisenberg conjugate by
$$O_H(t):=U(t)^*O\,U(t),\quad D(O_H(t)):=\{\xi\in\mathscr H:U(t)\xi\in D(O)\}.$$
The model supplies these domains and the evolution. This postulate neither
constructs the Hamiltonian, evolution family, state, or field representation,
nor any model-specific operator domain.

The model declaration identifies the selected species, field normalization,
regulator, preparation and measurement data using
[[def-qft-framework-units]]. It does not assert that every classical action
has a quantization, that every formal state is positive, or that any cutoff
can be removed. In particular it supplies no interacting continuum
four-dimensional QED Hilbert space, scattering operator, asymptotic
completeness, LSZ limit, or nonperturbative convergence. A formal coefficient
is not an exact probability without an additional controlled approximation
map and a constructed model. Agreement with reported data would test the
selected approximation and empirical inputs; it would not prove this
postulate or the model. No reported data are asserted here.
