items.design_state: planned B leaf; complete finite two-level conditional argument and formal versus numerical convergence proof authored
items.physical_scope: Conditional ideal two-level instrument; no observed outcome and no formal coefficient identified as an exact probability.
items.statement:
Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. At one fixed measurement time, take the
constructed two-dimensional Hilbert space $\mathcal H=\mathbb C^2$ with
inner product
$\langle x,y\rangle=x_0\overline{y_0}+x_1\overline{y_1}$, linear in the
first variable. Let $e_0=(1,0)$, $e_1=(0,1)$ and
$v=\alpha e_0+\beta e_1$ with
$|\alpha|^2+|\beta|^2=1$. Prepare the rank-one density operator
$\rho=T_{v,v}$, where
$T_{v,v}x=\langle x,v\rangle v$ as in
[[lem-nrqm-composites-rank-one-operator-calculus]]. Define the two measurement
operators

$$P_0=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad P_1=\begin{pmatrix}0&0\\0&1\end{pmatrix},\qquad M_{0,1}=P_0,\quad M_{1,1}=P_1.$$

This is a finite normalized instrument. The postulate
[[post-qft-constructed-model-and-measurement]] assigns model probabilities
$p_0=|\alpha|^2$ and $p_1=|\beta|^2$, which sum to one. When $p_i>0$ its
conditional state is $P_i$; when $p_i=0$ the normalized update is undefined.
This is a conditional model calculation, not a report of an observed result.

For the formal comparison, let $g$ be an indeterminate; the formal algebra
assigns it no SI unit or numerical value. The formal series

$$F(g):=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}n!g^n\in\mathbb R\llbracket g\rrbracket$$

has a coefficient for every $n$, while its numerical power series has radius
zero after the real coefficients are embedded in $\mathbb C$ for evaluation.
This example separates coefficient data from numerical convergence.
The Born postulate does not assign an exact probability to a coefficient in
isolation: an additional map from formal data to a constructed state and
measurement, together with any approximation and error assumptions, would be
needed. No such map or observed outcome is claimed.

items.title: QFT example units, metric, gauge, and pairing conventions
items.statement:
These are conventions for constructed and formal calculations in this page pair. They are not empirical claims, physical postulates, or existence claims about an interacting continuum theory.

Work on a nonempty open coordinate region $U\subseteq\mathbb R^4$, with coordinates $x^0=ct,x^1,x^2,x^3$ in metres and $\partial_a=\partial/\partial x^a$ for $a\in\{0,1,2,3\}$. Use the geometric spacetime metric $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$ and the time coordinate $x^0=ct$ in metres. For Clifford algebra and momentum contraction use the separate algebraic metric $h=-\eta=\operatorname{diag}(1,-1,-1,-1)$; a slash or a square of an energy four-vector uses $h$, never $\eta$.

A physical energy four-vector is $p=(E,c\mathbf p_{\rm phys})$, with each component in joules. Write $M=mc^2$ for rest energy in joules and $p^2=h(p,p)=E^2-c^2|\mathbf p_{\rm phys}|^2$. For two such vectors, $s=(p_1+p_2)^2$ is in $\mathrm J^2$. Natural momentum coordinates are the energy-vector components divided by $\hbar c$, in $\mathrm m^{-1}$; they are not substituted into SI formulas without restoring this factor. Here $m\ge0$ is a mass parameter in kilograms, so $\mu=mc/\hbar$ is in $\mathrm m^{-1}$. The natural-unit field convention below concerns smooth test fields, not pointwise quantum operators. A real scalar field is a map $\varphi\in C_c^\infty(U;\mathbb R)$; a Dirac test field is $\Psi\in C_c^\infty(U;\mathbb C^4)$. Fix dimensionless matrices $\gamma^a\in M_4(\mathbb C)$ satisfying $\gamma^a\gamma^b+\gamma^b\gamma^a=2h^{ab}I_4$, and put $\overline\Psi=\Psi^\dagger\gamma^0$. Adopt dimensionless action normalizations with kinetic terms $\tfrac12\int_U h^{ab}(\partial_a\varphi)(\partial_b\varphi)\,d^4x$ and $\int_U i\overline\Psi\gamma^a\partial_a\Psi\,d^4x$, summing repeated indices from $0$ to $3$. The coefficients are dimensionless and introduce no additional length scale. These conventions assign $[\varphi]=\mathrm m^{-1}$ and $[\Psi]=\mathrm m^{-3/2}$: the integrands have length degrees $2[\varphi]-2$ and $2[\Psi]-1$, while $d^4x$ has degree $4$. No dynamics or continuum existence assertion is adopted.

Take SI $e>0$ in coulombs, $\hbar>0$ in joule-seconds, $c>0$ in metres per second, $\mu_0>0$ in $\mathrm{H\,m^{-1}}=\mathrm{kg\,m\,C^{-2}}$, and $\epsilon_0=(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}$ in $\mathrm{F\,m^{-1}}$. Define
$$\alpha=\frac{e^2}{4\pi\epsilon_0\hbar c},\qquad g=e\sqrt{\frac{\mu_0c}{\hbar}}=\sqrt{4\pi\alpha}>0.$$
Here $g$ is a dimensionless coupling. It is not the metric and not a gyromagnetic factor.

For gauge notation take $\phi\in C^1(U;\mathbb R)$ in volts and $\mathbf A\in C^1(U;\mathbb R^3)$ in tesla-metres. Write $A_{\rm lower}=(-\phi/c,\mathbf A)$ for the components of the real one-form $A=\sum_{a=0}^3 A_a\,dx^a$, so every $A_a$ is in tesla-metres. Take $\chi\in C^2(U;\mathbb R)$ in webers and a charged test field $\psi\in C^1(U;\mathbb C^N)$, where $N\ge1$ is fixed. With a constant real charge parameter $q$ in coulombs, define $D_a\psi=\partial_a\psi-iqA_a\psi/\hbar$ componentwise. The transformed fields are again $C^1$, with $d\chi=\sum_a(\partial_a\chi)dx^a$. In operator notation the conventions are
$$D_a=\partial_a-\frac{iqA_a}{\hbar},\qquad \psi\mapsto e^{iq\chi/\hbar}\psi,\qquad A\mapsto A+d\chi.$$
For the electron parameter use $q=-e$. The equivalent natural-unit coordinates are $A_{\rm nat}=A_{\rm SI}/\sqrt{\mu_0\hbar c}$ and $q_{\rm nat}=q_{\rm SI}\sqrt{\mu_0c/\hbar}$.

Finite-matrix examples act on $\mathbb C^d$ with the operator norm. For Hilbert spaces, use the first-variable-linear pairing $(u,v)_1=v^\dagger u$; a displayed coordinate contraction $u^\dagger v$ is second-variable-linear and equals $\overline{(u,v)_1}$. Thus norms, traces, and modulus-squared amplitudes agree under conversion, although the unsquared pairing is conjugated. No amplitude is assigned a probability by these conventions.

items.title: Finite Dyson remainder, coefficient unitarity, and regulator counterexamples
items.statement:
Assume the Countable Choice axiom $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $d\ge1$, $T>0$, $\hbar>0$, and $\lambda\in\mathbb R$. Let $H_0=H_0^\dagger$ be a $d\times d$ Hermitian matrix with entries in joules, and let $V:[0,T]\to M_d(\mathbb C)$ be norm-continuous, Hermitian-valued, and in joules. Define
$$V_I(t)=e^{itH_0/\hbar}V(t)e^{-itH_0/\hbar},\qquad B=\sup_{0\le t\le T}\|V_I(t)\|,\qquad z=\frac{|\lambda|BT}{\hbar}.$$
The coupling $\lambda$ is dimensionless and $z$ is dimensionless. Put $S_0(t)=I$ and
$$S_{n+1}(t)=-\frac{i}{\hbar}\int_0^t V_I(r)S_n(r)\,dr,\qquad S(t)=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}\lambda^nS_n(t).$$
Then the series converges in operator norm on $[0,T]$, $S$ is the unique solution of $\dot S=-i\lambda V_I S/\hbar$, $S(0)=I$, and $S(t)$ is unitary. For every $N\ge0$,
$$\left\|S(T)-\sum_{n=0}^N\lambda^nS_n(T)\right\| \le e^z\frac{z^{N+1}}{(N+1)!}.$$

For a finite matrix $A$, define its Hermitian imaginary part by
$\operatorname{Im}_{\mathrm H}A:=(A-A^\dagger)/(2i)$; for a scalar entry $w\in\mathbb C$, $\operatorname{Im}w$ has its ordinary scalar meaning.

Define $S(T;\lambda)=I+iT(\lambda)$ and $T(\lambda)=\sum_{n\ge1}\lambda^nT_n$. For every pair of basis indices $f,i$, exact unitarity gives
$$2\,\operatorname{Im}T_{ii}(\lambda)=\sum_f|T_{fi}(\lambda)|^2,$$
and coefficient comparison gives $T_1=T_1^\dagger$ and $2\,\operatorname{Im}_{\mathrm H}T_2=T_1^\dagger T_1$. These are identities for this finite matrix model.

For $H=g_E\sigma_x$ on $\mathbb C^2$, where $g_E>0$ is in joules and $\sigma_x=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{pmatrix}$, the evolution matrix is
$$e^{-itH/\hbar}=\cos(g_Et/\hbar)I-i\sin(g_Et/\hbar)\sigma_x.$$
Its exact off-diagonal matrix-element square is $\sin^2(g_Et/\hbar)$; its first-order squared coefficient is $(g_Et/\hbar)^2$, which can exceed $1$. For every positive rate $\Gamma$ in $\mathrm{s}^{-1}$, the survival matrix-element square $\cos^2(g_Et/\hbar)$ is not $e^{-\Gamma t}$.

For an integer $N\ge0$, on the finite basis $|0\rangle,\ldots,|N\rangle$ define $a_N|n\rangle=\sqrt n\,|n-1\rangle$ (zero at $n=0$) and $a_N^\dagger|n\rangle=\sqrt{n+1}|n+1\rangle$ for $n<N$, with $a_N^\dagger|N\rangle=0$. Then
$$[a_N,a_N^\dagger]=I-(N+1)|N\rangle\langle N|.$$
No finite-dimensional matrices can satisfy $[A,B]=I$, because the trace of a commutator is zero while the trace of $I$ is the dimension.

items.title: Golden-rule kernel and its quantified approximate-identity limit
items.statement:
Assume the Countable Choice axiom $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ ([[def-countable-choice]]), $\hbar>0$ in joule-seconds, $T>0$ in seconds, an energy $E_0\in\mathbb R$ in joules, a dimensionless $\lambda\in\mathbb R$, and a bounded nonnegative Borel function $w:\mathbb R\to[0,\infty)$ continuous at $E_0$. Here $w$ is a specified transition-density weight in joules; no state density or matrix element is inferred from the name.

For angular frequency $\omega\in\mathbb R$ in $\mathrm{s}^{-1}$, define
$$K_T(\omega)=\frac1T\left|\int_0^T e^{i\omega t}\,dt\right|^2 =\begin{cases}\dfrac{4\sin^2(\omega T/2)}{T\omega^2},&\omega\ne0,\\[4pt]T,&\omega=0.\end{cases}$$
Then $K_T\ge0$, $\int_{\mathbb R}K_T(\omega)\,d\omega=2\pi$, and for every $r>0$,
$$\int_{|\omega|>r}\frac{K_T(\omega)}{2\pi}\,d\omega\le\frac{4}{\pi Tr}.$$
For bounded Borel $f:\mathbb R\to\mathbb C$ continuous at $0$, define
$$\omega_f(r)=\sup_{|\omega|\le r}|f(\omega)-f(0)|.$$
Then
$$\left|\int_{\mathbb R}\frac{K_T(\omega)}{2\pi}f(\omega)\,d\omega-f(0)\right| \le\omega_f(r)+\frac{8\|f\|_\infty}{\pi Tr},$$
so the left-hand integral tends to $f(0)$ as $T\to\infty$.

Define the finite-time second-order coefficient quantity
$$P_2(T)=\frac{\lambda^2}{\hbar^2} \int_{\mathbb R}w(E)\left|\int_0^T e^{i(E-E_0)t/\hbar}\,dt\right|^2dE.$$
It is finite and
$$\lim_{T\to\infty}\frac{P_2(T)}{T}=\frac{2\pi\lambda^2}{\hbar}w(E_0).$$
This is a theorem about the stated integral coefficient, not an exact long-time transition probability, an exponential decay law, or a product of distributions such as $\delta^2$.

items.title: One-mode oscillator, Feynman boundary prescription, and retarded contrast
items.statement:
Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ ([[def-countable-choice]]), $m_o>0$ in kilograms, $\omega>0$ in $\mathrm{s}^{-1}$, and $\hbar>0$ in $\mathrm{J\,s}$. Take the complete oscillator family $(\psi_n)_{n\ge0}$ and self-adjoint Hamiltonian $H_{\rm osc}$ of [[thm-nrqm-oscillator-oscillator-scaling-and-exact-realization]], with oscillator length $\ell=\sqrt{\hbar/(m_o\omega)}$ and $H_{\rm osc}\psi_n=\hbar\omega(n+\tfrac12)\psi_n$. Let $\mathcal C=\operatorname{span}\{\psi_n:n\ge0\}$ be the finite Hermite span. Multiplication by position $Xf(x)=xf(x)$ maps $\mathcal C$ into itself by the Hermite recurrence. Define $U(t)$ on $\mathcal C$ by $U(t)\psi_n=e^{-i\omega(n+1/2)t}\psi_n$ and extend continuously to a unitary on the oscillator Hilbert space. For $\psi_0$ the normalized ground state, define
$$C_F(t)=\frac{m_o}{\hbar}\bigl(T X(t)X(0)\psi_0,\psi_0\bigr)_1,\qquad X(t)=U(t)^\dagger XU(t),$$
where time ordering means $T X(t)X(0)=X(t)X(0)$ for $t\ge0$ and $X(0)X(t)$ for $t<0$. Define $G_R(t)=1_{[0,\infty)}(t)\sin(\omega t)/\omega$.

Then, for every real $t$,
$$C_F(t)=\frac{e^{-i\omega|t|}}{2\omega},\qquad (\partial_t^2+\omega^2)C_F=-i\delta_0,\qquad (\partial_t^2+\omega^2)G_R=\delta_0.$$
Use the complex Schwartz space of [[def-schwartz-space-and-its-seminorms]], with topology generated by $p_{jk}(\varphi)=\sup_x|x^j\varphi^{(k)}(x)|$ for integers $j,k\ge0$: a neighborhood of zero restricts finitely many such seminorms. A tempered distribution is a continuous complex-linear functional $u:\mathcal S(\mathbb R)\to\mathbb C$, with bilinear pairing $\langle u,\varphi\rangle=u(\varphi)$ (no conjugation). A bounded kernel $f$ acts by $\langle f,\varphi\rangle=\int f\varphi$. Define $\langle\partial_t^k u,\varphi\rangle=(-1)^k\langle u,\varphi^{(k)}\rangle$ and $\delta_a(\varphi)=\varphi(a)$. These derivatives also restrict to compactly supported smooth tests. Convergence of distributions here means convergence against every Schwartz test, the weak topology $\sigma(\mathcal S',\mathcal S)$. For $u\in\mathcal S'$ define its positive-sign Fourier transform by $\langle\mathcal T_+u,\varphi\rangle=\langle u,\mathcal T_+\varphi\rangle$, where $\mathcal T_+\varphi(t)=\int e^{i\nu t}\varphi(\nu)\,d\nu$. Both kernels have units of seconds, so the differential identities have units of inverse seconds. In particular, $C_F(t)\ne0$ for $t<0$ while $G_R(t)=0$ there.

For a Schwartz test function $\varphi\in\mathcal S(\mathbb R)$ and $\epsilon>0$, define $\operatorname{PV}\int\varphi(x)/x\,dx:=\lim_{r\downarrow0}\int_{|x|>r}\varphi(x)/x\,dx$ and $\delta_a(\varphi):=\varphi(a)$. The Plemelj boundary identity is
$$\lim_{\epsilon\downarrow0}\int_{\mathbb R}\frac{\varphi(x)}{x+i\epsilon}\,dx =\operatorname{PV}\int_{\mathbb R}\frac{\varphi(x)}x\,dx-i\pi\varphi(0),$$
with the opposite sign of $i\epsilon$ reversing the delta sign. In this boundary formula $x$ and $\epsilon$ use one common coordinate unit. For $\nu\in\mathbb R$ in $\mathrm{s}^{-1}$, the frequency regulator $\epsilon>0$ is in $\mathrm{s}^{-1}$ and $\epsilon t$ is dimensionless; the ordinary positive-sign Fourier transform of $e^{-\epsilon|t|}C_F(t)$ is
$$\frac{i}{2\omega}\left(\frac1{\nu-\omega+i\epsilon}-\frac1{\nu+\omega-i\epsilon}\right).$$
As $\epsilon\downarrow0$ its distributional limit is
$$\frac{i}{2\omega}\left[ \operatorname{PV}\frac1{\nu-\omega}-\operatorname{PV}\frac1{\nu+\omega} -i\pi\delta_{\omega}-i\pi\delta_{-\omega}\right],$$
which is conventionally denoted $i/(\nu^2-\omega^2+i0)$. Here that notation means the displayed pair of opposite boundary values at the two simple poles. This one-mode result makes no spatial-causality or interacting-field claim.

items.title: Worked example B01 — exact finite dynamics and its first coefficient
items.statement:
Use the two-level matrix model of [[thm-qft-example-finite-dyson-unitarity]] with $H=g_E\sigma_x$, where $g_E>0$ is in joules. At
$$t_1=\frac{\pi\hbar}{2g_E}>0,$$
the exact off-diagonal matrix-element square is $1$, while its first-order squared coefficient is $\pi^2/4>1$. At $t_2=\pi\hbar/g_E$, the exact survival matrix-element square is $1$, whereas $e^{-\Gamma t_2}<1$ for every positive rate $\Gamma$ in $\mathrm{s}^{-1}$. These are finite-matrix identities. This mathematical example assigns no probabilistic interpretation to the amplitudes or their matrix-element squares.

Then the normalized Feynman correlator is $-i/(2\omega)$, while the explicitly defined kernel $G_R$ is zero. This compares the two functions in the stated one-mode model and makes no claim about a response to an external source.

items.title: Proper orthochronous Lorentz maps factor into a boost and a rotation
items.statement: Fix an inertial frame of [[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]] and identify its vector coordinates with $\mathbb R^4$ and $\eta_0=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$. For a unit spatial vector $\mathbf n_B$ and $\chi\in\mathbb R$, define the boost $B_{\mathbf n_B}(\chi)$ by $B e_0=\cosh\chi\,e_0+\sinh\chi\,\mathbf n_B$, $B\mathbf n_B=\sinh\chi\,e_0+\cosh\chi\,\mathbf n_B$, and $Bw=w$ for every $w$ Euclidean-orthogonal to $\operatorname{span}(e_0,\mathbf n_B)$. Every proper orthochronous linear Lorentz map $\Lambda\in SO^+(1,3)$, as defined in [[def-lorentz-map-and-lorentz-group]], admits $\Lambda=B_{\mathbf n_B}(\chi)R_{\mathbf n_R}(\theta)$, where $R_{\mathbf n_R}(\theta)$ fixes the time axis and $\mathbf n_R$, and sends $\mathbf v_\perp$ to $\cos\theta\,\mathbf v_\perp+\sin\theta\,\mathbf n_R\times\mathbf v_\perp$ on the orthogonal plane, where $\mathbf v_\parallel=(\mathbf v\cdot\mathbf n_R)\mathbf n_R$ and $\mathbf v_\perp=\mathbf v-\mathbf v_\parallel$; the cross product is [[def-cross-product-in-r3]]. If $\Lambda e_0=e_0$, choose $\chi=0$ and $R_{\mathbf n_R}(\theta)=\Lambda$.

items.title: Dirac Clifford matrices and energy projections
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice [[def-countable-choice]], the mathematical scalar shell conventions of [[def-qft-scalar-mass-shell]], and the second-variable-linear Hilbert pairing of [[def-qft-fock-and-test-spaces]]. In the fixed inertial coordinates $x=(x^0,\mathbf x)$ of [[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]] on the affine Minkowski model [[def-sr-affine-minkowski-model]], $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$; these coordinates have length units under [[def-qft-scalar-mass-shell]]. The parameter $\mu\ge0$ and momentum coordinate $\mathbf k$ have inverse-length units, and $\omega(\mathbf k)=\sqrt{|\mathbf k|^2+\mu^2}$ has the same units. The parameter is not identified here with a physical rest mass. Matrix $h_D$ has inverse-length units; the dimensionless spin matrices have no physical unit assignment in this mathematical item.

Use the Pauli matrices $\sigma_1=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{pmatrix}$, $\sigma_2=\begin{pmatrix}0&-i\\i&0\end{pmatrix}$, and $\sigma_3=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&-1\end{pmatrix}$. On $\mathbb C^4=\mathbb C^2\oplus\mathbb C^2$, define
$$\beta=\begin{pmatrix}I_2&0\\0&-I_2\end{pmatrix},\qquad \alpha_j=\begin{pmatrix}0&\sigma_j\\\sigma_j&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad \gamma^0=\beta,\qquad \gamma^j=\beta\alpha_j.$$
For a spinor column $z\in\mathbb C^4$, its Dirac adjoint is $\bar z=z^\dagger\beta$. The Clifford contraction is $\Gamma(p):=\gamma^0p^0-\sum_{j=1}^3\gamma^jp_j$; this contraction uses the effective matrix $-\eta$ in the relation $\{\gamma^a,\gamma^b\}=-2\eta^{ab}I_4$.

Let $\mathcal H_D$ be the space of measurable functions $u:\mathbb R^3\to\mathbb C^4$, modulo equality almost everywhere, with
$$\|u\|^2=\int_{\mathbb R^3}u(\mathbf k)^\dagger u(\mathbf k)\,\frac{d^3\mathbf k}{(2\pi)^3}<\infty,$$
and pairing $\langle u,v\rangle=\int u(\mathbf k)^\dagger v(\mathbf k)\,d^3\mathbf k/(2\pi)^3$. Define the measurable matrix $h_D(\mathbf k)=\sum_j\alpha_j k_j+\beta\mu$ and its maximal multiplication operator with domain $D(h_D)=\{u\in\mathcal H_D:h_Du\in\mathcal H_D\}$. For $\omega(\mathbf k)>0$, define the matrix fields
$$P_\pm(\mathbf k)=\frac12\left(I_4\pm\frac{h_D(\mathbf k)}{\omega(\mathbf k)}\right).$$
When $\mu=0$ at $\mathbf k=0$, set $P_+(0)=\operatorname{diag}(I_2,0)$ and $P_-(0)=\operatorname{diag}(0,I_2)$. These are complementary rank-two orthogonal projections; the value at this Lebesgue-null point does not change their multiplication operators. Write $M_{P_\pm}$ for their maximal multiplication operators and $\mathcal H_\pm=\operatorname{ran}M_{P_\pm}$. The companion matrix lemma on this page proves these are bounded orthogonal projections with closed ranges. The conjugate Hilbert space $\overline{\mathcal H_-}$ has vectors $\bar u$, scalar multiplication $z\bar u=\overline{\bar z u}$, and pairing $\langle\bar u,\bar v\rangle=\langle v,u\rangle$.

Use the sine and cosine definitions of [[def-sine-and-cosine-by-power-series]]. For a length-coordinate increment $t\in\mathbb R$ and $\omega(\mathbf k)>0$, define the matrix multiplier
$$W_D(t,\mathbf k)=\cos(\omega t)I_4+i\frac{\sin(\omega t)}{\omega}h_D(\mathbf k).$$
At the massless apex set $W_D(t,0)=I_4$. Its unitarity, group law and generator identity are proved by the companion matrix lemma on this page.

The symbols $P_+$ and $P_-$ designate the positive- and negative-energy matrix formulas for this fixed free Dirac operator. This is purely mathematical data; no physical spin-statistics postulate or empirical assertion is included.

items.title: Dirac matrix identities and orthogonal energy projections
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice [[def-countable-choice]] and use the definitions in [[def-qft-dirac-projections]]. For every $\mu\ge0$ and almost every $\mathbf k$, the displayed Pauli blocks satisfy $h_D(\mathbf k)^\dagger=h_D(\mathbf k)$, $h_D(\mathbf k)^2=\omega(\mathbf k)^2I_4$, and $P_\pm(\mathbf k)$ are complementary orthogonal projections of rank two. The ranges $\mathcal H_\pm$ are closed separable Hilbert subspaces of $\mathcal H_D$, and $h_D$ is self-adjoint on $D(h_D)=\{u:\omega u\in\mathcal H_D\}$. The matrices also satisfy $\{\gamma^a,\gamma^b\}=-2\eta^{ab}I_4$ and $\gamma^{0\dagger}=\gamma^0$, $\gamma^{j\dagger}=-\gamma^j$.

For a unit spatial vector $\mathbf n$, put $\Sigma_{\mathbf n}=\operatorname{diag}(\boldsymbol\sigma\cdot\mathbf n,\boldsymbol\sigma\cdot\mathbf n)$, $S_R(\theta)=\cos(\theta/2)I_4-i\sin(\theta/2)\Sigma_{\mathbf n}$, and $S_B(\chi)=\cosh(\chi/2)I_4+\sinh(\chi/2)\boldsymbol\alpha\cdot\mathbf n$. With $R_{\mathbf n}(\theta)$ the rotation $\mathbf v_\parallel+\cos\theta\,\mathbf v_\perp+\sin\theta\,\mathbf n\times\mathbf v_\perp$ using [[def-cross-product-in-r3]], with $\mathbf v_\parallel=(\mathbf v\cdot\mathbf n)\mathbf n$ and $\mathbf v_\perp=\mathbf v-\mathbf v_\parallel$, and $B_{\mathbf n}(\chi)$ the boost defined in [[lem-qft-lorentz-boost-rotation-factorization]], these matrices satisfy $S_R\Gamma(p)S_R^{-1}=\Gamma(R_{\mathbf n}(\theta)p)$, $S_B\Gamma(p)S_B^{-1}=\Gamma(B_{\mathbf n}(\chi)p)$, and $S_R\beta S_R^\dagger=S_B\beta S_B^\dagger=\beta$.

For each real $t$, $W_D(t,\mathbf k)$ of [[def-qft-dirac-projections]] is unitary, satisfies $W_D(t+s,\mathbf k)=W_D(t,\mathbf k)W_D(s,\mathbf k)$, and obeys $\partial_tW_D(t,\mathbf k)=i h_D(\mathbf k)W_D(t,\mathbf k)$.

items.title: Smeared free Dirac CAR fields and graded locality
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice [[def-countable-choice]], let $\mu\ge0$, and use [[def-qft-dirac-projections]], [[lem-qft-dirac-projection-matrices]], and the antisymmetric Fock and CAR conventions of [[def-qft-fock-and-test-spaces]] and [[lem-qft-fock-ccr-car]]. Define
$$\mathscr S(\mathbb R^4;\mathbb C^4):=\{F=(F_0,F_1,F_2,F_3):F_a\in\mathcal S(\mathbb R^4)\text{ for }a=0,1,2,3\},$$
with the finite-product topology generated by the scalar Schwartz seminorms on each component; $\mathcal S(\mathbb R^4)$ and its seminorms are those of [[def-qft-fock-and-test-spaces]]. For $F$ in this space, define
$$\widehat F(t,\mathbf k)=\int_{\mathbb R^3}e^{-i\mathbf k\cdot\mathbf x}F(t,\mathbf x)\,d^3\mathbf x,\qquad u_F(\mathbf k)=\int_{\mathbb R}W_D(t,\mathbf k)\widehat F(t,\mathbf k)\,dt.$$
Then $u_F\in\mathcal H_D$, continuously in the Schwartz topology, and
$$\Psi(F)=c(P_+u_F)+c^\dagger(\overline{P_-u_F})$$
defines a bounded operator on $\mathcal F_a(\mathcal H_+\oplus\overline{\mathcal H_-})$, antilinear in $F$. It satisfies
$$\{\Psi(F),\Psi(G)\}=0,\qquad \{\Psi(F),\Psi(G)^\dagger\}=\langle u_F,u_G\rangle_{\mathcal H_D}I.$$
The positive and negative contraction kernels, defined as tempered distributions by their Fourier integrals, are
$$C_+(\tau,\mathbf x)=\int e^{-i(\omega\tau-\mathbf k\cdot\mathbf x)}P_+(\mathbf k)\,\frac{d^3\mathbf k}{(2\pi)^3},\qquad C_-(\tau,\mathbf x)=\int e^{+i(\omega\tau+\mathbf k\cdot\mathbf x)}P_-(\mathbf k)\,\frac{d^3\mathbf k}{(2\pi)^3}.$$
Their tested pairings give respectively $\langle P_+u_F,P_+u_G\rangle$ and $\langle P_-u_F,P_-u_G\rangle$; their sum is the anticommutator kernel $R$ below.
Its tested free equation is $u_{(i\partial_0-h_D(-i\nabla))F}=0$. For spatial Schwartz spinors $u,v$, the equal-time field $\Psi_t(u)=c(P_+W_D(t,\mathbf k)\widehat u)+c^\dagger(\overline{P_-W_D(t,\mathbf k)\widehat u})$ satisfies $\{\Psi_t(u),\Psi_t(v)^\dagger\}=\int u(\mathbf x)^\dagger v(\mathbf x)\,d^3\mathbf x\,I$ and $\{\Psi_t(u),\Psi_t(v)\}=0$.

The spacetime anticommutator kernel is
$$R(\tau,\mathbf x)=\int_{\mathbb R^3}W_D(-\tau,\mathbf k)e^{i\mathbf k\cdot\mathbf x}\,\frac{d^3\mathbf k}{(2\pi)^3}=\partial_\tau\Delta_\mu(\tau,\mathbf x)I_4-i h_D(-i\nabla)\Delta_\mu(\tau,\mathbf x),$$
where $\Delta_\mu$ is the scalar causal commutator distribution of [[lem-qft-scalar-causal-commutator]]. Thus the kernel is supported in the closed causal cone. Spinor tests with compact spacelike-separated supports have vanishing anticommutators with one another and with each other's adjoints. Consequently, even polynomials in the bounded smeared fields commute across spacelike-separated regions. These are mathematical properties of the specified free-field construction.

items.title: Fermionic Dirac translation generators and positive spectrum
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice [[def-countable-choice]] and use [[def-qft-dirac-projections]] and [[lem-qft-dirac-projection-matrices]]. Define $\chi(s)=\cos s+i\sin s$ for real $s$, using [[def-sine-and-cosine-by-power-series]]. Let $X=(\{+\}\times\mathbb R^3)\sqcup(\{-\}\times\mathbb R^3)$ carry counting measure on the species label and $d^3\mathbf k/(2\pi)^3$ on each copy. The fiber $\mathcal V_x$ is $\mathbb C^4$ for $x=(+,\mathbf k)$ and $\overline{\mathbb C^4}$ for $x=(-,\mathbf k)$; $L^2(X;\mathcal V)$ denotes measurable sections with square-integrable fiber norm, and is the direct sum $L^2(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C^4)\oplus L^2(\mathbb R^3;\overline{\mathbb C^4})$. Identify $\mathcal K=\mathcal H_+\oplus\overline{\mathcal H_-}$ with the closed subspace whose $+$ fibers lie in $\operatorname{ran}P_+(\mathbf k)$ and whose $-$ fibers lie in $\overline{\operatorname{ran}P_-(\mathbf k)}$; form its antisymmetric Fock space $\mathcal F_a(\mathcal K)$ using [[def-qft-fock-and-test-spaces]]. For $x=(+,\mathbf k)$ set $q(x)=(\omega(\mathbf k),\mathbf k)$, and for $x=(-,\mathbf k)$ set $q(x)=(\omega(\mathbf k),-\mathbf k)$. The one-particle translation multipliers $V(a)u(x)=\chi(q^0(x)a^0-\mathbf q(x)\cdot\mathbf a)u(x)$ preserve $\mathcal K$ and lift to a strongly continuous unitary representation on $\mathcal F_a(\mathcal K)$. Write $U_j(t)$ for its Fock lift along the $j$th coordinate axis of $\mathbb R^4$.

On the $n$-particle sector, let $s_n(x_1,\ldots,x_n)=\sum_{r=1}^n q(x_r)$ and set $s_0=0$ on the vacuum sector. The joint spectral measure is multiplication by $\mathbf1_{s_n^{-1}(B)}$ on each sector, restricted to its antisymmetric subspace. Its support is contained in the closed future cone $\{(E,\mathbf p):E\ge|\mathbf p|\}$. Define the time generator $H$ and spatial momentum components $P_j$ by $U(te_0)=\chi(tH)$ and $U(te_j)=\chi(-tP_j)$, where $e_\alpha$ are the coordinate vectors in translation space. Then $H$ and each $P_j$ are the maximal real multipliers by $s_{n,0}$ and $s_{n,j}$, respectively, with domains $\{\Psi:\sum_n\|s_{n,\alpha}\Psi_n\|^2<\infty\}$; the minus sign in spatial translation phases is the Minkowski pairing convention in $V(a)$. The vacuum is the unique zero-energy vector; for $\mu>0$ the nonvacuum spectrum has gap at least $\mu$, while for $\mu=0$ it has no positive gap.

items.title: Dirac Fock covariance, vacuum cyclicity and spectrum
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice [[def-countable-choice]] and the mathematical free Dirac data of [[def-qft-dirac-projections]], [[lem-qft-dirac-projection-matrices]], and [[lem-qft-free-dirac-car-locality]]. Let $G=\mathbb R^4\rtimes SO^+(1,3)$ act by $x\mapsto a+\Lambda x$, with product $(a_2,\Lambda_2)(a_1,\Lambda_1)=(a_2+\Lambda_2a_1,\Lambda_2\Lambda_1)$. Let $\widetilde G$ be the subgroup of triples $(a,\Lambda,S)$ generated by translations $(a,I,I)$ and the explicit rotation/boost triples $(0,R_{\mathbf n}(\theta),S_R(\theta))$ and $(0,B_{\mathbf n}(\chi),S_B(\chi))$ of [[lem-qft-dirac-projection-matrices]], with product $(a_2,\Lambda_2,S_2)(a_1,\Lambda_1,S_1)=(a_2+\Lambda_2a_1,\Lambda_2\Lambda_1,S_2S_1)$ and the subspace topology from $\mathbb R^4\times M_4(\mathbb R)\times GL(4,\mathbb C)$. Its projection onto $G$ is surjective by [[lem-qft-lorentz-boost-rotation-factorization]]. For $\tilde g=(a,\Lambda,S)$ define the spinor test pullback
$$\tau_{\tilde g}F(x)=(S^{-1})^\dagger F(\Lambda^{-1}(x-a)).$$
The fermionic Fock space of [[def-qft-fock-and-test-spaces]] carries a strongly continuous unitary representation $U$ of $\widetilde G$ such that
$$U(\tilde g)\Psi(F)U(\tilde g)^{-1}=\Psi(\tau_{\tilde g}F).$$
Let $\mathcal A_D^{\mathrm{gr}}$ be the algebra generated by all bounded $\Psi(F)$ and $\Psi(F)^\dagger$ for Schwartz spinor tests $F$. The vacuum $\Omega$ is invariant and cyclic for $\mathcal A_D^{\mathrm{gr}}$. A $2\pi$ spatial spin rotation acts as $(-1)^N$ on the $n$-particle sector with value $(-1)^n$; a $4\pi$ rotation acts as the identity. The translation generators and joint spectral measure are those of [[lem-qft-dirac-fermionic-translation-spectrum]], so the joint spectrum is contained in the closed future cone, $\Omega$ is the unique zero-energy vector, and for $\mu>0$ the nonvacuum energy has gap at least $\mu$. The first-quantized $h_D$ has both signs of energy; this Fock-space generator is a different operator on a different Hilbert space. No general spin-statistics theorem or local cyclicity claim is asserted.

items.title: Dirac rest projections and two spin-component sectors
items.statement: Take the fiber matrices of [[def-qft-dirac-projections]] at $\mathbf k=0$ with $\mu>0$. Then $\omega=\mu$ and the positive and negative matrix eigenspaces each have dimension two. Define the dimensionless third spin-component matrix in this Pauli-block representation by $S_3:=\tfrac12\operatorname{diag}(\sigma_3,\sigma_3)$; here the two spin-component sectors mean its $+\tfrac12$ and $-\tfrac12$ eigenspaces within each energy eigenspace. The coordinate spinors below are vectors in the finite-dimensional fiber $\mathbb C^4$; they are not point-supported, normalizable vectors in the continuum Hilbert space $\mathcal H_D$. For $\mu=0$, the point $(\omega,\mathbf k)=(0,0)$ is the omitted mass-shell apex, so this example makes no massless rest-state claim.

items.title: Tempered time-ordered scalar two-point carrier
items.design_state: Planned tempered scalar time-ordered carrier with fixed local Fourier and metric conventions; conditional distributional construction and Green-source proof authored.
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Fix the scalar shell parameter $\mu\ge0$ and all shell, Fourier, and metric conventions of [[def-qft-scalar-mass-shell]], with $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$ and $\Box=-\partial_t^2+\Delta_{\mathbf x}$. For $\phi\in\mathcal S(\mathbb R^4)$ define the partial spatial Fourier transform
$$\widehat\phi_t(\mathbf k)=\int_{\mathbb R^3}e^{-i\mathbf k\cdot\mathbf x}\phi(t,\mathbf x)\,d^3\mathbf x$$
and define $H_\mu\in\mathcal S'(\mathbb R^4)$ by
$$\langle H_\mu,\phi\rangle=\int_{\mathbb R}dt\int_{\mathbb R^3}\frac{d^3\mathbf k}{(2\pi)^3\,2\omega_\mu(\mathbf k)}e^{-i\omega_\mu(\mathbf k)|t|}\widehat\phi_t(-\mathbf k).$$
This is a continuous distributional extension of the free scalar time-ordered two-point function: on $t>0$ its kernel is the Wightman two-point distribution $W_\mu(t,\mathbf x)$, and on $t<0$ it is $W_\mu(-t,-\mathbf x)$. The displayed partial Fourier formula fixes the extension at $t=0$; no product of a step function with an unspecified singular distribution is used. The kernel is symmetric under $(t,\mathbf x)\mapsto(-t,-\mathbf x)$, agrees with the two orderings on spacelike-separated supports, and obeys
$$ (\Box-\mu^2)H_\mu=i\delta_0 $$
in $\mathcal S'(\mathbb R^4)$. There is no extra prefactor $i$ in the definition of $H_\mu$.

items.title: Classical free action variations and normalization
items.design_state: Planned compact-variation scalar and commuting-spinor action equations; both directions authored.
items.statement:
Fix $\mu\ge0$, $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$, $\Box=\eta^{ab}\partial_a\partial_b$, and the Dirac matrices and adjoint of [[def-qft-dirac-projections]]; $\mu$ is the inverse-length mathematical shell parameter of [[def-qft-scalar-mass-shell]]. For a smooth real scalar field $\phi$ and smooth commuting complex spinor $\psi:\mathbb R^4\to\mathbb C^4$, use the normalized free Lagrangian densities
$$\mathcal L_\phi=-\frac12\left(\eta^{ab}\partial_a\phi\,\partial_b\phi+\mu^2\phi^2\right),\qquad \mathcal L_D=\bar\psi\left(i\gamma^a\partial_a-\mu\right)\psi,\qquad \bar\psi=\psi^\dagger\beta.$$
For compactly supported smooth real variations $h$ and compactly supported smooth complex spinor variations $\chi$, the action symbols are used only through the following finite, compactly supported first variations; no global integrability of the background fields is assumed:
$$\delta S_\phi(\phi;h)=\int_{\mathbb R^4}h(\Box-\mu^2)\phi\,d^4x,\qquad \delta S_D(\psi;\chi)=2\operatorname{Re}\int_{\mathbb R^4}\chi^\dagger\beta\left(i\gamma^a\partial_a-\mu\right)\psi\,d^4x.$$
Each field is stationary under all such variations if and only if its corresponding Euler–Lagrange equation holds pointwise:
$$(\Box-\mu^2)\phi=0,\qquad (i\gamma^a\partial_a-\mu)\psi=0.$$
The adjoint Dirac equation follows from the second equation because the fixed matrices satisfy $(\gamma^a)^\dagger\beta=\beta\gamma^a$. These are mathematical variation identities for commuting classical fields; they assert no quantization, Grassmann calculus, or physical measurement.

items.title: Domain-qualified free observables and point-field obstruction
items.design_state: Planned free-field domains, moments and compositions, with representation-specific point-smearing obstructions authored.
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice and use the scalar and Dirac free-field constructions of [[lem-qft-smeared-free-scalar]] and [[lem-qft-free-dirac-car-locality]] with their current draft hypotheses, including the Dirac projection and CAR inputs in [[lem-qft-dirac-projection-matrices]] and [[lem-qft-fock-ccr-car]]. For a real scalar test $f\in\mathcal S(\mathbb R^4)$, $\overline{\Phi_\mu(f)}=\sqrt2\,\Phi_{\rm Segal}(K_\mu f)$ is self-adjoint on the exact domain given by [[lem-qft-segal-weyl-domain]]. On scalar bosonic Fock space, $N_s=d\Gamma(1)$, $H_s=d\Gamma(\omega_\mu)$, and $P_{s,j}=d\Gamma(-k_j)$ are the maximal real multipliers of [[lem-qft-second-quantized-spectrum]]; in particular,
$$D(N_s)=\left\{\Psi=(\Psi_n):\sum_{n\ge1}n^2\|\Psi_n\|^2<\infty\right\},$$
and the Hamiltonian and momentum domains are exactly the square-integrability domains of the sums of their one-particle multipliers.

On the specified Dirac Fock space, spacetime-smeared fields $\Psi(F)$ are bounded, while the translation generators $H_D,P_{D,j}$ have the exact maximal domains and joint PVM stated in [[lem-qft-dirac-fermionic-translation-spectrum]]. For any one of these self-adjoint real-multiplier operators $A$, a normalized $\Psi\in D(A)$ has finite mean $\langle\Psi,A\Psi\rangle$ and finite variance
$$\operatorname{Var}_\Psi(A)=\|(A-\langle\Psi,A\Psi\rangle)\Psi\|^2.$$
Membership in $D(A)$ suffices for finite variance and does not require $\Psi\in D(A^2)$. A product $AB\Psi$ is defined only when $\Psi\in D(B)$ and $B\Psi\in D(A)$, as specified in [[lem-nrqm-uncertainty-schrodinger-robertson-anticommutator-bound]].

For the scalar point limit, fix $x_0\in\mathbb R^4$ and real tests $f_\varepsilon\in\mathcal S(\mathbb R^4)$, $0<\varepsilon\le1$, such that $\int f_\varepsilon(x)\phi(x)\,d^4x\to\phi(x_0)$ for every Schwartz test $\phi$ and $K_\mu f_\varepsilon(p)\to e^{ip\circ x_0}$ for $\nu_\mu$-almost every shell momentum. Then $\|\Phi_\mu(f_\varepsilon)\Omega\|\to\infty$. A sufficient condition for both convergences is $\int f_\varepsilon=1$, $\sup_\varepsilon\|f_\varepsilon\|_1<\infty$, and $\int_{|x-x_0|\ge\delta}|f_\varepsilon(x)|\,d^4x\to0$ for each $\delta>0$. This includes all nonnegative normalized Schwartz approximate identities with mass concentrating at $x_0$, as well as signed families satisfying that condition; weak distributional convergence alone is not substituted for convergence of the mass-shell Fourier restriction. For the equal-time Dirac CAR field, fix $\mathbf x_0\in\mathbb R^3$ and $z_0\in\mathbb C^4\setminus\{0\}$. For every family $u_\varepsilon\in\mathcal S(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C^4)$ satisfying $\int h(\mathbf x)^\dagger u_\varepsilon(\mathbf x)\,d^3\mathbf x\to h(\mathbf x_0)^\dagger z_0$ for each spinor Schwartz test $h$, the bounded equal-time smeared operators satisfy $\|\Psi_t(u_\varepsilon)\|_{\rm op}\to\infty$ at each fixed time $t$. Thus neither construction gives a point-field value in the indicated norm topology. The supplied free-field results define only smeared fields and do not define coincident diagonal products.

references.locator: Complete 616-page draft; §3 canonical scalar mode expansion, §8 free propagator, and §36 spinor-field Lagrangian. The spinor discussion uses anticommuting fields. Its formal field notation is contextual; exact domains and point-limit conclusions below follow from the stated Fock suppliers and local norm arguments.

items.proof:
**Given:** [A1] and [F1]–[F18].

1.1 The measure $d\nu_\mu$ is sigma-finite by [F9], and $\omega_\mu$ and $k_j$ are finite measurable multipliers by [F2]. Applying [F5] with one-particle multiplier vector $(1,\omega_\mu,-k_1,-k_2,-k_3)$ gives the self-adjoint scalar operators $N_s,H_s,P_{s,j}$. On sector $n$, their multipliers are $n$, $\sum_{r=1}^n\omega_\mu(\mathbf k_r)$, and $-\sum_{r=1}^n k_{r,j}$. Squaring these multipliers and integrating against the completed product measure yields exactly the stated domains. [A1, F1, F2, F5, F9, given]

1.2 The Dirac data in [F6] satisfy the measurable, finite-multiplier hypotheses of [F7], and [F16] supplies the complementary orthogonal projections and closed ranges required by that carrier. The one-particle measure is sigma-finite: each of the two species copies of R^3 is the countable union of bounded balls with finite Lebesgue measure. Let Y_m be the two species copies restricted to the ball of radius m; each Y_m has finite measure. For fixed n, the product sets Y_m^n have finite product measure and cover X^n as m grows. Their countable union over n and m is a sigma-finite cover of the Fock direct-sum measure. The particle and antiparticle sector multipliers are therefore self-adjoint on the maximal domains in [F7], which are the displayed square-integrability conditions for $H_D$ and each $P_{D,j}$. The field boundedness and equal-time CAR are exactly the inspected interfaces in [F8]. [A1, F1, F6, F7, F8, F16, given]

2.1 For real $f$, [F3] identifies the scalar field on $\mathcal D_{\rm fin}$ with $\sqrt2\,\Phi_{\rm Segal}(K_\mu f)$. The Hilbert space $H_\mu$ is separable by [F13], so the hypothesis of the Segal-domain result [F4] holds. Multiplication by the nonzero scalar $\sqrt2$ does not change an operator domain; hence the closure is self-adjoint on the domain in [F4] with $h=K_\mu f$. If $K_\mu f=0$, both operators are zero on all Fock space. [F1, F3, F4, F13, step 1.1, algebra]

2.2 For a normalized $\Psi\in D(A)$, Cauchy–Schwarz [F12] gives $|\langle\Psi,A\Psi\rangle|\le\|A\Psi\|<\infty$. Since $A$ is self-adjoint, this expectation is real. The vector $A\Psi-\langle A\rangle_\Psi\Psi$ belongs to the Hilbert space because both terms do, so its norm and the stated variance are finite without requiring $\Psi\in D(A^2)$. By [F14], a product $AB$ acts only on vectors $\Psi\in D(B)$ for which $B\Psi\in D(A)$; it is not defined merely because both $A$ and $B$ separately exist on a common dense core. [F1, F12, F14, step 1.1, step 1.2, given]

2.3 Choose $b_d$ from [F18] for $d=3,4$. Put
$Z_d=\int b_d(x)\,d^dx$ and $\rho_d=Z_d^{-1}b_d$.
The integral is finite because $0\le b_d\le1$ and its support lies in a
bounded ball, and it is positive because $b_d=1$ on a ball of positive
volume. Every derivative of $b_d$ is continuous with compact support, so
all its coordinate-weighted derivatives are bounded. Thus $\rho_d$ is
Schwartz, nonnegative, nonzero, and has integral one. In particular
$0<\|\rho_d\|_2<\infty$. Define
$\widehat\rho_d(\xi)=\int e^{-i\xi\cdot x}\rho_d(x)\,d^dx$.
The integral triangle inequality gives $|\widehat\rho_d(\xi)|\le\int\rho_d=1$;
dominated convergence [F10], with majorant $\rho_d$, gives
$\widehat\rho_d(\xi)\to1$ as $\xi\to0$.
Set $\rho=\rho_4$ and, for $\varepsilon>0$, define $\rho_{\varepsilon,x_0}(x)=\varepsilon^{-4}\rho_4((x-x_0)/\varepsilon)$. For every Schwartz test $\phi$, change of variables and dominated convergence [F10], with majorant $\|\phi\|_\infty\rho_4(y)$, give $\int\rho_{\varepsilon,x_0}(x)\phi(x)\,d^4x\to\phi(x_0)$, so this is a point-mass approximation. For $p=(p^0,\mathbf p)\in H_\mu^+$ the same change of variables gives
$$K_\mu\rho_{\varepsilon,x_0}(p)=e^{ip\circ x_0}\widehat\rho_4\bigl(\varepsilon(-p^0,\mathbf p)\bigr).$$
Thus $K_\mu\rho_{\varepsilon,x_0}(p)\to e^{ip\circ x_0}$ for every fixed shell momentum and $|K_\mu\rho_{\varepsilon,x_0}(p)|\le1$. The shell measure has infinite total mass: in radial coordinates, for $r\ge\max(1,\mu)$, $\omega_\mu(r)\le\sqrt2\,r$, so its radial density is bounded below by a positive constant times $r\,dr$, whose integral diverges. Fatou's lemma [F11] therefore gives $\liminf_{\varepsilon_m\downarrow0}\|K_\mu\rho_{\varepsilon_m,x_0}\|^2\ge\int_{H_\mu^+}1\,d\nu_\mu=\infty$. By [F1, F3] and the creation formula on the vacuum, $\|\Phi_\mu(\rho_{\varepsilon_m,x_0})\Omega\|=\|K_\mu\rho_{\varepsilon_m,x_0}\|$, so these vacuum vectors have no finite-norm point-field limit. More generally, suppose $f_\varepsilon$ satisfies the scalar hypotheses in the Statement. For any sequence $\varepsilon_j\to0$, Fatou [F11] applied to $|K_\mu f_{\varepsilon_j}|^2$ gives $\liminf_j\|K_\mu f_{\varepsilon_j}\|^2\ge\int1\,d\nu_\mu=\infty$. Thus the norms diverge as $\varepsilon\to0$: otherwise a bounded sequence with $\varepsilon_j<1/j$ could be selected using [A1], contradicting this conclusion. The vacuum creation identity gives the asserted field-vector norm. To verify the sufficient concentration condition, let $M=\sup_\varepsilon\|f_\varepsilon\|_1$ and let $g$ be any bounded continuous scalar function. Since $\int f_\varepsilon=1$, splitting the integral at radius $\delta$ gives $|\int f_\varepsilon(x)g(x)\,d^4x-g(x_0)|\le M\sup_{|x-x_0|<\delta}|g(x)-g(x_0)|+2\|g\|_\infty\int_{|x-x_0|\ge\delta}|f_\varepsilon(x)|\,d^4x$. First choose $\delta$ using continuity at $x_0$, then take $\varepsilon\to0$. Applying this to Schwartz $g$ and to $g(x)=e^{ip\circ x}$ proves both required limits. Every rescaling of a nonnegative normalized Schwartz profile has $M=1$ and satisfies concentration by its integrable tail; hence the general conclusion includes every such profile, not only the chosen bumps. [A1, F1, F2, F3, F9, F10, F11, F18, step 1.1, algebra]

3.1 The scalar one-particle space contains a unit vector $e$, for example a normalized indicator of an annulus $1<|\mathbf k|<2$, whose shell measure is finite and positive by [F2]. The symmetric vectors $e^{\otimes n}$ are unit vectors in mutually orthogonal sectors. Put $C=(\sum_{n\ge1}n^{-4})^{-1/2}$ and $\Psi_n=Cn^{-2}e^{\otimes n}$. By [F15], $\sum n^{-4}$ converges and is positive, so $C$ is well-defined and $\Psi$ is normalized. Also by [F15], $\sum n^{-2}<\infty$, so $\Psi\in D(N_s)$ and $N_s\Psi=(Cn^{-1}e^{\otimes n})_{n\ge1}$ is a Fock vector. Its image under one more application of $N_s$ would have squared norm $C^2\sum_{n\ge1}1=\infty$, so $N_s\Psi\notin D(N_s)$. By the composition-domain rule [F14] with $A=B=N_s$, $\Psi\notin D(N_s^2)$. Its mean and variance are finite by 2.2. [F1, F2, F5, F14, F15, step 2.2, construct, algebra]

4.1 Fix a unit spinor $z\in\mathbb C^4$ and, for $\varepsilon>0$, define $u_\varepsilon(\mathbf x)=\varepsilon^{-3}\rho_3((\mathbf x-\mathbf x_0)/\varepsilon)z$. For every spatial Schwartz test, change of variables and [F10] show that its pairing with $u_\varepsilon$ tends to the test's value at $\mathbf x_0$ times $z$, while $\|u_\varepsilon\|_2=\varepsilon^{-3/2}\|\rho_3\|_2\to\infty$. For a general family in the Dirac Statement, set $e=z_0/\|z_0\|$ and $h_a(\mathbf x)=b_3((\mathbf x-\mathbf x_0)/a)e$ for $a>0$. By [F18], this is a spinor Schwartz test, $h_a(\mathbf x_0)^\dagger z_0=\|z_0\|$, and $\|h_a\|_2=a^{3/2}\|b_3\|_2$. Given $L>0$, choose $a$ with $\|h_a\|_2<\|z_0\|/(2L)$. The assumed pairing limit then gives $|\langle h_a,u_\varepsilon\rangle_2|>\|z_0\|/2$ for all sufficiently small $\varepsilon$. Cauchy–Schwarz [F12] implies $\|u_\varepsilon\|_2>L$. Thus every such family has $\|u_\varepsilon\|_2\to\infty$. The following operator estimate applies to either the explicit bump family or this arbitrary family. By [F16], choose countable dense sets in the two Dirac energy ranges. Conjugating the negative-range dense set preserves density, and the Cartesian product of the two dense sets is countable and dense in the Hilbert direct sum. Therefore the one-particle space for the CAR Fock representation is separable and [F17] applies. For $A_\varepsilon=\Psi_t(u_\varepsilon)$, [F8] gives $A_\varepsilon A_\varepsilon^\dagger+A_\varepsilon^\dagger A_\varepsilon=\|u_\varepsilon\|_2^2I$. By [F17], the creation and annihilation terms are bounded, hence so is their sum. Cauchy–Schwarz [F12] gives $\sup_{\|x\|=\|y\|=1}|\langle A_\varepsilon x,y\rangle|\le\|A_\varepsilon\|$, while choosing $y=A_\varepsilon x/\|A_\varepsilon x\|$ for each unit $x$ with $A_\varepsilon x\ne0$ gives equality after taking the supremum over $x$. The adjoint identity swaps $x$ and $y$, so the same two-vector supremum equals $\|A_\varepsilon^\dagger\|$. For bounded operators $X,Y$, each unit $\xi$ satisfies $\|XY\xi\|\le\|X\|\,\|Y\xi\|\le\|X\|\,\|Y\|$ and $\|(X+Y)\xi\|\le\|X\xi\|+\|Y\xi\|\le\|X\|+\|Y\|$; taking suprema gives product submultiplicativity and the triangle inequality. Applying these inequalities to the CAR identity yields $\|u_\varepsilon\|_2^2=\|A_\varepsilon A_\varepsilon^\dagger+A_\varepsilon^\dagger A_\varepsilon\|\le2\|A_\varepsilon\|^2$. Thus $\|A_\varepsilon\|\ge\|u_\varepsilon\|_2/\sqrt2\to\infty$, excluding a bounded equal-time point-field norm limit. [F8, F10, F12, F16, F17, F18, step 2.3, given, algebra] ∎

items.statement:
Let $\mu\ge0$, $\omega_\mu(\mathbf k)=\sqrt{|\mathbf k|^2+\mu^2}$, and for a fixed $\mathbf k$ with $\omega_\mu(\mathbf k)>0$ set
$$g_{\omega_\mu}(t)=\frac{e^{-i\omega_\mu(\mathbf k)|t|}}{2\omega_\mu(\mathbf k)}.$$
This is the time-mode factor of the tempered scalar carrier in [[lem-qft-free-time-ordered-kernel]]. Its first derivative has jump $-i$ at $t=0$, giving the Green source $i\delta_0$ after applying the $(-,+,+,+)$ Klein–Gordon operator and Fourier-inverting the spatial momentum.

items.title: Positive transverse photon one-particle space
items.design_state: Assigned QFT-MG01 research interface authored as a conditional mathematical item with exact hypotheses and a complete local proof.
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice [[def-countable-choice]]. Let
$$\mathcal H=L^2(\mathbb R^3,d^3\mathbf k;\mathbb C^3),\qquad \langle u,v\rangle_2=\int_{\mathbb R^3}\overline{u(\mathbf k)}\cdot v(\mathbf k)\,d^3\mathbf k,$$
with the second-variable-linear convention of [[def-qft-fock-and-test-spaces]]; the real momentum dot product and norm are those of
[[def-euclidean-inner-product]]. Explicitly extend the real dot product
complex-bilinearly to $a\cdot b=\sum_{j=1}^3a_jb_j$ for $a,b\in\mathbb C^3$.
Each complex fiber instead has the positive Hermitian pairing
$\langle a,b\rangle_2=\overline a\cdot b=\sum_j\overline a_jb_j$ and
norm $\|a\|^2=\sum_j|a_j|^2$; the displayed integral uses this pairing.
Hilbert completeness follows from [[lem-l-two-with-the-integral-pairing-is-a-hilbert-space]]. For $\mathbf k\ne0$, write $n(\mathbf k)=\mathbf k/|\mathbf k|$ and
$$P_T(\mathbf k)=I_3-n(\mathbf k)n(\mathbf k)^T.$$
Assign any value at $\mathbf k=0$, which is a Lebesgue-null set. Let $M_{P_T}$ be multiplication by this measurable matrix field and define the positive transverse photon space
$$\mathcal H_T=\operatorname{Ran}M_{P_T} =\{u\in\mathcal H:\mathbf k\cdot u(\mathbf k)=0\text{ for almost every }\mathbf k\ne0\}.$$
The inner product on $\mathcal H_T$ is the restriction of that on $\mathcal H$. Each nonzero momentum fiber is the two-complex-dimensional plane $\{a\in\mathbb C^3:\mathbf k\cdot a=0\}$ perpendicular to the real vector $\mathbf k$ in that Hermitian pairing; no global continuous polarization frame is part of the definition.

items.title: Charged gauge data and SI-natural conventions
items.design_state: Assigned QFT-MG01 research interface authored as a conditional mathematical item with exact hypotheses and a complete local proof.
items.statement:
Use the fixed Minkowski coordinates $x=(x^0,\mathbf x)=(ct,x^1,x^2,x^3)$, with $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$, on an open coordinate domain $U\subseteq\mathbb R^4$ with its standard topology. Each $x^a$ has unit metre. For a smooth scalar component $u:U\to\mathbb R$ or $u:U\to\mathbb C$, define $\partial_a u:=\partial u/\partial x^a$; thus $\partial_0=c^{-1}\partial_t$ at fixed $\mathbf x$, $\partial_j=\partial/\partial x^j$ for $j=1,2,3$, and each $\partial_a$ has unit $\mathrm m^{-1}$. Raise derivative indices with $\partial^a:=\eta^{ab}\partial_b$. The fields in this definition are smooth maps
$$\phi\in C^\infty(U;\mathbb R),\qquad \mathbf A\in C^\infty(U;\mathbb R^3),\qquad \psi\in C^\infty(U;\mathbb C^4),\qquad \chi\in C^\infty(U;\mathbb R).$$
Define the lower-potential component maps $A_a:U\to\mathbb R$ by $A_0=-\phi/c$ and $A_j=\mathbf A_j$; collectively $(A_a)$ is the real covector potential in this chart. Then $F_{ab}:=\partial_aA_b-\partial_bA_a$ has smooth real component maps $F_{ab}:U\to\mathbb R$. The spinor is an ordinary commuting $\mathbb C^4$-valued map, not a tuple of Grassmann generators. Its Dirac adjoint is the smooth row-valued map $\bar\psi:=\psi^\dagger\beta:U\to(\mathbb C^4)^*$, using the fixed matrices and adjoint of [[def-qft-dirac-projections]], so $\{\gamma^a,\gamma^b\}=-2\eta^{ab}I_4$. In fixed SI units, $\phi$ is in volts, each $A_a$ is in $\mathrm{T\,m}$, $\psi$ is assigned field dimension $\mathrm m^{-3/2}$, and $\chi$ is in webers; these unit labels accompany the maps and do not identify $q$ with a measured charge. For periodic spatial domains, the same component and unit conventions apply to smooth periodic coordinate lifts, with the quotient domain specified by the item using them.

For the SI-normalization bookkeeping, let $c>0$ (m s$^{-1}$), $\hbar>0$ (J s), $\mu_0>0$ (N A$^{-2}$), a real charge parameter $q$ (C), and a mass parameter $m>0$ (kg) be symbolic inputs; put $\epsilon_0=(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}$. In the current SI, $c$ and $h$ are defining constants while $\mu_0$ is experimentally determined; the formula below keeps $\mu_0$ symbolic and assigns it no numerical value. Use the lower-potential convention
$$A_a=(-\phi/c,\mathbf A),$$
where $A_a$ has units T m, $\phi$ is in volts, and $\mathbf A$ is in T m. Define
$$S_0=\sqrt{\mu_0\hbar c},\qquad a_a=A_a/S_0,\qquad f_{ab}=\partial_aa_b-\partial_ba_a,$$
$$\mu=mc/\hbar,\qquad g=q\sqrt{\mu_0c/\hbar}=q/\sqrt{\epsilon_0\hbar c},\qquad D_a=\partial_a-ig a_a.$$
Here $D_a$ acts on $\psi\in C^\infty(U;\mathbb C^4)$ by $(D_a\psi)(x)=\partial_a\psi(x)-ig a_a(x)\psi(x)$, again a smooth map $U\to\mathbb C^4$. Thus $a_a$ and $\mu$ have units m$^{-1}$, $f_{ab}$ has units m$^{-2}$, and $g$ is dimensionless. For $\psi$ with units m$^{-3/2}$, both $-\tfrac14 f_{ab}f^{ab}$ and $\bar\psi(i\gamma^aD_a-\mu)\psi$ have units m$^{-4}$; their integral over $d^4x$ is dimensionless and represents the action divided by $\hbar$ in this normalization.

For the real smooth gauge-parameter map $\chi:U\to\mathbb R$ in webers, put $\alpha:=\chi/S_0\in C^\infty(U;\mathbb R)$ (dimensionless) and use
$$A'_a=A_a+\partial_a\chi,\qquad a'_a=a_a+\partial_a\alpha,\qquad \psi'=e^{ig\alpha}\psi.$$
The induced covariant derivative is $D'_a=\partial_a-ig a'_a$. These are formal mathematical conventions for the later conditional deductions. They do not adopt a measured value of $\mu_0$, identify $q$ with an electron charge, impose charge quantization, or assert that interacting continuum fields exist.

items.statement: Assume Countable Choice. For $n\in S^2\subset\mathbb R^3$, let $E_n=n^\perp=\operatorname{Ran}(I-nn^T)$ be the real transverse plane. There do not exist continuous maps $e_1,e_2:S^2\to\mathbb R^3$ such that, for every $n$, $(e_1(n),e_2(n))$ is an orthonormal basis of $E_n$. A continuous real orthonormal polarization frame would in particular give a continuous nowhere-zero tangent vector field on $S^2$.

items.title: Lorenz auxiliary subsidiary null quotient
items.design_state: Assigned QFT-MG01 research interface authored as a conditional mathematical item with exact hypotheses and a complete local proof.
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice and use $\mathcal H_T$ from [[def-qft-photon-transverse-space]]. On $\mathcal K=L^2(\mathbb R^3,d^3\mathbf k;\mathbb C^4)$ define
$$[\epsilon,\delta]_\eta=\int_{\mathbb R^3}\epsilon(\mathbf k)^\dagger\eta\,\delta(\mathbf k)\,d^3\mathbf k,\qquad \eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1).$$
For $\mathbf k\ne0$, let $n=\mathbf k/|\mathbf k|$ and set
$$\mathcal K_0=\{\epsilon\in\mathcal K:-\epsilon^0+n\cdot\boldsymbol\epsilon=0\text{ a.e.}\},\qquad T\epsilon=\boldsymbol\epsilon-n\epsilon^0.$$
Then $\mathcal K_0$ is closed, $T:\mathcal K_0\to\mathcal H_T$ is bounded and onto, and
$$[\epsilon,\delta]_\eta=\langle T\epsilon,T\delta\rangle_2\quad(\epsilon,\delta\in\mathcal K_0).$$
Its radical (the vectors pairing to zero with all of $\mathcal K_0$) is
$$\mathcal N=\ker T=\{b(\mathbf k)(1,n(\mathbf k)):b\in L^2(\mathbb R^3)\}.$$
Consequently $\mathcal K_0/\mathcal N$ with the induced form is a positive Hilbert space isometric to $\mathcal H_T$. The form on the four-component auxiliary space is indefinite; only the subsidiary quotient is the positive physical one-particle space.

items.title: Smeared Coulomb photon operator distribution
items.design_state: Assigned QFT-MG01 research interface authored as a conditional mathematical item with exact hypotheses and a complete local proof.
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice. Let $j=(j_1,j_2,j_3)\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^4;\mathbb R^3)$ and use $\mathcal H_T$ and $P_T$ from [[def-qft-photon-transverse-space]]. For $\omega=|\mathbf k|$ and $\mathbf k\ne0$, define
$$g_j(\mathbf k)=\frac{1}{(2\pi)^{3/2}(2\omega)^{1/2}}\, P_T(\mathbf k)\int_{\mathbb R^4}j(x)e^{i\omega x^0-i\mathbf k\cdot\mathbf x}\,d^4x.$$
Then $g_j\in\mathcal H_T$. On the finite-particle domain $\mathcal D_{\rm fin}$ of the bosonic Fock space $\mathcal F_s(\mathcal H_T)$, the smeared transverse potential is
$$A_T(j)=a(g_j)+a^\dagger(g_j).$$
Its matrix elements are continuous in the test-function topology; it is an operator-valued distribution and does not assign a pointwise operator to $A_i(x)$. With $E_i=-\partial_0A_i$, the equal-time canonical commutator is the distribution
$$[A_i(0,\mathbf x),E_j(0,\mathbf y)] =-i\,P_{T,ij}(-i\nabla_{\mathbf x})\delta^3(\mathbf x-\mathbf y).$$

items.title: Newtonian off-diagonal kernel of the transverse projector
items.design_state: Local A-page prerequisite added because the Coulomb-potential counterexample needs the Fourier projector kernel; complete proof derives it by Abel regularization and identifies its Newtonian off-diagonal part.
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice. Let $G(\mathbf x)=1/(4\pi|\mathbf x|)$ on $\mathbb R^3\setminus\{0\}$, interpreted as its locally integrable distribution, and use the Fourier convention
$$\widehat f(\mathbf k)=\int_{\mathbb R^3}e^{-i\mathbf k\cdot\mathbf x}f(\mathbf x)\,d^3\mathbf x,\qquad f(\mathbf x)=(2\pi)^{-3}\int_{\mathbb R^3}e^{i\mathbf k\cdot\mathbf x}\widehat f(\mathbf k)\,d^3\mathbf k.$$
Then $\mathcal F^{-1}(|\mathbf k|^{-2})=G$ distributionally. Consequently, for $P_{T,ij}(\mathbf k)=\delta_{ij}-k_i k_j/|\mathbf k|^2$,
$$P_{T,ij}(-i\nabla)\delta^3 =\delta_{ij}\delta^3+\partial_i\partial_jG.$$
For $\mathbf x\ne0$,
$$\partial_i\partial_jG(\mathbf x) =-\frac{\delta_{ij}}{4\pi|\mathbf x|^3} +\frac{3x_ix_j}{4\pi|\mathbf x|^5}.$$
Thus the equal-time transverse-potential commutator of [[lem-qft-photon-smeared-potential]] has this off-diagonal Newtonian kernel (with its stated factor $-i$). The identity is distributional at the origin; the displayed classical derivative formula is only asserted away from it.

items.title: Dirac gauge covariance, action and conserved current
items.design_state: Assigned QFT-MG01 research interface authored as a conditional mathematical item with exact hypotheses and a complete local proof.
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice and use the conventions of [[def-qft-qed-gauge-data]]. Let $U\subseteq\mathbb R^4$ be open, let each $a_a:U\to\mathbb R$
be a smooth real potential component, and let $\psi:U\to\mathbb C^4$
be a smooth commuting spinor. The real gauge parameter is a smooth
$\alpha:U\to\mathbb R$, and all fields, derivatives and compactly supported
smooth variations below are on this same $U$ (including $U=\mathbb R^4$). Use the symmetrized classical density
$$\mathcal L_D=\frac i2\{\bar\psi\gamma^aD_a\psi-(D_a\bar\psi)\gamma^a\psi\}-\mu\bar\psi\psi,\qquad D_a\bar\psi=\partial_a\bar\psi+ig a_a\bar\psi.$$
For compactly supported smooth variations, its spinor Euler equation is $(i\gamma^aD_a-\mu)\psi=0$ and its adjoint. The density is invariant under the gauge transformation in [[def-qft-qed-gauge-data]]. On solutions,
$$\partial_a j^a=0,\qquad j^a=g\bar\psi\gamma^a\psi.$$
In SI variables the corresponding Hamiltonian density has the sign convention
$$\psi^\dagger\!\left[c\,\boldsymbol\alpha\cdot(-i\hbar\nabla-q\mathbf A)+\beta mc^2+q\phi\right]\psi.$$
These are conditional variational identities for smooth commuting classical fields. They assert no global existence theorem for the coupled field equations, no quantum current product, and no empirical measurement.

items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice and the conventions of [[def-qft-qed-gauge-data]]. Let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be a nonempty open time interval, with $t$ measured in seconds and $x^0=ct$, and let $T_L^3=(\mathbb R/L\mathbb Z)^3$ be the flat spatial torus with period $L>0$ metres and periodic coordinates $\mathbf x$. Take jointly smooth periodic maps
$$\mathbf A:I	imes T_L^3	o\mathbb R^3,\qquad \phi:I	imes T_L^3	o\mathbb R,\qquad ho:I	imes T_L^3	o\mathbb R,\qquad \mathbf J:I	imes T_L^3	o\mathbb R^3.$$
Write $\dot{\mathbf A}:=\partial_t\mathbf A$ for the time partial derivative at fixed $\mathbf x$, and $\mathbf B:=
abla	imes\mathbf A$. All spatial differential operators below are the periodic coordinate derivatives, and each displayed spatial integral and Hamiltonian is evaluated at a fixed $t\in I$; the time argument is suppressed in the formulas. In SI units, $\mathbf A$ has unit $\mathrm{T\,m}$, $\phi$ has unit $\mathrm V$, $ho$ has unit $\mathrm{C\,m^{-3}}$, and $\mathbf J$ has unit $\mathrm{A\,m^{-2}}$. Thus $\dot{\mathbf A}$ and $
abla\phi$ both have unit $\mathrm{V\,m^{-1}}=\mathrm{T\,m\,s^{-1}}$, and every term of the formal classical Lagrangian density has unit $\mathrm{J\,m^{-3}}$. Let $c>0$ have unit $\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$, let $\mu_0>0$ be the symbolic magnetic constant with unit $\mathrm{N\,A^{-2}}$, and put $\epsilon_0=(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}$ with unit $\mathrm{F\,m^{-1}}$; no numerical value for these constants is adopted. Define the formal classical density
$$\mathcal L= rac{\epsilon_0}{2}|\dot{\mathbf A}+
abla\phi|^2- rac1{2\mu_0}|
abla	imes\mathbf A|^2-ho\phi+\mathbf J\cdot\mathbf A.$$
The canonical momenta are $ oldsymbol\pi_A=\epsilon_0(\dot{\mathbf A}+
abla\phi)$, with unit $\mathrm{C\,m^{-2}}$, and $\pi_\phi=0$. Periodic integration by parts gives the fixed-time Hamiltonian
$$H(t)=\int_{T_L^3}\left( rac{| oldsymbol\pi_A|^2}{2\epsilon_0}+ rac{|\mathbf B|^2}{2\mu_0}+\phi(
abla\cdot oldsymbol\pi_A+ho)-\mathbf J\cdot\mathbf Aight)d^3\mathbf x.$$
Variation of the multiplier $\phi$ imposes $
abla\cdot oldsymbol\pi_A+ho=0$. In Coulomb gauge $
abla\cdot\mathbf A=0$, this becomes $-\Delta\phi=ho/\epsilon_0$. At each fixed $t$, a smooth periodic solution can exist only if $\int_{T_L^3}ho(\mathbf x,t)\,d^3\mathbf x=0$. If $\int_{T_L^3}ho(\mathbf x,t)\,d^3\mathbf x=0$ for every $t\in I$, there is a unique jointly smooth periodic solution with zero spatial mean, whose Fourier coefficients are
$$\widehat\phi_0(t)=0,\qquad \widehat\phi_k(t)= rac{\widehatho_k(t)}{\epsilon_0|2\pi k/L|^2}\quad(k
e0),\qquad \widehatho_k(t)=L^{-3}\int_{[0,L]^3}ho(\mathbf x,t)e^{-2\pi i k\cdot\mathbf x/L}\,d^3\mathbf x.$$
For every $t\in I$ it satisfies
$$ rac{\epsilon_0}{2}\int_{T_L^3}|
abla\phi|^2\,d^3\mathbf x= rac12\int_{T_L^3}ho\phi\,d^3\mathbf x= rac{L^3}{2\epsilon_0}\sum_{k
e0} rac{|\widehatho_k(t)|^2}{|2\pi k/L|^2}\ge0.$$
This is a classical conditional solver for smooth periodic neutral data; it makes no claim about quantum density products or nonperiodic boundary conditions.

items.title: Finite-mode Dirac first-order constraint reduction
items.design_state: Assigned QFT-MG01 research interface authored as a conditional mathematical item with exact hypotheses and a complete local proof.
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice, the constants in [[def-qft-qed-gauge-data]], $\hbar>0$, and a finite integer $N\ge1$. Let the real configuration space be $Q=\mathbb R^{2N}$ with coordinates $(x_1,y_1,\ldots,x_N,y_N)$ and let $T^*Q\cong\mathbb R^{4N}$ have corresponding real canonical momentum coordinates $(P^x_1,P^y_1,\ldots,P^x_N,P^y_N)$. On real smooth functions define the canonical Poisson bracket
$$\{F,G\}=\sum_{j=1}^N\left(\frac{\partial F}{\partial x_j}\frac{\partial G}{\partial P^x_j}-\frac{\partial F}{\partial P^x_j}\frac{\partial G}{\partial x_j}+\frac{\partial F}{\partial y_j}\frac{\partial G}{\partial P^y_j}-\frac{\partial F}{\partial P^y_j}\frac{\partial G}{\partial y_j}\right),$$
and extend it $\mathbb C$-bilinearly to complex-valued smooth functions on $T^*Q$. Define the complex coordinate notation
$$z_j=x_j+iy_j,\qquad \bar z_j=x_j-iy_j,\qquad p_j=\frac{P^x_j-iP^y_j}{2},\qquad \bar p_j=\frac{P^x_j+iP^y_j}{2}.$$
These definitions give
$$\{z_j,p_k\}=\delta_{jk},\qquad \{\bar z_j,\bar p_k\}=\delta_{jk},$$
with all other elementary brackets zero; the bracket is extended by bilinearity and the Leibniz rule. The first-order kinetic term $\frac{i\hbar}{2}\sum_j(\bar z_j\dot z_j-\dot{\bar z}_jz_j)$ gives primary constraints
$$C_j=p_j-\frac{i\hbar}{2}\bar z_j,\qquad \bar C_j=\bar p_j+\frac{i\hbar}{2}z_j.$$
In the order $(C_1,\ldots,C_N,\bar C_1,\ldots,\bar C_N)$ their constraint matrix and inverse are
$$M=\begin{pmatrix}0&-i\hbar I_N\\i\hbar I_N&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad M^{-1}=\begin{pmatrix}0&-iI_N/\hbar\\iI_N/\hbar&0\end{pmatrix}.$$
Here, “second class” means that the constraint matrix $M_{AB}=\{\chi_A,\chi_B\}$ is invertible. Thus these constraints are second class. For a real smooth finite-mode Hamiltonian $H\in C^\infty(Q;\mathbb R)$, viewed as independent of the momenta, define the Wirtinger derivative
$$\frac{\partial H}{\partial\bar z_j}:=\frac12\left(\frac{\partial H}{\partial x_j}+i\frac{\partial H}{\partial y_j}\right).$$
The Dirac bracket
$$\{F,G\}_D=\{F,G\}-\{F,\chi_A\}(M^{-1})_{AB}\{\chi_B,G\}, \quad \chi=(C_1,\ldots,C_N,\bar C_1,\ldots,\bar C_N),$$
satisfies $\{z_j,\bar z_k\}_D=-i\delta_{jk}/\hbar$ and $\{z_j,z_k\}_D=\{\bar z_j,\bar z_k\}_D=0$. For a real smooth finite-mode Hamiltonian $H(z,\bar z)$ the reduced equation is $i\hbar\dot z_j=\partial H/\partial\bar z_j$. These are ordinary commuting coordinates; they do not derive CAR by canonical quantization.

items.title: Photon quotient Lorentz representation and positive dynamics
items.design_state: Assigned QFT-MG01 research interface authored as a conditional mathematical item with exact hypotheses and a complete local proof.
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice. On the future null cone write $p=(\omega,\mathbf k)$, $\omega=|\mathbf k|$, $\mathbf k\ne0$, and use the measure $d\nu=d^3\mathbf k/(2\omega)$. The fiber $p^\perp/\mathbb Cp$ has the positive quotient form of [[lem-qft-photon-null-quotient]]. Give the proper orthochronous Lorentz group its matrix topology: the subspace topology inherited from $\mathbb R^{16}$ with Euclidean matrix norm $\|A\|_{\rm mat}=(\sum_{i,j=0}^3|A_{ij}|^2)^{1/2}$. For each proper orthochronous Lorentz transformation $\Lambda$, the action
$$[s(p)]\longmapsto[\Lambda s(\Lambda^{-1}p)]$$
is a unitary representation on the square-integrable quotient sections. It is strongly continuous for this topology, meaning $\|U_\Lambda s-U_{\Lambda_0}s\|\to0$ for every section $s$ as $\|\Lambda-\Lambda_0\|_{\rm mat}\to0$. Its bosonic Fock lift is strongly continuous for the same topology. Under the unitary identification with $\mathcal H_T$ given by
$T_p[\epsilon]:=\boldsymbol\epsilon-(\mathbf k/\omega)\epsilon^0$
and $u(\mathbf k)=T_p[s(p)]/\sqrt{2\omega}$, as in [[lem-qft-photon-null-quotient]], the free translation representation for $a=(a^0,\mathbf a)\in\mathbb R^4$ has phase $e^{i(\omega a^0-\mathbf k\cdot\mathbf a)}$. Its bosonic Fock lift has the joint PVM $\mathsf E$ whose $n$-particle sector acts by multiplication by $\mathbf1_{\{(\sum_{r=1}^n|\mathbf k_r|,-\sum_{r=1}^n\mathbf k_r)\in B\}}$ for Borel $B\subseteq\mathbb R^4$; on the vacuum it acts by $\mathbf1_B(0)$. Define its joint spectrum to be
$$\operatorname{supp}(\mathsf E):=\{q\in\mathbb R^4:\mathsf E(U)\ne0\text{ for every open neighborhood }U\text{ of }q\}.$$
Then this joint spectrum is the closed future cone
$$\overline V_+=\{(E,\mathbf P):E\ge|\mathbf P|\},$$
with the vacuum at $(0,\mathbf0)$. In the product realization of the sectors in [[lem-qft-second-quantized-spectrum]], on sector $n$ the energy operator multiplies by $\sum_{r=1}^n|\mathbf k_r|$ and has the exact maximal domain
$$D(H_E)=\left\{\Psi=(\Psi_n):\sum_{n\ge1}\int_{(\mathbb R^3)^n}\left(\sum_{r=1}^n|\mathbf k_r|\right)^2\|\Psi_n(\mathbf k_1,\ldots,\mathbf k_n)\|^2\,d^3\mathbf k_1\cdots d^3\mathbf k_n<\infty\right\},$$
with the vacuum component unrestricted; here $\Psi_n$ is the symmetric transverse wavefunction in the product realization and the norm is the product-fiber Hilbert norm. Each momentum operator $P_j$ multiplies by $-\sum_{r=1}^n k_{r,j}$ and has maximal domain
$$D(P_j)=\left\{\Psi=(\Psi_n):\sum_{n\ge1}\int_{(\mathbb R^3)^n}\left|\sum_{r=1}^n k_{r,j}\right|^2\|\Psi_n(\mathbf k_1,\ldots,\mathbf k_n)\|^2\,d^3\mathbf k_1\cdots d^3\mathbf k_n<\infty\right\},$$
again with unrestricted vacuum component. These are mathematical free-field representation statements.

items.proof:
**Given:** [A1], [F1]–[F11], the future-cone parametrization, and the componentwise Lorentz action.

1.1 By [F5], $\Lambda$ preserves $\eta$ and sends a future null vector $p$ to a future null vector $\Lambda p$. It maps $p^\perp$ onto $(\Lambda p)^\perp$ and $\mathbb Cp$ onto $\mathbb C\Lambda p$, so it induces a well-defined map on the quotient fiber. The induced form is preserved because $\eta(\Lambda v,\Lambda w)=\eta(v,w)$; hence the fiber map is an isometry. The map $T_p$ is independent of the representative: replacing $\epsilon$ by $\epsilon+cp$ changes its value by $c(\mathbf k-(\mathbf k/\omega)\omega)=0$. For $\epsilon\in p^\perp$, $\mathbf k\cdot T_p[\epsilon]=0$; its pairing is the positive quotient pairing of [F1]. The lift $\epsilon=(0,\sqrt{2\omega}\,u(\mathbf k))$ for transverse $u$ proves surjectivity, and $d\nu=d^3\mathbf k/(2\omega)$ gives $\int\|T_p[s(p)]\|^2d\nu=\int\|u(\mathbf k)\|^2d^3\mathbf k$. Thus the stated section identification is well-defined and unitary. Applying two Lorentz maps successively gives the representation composition law. [F1, F5, given, algebra]

1.2 The component identification of [F3] uses $X=\mathbb R^3\times\{1,2,3\}$ with Lebesgue measure times counting measure; $X$ is sigma-finite because the boxes $[-m,m]^3\times\{1,2,3\}$ have finite measure by [F8]. The finite measurable map $\boldsymbol\omega(\mathbf k,j)=(|\mathbf k|,-\mathbf k)$ lets us apply [F3]. It gives the PVM $\mathsf E(B)$ whose $n$-particle multiplier is $\mathbf1_{\{(\sum_r|\mathbf k_r|,-\sum_r\mathbf k_r)\in B\}}$, with vacuum multiplier $\mathbf1_B(0)$, and it gives the maximal componentwise multiplier domains. By [F7], $P_T(\mathbf k)$ is pointwise self-adjoint and idempotent, so it commutes with each scalar multiplier; its tensor powers commute with the n-particle PVM and multiplier. The symmetric transverse sector is reducing, so restriction preserves the maximal domain, which for the energy is exactly $D(H_E)$ displayed in the Statement. [A1, F3, F7, F8, given, algebra]

2.1 For the boost $B_n(\chi)$ in [F2], put $\beta=\tanh\chi$ and $\gamma=\cosh\chi$, so $|\beta|<1$ and $\gamma=(1-\beta^2)^{-1/2}$. In Euclidean unit direction $n$ [F5], its spatial cone coordinates satisfy
$$\mathbf k'=\mathbf k+(\gamma-1)(n\cdot\mathbf k)n+\gamma\beta\omega n,\qquad \omega'=\gamma(\omega+\beta n\cdot\mathbf k).$$
Taking $n$ as the third coordinate axis, the first two spatial coordinates are unchanged and
$$\frac{\partial k'_3}{\partial k_3} =\gamma\left(1+\beta\frac{k_3}{\omega}\right)=\frac{\omega'}{\omega}.$$
Thus $\det(\partial\mathbf k'/\partial\mathbf k)=\omega'/\omega$. A rotation has determinant one and preserves $\omega$. By [F2], every proper orthochronous $\Lambda$ is a product of these, so $d^3\mathbf k'/(2\omega')=d^3\mathbf k/(2\omega)$. Combining this change of variables with the fiber isometry in step 1.1 proves unitarity on the quotient-section space and verifies the stated identification with $\mathcal H_T$. [F2, F5, step 1.1, given, algebra]

2.2 Each joint multiplier value $(\sum_r|\mathbf k_r|,-\sum_r\mathbf k_r)$ lies in $\overline V_+$ by the triangle inequality [F9], so the PVM vanishes outside that closed cone. Fix a nonzero $\mathbf k_0$ and the boundary point $(|\mathbf k_0|,-\mathbf k_0)$. Choose $v\in\mathbb R^3$ not parallel to $\mathbf k_0$. By [F7], $P_T(\mathbf k_0)v\ne0$, and continuity gives a bounded open momentum neighborhood $V$ of $\mathbf k_0$, disjoint from zero, on which $\|P_T(\mathbf k)v\|$ is bounded below by a positive constant. Given any open neighborhood $G$ of $(|\mathbf k_0|,-\mathbf k_0)$, shrink $V$ so the map $\mathbf k\mapsto(|\mathbf k|,-\mathbf k)$ sends $V$ into $G$. Choose a ball inside $V$ and a positive finite-measure box $Q$ inside that ball by [F8]. The vector $u(\mathbf k)=\mathbf1_Q(\mathbf k)P_T(\mathbf k)v$ is a nonzero element of $\mathcal H_T$ supported over $G$, so $\mathsf E(G)u=u\ne0$. The vacuum supplies the origin. [A1, F3, F5, F7, F8, F9, step 1.2, given, construct]

3.1 Matrix multiplication is continuous, and the Lorentz equation gives $\Lambda^{-1}=\eta\Lambda^T\eta$, so inversion is continuous in the stated matrix topology. For $v\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C^3)$ with support in $B_R$, $R\ge1$, take the four-component representative $s_v(p)=(0,\sqrt{2\omega}\,P_T(\mathbf k)v(\mathbf k))$; under the stated unitary identification its class corresponds to $u=P_Tv\in\mathcal H_T$. Put $q=\Lambda^{-1}p$ and $a_\Lambda(\mathbf k)=T_p\Lambda(0,\sqrt{2q^0}\,P_T(\mathbf q)v(\mathbf q))$, the transverse chart representative of the transformed quotient section. If $\Lambda$ is sufficiently close to $I$, uniformly for future null $p$ one has $\omega/2\le q^0=|\mathbf q|\le2\omega$ and $\|\Lambda\|_{\rm op}\le2$: use $\|p\|_2=\sqrt2\omega$, the displayed inverse formula and the Euclidean Cauchy–Schwarz bound for a matrix acting on a vector. Thus $a_\Lambda$ vanishes outside $B_{2R}$, and $\|T_p\|_{\rm op}\le\sqrt2$, $\|P_T\|_{\rm op}\le1$ give $|a_\Lambda(\mathbf k)|\le C M\sqrt\omega$, where $M=\sup|v|$ and $C$ is independent of sufficiently small $\Lambda-I$. Consequently $|a_\Lambda-a_I|$ is bounded by a fixed constant $C_R M$ on the common support. Its squared $L^2(d\nu)$ contribution on $B_\delta$ is at most $C_R^2M^2\nu(B_\delta)=C_R^2M^2\pi\delta^2$ by [F6, F10]. On the annulus $\delta\le|\mathbf k|\le2R$, extend the explicit formula to matrices $A$ in a sufficiently small closed Euclidean matrix box about $I$ by putting $q=\eta A^T\eta p$. On that box $q^0$ and $|\mathbf q|$ remain positive, bounded away from zero on the annulus; the formula using $P_T(\mathbf q)=I-(\mathbf q/|\mathbf q|)(\mathbf q/|\mathbf q|)^T$ is therefore continuous. The box times annulus is closed bounded in $\mathbb R^{19}$, hence compact, and [F11] gives uniform continuity of this formula there. Restricting back to Lorentz matrices yields $a_\Lambda\to a_I$ uniformly on the annulus, which has finite $\nu$-measure by [F6]. First choose $\delta$, then $\Lambda-I$, to obtain $\|a_\Lambda-a_I\|_{L^2(d\nu)}\to0$; this is exactly the quotient-section norm. No fiber value at the omitted apex is used. These sections are dense by [F4, F7]: approximate any $u\in\mathcal H_T$ by smooth compactly supported $v$ and project by $P_T$. Unitarity from step 2.1 gives $\|U_\Lambda s-s\|\le2\|s-s_v\|+\|U_\Lambda s_v-s_v\|$, extending continuity to every section. At any $\Lambda_0$, the representation identity reduces continuity to $U_{\Lambda_0^{-1}\Lambda}\to I$, and $\Lambda_0^{-1}\Lambda\to I$ in the matrix topology. For an elementary $n$-tensor, telescoping and unitarity give $\|(U_\Lambda^{\otimes n}-I)(h_1\otimes\cdots\otimes h_n)\|\le\sum_{j=1}^n\|(U_\Lambda-I)h_j\|\prod_{l\ne j}\|h_l\|\to0$. Finite linear combinations are dense in the Hilbert tensor product; the symmetric projection is a contraction commuting with the tensor action, so continuity holds on each symmetric sector. The vacuum is fixed. Truncating an arbitrary Fock vector to finitely many sectors leaves an error bounded by twice its tail norm under these unitary maps; letting that tail tend to zero proves strong continuity on all Fock space. [A1, F1, F4, F5, F6, F7, F9, F10, F11, step 1.1, step 2.1, given, algebra]

4.1 Fix $(E,\mathbf P)$ with $E>|\mathbf P|$. Choose a unit $n\perp\mathbf P$; if $\mathbf P\ne0$, select a standard basis vector $w$ not parallel to $\mathbf P$ and normalize $w-(w\cdot\mathbf P/|\mathbf P|^2)\mathbf P$, while if $\mathbf P=0$ take any standard basis vector. Put $q=\tfrac12\sqrt{E^2-|\mathbf P|^2}$ and let $\mathbf k_1=-\mathbf P/2+qn$, $\mathbf k_2=-\mathbf P/2-qn$. Since $n\cdot\mathbf P=0$, $|\mathbf k_i|^2=|\mathbf P|^2/4+q^2=E^2/4$, so they are distinct nonzero momenta with $|\mathbf k_1|+|\mathbf k_2|=E$ and $-(\mathbf k_1+\mathbf k_2)=\mathbf P$. Given any open neighborhood $G$ of $(E,\mathbf P)$, continuity of the two-particle sum map gives disjoint bounded momentum neighborhoods $V_1,V_2$ of $\mathbf k_1,\mathbf k_2$ whose pairwise sums map into $G$. Choose fixed $v_i$ not parallel to $\mathbf k_i$ and shrink $V_i$ so $P_T(\mathbf k)v_i$ never vanishes there by [F7]; choose balls inside $V_i$ and positive finite-measure boxes $Q_i$ inside those balls by [F8]. The vectors $u_i(\mathbf k)=\mathbf1_{Q_i}(\mathbf k)P_T(\mathbf k)v_i$ are nonzero in $\mathcal H_T$. The symmetric vector $\Psi_2=P_{s,2}(u_1\otimes u_2)$ is nonzero because $Q_1$ and $Q_2$ are disjoint, and its two-particle multiplier values lie in $G$. Hence $\mathsf E(G)\Psi_2=\Psi_2\ne0$. Thus every neighborhood of $(E,\mathbf P)$ has nonzero two-particle spectral projection. Together with steps 1.2–2.2 this proves $\operatorname{supp}(\mathsf E)=\overline V_+$; [F3] gives the exact energy domain from step 1.2. [A1, F3, F5, F7, F8, step 1.2, step 2.2, given, construct] ∎

items.title: Local covariant physical field-strength observables
items.design_state: Assigned QFT-MG01 research interface authored as a conditional mathematical item with exact hypotheses and a complete local proof.
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice. Work in the fixed length coordinates $x=(x^0,\mathbf x)\in\mathbb R^4$ with $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$ and $\eta(v,w)=-v^0w^0+\mathbf v\cdot\mathbf w$; write $\partial_a:=\partial/\partial x^a$. For subsets $S,T\subseteq\mathbb R^4$, say they are **spacelike separated** when $\eta(x-y,x-y)=|\mathbf x-\mathbf y|^2-(x^0-y^0)^2>0$ for every $x\in S$ and $y\in T$. Let $A_0=0$ and let $A_i$ be the transverse potential operator-valued distribution of [[lem-qft-photon-smeared-potential]]. Set
$$F_{ab}=\partial_aA_b-\partial_bA_a,\qquad E_i=-\partial_0A_i,\qquad B_i=\epsilon_{irs}\partial_rA_s,$$
where $\epsilon_{irs}$ is the totally antisymmetric symbol with $\epsilon_{123}=1$. In the commutator formulas below, $\Delta=\sum_{r=1}^3\partial_r^2$ is the spatial Laplacian acting on $x-y$.
For a real antisymmetric test tensor $h=(h^{ab})$ with $h^{ab}\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^4;\mathbb R)$ and $h^{ab}=-h^{ba}$, define
$$F(h)=\frac12\int_{\mathbb R^4}F_{ab}(x)h^{ab}(x)\,d^4x =-A_b(\partial_a h^{ab}).$$
The effective test is conserved, $\partial_b\partial_a h^{ab}=0$, and $F(h)$ is unchanged by $A_b\mapsto A_b+\partial_b\lambda$ for smooth $\lambda$. Its one-particle coefficient $g_h$ is the vector $g_j$ of [[lem-qft-photon-smeared-potential]] for $j_i=-\partial_a h^{ai}$, so $F(h)=a(g_h)+a^\dagger(g_h)$ on $\mathcal D_{\rm fin}$.

Let $C_0=-i\Delta_0$, where $\Delta_0$ is the massless scalar causal commutator of [[lem-qft-scalar-causal-commutator]]. As distributions in $x-y$,
$$[E_i(x),E_j(y)]=[B_i(x),B_j(y)] =(-\delta_{ij}\Delta+\partial_i\partial_j)C_0(x-y),$$
$$[E_i(x),B_j(y)]=\epsilon_{jri}\partial_0\partial_rC_0(x-y).$$
Every right-hand side has support in the closed causal cone. Hence compactly supported tests whose supports are spacelike separated in the stated Minkowski sense give commuting field-strength operators on $\mathcal D_{\rm fin}$. The quotient representation of [[lem-qft-photon-covariance-spectrum]] makes these smeared field strengths Lorentz covariant: their on-shell coefficient depends on a polarization class only through $p_a\epsilon_b-p_b\epsilon_a$. These conclusions concern gauge-invariant free observables and do not assert locality of the Coulomb potential.

items.design_state: Assigned QFT-MG01 research interface authored as a conditional mathematical item with exact hypotheses and a complete local proof.
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice and use the Minkowski coordinates and separation condition of [[lem-qft-photon-local-field-strength]], so $\eta(x-y,x-y)=|\mathbf x-\mathbf y|^2-(x^0-y^0)^2$. Use the Hilbert space and projection of [[def-qft-photon-transverse-space]]: $\mathcal H=L^2(\mathbb R^3,d^3\mathbf k;\mathbb C^3)$ with pairing $\langle u,v\rangle_2=\int\overline u\cdot v\,d^3\mathbf k$, the matrix $P_T(\mathbf k)=I_3-nn^T$ for $n=\mathbf k/|\mathbf k|$ and $\mathbf k\ne0$, and its bounded multiplication operator $M_{P_T}:\mathcal H\to\mathcal H$, $(M_{P_T}u)(\mathbf k)=P_T(\mathbf k)u(\mathbf k)$. The value at zero is immaterial in $L^2$, and $\mathcal H_T=\operatorname{Ran}M_{P_T}=\{u\in\mathcal H:\mathbf k\cdot u(\mathbf k)=0\text{ a.e.}\}$ has the inherited Hilbert pairing. A spacetime region $O$ means an open subset of $\mathbb R^4$ in its standard topology. A real antisymmetric test $h=(h^{ab})$ is supported in $O$ when each component $h^{ab}\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^4;\mathbb R)$ has support contained in $O$. Two open regions $O_1,O_2$ are spacelike separated when $\eta(x-y,x-y)>0$ for every $x\in O_1$ and $y\in O_2$. Let $g_h\in\mathcal H_T$ be the one-particle vector for such a test from [[lem-qft-photon-local-field-strength]]. The space $\mathcal H_T$ is separable in its Hilbert norm topology: it is the range of $M_{P_T}$ on the separable space $\mathcal H$. Define
$$W_O(h)=W_{\rm Segal}(\sqrt2\,g_h),$$
where $W_{\rm Segal}$ is the Weyl unitary of [[lem-qft-segal-weyl-domain]]. It is bounded and unitary, and its one-parameter group has the self-adjoint field-strength closure as generator. For every open region $O\subseteq\mathbb R^4$, let $\mathcal A(O)$ be the norm-closed unital $*$-algebra generated by $W_O(h)$ for real antisymmetric tests supported in $O$; equivalently its bounded real and imaginary parts are included as observables. If $O_1,O_2$ are spacelike separated by the stated Minkowski condition, then $\mathcal A(O_1)$ and $\mathcal A(O_2)$ commute.
