items.title: Two physical photon fibers without global frame
items.design_state: Assigned QFT-MG01 research interface authored as a conditional mathematical item with exact hypotheses and a complete local proof.
items.statement: Assume Countable Choice. For each nonzero $\mathbf k$, the physical photon fiber is the real plane $n^\perp$ (or its complexification), where $n=\mathbf k/|\mathbf k|$, and therefore has dimension two. Locally in direction space one can choose two continuous orthonormal polarization vectors. There is no continuous real orthonormal polarization frame on all of $S^2$. The global subsidiary quotient $\mathcal K_0/\mathcal N$ of [[lem-qft-photon-null-quotient]] is isometric to the transverse space $\mathcal H_T$ of square-integrable sections from [[def-qft-photon-transverse-space]]. At a fixed direction $n$, the auxiliary fiber $K_{0,n}=\{(a,v)\in\mathbb C\times\mathbb C^3:n\cdot v=a\}$, with form $[(a,v),(b,w)]_\eta=-\overline a b+\overline v\cdot w$, has radical $N_n=\mathbb C(1,n)$ and quotient isometric to the complex transverse plane. Thus four auxiliary components do not represent four positive physical polarizations; the global section space is not a single fiber.

items.title: Finite-graph U(1) phases for matrix kernels
items.statement:
Let $X$ and $E$ be finite sets, let $s,t:E\to X$ give the source and target of each directed edge, and assume $X\ne\varnothing$. Fix a positive integer $r$, a matrix $T_e\in M_r(\mathbb C)$ for each $e\in E$, and an external link phase $\zeta_e\in U(1):=\{z\in\mathbb C:|z|=1\}$. The finite spin space is $\mathcal H_X:=\bigoplus_{x\in X}\mathbb C^r$, of dimension $d=r|X|$.

For a real vertex phase $\theta=(\theta_x)_{x\in X}\in\mathbb R^X$, define
$$ \zeta_e^\theta:=e^{i(\theta_{s(e)}-\theta_{t(e)})}\zeta_e,\qquad D_\theta:=\operatorname{diag}_{x\in X}(e^{i\theta_x}I_r)\in GL_d(\mathbb C). $$
Define the link-hopping matrix $V(\zeta)\in M_d(\mathbb C)$ by its $x,y$ block indexed by $x,y\in X$
$$ V(\zeta)_{xy}:=\sum_{\substack{e\in E\\s(e)=x,\ t(e)=y}}T_e\zeta_e . $$
An empty sum is the zero $r\times r$ matrix. Additional fixed diagonal blocks belong to a separate base matrix. These data are finite-dimensional algebraic data; the phases are external parameters, not rotor multiplication operators on $L^2(\mathbb T^E)$.

The graph action uses the dimensionless phase angle $\theta$ as an independent external parameter. It does not choose an embedding of $G=(X,E,s,t)$ into spacetime or assert a continuum limit.

items.title: Finite Grassmann algebra and top-coefficient integral
items.statement:
Let $R$ be a commutative unital $\mathbb C$-algebra and let $d\ge1$. Let $\Lambda_d(R)$ be the exterior algebra over $R$ on $2d$ distinct generators $\psi_1,\ldots,\psi_d,\bar\psi_1,\ldots,\bar\psi_d$. Thus every pair of generators anticommutes, each generator squares to zero, and coefficients from $R$ commute with every generator. The bar is part of a generator's name; no complex-conjugation relation is imposed.

Order the generators as $\bar\psi_1,\ldots,\bar\psi_d,\psi_1,\ldots,\psi_d$. The corresponding ordered monomials form the $R$-basis of $\Lambda_d(R)$. Let
$$ M_d:=\bar\psi_1\cdots\bar\psi_d\psi_1\cdots\psi_d $$
and let $[M_d]P\in R$ denote the coefficient of $M_d$ in $P\in\Lambda_d(R)$. Define the finite Grassmann integral by the $R$-linear functional
$$ \mathcal I_d(P):=(-1)^{d(d+1)/2}[M_d]P . $$
For $K\in M_d(R)$, put $B_K:=\sum_{i,j=1}^d\bar\psi_iK_{ij}\psi_j$. Since every monomial of degree greater than $2d$ vanishes, its exponential is the finite sum
$$ \exp(-B_K):=\sum_{n=0}^{d}\frac{(-B_K)^n}{n!}. $$
The sign factor in $\mathcal I_d$ is the chosen normalization. Its Gaussian determinant identity, including the value at $K=I_d$, is proved separately.

items.title: Free transverse-photon energy multiplier
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice [[def-countable-choice]]. Use the transverse space $\mathcal H_T=\operatorname{Ran}M_{P_T}$ of [[def-qft-photon-transverse-space]], with $P_T(\mathbf k)=I_3-\mathbf n\mathbf n^T$ for $\mathbf k\ne0$ and any assigned value at the null point $\mathbf k=0$. In the QFT length convention, assign $\mathbf k$ units m$^{-1}$ and define the nonnegative measurable multiplier
$$ \omega(\mathbf k):=|\mathbf k|. $$
Its maximal multiplication operator on $\mathcal H_T$ is
$$ (M_\omega f)(\mathbf k):=\omega(\mathbf k)f(\mathbf k),\qquad D(M_\omega):=\{f\in\mathcal H_T:\omega f\in L^2(\mathbb R^3,d^3\mathbf k;\mathbb C^3)\}. $$
Because $\omega$ is a scalar multiplier, $\mathbf k\cdot f(\mathbf k)=0$ a.e. implies $\mathbf k\cdot(M_\omega f)(\mathbf k)=0$ a.e.; thus the displayed multiplication maps its stated domain into $\mathcal H_T$. The value $\omega(0)=0$ is immaterial to the $L^2$ operator. For $\hbar,c>0$, the corresponding one-particle energy convention is $E_1:=\hbar c M_\omega$, in joules.

items.title: Finite matrix formal kernel and inverse series
items.statement:
For a formal indeterminate $z$, let $\mathbb C\llbracket z\rrbracket$ be the commutative ring of sequences $(a_0,a_1,\ldots)$ written $\sum_{n\ge0}a_nz^n$, with coefficientwise addition and Cauchy-product multiplication. No convergence of a numerical series is part of this definition. For $d\ge1$, matrices over $\mathbb C\llbracket z\rrbracket$ use the usual finite matrix addition and multiplication.

Use the finite graph phase data of [[def-qft-qed-finite-graph-gauge-data]] and the QED $U(1)$, Clifford, and natural-unit conventions of [[def-qft-qed-gauge-data]]. Let $K_0(\zeta)\in GL_d(\mathbb C)$ be an invertible base matrix and let $V(\zeta)\in M_d(\mathbb C)$ be its finite link-hopping matrix. The admissible covariant families satisfy
$$ K_0(\zeta^\theta)=D_\theta K_0(\zeta)D_\theta^{-1},\qquad V(\zeta^\theta)=D_\theta V(\zeta)D_\theta^{-1}. $$
The scalar base $K_0=mI_d$, $m\in\mathbb C\setminus\{0\}$, is an explicit admissible case. Define
$$ K(z;\zeta):=K_0(\zeta)+zV(\zeta),\qquad S(z;\zeta):=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}(-zK_0(\zeta)^{-1}V(\zeta))^nK_0(\zeta)^{-1}. $$
The coefficient of each power $z^n$ in $S$ is one finite matrix. The item defines this formal candidate; the following lemma proves its two-sided inverse and covariance properties. Define $\det A$ for a finite matrix $A$ over $\mathbb C\llbracket z\rrbracket$ by the Leibniz formula $\det A=\sum_{\sigma\in S_d}\operatorname{sgn}(\sigma)\prod_{j=1}^d A_{j,\sigma(j)}$.

items.title: Logarithmic coherent infrared tail: finite energy, no Fock limit
items.statement:
Use the transverse one-particle space $\mathcal H_T$ and multiplier $\omega(\mathbf k)$ of [[def-qft-qed-photon-energy-multiplier]], and form its symmetric Fock space $\mathcal F_s(\mathcal H_T)$. Let $H_{\rm ph}:=\hbar c\,d\Gamma(\omega)$, with $\hbar,c>0$ and $d\Gamma(\omega)$ acting on the $n$-particle sector as multiplication by $\sum_{j=1}^n|\mathbf k_j|$, as in [[lem-qft-second-quantized-spectrum]]. For a coherent vector use
$$ \epsilon(f):=\bigoplus_{n=0}^{\infty}\frac{f^{\otimes n}}{\sqrt{n!}},\qquad C(f):=e^{-\|f\|^2/2}\epsilon(f), $$
using the tensor and direct-sum conventions of [[def-qft-fock-and-test-spaces]].

Let $\kappa>0$. Let $b:S^2\to\mathbb C^3$ be measurable with $b\in L^2(S^2,d\Omega;\mathbb C^3)$, $\mathbf n\cdot b(\mathbf n)=0$ for a.e. $\mathbf n$, and
$$ C_b:=\int_{S^2}|b(\mathbf n)|^2\,d\Omega>0. $$
Take $\mathbf k,\kappa,\epsilon$ in inverse metres and $b$ dimensionless; then $f_\epsilon$ has momentum-wavefunction units $\mathrm m^{3/2}$, $C_b$ is dimensionless, and $\hbar c(\kappa-\epsilon)$ has energy units.
For $0<\epsilon<\kappa$, define $f_\epsilon(0)=0$ and
$$ f_\epsilon(\mathbf k):=\mathbf1_{\{\epsilon<|\mathbf k|<\kappa\}}|\mathbf k|^{-3/2}b\!\left(\frac{\mathbf k}{|\mathbf k|}\right). $$
Then
$$ \|f_\epsilon\|^2=C_b\log\frac{\kappa}{\epsilon},\qquad \langle C(f_\epsilon),H_{\rm ph}C(f_\epsilon)\rangle =\hbar c\,C_b(\kappa-\epsilon). $$
Each $C(f_\epsilon)$ is a unit vector in $D(H_{\rm ph})$. As $\epsilon\downarrow0$, $C(f_\epsilon)\rightharpoonup0$ weakly, but the family has no strong Fock-space limit. The statement is an exact free transverse-mode construction; it asserts no interacting charged sector, continuum QED limit, or empirical observation.

items.title: Finite/formal gauge covariance and matrix Ward identity
items.statement:
Let $K(z;\zeta)=K_0(\zeta)+zV(\zeta)$ and $S(z;\zeta)$ be the finite-dimensional formal matrices of [[def-qft-qed-formal-ring]], with $d\ge1$, $K_0(\zeta)$ invertible, and both coefficient matrices covariant under the vertex phase angles of [[def-qft-qed-finite-graph-gauge-data]]. Then $S$ is a two-sided inverse of $K$ in $M_d(\mathbb C\llbracket z\rrbracket)$, and
$$ S(z;\zeta^\theta)=D_\theta S(z;\zeta)D_\theta^{-1} $$
coefficientwise. For a real vertex tuple $\theta$, put
$\Theta:=\operatorname{diag}_{x\in X}(\theta_xI_r)$,
$\zeta_s:=\zeta^{s\theta}$, and $D_s:=D_{s\theta}=e^{is\Theta}$.
Write $K_s:=K(z;\zeta_s)$ and $S_s:=S(z;\zeta_s)$, and define
$\delta K:=\left.\frac{d}{ds}K_s\right|_{s=0}$ and
$\delta S:=\left.\frac{d}{ds}S_s\right|_{s=0}$ coefficientwise along this
differentiable phase path. The variations satisfy
$$ \delta K=i[\Theta,K],\qquad \delta S=i[\Theta,S]=-S(\delta K)S . $$
For ordinary finite matrices $A,B\in GL_d(\mathbb C)$, the corresponding resolvent identity is $B^{-1}(B-A)A^{-1}=A^{-1}-B^{-1}$. These are formal or finite algebraic statements; they assert no convergence of a perturbation series, continuum limit, or loop Ward identity.

items.title: Off-shell free Dirac Ward telescoping and tree currents
items.statement:
Use the $(-+++)$ coordinate convention, $h=-\eta=\operatorname{diag}(1,-1,-1,-1)$, and the Clifford matrices of [[def-qft-dirac-projections]]; the shell parameter $\mu>0$ has inverse-length units as in [[def-qft-scalar-mass-shell]]. For $p=(p^0,\mathbf p)\in\mathbb R^4$, write
$$ \Gamma(p):=\gamma^0p^0-\sum_{j=1}^3\gamma^jp_j,\qquad K(p):=\Gamma(p)-\mu I_4. $$
When $h(p,p)\ne\mu^2$, define the finite rational inverse
$$ S_0(p):=\frac{\Gamma(p)+\mu I_4}{h(p,p)-\mu^2}. $$
For $p,p+k$ with both denominators nonzero,
$$ S_0(p+k)\Gamma(k)S_0(p)=S_0(p)-S_0(p+k). $$
For any finite chain of off-shell momenta, the corresponding insertion differences telescope with both endpoint terms retained. If $u(p),u(p')$ satisfy $(\Gamma(p)-\mu)u(p)=0$, $(\Gamma(p')-\mu)u(p')=0$ and $p,p'$ lie on the future shell, then $\bar u(p')\Gamma(p-p')u(p)=0$, where $\bar u=u^\dagger\beta$. If $v(q)$ satisfies $(\Gamma(q)+\mu)v(q)=0$ on the future shell, then $\bar v(q)\Gamma(p+q)u(p)=0$. These are finite rational/tree identities; no Feynman boundary value, singular distribution product, loop theorem, or all-diagram gauge-independence claim is included.

items.title: Finite Grassmann Gaussian and gauge-invariant determinant
items.statement:
Let $R=\mathbb C\llbracket z\rrbracket$, let $d\ge1$, and let $K\in M_d(R)$ be a finite matrix as in [[def-qft-qed-formal-ring]]. With $\mathcal I_d$ the top-coefficient functional of [[def-qft-qed-finite-grassmann-algebra]],
$$ \mathcal I_d\!\left(\exp\!\left(-\sum_{i,j=1}^d\bar\psi_iK_{ij}\psi_j\right)\right)=\det K. $$
If $D=\operatorname{diag}(u_1,\ldots,u_d)$ with each $u_i\in R^\times$ and $K'=DKD^{-1}$, then the finite Grassmann integral and determinant are gauge invariant: $\mathcal I_d(\exp(-\bar\psi K'\psi))=\det K'=\det K$. No infinite-dimensional Grassmann measure, continuum limit, or anomaly claim is made.

items.title: Gauge-longitudinal kernel decoupling for explicit tree currents
items.statement:
Let $p_1,p_1',p_2,p_2'$ be future-shell momenta for the same $\mu>0$ convention as [[lem-qft-qed-tree-ward]], and suppose $k=p_1-p_1'=p_2'-p_2$. Define
$$ J_1^\mu:= ar u(p_1')\gamma^\mu u(p_1),\qquad J_2^
u:= ar u(p_2')\gamma^
u u(p_2), $$
with the on-shell Dirac equations in [[lem-qft-qed-tree-ward]]. If a finite rational covariant-gauge kernel changes by $\Delta D_{\mu
u}(k)=c(k)k_\mu k_
u$, where $c(k)\in\mathbb C$ is finite at the chosen $k$, then
$$ J_1^\mu\Delta D_{\mu
u}(k)J_2^
u=0. $$
Likewise, for any conserved tree current $J^\mu$ of the forms proved in [[lem-qft-qed-tree-ward]], the contraction $\epsilon_\mu J^\mu$ is unchanged by $\epsilon^\mu\mapsto\epsilon^\mu+\alpha k^\mu$. These statements concern only the displayed finite tree-current contractions; they assert no gauge independence for arbitrary loop diagrams or renormalization schemes.

items.title: Two-body phase-space and formal coefficient data
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice [[def-countable-choice]] and use the energy-vector, metric, and unit conventions of [[def-qft-example-data]]. A rest-energy parameter $\mathsf M\geq0$ is measured in joules. Its positive shell is parameterized by $p=(E,\mathbf p)$ with $E=\sqrt{|\mathbf p|^2+\mathsf M^2}>0$; the shell measure is $d\nu_{\mathsf M}=d^3\mathbf p/((2\pi)^3\,2E)$. The value $\mathsf M=0$, $\mathbf p=0$ is excluded.

Let $\mathsf M_1,\mathsf M_2\geq0$ and let $s>(\mathsf M_1+\mathsf M_2)^2$. Define
$$k_*=\frac{\sqrt{[s-(\mathsf M_1+\mathsf M_2)^2][s-(\mathsf M_1-\mathsf M_2)^2]}}{2\sqrt{s}}, \qquad E_i^*=\sqrt{k_*^2+\mathsf M_i^2}.$$
Both factors under the square root are positive, so $k_*>0$. On the Euclidean unit sphere $S^2$, let $d\Omega$ be the chart surface measure of [[lem-euclidean-chart-measure-agrees-with-polar-surface-measure]]. The center-of-momentum two-body phase-space measure is the finite Borel measure
$$d\Phi_2=\frac{k_*}{16\pi^2\sqrt{s}}\,d\Omega, \qquad \mathbf n\longmapsto ((E_1^*,k_*\mathbf n),(E_2^*,-k_*\mathbf n)).$$

For future energy four-vectors $p_1,p_2$ with nonnegative rest energies $\mathsf M_{1,\mathrm{in}},\mathsf M_{2,\mathrm{in}}\geq0$, define the invariant flux when its radicand is nonnegative by
$$F(p_1,p_2)=4\sqrt{(p_1\cdot p_2)^2-\mathsf M_{1,\mathrm{in}}^2\mathsf M_{2,\mathrm{in}}^2}, \qquad p\cdot q=h(p,q).$$
Let $\mathcal S_{\rm in}$ and $\mathcal S_{\rm out}$ be finite nonempty initial and final label sets, respectively, and let $w_i\geq0$ for $i\in\mathcal S_{\rm in}$ satisfy $\sum_iw_i=1$. A spin-resolved formal amplitude is a family of dimensionless Borel functions $\mathcal A_{if}:S^2\to\mathbb C$, indexed by $i\in\mathcal S_{\rm in}$ and $f\in\mathcal S_{\rm out}$. Define the Borel function
$$\overline{|\mathcal A(\mathbf n)|^2}:=\sum_{i\in\mathcal S_{\rm in}}w_i\sum_{f\in\mathcal S_{\rm out}}|\mathcal A_{if}(\mathbf n)|^2.$$
For a final pair, set $S_f=2$ when the two final particles are identical and $S_f=1$ when they are distinguishable. When the incoming flux is positive, $F>0$, define the center-of-momentum differential cross-section coefficient measure by
$$d\sigma_{\mathrm{coeff}}=\frac{(\hbar c)^2}{F S_f}\, \overline{|\mathcal A(\mathbf n)|^2}\,d\Phi_2.$$
For a parent at rest with energy $\mathsf M_0>0$ and a specified single-channel Borel formal decay amplitude $\mathcal G:S^2\to\mathbb C$ measured in joules, define the extended nonnegative coefficient
$$\Gamma_{\mathrm{coeff}}=\frac{1}{2\hbar\mathsf M_0 S_f} \int_{S^2}|\mathcal G(\mathbf n)|^2\,d\Phi_2.$$
It is a finite rate coefficient when this integral is finite; otherwise the displayed integral has value $+\infty$.
These are mathematical coefficient maps for the explicitly specified formal amplitudes; their definitions assert no exact interacting scattering operator or decay law.

items.title: Clifford traces and normalized spin completeness
items.statement:
Use the finite Dirac matrices and adjoint of [[def-qft-dirac-projections]], and the separate geometric metric $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$ and algebraic contraction $h=-\eta=\operatorname{diag}(1,-1,-1,-1)$ of [[def-qft-example-data]]. Write $p=(E,\mathbf p)$ for an energy four-vector with components in joules, $M\geq0$ for a rest-energy parameter in joules, and $E=\sqrt{|\mathbf p|^2+M^2}>0$. In the natural-length variables of the Dirac definition, $\mathbf k=\mathbf p/(\hbar c)$, $\mu=M/(\hbar c)$, and $\omega=E/(\hbar c)$.

Let $\beta=\gamma^0$, $\alpha_j=\beta\gamma^j$, $\Sigma_j=\operatorname{diag}(\sigma_j,\sigma_j)$, and $\gamma_5=i\gamma^0\gamma^1\gamma^2\gamma^3$. Define $H_\pm=\boldsymbol\alpha\cdot\mathbf p\pm\beta M$ and $P_\pm=(I_4+H_\pm/E)/2$. Each $P_\pm$ is a Hermitian rank-two projection. Choose orthonormal bases $\xi_{\pm,1},\xi_{\pm,2}$ of their ranges and put $u_s=\sqrt{2E}\xi_{+,s}$ and $v_s=\sqrt{2E}\xi_{-,s}$ for $s=1,2$. With $\bar z=z^\dagger\beta$ and $\not p=\gamma^0E-\sum_j\gamma^jp_j$, the following hold:

$$\operatorname{Tr}I_4=4,\quad \operatorname{Tr}\gamma^a=0,\quad \operatorname{Tr}(\gamma^a\gamma^b)=4h^{ab},\quad \operatorname{Tr}(\gamma^a\gamma^b\gamma^c)=0,$$

$$\operatorname{Tr}(\gamma^a\gamma^b\gamma^c\gamma^d) =4(h^{ab}h^{cd}-h^{ac}h^{bd}+h^{ad}h^{bc}), \qquad \sum_s u_s\bar u_s=\not p+M,\quad \sum_s v_s\bar v_s=\not p-M.$$

The columns satisfy $(\not p-M)u_s=0$ and $(\not p+M)v_s=0$. For all $x,y\in\mathbb C^4$, complex conjugation of a Dirac current is $\overline{\bar x\gamma^a y}=\bar y\gamma^a x$. The Countable Choice hypothesis written in the current draft [[def-qft-dirac-projections]] is retained as a supplier assumption; this finite-dimensional proof makes no additional choice use.

items.title: Complete two-body phase space and coefficient flux map
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice [[def-countable-choice]], and use [[def-qft-example-data]] and [[def-qft-example-two-body-phase-space-data]]. Write
$$\mathcal H^+_{\mathsf M}=\{(E,\mathbf q)\in(0,\infty)\times\mathbb R^3:E=\sqrt{|\mathbf q|^2+\mathsf M^2}\}$$
for the positive shell in that Definition, and $C_+=\{(E,\mathbf q)\in\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^3:E\geq|\mathbf q|\}$ for the closed future cone of $h=(+,-,-,-)$. A proper orthochronous linear $h$-Lorentz map is a real linear $\Lambda$ with $\Lambda^Th\Lambda=h$, $\det\Lambda=1$, and $\Lambda(C_+)=C_+$. For energy four-vectors on these positive shells, the shell measure $d^3\mathbf p/((2\pi)^3\,2E)$ is invariant under every such map. Let $\mathsf M_1,\mathsf M_2\geq0$, let $P$ be future timelike, meaning $P^0>0$ and $h(P,P)>0$, set $s=h(P,P)>(\mathsf M_1+\mathsf M_2)^2$, and write $E_i(r)=\sqrt{r^2+\mathsf M_i^2}$. Let $f$ be a nonnegative Borel function on $\mathcal H^+_{\mathsf M_1}\times\mathcal H^+_{\mathsf M_2}$. For a proper orthochronous $h$-Lorentz map $\Lambda_P$ with $\Lambda_P P=(\sqrt{s},\mathbf0)$, define the finite Borel measure $\Phi_{2,P}$ as the pushforward of $\frac{k_*}{16\pi^2\sqrt{s}}d\Omega$ under
$$\mathbf n\longmapsto\left(\Lambda_P^{-1}(E_1^*,k_*\mathbf n),\Lambda_P^{-1}(E_2^*,-k_*\mathbf n)\right),$$
where $E_i^*$ and $k_*$ are from [[def-qft-example-two-body-phase-space-data]]. The proof below shows that $\Phi_{2,P}$ is independent of the choice of $\Lambda_P$; for $P=(\sqrt{s},\mathbf0)$ it is exactly the center-of-momentum measure $d\Phi_2$ in that Definition. The standard two-body on-shell integral
$$(2\pi)^4\int d\nu_{\mathsf M_1}(k_1)d\nu_{\mathsf M_2}(k_2)\, \delta^{(4)}(P-k_1-k_2)\,f(k_1,k_2)$$
is interpreted by first evaluating the spatial delta in $k_2$, then the one-dimensional energy delta by the increasing radial change of variable $r\mapsto E_1(r)+E_2(r)$. Explicitly, for each fixed angular direction and nonnegative Borel radial function $g:(0,\infty)\to[0,\infty]$, the radial action after spatial evaluation is $\int_0^\infty g(r)\delta(\sqrt{s}-E_1(r)-E_2(r))\,dr=g(k_*)/(d(E_1+E_2)/dr|_{k_*})$; this is the pushforward evaluation under that $C^1$ diffeomorphism, not a product of distributions. It equals $\int f\,d\Phi_{2,P}$. The threshold root is $k_*$ in that Definition, and
$$\int d\Phi_{2,P}=\int d\Phi_2=\frac{k_*}{4\pi\sqrt{s}}.$$
For equal rest energies $\mathsf M_1=\mathsf M_2=\mathsf M$, set $\beta=\sqrt{1-4\mathsf M^2/s}$; then $k_*=\sqrt{s}\beta/2$ and $\int d\Phi_{2,P}=\int d\Phi_2=\beta/(8\pi)$. For the scattering flux identities, take incoming $p_i=(E_i,\mathbf p_i)\in\mathcal H^+_{\mathsf M_{i,\mathrm{in}}}$, where $\mathsf M_{i,\mathrm{in}}\geq0$, and require $p_1+p_2=P$. A center-of-momentum map is a proper orthochronous $h$-Lorentz map $\Lambda$ with $\Lambda P=(\sqrt{s},\mathbf0)$; write $\Lambda p_1=(E_1^*,\mathbf p_1^*)$ and define $p_*=|\mathbf p_1^*|$. The value is independent of the choice of $\Lambda$, since two such maps differ by a spatial rotation. Their invariant flux is $F=4p_*\sqrt{s}$. For equal incoming rest energies $\mathsf M_{\mathrm{in}}\geq0$ with $s\geq4\mathsf M_{\mathrm{in}}^2$, define $\beta_{\mathrm{in}}=\sqrt{1-4\mathsf M_{\mathrm{in}}^2/s}$; then $p_*=\sqrt{s}\beta_{\mathrm{in}}/2$ and $F=2s\beta_{\mathrm{in}}$. For finite nonempty incoming and outgoing label sets, normalized initial weights, and the Borel amplitude family of the Definition, whenever $F>0$ the cross-section coefficient map gives
$$\frac{d\sigma_{\mathrm{coeff}}}{d\Omega} =\frac{(\hbar c)^2}{64\pi^2s}\, \frac{k_*}{p_*}\, \frac{\overline{|\mathcal A|^2}}{S_f}.$$
For a parent at rest, represented by $P_0=(\mathsf M_0,\mathbf0)$ with $\mathsf M_0>2\mathsf M$, and two equal-rest-energy daughters on $\mathcal H^+_{\mathsf M}$ with total four-vector $P_0$ and constant amplitude $G_E$ in joules, the rate coefficient is $|G_E|^2\sqrt{1-4\mathsf M^2/\mathsf M_0^2}/(32\pi\hbar\mathsf M_0)$ when the daughters are identical. This is a coefficient calculation, not a claim of exponential survival.

items.title: Full-mass unpolarized formal pair-production coefficient
items.statement:
Let $m,M\geq0$ be the electron and muon rest energies in joules. Use the positive shells of [[def-qft-example-two-body-phase-space-data]]: $p_i=(E_i,\mathbf p_i)$ with $E_i=\sqrt{|\mathbf p_i|^2+m^2}>0$ for $i=1,2$, and $k_i=(\varepsilon_i,\mathbf k_i)$ with $\varepsilon_i=\sqrt{|\mathbf k_i|^2+M^2}>0$ for $i=1,2$. With $p_1+p_2=k_1+k_2=P$, set $s=h(P,P)>4\max(m^2,M^2)$, using the algebraic metric $h=(+,-,-,-)$ of [[def-qft-example-data]]. Since $P^0=E_1+E_2>0$ and $h(P,P)=s>0$, $P$ is future timelike. A center-of-momentum map is a proper orthochronous linear $h$-Lorentz map $\Lambda$ with $\Lambda^Th\Lambda=h$, $\det\Lambda=1$, $\Lambda(C_+)=C_+$ for $C_+=\{(E,\mathbf q)\in\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^3:E\geq|\mathbf q|\}$, and $\Lambda P=(\sqrt{s},\mathbf0)$. Write $\mathbf p_1^*$ and $\mathbf k_1^*$ for the spatial components of $\Lambda p_1$ and $\Lambda k_1$, respectively. The strict threshold makes both nonzero; define $\theta\in[0,\pi]$ by $\cos\theta=(\mathbf p_1^*\cdot_{\mathbb R^3}\mathbf k_1^*)/(|\mathbf p_1^*||\mathbf k_1^*|)$. This angle is independent of the chosen center-of-momentum map because any two choices differ by a spatial rotation. Use the dimensionless coupling $g=\sqrt{4\pi\alpha}$ from [[def-qft-example-data]]. Adopt only the formal single-photon tree coefficient
$$\mathcal M=\frac{g^2}{s} [\bar v(p_2)\gamma^a u(p_1)] [\bar u(k_1)\gamma_a v(k_2)],$$
with equal weight $1/4$ on the four initial spin-label pairs and a sum over final spin labels. No interacting continuum $S$-matrix or exact QED cross section is assumed.

In the auxiliary finite-matrix setting of [L1], assume $d\geq1$, an invertible $K_0$, and the stated covariance of $K_0$ and $V$ under the finite-graph phase action; then the coefficientwise inverse and covariance identities in [L1] hold. Separately stipulate the displayed formal pair-production amplitude above. Its on-shell spin average is
$$\overline{|\mathcal M|^2} =g^4[3-\beta_e^2-\beta_\mu^2 +\beta_e^2\beta_\mu^2\cos^2\theta], \qquad \beta_e=\sqrt{1-\frac{4m^2}{s}}, \quad \beta_\mu=\sqrt{1-\frac{4M^2}{s}},$$
where the angle $\theta$ is defined above. The resulting formal differential and total coefficients are
$$\frac{d\sigma_{\mathrm{coeff}}}{d\Omega} =\frac{\alpha^2(\hbar c)^2\beta_\mu}{4s\beta_e} [3-\beta_e^2-\beta_\mu^2+\beta_e^2\beta_\mu^2\cos^2\theta],$$
$$\sigma_{\mathrm{coeff}} =\frac{\pi\alpha^2(\hbar c)^2}{s}\frac{\beta_\mu}{\beta_e} [3-\beta_e^2-\beta_\mu^2+\tfrac13\beta_e^2\beta_\mu^2].$$
If $\delta=4m^2/s\leq1/2$, the full differential coefficient divided by its $m=0$ value is between $1$ and $1+4\delta$. This bound concerns only omission of the incoming electron mass in this formal tree coefficient, not loop, soft-radiation, threshold, or empirical errors.

The same on-shell equations give $P_a\bar v(p_2)\gamma^a u(p_1)=0$ and $P_a\bar u(k_1)\gamma^a v(k_2)=0$. Thus a propagator term proportional to $P_aP_b$ does not change this specified tree coefficient. These current cancellations are proved locally for all $m,M\geq0$; the actual QFT-MG03 matrix-Ward carrier supplies only its finite-matrix inverse and covariance interface, not the broader tree-current clauses in the historical Q7 research module.

items.title: Scalar symmetry factors and decay coefficient units
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice, $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ [[def-countable-choice]], as required by the phase-space and coefficient-map suppliers used below.

Let $m\geq0$ be a scalar rest energy in joules, and let $p_1,p_2,k_1,k_2$ be the incoming and outgoing scattering vectors on the positive $m$-shell of [[def-qft-example-two-body-phase-space-data]], so each $(E,\mathbf q)$ satisfies $E=\sqrt{|\mathbf q|^2+m^2}>0$. Require $p_1+p_2=k_1+k_2=P$ and $s=h(P,P)>4m^2$, with $h$ as in [[def-qft-example-data]]. Evaluate the coefficient map in a center-of-momentum frame $\Lambda P=(\sqrt{s},\mathbf0)$ as defined in [[lem-qft-example-two-body-phase-space]]. For one scalar initial label of weight $1$ and one specified final channel, take the dimensionless real quartic tree amplitude $\mathcal A=-\lambda$. The coefficient map of [[lem-qft-example-two-body-phase-space]] gives
$$\frac{d\sigma_{\mathrm{coeff}}}{d\Omega} =\frac{\lambda^2(\hbar c)^2}{128\pi^2s}, \qquad \sigma_{\mathrm{coeff}}=\frac{\lambda^2(\hbar c)^2}{32\pi s}$$
for identical final scalars integrated over the full labeled sphere. For distinguishable final scalars the two coefficients are twice these values.

For a parent at rest, $P_0=(\mathsf M_0,\mathbf0)$ with energy $\mathsf M_0>2m$, decaying through a specified single channel to two identical scalars on the positive $m$-shell whose total four-vector is $P_0$, under a constant amplitude $G_E$ in joules, the rate coefficient is
$$\Gamma_{\mathrm{coeff}} =\frac{|G_E|^2}{32\pi\hbar\mathsf M_0} \sqrt{1-\frac{4m^2}{\mathsf M_0^2}}.$$
This result concerns the defined formal coefficients. It does not assert an exact exponential survival law.

items.title: Minimal Dirac magnetic square and formal Pauli benchmark
items.statement:
Let $m>0$ be a particle mass in kilograms, $q\in\mathbb R$ its charge in coulombs, and $A:\mathbb R^3\to\mathbb R^3$ a smooth spatial vector potential with components in tesla-metres. Use standard Cartesian coordinates $x_i$ measured in metres and write $\partial_i:=\partial/\partial x_i$. Let $\epsilon_{ijk}$ be the alternating symbol with $\epsilon_{123}=1$, and sum repeated spatial indices from $1$ to $3$. Define $B_k(x)=\epsilon_{kij}\partial_iA_j(x)$ and $\mathbf B=(B_1,B_2,B_3):\mathbb R^3\to\mathbb R^3$; its smooth components are in tesla.

Let $\mathcal C=C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C^4)$ be the common invariant test domain. In this item, “common core” refers only to this shared domain of the displayed differential expressions; no operator-theoretic core property for a closure is asserted. Define the dimensionless finite matrices
$$\sigma_1=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad \sigma_2=\begin{pmatrix}0&-i\\i&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad \sigma_3=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&-1\end{pmatrix},$$
$$\beta=\begin{pmatrix}I_2&0\\0&-I_2\end{pmatrix},\qquad \alpha_i=\begin{pmatrix}0&\sigma_i\\\sigma_i&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad \Sigma_i=\operatorname{diag}(\sigma_i,\sigma_i),$$
and use $\hbar,c$ of [[def-qft-example-data]]. On $\mathcal C$, define
$$\pi_i\psi=-i\hbar\partial_i\psi-qA_i\psi,\qquad H_D\psi=c\sum_{i=1}^3\alpha_i\pi_i\psi+\beta mc^2\psi.$$
These maps preserve $\mathcal C$. The components $\pi_i$ have units $\mathrm{kg\,m\,s^{-1}}$ and $H_D$ has units joules. Define the operator expressions
$$\boldsymbol\pi^2\psi:=\sum_{i=1}^3\pi_i(\pi_i\psi),\qquad (\boldsymbol\Sigma\cdot\mathbf B)\psi:=\sum_{i=1}^3\Sigma_iB_i\psi.$$
Here $[\pi_i,\pi_j]:=\pi_i\circ\pi_j-\pi_j\circ\pi_i$, and $H_D^2$ denotes composition on $\mathcal C$. On $\mathcal C$, the identities are
$$[\pi_i,\pi_j]=iq\hbar\epsilon_{ijk}B_k,\qquad H_D^2=m^2c^4I_4+c^2(\boldsymbol\pi^2-q\hbar\boldsymbol\Sigma\cdot\mathbf B).$$
The operator $K:=\boldsymbol\pi^2-q\hbar\boldsymbol\Sigma\cdot\mathbf B$ maps $\mathcal C$ to itself and has units $(\mathrm{kg\,m\,s^{-1}})^2$.

For commuting formal indeterminates $t,X$ over $\mathbb R$, define the first-order square-root coefficient $a$ by
$$(mc^2+taX)^2\equiv m^2c^4+tc^2X\pmod{t^2}.$$
Comparing the coefficient of $tX$ gives $a=1/(2m)$; substituting $K$ for $X$ gives the formal first-degree correction $K/(2m)$, with no operator square-root assertion. Its spin term is $-(q/m)\mathbf S\cdot\mathbf B$, where $S_i=\hbar\Sigma_i/2$, $\mathbf S=(S_1,S_2,S_3)$, and $(\mathbf S\cdot\mathbf B)\psi:=\sum_{i=1}^3S_iB_i\psi$. The magnetic-moment dot product below uses the same componentwise sum convention.

Under the coefficient convention $H_{\mathrm{mag}}=-\boldsymbol\mu_{\mathrm{mag}}\cdot\mathbf B$ and $\boldsymbol\mu_{\mathrm{mag}}=g_s(q/(2m))\mathbf S$, equality of the formal coefficients as a linear function of $q$ gives $g_s=2$ for the minimal tree-level term. Here $H_{\mathrm{mag}}$ has units joules and $\boldsymbol\mu_{\mathrm{mag}}$ has units $\mathrm{A\,m^2}$. No magnetic self-adjoint closure, full spectrum, operator square-root theorem, radiative correction, or empirical prediction is asserted.

items.title: Four-dimensional radial measure from two polar planes
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. For every radius $R>0$ and every
nonnegative Borel function $\varphi:[0,R]\to[0,\infty]$, with extended
Lebesgue integrals and the convention $0\cdot\infty=0$,
$$ \int_{\{x\in\mathbb R^4:\ |x|\le R\}}\varphi(|x|)\,d\lambda_4(x) =2\pi^2\int_0^R\varphi(r)r^3\,dr. $$
In particular, the radial Jacobian and angular factor on a four-dimensional
ball are $r^3$ and $2\pi^2$, respectively.

items.title: Finite UV subtraction and a divergent factorial toy series
items.statement:
Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ and the unit convention of
[[def-qft-example-data]]. Let $\mu,\Lambda,\mu_R>0$ have units
$\mathrm m^{-1}$. For $k\in\mathbb R^4$, $|k|$ is the Euclidean norm and
$\log$ is the natural logarithm. Define the cutoff integral
$$ I_\Lambda=\int_{|k|\le\Lambda} \frac{d^4k}{(2\pi)^4(|k|^2+\mu^2)}. $$
Each term in the subtracted expression has units $\mathrm m^{-2}$.
Then
$$ I_\Lambda= \frac{\Lambda^2-\mu^2\log(1+\Lambda^2/\mu^2)}{16\pi^2}, $$
and the explicitly chosen subtraction has the finite limit
$$ \lim_{\Lambda\to\infty} \left(I_\Lambda-\frac{\Lambda^2}{16\pi^2} +\frac{\mu^2}{16\pi^2}\log\frac{\Lambda^2}{\mu_R^2}\right) =\frac{\mu^2}{16\pi^2}\log\frac{\mu^2}{\mu_R^2}. $$
Separately, let $x\ge0$ be dimensionless and let dimensionless $\lambda\ge0$:
$$ F(\lambda)=\int_0^\infty\frac{\exp(-x)}{1+\lambda x}\,dx. $$
For every integer $N\ge0$ the exact finite identity is
$$ F(\lambda)=\sum_{n=0}^{N}(-1)^n n!\lambda^n +(-1)^{N+1}\lambda^{N+1} \int_0^\infty\frac{\exp(-x)x^{N+1}}{1+\lambda x}\,dx. $$
The last integral is finite and bounded by $(N+1)!$. The resulting formal real
power series $\sum_{n\ge0}(-1)^n n!\lambda^n$ has radius of convergence zero,
using the definition in [[def-real-power-series-and-radius-of-convergence]].
The cutoff expression is one evaluated model integral and one chosen
subtraction scheme; it is not a full gauge-invariant QED renormalization
theorem or a continuum-existence claim.

items.title: Soft-current angular norm and exact cutoff coherent model
items.statement:
This is a conditional mathematical theorem about the prescribed current and
free coherent-state construction defined below, under the exact supplier
interfaces [F2] and [L1]. Here “soft current” is only a name for the displayed
rational function: no scattering-amplitude factorization or approximation
claim is made. The weak-zero and no-strong-limit conclusions are conditional
on [L1]; the projective-ray conclusion is proved separately in step 7.1.

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, the constants and conventions of
[[def-qft-example-data]], and that the two supplier interfaces [F2]
and [L1] hold exactly as stated below. Let $I$ be a finite, possibly empty,
set of leg labels. A leg $i\in I$ carries an energy $E_i>0$ in joules,
a dimensionless velocity $v_i=\mathbf v_{i,\rm phys}/c\in\mathbb R^3$ with
$\mathbf v_{i,\rm phys}$ in m s$^{-1}$ and
$|v_i|<1$, a dimensionless charge number $Q_i\in\mathbb R$ (physical charge
$eQ_i$ coulombs), and an orientation sign $\eta_i\in\{-1,1\}$, with
$\eta_i=-1$ for an incoming leg and $+1$ for an outgoing leg. Require charge
balance $\sum_{i\in I}\eta_iQ_i=0$. Use
$h=\operatorname{diag}(1,-1,-1,-1)$ and
$h(a,b)=a^0b^0-\mathbf a\cdot\mathbf b$ for algebraic four-vector
contractions. For $n\in S^2:=\{x\in\mathbb R^3:|x|=1\}$ and energy
$\omega>0$ in joules, put
$$ p_i=E_i(1,v_i),\qquad q=\omega(1,n),\qquad K:S^2\to\mathbb R^4,\quad K(n)=\sum_{i\in I}\eta_iQ_i\frac{(1,v_i)}{1-v_i\cdot n}. $$
Each $p_i$ has positive energy and
$h(p_i,p_i)=E_i^2(1-|v_i|^2)>0$; this timelike condition is the precise
meaning of “massive” here, with rest mass
$m_i=E_i\sqrt{1-|v_i|^2}/c^2>0$. The prescribed current is the function
$J(q)=\sum_{i\in I}\eta_iQ_i\,p_i/h(p_i,q)$ on
$\{\omega(1,n):\omega>0,\ n\in S^2\}$. Since
$h(p_i,q)=E_i\omega(1-v_i\cdot n)>0$, this equals $K(n)/\omega$.
Thus $K$ is dimensionless and $J(q)$ has units $\mathrm J^{-1}$.
Write $K(n)=(K^0(n),\mathbf K(n))$, let $P_T(n)=I-n\otimes n$, and
$K_\perp(n)=P_T(n)\mathbf K(n)$. Define $d\Omega$ as Euclidean chart
surface measure on $S^2$ and
$$ C=\frac{g^2}{2(2\pi)^3}\int_{S^2}|K_\perp(n)|^2\,d\Omega(n)\ge0. $$
Here $g>0$ is the dimensionless coupling of [[def-qft-example-data]] and
$\lambda,\Lambda$ are energy cutoffs in joules. Write $\mathbf q=\omega n$
for the spatial energy coordinate, distinct from the four-vector
$q=(\omega,\mathbf q)$ above. For $\mathbf q\ne0$, put $\omega=|\mathbf q|$
and $n=\mathbf q/|\mathbf q|$ and define
$$ h_\lambda(\mathbf q)=g\frac{K_\perp(n)}{\omega}\mathbf1_{\{\lambda<\omega<\Lambda\}},\qquad 0<\lambda<\Lambda; $$
Set $h_\lambda(0)=0$ and regard $h_\lambda$ as a function of $\mathbf q$.
Define
$\mathcal H_{E,T}:=\{h\in L^2(\mathbb R^3,d^3\mathbf q/[(2\pi)^3 2|\mathbf q|];\mathbb C^3):\mathbf q\cdot h(\mathbf q)=0\ {\rm a.e.}\}$,
with the componentwise Hermitian integral pairing linear in its second
variable. On this energy-coordinate transverse Hilbert space the exact norm is
$$ N_\lambda=\|h_\lambda\|^2=C\log(\Lambda/\lambda). $$
The energy-coordinate wavefunction has units $\mathrm J^{-1}$ and its
one-particle measure has units $\mathrm J^2$, so $N_\lambda$ and $C$ are
dimensionless; its value at $q=0$ is immaterial to this $L^2$ vector.
Under the canonical unitary $U:\mathcal H_{E,T}\to\mathcal H_T$ specified and proved in step 3.1,
the same vector is represented by the length-coordinate vector $f_\lambda$
defined as follows. Set $f_\lambda(0)=0$ and, for $k\ne0$, define
$$ f_\lambda(k)=\mathbf1_{\{\lambda/(\hbar c)<|k|<\Lambda/(\hbar c)\}} |k|^{-3/2}b(k/|k|),\qquad b(n)=\frac{gK_\perp(n)}{\sqrt{2(2\pi)^3}},\qquad \int_{S^2}|b|^2\,d\Omega=C. $$
Here $b$ is dimensionless and the $L^2(d^3k)$ wavefunction $f_\lambda$ has
units $\mathrm m^{3/2}$.
The normalized coherent vector
$\Psi_\lambda=W(-i\sqrt2 f_\lambda)\Omega
=\exp(-N_\lambda/2)\epsilon(f_\lambda)$ has squared norm in sector $m$
$$ s_m=\exp(-N_\lambda)\frac{N_\lambda^m}{m!},\qquad \sum_{m\ge0}s_m=1,\qquad \sum_{m\ge0}m s_m=N_\lambda, $$
with $N_\lambda^0=1$ also when $N_\lambda=0$.
These are Hilbert-space sector norms and their index sum; no measured
probability is asserted. For the free photon energy operator
$H_\gamma=\hbar c\,d\Gamma(|k|)$, $\Psi_\lambda$ is in its operator domain
and its quadratic expectation is $C(\Lambda-\lambda)$ joules.

If $C=0$, $f_\lambda=0$ almost everywhere and $\Psi_\lambda=\Omega$ for each
cutoff. If $C>0$, the exact hypotheses of the current [L1] hold with
$\epsilon=\lambda/(\hbar c)$, $\kappa=\Lambda/(\hbar c)$ and the displayed
nonzero transverse angular function $b$. Conditional on [L1], the family has
no strong Fock-vector limit and converges weakly to zero, while its free
energy expectation stays bounded. For a unit Fock vector $u$, define its
projective ray $[u]:=\{zu:z\in\mathbb C,\ |z|=1\}$. For unit vectors $u,v$
define their projective-ray distance by
$d([u],[v]):=\inf_{|z|=1}\|u-zv\|$. This is a metric on phase classes: symmetry follows by replacing $z$ with
$\overline z$, the triangle inequality follows from the norm triangle
inequality and phase invariance, and compactness of the unit circle makes zero
distance equivalent to equality of the classes. Projective convergence means convergence in this
distance, equivalently norm convergence to a fixed unit vector after allowing
a unit-modulus phase at each cutoff. Step 7.1 proves separately that
these rays have no projective limit, including after arbitrary phase choices. This is
not a result about full interacting QED, universal charged sectors,
detector-inclusive observables, or measured photon statistics.

items.title: Worked mathematical example B06 — a cutoff coherent soft state
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice, $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, as defined in
[[def-countable-choice]] and required by the measure and coherent-state suppliers.
Let the two-leg set be $I=\{\mathrm{in},\mathrm{out}\}$, with
$\eta_{\mathrm{in}}=-1$, $\eta_{\mathrm{out}}=+1$ and dimensionless charge
numbers $Q_{\mathrm{in}}=Q_{\mathrm{out}}=1$. Set the incoming dimensionless
velocity to $\mathbf v_{\mathrm{in}}=\mathbf0$ and the outgoing one to
$\mathbf v_{\mathrm{out}}=v\mathbf e_z$, where $\mathbf e_z=(0,0,1)$ and
$0<v<1$; take any positive incoming and outgoing energies. The coefficient
in [[thm-qft-example-soft-current-angular-coherent]] is
$$ C(v)=\frac{\alpha}{\pi} \left(\frac1v\log\frac{1+v}{1-v}-2\right)>0. $$
At $v=1/2$ this is
$C=(\alpha/\pi)(2\log3-2)>0$. Let $\exp$ denote the real exponential of
[[def-real-exponential-function-and-e]] and let $\mathrm e:=\exp(1)$ be its
value at $1$, distinct from the SI charge $e$ in [[def-qft-example-data]].
Set the upper energy cutoff $\Lambda>0$ joules and
the lower cutoff $\lambda=\Lambda/\mathrm e$. The exact model then has sector
squared norms $s_m=\exp(-C)C^m/m!$, vacuum-sector squared norm $\exp(-C)$,
sector-index sum $C$, and free-energy quadratic expectation
$C\Lambda(1-\mathrm e^{-1})$ joules. Halving $\lambda$ repeatedly adds
$C\log2$ to the cutoff norm squared at each step; the exact coherent
overlap proof shows that this fixed shell overlap prevents a projective-ray
limit, including arbitrary
phase choices. The separate weak-zero and no-strong-limit claims in
[[thm-qft-example-soft-current-angular-coherent]] remain conditional on
[[lem-qft-qed-coherent-ir-obstruction]]. The squared norms are mathematical
Hilbert-space quantities, not reported photon probabilities or measured
emissions.

items.title: Ideal linear Penning mode-frequency invariant
items.design_state: Complete conditional trace proof; reader state-solution clarification retained and manifest synchronized at Step 3a. Actual draft def-qft-example-data convention inspected; independent supplier acceptance is not asserted.
items.statement:
Let $q
e0$ be a signed charge in coulombs, $M>0$ a rest-mass energy in joules, $c>0$ the speed of light in metres per second, and $\mathbf B\in\mathbb R^3\setminus\{0\}$ a constant magnetic-field vector in teslas. Set $m:=M/c^2>0$. Let $K\in\mathbb R^{3	imes3}$ be a real symmetric matrix with $\operatorname{tr}K=0$, with units volts per square metre, and define the quadratic scalar potential $\Phi(\mathbf r):=	frac12\mathbf r^{T}K\mathbf r$ for $\mathbf r\in\mathbb R^3$ in metres. Thus $\partial_i\partial_j\Phi=K_{ij}$ and $\sum_{i=1}^3\partial_i^2\Phi=\operatorname{tr}K=0$. Put $\alpha:=qc^2/M=q/m$, $D:=-\alpha K$, and define $C:\mathbb R^3	o\mathbb R^3$ by $C\mathbf w:=\alpha\,\mathbf w	imes\mathbf B$. The ideal linear model is the real linear map $A:\mathbb R^3	imes\mathbb R^3	o\mathbb R^3	imes\mathbb R^3$, $A(\mathbf r,\mathbf v):=(\mathbf v,D\mathbf r+C\mathbf v)$, equivalently $A= egin{pmatrix}0&I_3\D&C\end{pmatrix}$. Equivalently, its equations are $\dot{\mathbf r}=\mathbf v$ and $\dot{\mathbf v}=-(qc^2/M)K\mathbf r+(qc^2/M)\mathbf v	imes\mathbf B$. The entries of $\mathbf r,\mathbf v$ are their real numerical coordinates in the fixed SI units. A state solution on an open time interval $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ is a $C^1$ map $y=(\mathbf r,\mathbf v):I	o\mathbb R^3	imes\mathbb R^3$ satisfying the displayed equations for every $t\in I$. Here $\mathbf v$ has units metres per second, $D$ has units inverse seconds squared, and $C$ has units inverse seconds.

Define a linear mode to be a complex eigenvector of the complexified state matrix $A$; its eigenvalue $+i\omega$ or $-i\omega$ gives the time factor $e^{\pm i\omega t}$, with angular frequency $\omega>0$ in radians per second. Assume the complexification of $A$ is diagonalizable with eigenvalues $+i\omega_1,-i\omega_1,+i\omega_2,-i\omega_2,+i\omega_3,-i\omega_3$, where each $\omega_j$ is counted with its eigenvalue multiplicity. Define the free cyclotron angular frequency $\omega_c:=|q|c^2|\mathbf B|/M$. Then

$$\omega_c^2=\omega_1^2+\omega_2^2+\omega_3^2.$$

Consequently, if $
u_c:=\omega_c/(2\pi)$ and $
u_j:=\omega_j/(2\pi)$ are the corresponding ordinary frequencies in hertz, then $
u_c^2=
u_1^2+
u_2^2+
u_3^2$. The claim is conditional on the stated uniform-field, harmonic-quadrupole, and complete stable-mode hypotheses; it is an identity for this linear model.
items.strategy:
**Proof technique:** direct.

1.1 By [L1], the inertial-mass coefficient in the SI equation is $q/m=qc^2/M=\alpha$. Block multiplication gives $A^2=\begin{pmatrix}D&C\\CD&D+C^2\end{pmatrix}$, so $\operatorname{tr}(A^2)=2\operatorname{tr}D+\operatorname{tr}(C^2)$. [L1, A1, algebra]

1.2 By [A2], write the complexification as $A=P\Lambda P^{-1}$, where $\Lambda$ is diagonal with the six stated eigenvalues. Then $A^2=P\Lambda^2P^{-1}$; the finite-sum identity $\operatorname{tr}(XY)=\sum_{k,\ell}X_{k\ell}Y_{\ell k}=\operatorname{tr}(YX)$ gives $\operatorname{tr}(A^2)=\operatorname{tr}(\Lambda^2)=\sum_{j=1}^3((i\omega_j)^2+(-i\omega_j)^2)=-2\sum_{j=1}^3\omega_j^2$. [A2, algebra]

2.1 Since $D=-\alpha K$ and $\operatorname{tr}K=0$, $\operatorname{tr}D=0$. In the fixed right-handed Cartesian coordinates, $C$ has matrix $\alpha\begin{pmatrix}0&B_3&-B_2\\-B_3&0&B_1\\B_2&-B_1&0\end{pmatrix}$, so the diagonal entries of $C^2$ are $-\alpha^2(B_2^2+B_3^2)$, $-\alpha^2(B_1^2+B_3^2)$, and $-\alpha^2(B_1^2+B_2^2)$. Therefore $\operatorname{tr}(C^2)=-2\alpha^2|\mathbf B|^2=-2\omega_c^2$ and $\operatorname{tr}D=0$ gives $\operatorname{tr}(A^2)=-2\omega_c^2$ by step 1.1. [A1, step 1.1, algebra]

3.1 Equating the trace calculations in steps 2.1 and 1.2 and dividing by $-2$ gives $\omega_c^2=\omega_1^2+\omega_2^2+\omega_3^2$. [step 2.1, step 1.2, algebra]

4.1 Dividing the angular-frequency identity in step 3.1 by $(2\pi)^2$ gives the same sum-of-squares identity for $\nu_c,\nu_1,\nu_2,\nu_3$. [step 3.1, algebra] ∎

items.title: Deterministic ratio error and Taylor remainder
items.design_state: Complete local algebraic proof; no in-run supplier.
items.statement:
Define $R:\mathbb R\times(0,\infty)\to\mathbb R$ by $R(a,c):=1+a/c$. Here $c$ is only the positive denominator variable in this lemma, not the speed of light. For real $\delta a,\delta c$ and nonnegative bounds $\epsilon_a,\epsilon_c$ satisfying $|\delta a|\le\epsilon_a$ and $|\delta c|\le\epsilon_c<c$, both denominators are positive and

$$\left|R(a+\delta a,c+\delta c)-R(a,c)\right|\le\frac{c\epsilon_a+|a|\epsilon_c}{c(c-\epsilon_c)}.$$

For the first-order statement, write $x=(a,c)$, $h=(u,v)$, and $\|h\|_2:=\sqrt{u^2+v^2}$. Suppose the segment $\{x+th:0\le t\le1\}$ lies in the closed rectangle $Q=[A_-,A_+]\times[c_-,c_+]$, where $A_-\le A_+$ and $0<c_-\le c_+$. Define $A_*:=\max(|A_-|,|A_+|)$, $K_Q:=(A_*+c_+/2)/c_-^3$, and the real-linear map $L_x(u,v):=u/c-av/c^2$. The total derivative of $R$ at $x$ means a real-linear map $L$ such that $\lim_{h\to0}|R(x+h)-R(x)-L(h)|/\|h\|_2=0$. Then $L_x$ is the total derivative, and

$$\left|R(x+h)-R(x)-L_x(h)\right|\le K_Q\|h\|_2^2.$$
items.strategy:
**Proof technique:** direct.

1.1 From [A1], $c+\delta c\ge c-\epsilon_c>0$. Thus both ratio values are defined, and subtracting their fractions gives
$R(a+\delta a,c+\delta c)-R(a,c)=\frac{c\delta a-a\delta c}{c(c+\delta c)}$. [A1, algebra]

1.2 For $\eta\to0$ with $c+\eta>0$, the coordinate difference quotients are
$\frac{R(a+\eta,c)-R(a,c)}{\eta}=\frac1c$ and
$\frac{R(a,c+\eta)-R(a,c)}{\eta}=-\frac{a}{c(c+\eta)}$.
Their limits give the candidate linear map $L_x(u,v)=u/c-av/c^2$; the total-derivative conclusion follows from the full remainder estimate below. [A2, algebra]

1.3 Direct subtraction gives
$R(x+h)-R(x)-L_x(h)=\frac{av^2-cuv}{c^2(c+v)}$. [A2, algebra]

2.1 The triangle inequality gives $|c\delta a-a\delta c|\le c\epsilon_a+|a|\epsilon_c$, while [A1] gives $c(c+\delta c)\ge c(c-\epsilon_c)>0$. Dividing these positive-denominator bounds proves the displayed deterministic ratio-error inequality. [A1, step 1.1, algebra]

2.2 Since the segment lies in $Q$, $c,c+v\ge c_-$, $c\le c_+$, and $|a|\le A_*$. Also $2|uv|\le u^2+v^2$, because $(|u|-|v|)^2\ge0$. Therefore
$|av^2-cuv|\le A_*v^2+c_+|uv|\le(A_*+c_+/2)(u^2+v^2)$, and $c^2(c+v)\ge c_-^3$. Combining these estimates with the exact remainder in step 1.3 gives
$|R(x+h)-R(x)-L_x(h)|\le K_Q\|h\|_2^2$. [A2, step 1.3, algebra]

3.1 For fixed $x=(a,c)$ with $c>0$, choose $Q=[a-1,a+1]\times[c/2,3c/2]$, so $x$ is interior and its lower second-coordinate bound is positive. For every sufficiently small $h$, both endpoints lie in $Q$, and convexity places the segment there. Step 2.2 then gives
$\frac{|R(x+h)-R(x)-L_x(h)|}{\|h\|_2}\le K_Q\|h\|_2\to0$.
By the stated definition, $DR(x)=L_x$. [A2, step 2.2, algebra] ∎

items.design_state: Complete conditional numerical verification with stipulated interval values; no empirical data are used.
items.statement: Take the stipulated nominal values $a=1\,\mathrm{Hz}$, $c=100\,\mathrm{Hz}$, and interval bounds $\epsilon_a=0.1\,\mathrm{Hz}$, $\epsilon_c=1\,\mathrm{Hz}$. The nominal ratio $R=1+a/c$ is dimensionless, and the exact absolute error bound is $11/9900$. These inputs are hypothetical interval values: they are not measurements, error bars, a standard error, or a confidence interval, and no reported Fan et al. data are used.
items.strategy:
**Proof technique:** direct.

1.1 Apply [F1] using [A1]. The numerator is $100\,\mathrm{Hz}\cdot0.1\,\mathrm{Hz}+1\,\mathrm{Hz}\cdot1\,\mathrm{Hz}=11\,\mathrm{Hz}^2$, and the denominator is $100\,\mathrm{Hz}\cdot99\,\mathrm{Hz}=9900\,\mathrm{Hz}^2$. Thus every allowed perturbation has $|R(a+\delta a,c+\delta c)-R(a,c)|\le11/9900$. [A1, F1, algebra]

2.1 The nominal value is $R(a,c)=1+1/100=101/100=1.01$; both the ratio and its bound are dimensionless because the frequency units cancel. The bound is a deterministic calculation for the stated intervals only, with no empirical or statistical interpretation. [A1, step 1.1, algebra] ∎

items.title: Example observable types and scoped meanings
items.statement:
Use the framework-local unit and domain dictionary of
[[def-qft-framework-units]] and the energy, SI/natural-unit, and finite-matrix
conventions of [[def-qft-example-data]]. A physical quantity is always typed
relative to the selected QFT formulation and its declared model data; its name
or units alone do not identify it with a quantity in another formulation.

For the **exact finite-regulator class** used on this page, the state space is
the finite-dimensional Hilbert space $\mathcal H=\mathbb C^d$ for an integer
$d\ge1$. Model inputs include the selected Hermitian Hamiltonian matrices,
their time-dependent Hermitian interaction when present, a dimensionless
coupling parameter, an initial state, and an explicitly supplied finite
outcome measurement. A pure initial state is a vector $\psi\in\mathbb C^d$
with $\|\psi\|=1$; a mixed state is a matrix $\rho=\rho^*$ with
$\langle\rho v,v\rangle\ge0$ for every $v$ and $\operatorname{tr}\rho=1$.
An exact regulated observable on this finite space is a specified Hermitian
matrix $O=O^*$ with a declared physical unit. The matrix and state are model
data; the measurement procedure and any physical rule assigning outcomes are
additional data. This definition does not say that an operator symbol by
itself is a detector outcome or probability.

A **finite probability law** on the declared outcome set
$\{1,\ldots,m\}$, $m\ge1$, is a vector $(p_1,\ldots,p_m)$ with
$p_a\ge0$ and $\sum_{a=1}^m p_a=1$. It is a mathematical type. Assigning that
law to a particular preparation and measurement is a separate physical
postulate. A prediction derived from an actually constructed regulated model
is conditional on those inputs and the adopted rule.

A **formal coefficient record** is a sequence $(c_n)_{n\in\mathbb N}$ of
specified coefficients, sometimes displayed as the symbol
$\sum_{n\ge0}c_n\lambda^n$. Unless convergence and an evaluation map are
separately proved and adopted, the symbol records coefficients only: it is not
an evaluated function, exact probability, convergent perturbation series, or
error bound. A formal coefficient can be assigned a phenomenological meaning
only by a separate, model-specific physical adoption with its approximation
scope stated.

An **empirical estimate** is a source-reported number obtained by analyzing a
finite record of measurement outcomes under the stated preparation, apparatus,
calibration, sampling, and analysis conditions. Its reported uncertainty and
conditions travel with the estimate. It is not the exact model value, and it
does not prove the framework used to interpret it. The 2022 Fan et al. report
is an example of a source-reported electron magnetic-moment determination;
this definition supplies no numerical result, uncertainty reconstruction, or
new experimental claim.

Primitive and derived status is formulation-relative. In a selected regulated
model, the regulator, Hamiltonian data, coupling, initial state, and supplied
measurement are declared inputs; an evolution, amplitude, or probability law
is derived only when the construction and adopted rule establish it. In a
formal calculation, the specified masses, couplings, coefficient rules, and
subtraction prescription are inputs, while its listed coefficients are
derived within that formal calculation. An empirical estimate is a reported
data-analysis result, not a primitive model parameter or a theorem.

The following units are examples of types, not identifications of quantities:
a cross section $\sigma$ is area-valued with SI unit $\mathrm{m^2}$; a rate
$\Gamma$ is inverse-time-valued with unit $\mathrm{s^{-1}}$; an energy width
$\Gamma_E$ has unit joule. Only a separately stated convention may identify
$\Gamma_E=\hbar\Gamma$. The fine-structure parameter $\alpha$, a dimensionless
coupling $g$, and a gyromagnetic factor $g_s$ are dimensionless but have
different physical meanings. The name “width,” a common symbol, or matching
dimensions does not supply an exponential-decay law or an equality between
these parameters.

references.title: David Tong, Quantum Field Theory, §0.1 “Units and Scales”
X. Fan et al., Measurement of the Electron Magnetic Moment, Physical Review Letters 130, 071801 (2023), arXiv:2209.13084v2 (2022)

items.physical_scope: Framework-local primitive/derived, unit, observable, formal-coefficient, and empirical-data distinctions for the finite regulated examples and specified formal calculations on this page. No general continuum observable, detector, scattering, or empirical-estimator construction is asserted.

items.title: Exact regulated transition probabilities and controlled coefficients
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice]]), and use the finite regulated model type of
[[def-qft-example-observable-types]]. Let $d\ge1$, let $\tau>0$ be a time
interval endpoint in seconds, let $\hbar>0$ have unit $\mathrm{J\,s}$, and
let $\lambda\in\mathbb R$ be dimensionless. Let
$H_0=H_0^*\in M_d(\mathbb C)$ have unit joule and let
$V:[0,\tau]\to M_d(\mathbb C)$ be norm-continuous, Hermitian-valued, and
joule-valued. Set
$$V_I(t)=e^{itH_0/\hbar}V(t)e^{-itH_0/\hbar},\qquad B=\sup_{0\le t\le\tau}\|V_I(t)\|,\qquad z=\frac{|\lambda|B\tau}{\hbar}.$$
Define $S_0(t)=I$ and
$$S_{n+1}(t)=-\frac{i}{\hbar}\int_0^tV_I(r)S_n(r)\,dr,\qquad S(t)=\sum_{n=0}^\infty\lambda^nS_n(t).$$
For $W\in M_d(\mathbb C)$, **unitary** means $W^*W=WW^*=I$.
Write $U(\tau)=e^{-iH_0\tau/\hbar}S(\tau)$ and, for $N\ge0$,
$$U_N(\tau)=e^{-iH_0\tau/\hbar}\sum_{n=0}^N\lambda^nS_n(\tau),\qquad R_N=e^z\frac{z^{N+1}}{(N+1)!}.$$

Let $\psi\in\mathbb C^d$ be a unit initial vector. A supplied finite
projective measurement is a family $P_1,\ldots,P_m\in M_d(\mathbb C)$,
$m\ge1$, satisfying $P_a=P_a^*=P_a^2$, $P_aP_b=0$ for $a\ne b$, and
$\sum_{a=1}^mP_a=I$. Equivalently, the one-Kraus-per-outcome data
$M_{a,1}=P_a$ form a normalized finite instrument in the sense of
[[def-qft-finite-bounded-kraus-instrument]]. Adopt the constructed-model Born
interpretation of [[post-qft-constructed-model-and-measurement]] only for this
actually constructed finite model and measurement. For its physical reading,
also adopt the explicit preparation/evolution assumption [A3]: the initial
density is $\rho_0:=T_{\psi,\psi}$, and the model density at the measurement
time is $\rho_\tau:=U(\tau)\rho_0U(\tau)^*=T_{U(\tau)\psi,U(\tau)\psi}$.
Here $T_{u,v}$ is the rank-one map $x\mapsto\langle x,v\rangle u$ of
[[lem-qft-finite-instrument-normalization]]. The Dyson result proves that this
matrix $U(\tau)$ is unitary; identifying it with the selected model's state
update is an adopted physical assumption, not a conclusion about nature.
Define the exact model probability and the truncated squared norm by
$$p_a=\|P_aU(\tau)\psi\|^2,\qquad q_{a,N}=\|P_aU_N(\tau)\psi\|^2.$$
Then $p_a\in[0,1]$, $\sum_ap_a=1$, and
$$|p_a-q_{a,N}|\le\bigl(2\sqrt{q_{a,N}}+R_N\bigr)R_N.$$
The nonnegative number $q_{a,N}$ is a truncation-derived square, not generally
a probability.

For the exact finite interaction matrix write $S(\tau;\lambda)=I+i\mathsf T(\lambda)$
and $\mathsf T(\lambda)=\lambda\mathsf T_1+\lambda^2\mathsf T_2+\cdots$.
Use the standard basis $e_1,\ldots,e_d$ for matrix entries, so
$\mathsf T_{fi}:=e_f^*\mathsf T e_i$ for $1\le f,i\le d$. For a matrix
$A$, define its Hermitian imaginary part by
$\operatorname{Im}_{\mathrm H}A:=(A-A^*)/(2i)$. Exact unitarity gives
$$2\operatorname{Im}\mathsf T_{ii}(\lambda)=\sum_{f=1}^d|\mathsf T_{fi}(\lambda)|^2,\qquad \mathsf T_1=\mathsf T_1^*,\qquad 2\operatorname{Im}_{\mathrm H}\mathsf T_2=\mathsf T_1^*\mathsf T_1.$$
These are finite-regulator coefficient identities, not continuum optical or
scattering theorems.

In the two-level case $H_0=0$, $\lambda=1$, and
$V(t)=g_E\sigma_x$ with $g_E>0$ in joules and
$\sigma_x=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{pmatrix}$, the exact transition
probability from $e_1=(1,0)$ to the projector $P=|e_2\rangle\langle e_2|$
is $\sin^2z$, where the previously defined $z$ equals $g_E\tau/\hbar$
because $V_I=V$ and $\|\sigma_x\|=1$; the first-order squared transition
coefficient is $z^2$ and may exceed $1$. For all real $z$,
$$|\sin^2z-z^2|\le\frac{|z|^4}{3}.$$
The exact survival factor is $\cos^2z$, which is not $e^{-\Gamma\tau}$ for
any $\Gamma>0$ on all $\tau\ge0$.

For the occupation truncation with orthonormal basis
$e_0,\ldots,e_N$, define $a_Ne_n=\sqrt n\,e_{n-1}$ (zero for $n=0$),
$a_N^*e_n=\sqrt{n+1}\,e_{n+1}$ for $n<N$, and $a_N^*e_N=0$. Then
$$[a_N,a_N^*]=I-(N+1)|e_N\rangle\langle e_N|.$$
More generally, no finite-dimensional matrices $A,B$ satisfy $[A,B]=I$.
These exact regulator facts assert neither an infinite-dimensional CCR
construction nor a continuum limit.

references.title: David Tong, Quantum Field Theory, Chapter 3 “Interacting Fields,” §3.1.1 “Dyson’s Formula”
J. Watrous, The Theory of Quantum Information, author-hosted prepublication manuscript, §§2.3.1–2.3.2
R. B. Griffiths, Notes on Quantum Information Theory, complete §7

items.physical_scope: Exact deductions in an explicitly constructed finite-dimensional regulated model with a supplied finite projective measurement, an adopted pure-state update by the constructed unitary, and the constructed-model Born postulate. Finite-order squares are not generally probabilities. No continuum QFT, regulator removal, asymptotic scattering operator, empirical result, or sample-based inference is asserted.

items.title: Exact two-level transition versus its first coefficient
items.statement:
Under the explicit pure-state preparation and unitary-evolution assumption of
[[pthm-qft-example-regulated-probability-control]], take
$\mathcal H=\mathbb C^2$, $H_0=0$, $V(t)=g_E\sigma_x$ with
$g_E>0$ joules, dimensionless $\lambda=1$, initial vector $e_1=(1,0)$, and
the two-outcome projective measurement $P=|e_2\rangle\langle e_2|$,
$I-P$, where $e_2=(0,1)$. At
$\tau=\pi\hbar/(2g_E)$ seconds the exact model transition probability is
$1$, whereas the first-order squared transition coefficient is
$\pi^2/4>1$. The latter is a coefficient-derived square, not a probability.
This is an exact constructed-model calculation, not a simulated or reported
experiment.

items.title: One-mode time-ordered correlator versus retarded response
items.statement:
For the exact single oscillator mode of
[[lem-qft-example-oscillator-feynman-prescription]], let $\omega>0$ in
$\mathrm{s^{-1}}$ and choose $t=-\pi/(2\omega)$. The normalized
time-ordered vacuum correlator is $-i/(2\omega)$, while the retarded response
kernel is $0$. The correlator at negative time is not a response to a future
source. This fixed-mode calculation does not establish a spatial-causality or
superluminal-signalling result.

items.title: Finite fermion-mode occupation basis
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice. Let $\mathcal K$ be a finite-dimensional complex Hilbert space with a finite ordered orthonormal basis $(e_j)_{j\in J}$, and use the antisymmetric Fock construction and second-variable-linear convention of [[def-qft-fock-and-test-spaces]]. Assume its fermionic operators satisfy the CAR of [[lem-qft-fock-ccr-car]]. For $S=\{j_1<\cdots<j_k\}\subseteq J$, set
$$\xi_S=c^\dagger(e_{j_1})\cdots c^\dagger(e_{j_k})\Omega,\qquad \xi_\varnothing=\Omega.$$
Then $(\xi_S)_{S\subseteq J}$ is an orthonormal basis of $\mathcal F_a(\mathcal K)$. For each $j\in J$, the bounded number operator $N_j=c^\dagger(e_j)c(e_j)$ is an orthogonal projection and
$$N_j\xi_S=\mathbf1_{j\in S}\xi_S.$$
Consequently, for any partition $J=\bigsqcup_{x\in V}J_x$ into finite site-mode sets, $n_x=\sum_{j\in J_x}N_j$ is bounded self-adjoint and acts on $\xi_S$ by the occupation count $N_x(S)=|S\cap J_x|\in\{0,\ldots,|J_x|\}$.

items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice. Let $\Gamma=(V,E,s,t,\mathcal P)$ be a finite oriented graph with nonempty finite vertex set $V$, nonempty finite link set $E$, endpoint maps $s,t:E\to V$, and a finite list $\mathcal P$ of oriented simple cycles. Parallel links and self-loops are allowed. An oriented simple cycle $p\in\mathcal P$ is a finite closed path using each link at most once; write $\sigma_{p,e}\in\{-1,0,1\}$ for its signed use of link $e$, so its signed incidence at every vertex is zero. Fix enumerations $E=(\ell_1,\ldots,\ell_N)$ and $V=(v_1,\ldots,v_M)$, where $N=|E|$ and $M=|V|$. Write $\mathbb T_1=\mathbb R/\mathbb Z$ and $\mathbb T_{2\pi}=\mathbb R/(2\pi\mathbb Z)$, and set $\mathbb T=\mathbb T_{2\pi}$ with normalized Haar measure $d\theta/(2\pi)$ and product measure $m_E$ on $\mathbb T^E$.

The coordinatewise map
$$\Phi_E:\mathbb T_{2\pi}^E\to\mathbb T_1^E,\qquad ([\theta_e])_{e\in E}\mapsto([\theta_e/(2\pi)])_{e\in E},$$
is a well-defined measure-preserving group isomorphism for the normalized product Haar measures. The fixed enumeration of $E$ identifies $\mathbb T_1^E$ with $\mathbb T_1^N$; pulling back the Fourier characters $x\mapsto\exp(2\pi i\sum_{e\in E}n_ex_e)$ along $\Phi_E$ gives $e_{\mathbf n}(\theta)=\exp(i\sum_{e\in E}n_e\theta_e)$. Thus the Fourier basis theorem [[thm-fourier-basis-and-parseval-on-the-n-torus]], whose torus is $\mathbb R/\mathbb Z$ and whose characters are $\exp(2\pi i kx)$, gives an orthonormal basis $\{e_{\mathbf n}:\mathbf n\in\mathbb Z^E\}$ of $L^2(\mathbb T^E)$. The second-variable-linear $L^2$ pairing used below is the conjugate of the first-variable-linear pairing in that theorem, so orthonormality and completeness are unchanged.

Fix an integer $s\ge1$ and let $\mathcal K=\bigoplus_{x\in V}\mathbb C^s$ with orthonormal modes $e_{x\alpha}$, $1\le\alpha\le s$. This is finite-dimensional and hence separable. Fix the lexicographic order on $J=V\times\{1,\ldots,s\}$ induced by the chosen order on $V$ and the usual order on $\{1,\ldots,s\}$. Use the antisymmetric Fock space and second-variable-linear inner product convention of [[def-qft-fock-and-test-spaces]]. The current draft supplier [[lem-qft-fock-ccr-car]] states that, assuming Countable Choice, $\mathcal F_a(\mathcal K)$ is a Hilbert space and its creation and annihilation operators are bounded and satisfy the CAR; that supplier is still a draft carrier, not an accepted result in this run. For $\mathbf m=(m_{x\alpha})\in\{0,1\}^J$, put $S(\mathbf m)=\{(x,\alpha):m_{x\alpha}=1\}$ and write $\xi_{\mathbf m}=\xi_{S(\mathbf m)}$ for the ordered wedge basis vector of [[lem-qft-finite-mode-occupation-basis]]. This is a complete orthonormal basis of $\mathcal F_a(\mathcal K)$; changing the chosen order changes individual wedge vectors only by signs. Write $c_{x\alpha}=c(e_{x\alpha})$, $c^\dagger_{x\alpha}=c^\dagger(e_{x\alpha})$, and $n_x=\sum_{\alpha=1}^s c^\dagger_{x\alpha}c_{x\alpha}$. On $\xi_{\mathbf m}$, $n_x$ acts by $N_x(\mathbf m)=\sum_{\alpha=1}^s m_{x\alpha}$; it is bounded self-adjoint with spectrum contained in $\{0,\ldots,s\}$.

Use the second-variable-linear $L^2$ pairing $\langle f,g\rangle_2=\int_{\mathbb T^E}\overline{f(\theta)}g(\theta)\,dm_E(\theta)$. The kinematical Hilbert space is
$$\mathcal H_{\rm kin}=L^2(\mathbb T^E)\widehat\otimes\mathcal F_a(\mathcal K),$$
where $\widehat\otimes$ has the same completion norm as [[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]] and the second-variable-linear pairing obtained by conjugating its first-variable-linear tensor pairing, as in [[def-qft-fock-and-test-spaces]]. Concretely, the tensor supplier is applied to the conjugate first-variable-linear pairings $(f,g)_1=\langle g,f\rangle_2$ and $(\Phi,\Psi)_1=\langle\Psi,\Phi\rangle_2$, and the resulting tensor pairing is conjugated; this preserves the norm and the product-basis assertion. Consequently
$$\{e_{\mathbf n}\otimes\xi_{\mathbf m}:\mathbf n\in\mathbb Z^E,\ \mathbf m\in\{0,1\}^J\}$$
is a complete orthonormal basis of $\mathcal H_{\rm kin}$ by the product-basis assertion of [[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]]. This is the joint basis used for all diagonal multipliers below. Write
$\psi=\sum_{\mathbf n,\mathbf m}\psi_{\mathbf n,\mathbf m}e_{\mathbf n}\otimes\xi_{\mathbf m}$.
All matter operators previously defined on $\mathcal F_a(\mathcal K)$ act on
$\mathcal H_{\rm kin}$ as identity on the rotor factor tensor that operator.
On the full kinematical basis define
$$E_e(e_{\mathbf n}\otimes\xi_{\mathbf m})=n_e(e_{\mathbf n}\otimes\xi_{\mathbf m}),\qquad D(E_e)=\left\{\psi\in\mathcal H_{\rm kin}:\sum_{\mathbf n,\mathbf m}n_e^2|\psi_{\mathbf n,\mathbf m}|^2<\infty\right\}.$$
Thus $E_e$ is the maximal real diagonal multiplier, self-adjoint with integer
spectrum, and on its domain its coefficients are $n_e\psi_{\mathbf n,\mathbf m}$.
Define the bounded unitary $U_e$ as multiplication by $e^{i\theta_e}$ on the
rotor factor and identity on the matter factor. Equivalently,
$$U_e(e_{\mathbf n}\otimes\xi_{\mathbf m})=e_{\mathbf n+\delta_e}\otimes\xi_{\mathbf m},\qquad (U_e\psi)_{\mathbf n,\mathbf m}=\psi_{\mathbf n-\delta_e,\mathbf m}.$$
Each $U_f$ preserves $D(E_e)$, since
$(n_e+\delta_{ef})^2\le2n_e^2+2$ and the coefficient sequence is square
summable; its inverse preserves that domain by the same estimate. Computing
on coefficients gives $[E_e,U_f]=\delta_{ef}U_f$ on $D(E_e)$.


Fix background integers $b_x\in\{0,\ldots,s\}$. In the joint basis define the real integer multiplier
$$\gamma_x(\mathbf n,\mathbf m)=\sum_{e:s(e)=x}n_e-\sum_{e:t(e)=x}n_e-\left(\sum_{\alpha=1}^s m_{x\alpha}-b_x\right),$$
and let $G_x$ be its maximal diagonal operator, with domain $D(G_x)=\{\psi:\sum_{\mathbf n,\mathbf m}|\gamma_x(\mathbf n,\mathbf m)|^2|\psi_{\mathbf n,\mathbf m}|^2<\infty\}$. On the common link-electric domain this is the finite sum $\sum_{s(e)=x}E_e-\sum_{t(e)=x}E_e-(n_x-b_xI)$. These are the Gauss operators; the operator constraint defines $\mathcal H_{\rm phys}:=\bigcap_{x\in V}\ker G_x$. For $\alpha\in\mathbb T^V$ define the diagonal multiplier $U(\alpha)=\exp(i\sum_x\alpha_xG_x)$; the next lemma proves that these operators form a strongly continuous representation and that their normalized Haar average is the orthogonal projection onto $\mathcal H_{\rm phys}$.

For each $x$, choose a Hermitian matrix $M_x\in M_s(\mathbb C)$, and for each link $e$ choose a matrix $T_e\in M_s(\mathbb C)$. Choose real coefficients $\lambda_E>0$ and $\lambda_p\in\mathbb R$ for $p\in\mathcal P$. Write
$$W_p=\prod_{e\in E}U_e^{\sigma_{p,e}},\qquad V_B=-\frac12\sum_{p\in\mathcal P}\lambda_p(W_p+W_p^\dagger),$$
and
$$V_F=\sum_{x\in V}\sum_{\alpha,\beta=1}^s c^\dagger_{x\alpha}(M_x)_{\alpha\beta}c_{x\beta}+\sum_{e\in E}\left(A_e+A_e^\dagger\right),\qquad A_e=\sum_{\alpha,\beta=1}^s c^\dagger_{s(e),\alpha}(T_e)_{\alpha\beta}U_e c_{t(e),\beta}.$$
The operator $H_0=\lambda_E\sum_{e\in E}E_e^2$ is the diagonal multiplier with domain
$$D(H_0)=\left\{\psi:\sum_{\mathbf n,\mathbf m}\left(\lambda_E\sum_{e\in E}n_e^2\right)^2|\psi_{\mathbf n,\mathbf m}|^2<\infty\right\},$$
where $\mathbf m=(m_{x\alpha})$ ranges over occupation configurations with each $m_{x\alpha}\in\{0,1\}$, and $N_x(\mathbf m)=\sum_{\alpha=1}^s m_{x\alpha}$ is the eigenvalue of $n_x$ on that basis vector. The coefficients $\lambda_E,\lambda_p$ and entries of $M_x,T_e$ are ordinary real or complex scalars here; no physical units are assigned. Set $H=H_0+V_B+V_F$ on $D(H_0)$. This is a mathematical finite-graph regulator definition. It asserts no physical adoption, continuum limit, Lorentz invariance, or identification with a particular continuum QED model.

For sign comparison only, if a smooth path $\gamma_e:[0,1]\to X$ in a smooth manifold $X$, a real $C^1$ connection one-form $a$, and a real $C^1$ function $\lambda$ are supplied, take $U_e^{\rm cont}=\exp(-ig\int_0^1a_{\gamma_e(r)}(\dot\gamma_e(r))\,dr)$ for real $g$. Under $a\mapsto a+d\lambda$, the fundamental theorem along the supplied path gives the endpoint factor
$e^{ig(\lambda(\gamma_e(0))-\lambda(\gamma_e(1)))}$.
This is an edgewise sign comparison: it has the same source-minus-target
angle pattern as the finite vertex-phase convention. Neither $s(e)$ nor
$t(e)$ is evaluated by $\lambda$; they are vertices in $V$, whereas
$\gamma_e(0),\gamma_e(1)$ are points of $X$. No map $V\to X$ or compatible
paths for the whole graph are supplied, and no continuum limit is asserted.

items.reference: research/extended-frameworks-2026-10-03/quantum-field-theory/workers/qed/proofs.md#Q5; reserved proposed inventory, exact conditional statement authored in items/lem-qft-lattice-gauss-projection.md

items.statement:
Assume the conditional compact-rotor/CAR data of [[def-qft-compact-lattice-gauge-data]]. In the joint Fourier/occupation basis write
$$\gamma_x(\mathbf n,\mathbf m)=\sum_{e:s(e)=x}n_e-\sum_{e:t(e)=x}n_e-\sum_{\alpha=1}^s m_{x\alpha}+b_x\in\mathbb Z.$$
For every vertex $x$, let $G_x$ be multiplication by $\gamma_x$ on its maximal diagonal domain
$$D(G_x)=\left\{\psi:\sum_{\mathbf n,\mathbf m}|\gamma_x(\mathbf n,\mathbf m)|^2|\psi_{\mathbf n,\mathbf m}|^2<\infty\right\}.$$
Then each $G_x$ is self-adjoint, the $G_x$ strongly commute, and $U(\alpha)=\exp(i\sum_x\alpha_xG_x)$ is a strongly continuous unitary representation of $\mathbb T^V$. Its action obeys
$$U(\alpha)c_{x\beta}U(\alpha)^\dagger=e^{i\alpha_x}c_{x\beta},\qquad U(\alpha)U_eU(\alpha)^\dagger=e^{i(\alpha_{s(e)}-\alpha_{t(e)})}U_e.$$
The normalized Haar average
$$P=\frac1{(2\pi)^{|V|}}\int_{[0,2\pi]^{|V|}}U(\alpha)\,d\alpha$$
is the orthogonal projection onto $\mathcal H_{\rm phys}=\bigcap_x\ker G_x$. This subspace is nonzero for every admissible fixed background $b$: it contains the normalized state with link Fourier labels $n_e=0$ and site occupations $m_{x\alpha}$ chosen so $\sum_\alpha m_{x\alpha}=b_x$.

items.reference: research/extended-frameworks-2026-10-03/quantum-field-theory/workers/qed/proofs.md#Q5; reserved proposed inventory, exact conditional statement authored in items/lem-qft-lattice-physical-evolution.md
items.design_state: reserved claim; complete conditional argument authored; Step-1 readiness escalated pending batch-37 carrier
items.statement:
Assume the model data of [[def-qft-compact-lattice-gauge-data]] and the Axiom of Choice. Let $H$ be the self-adjoint Hamiltonian on the exact domain supplied by [[lem-qft-lattice-hamiltonian-selfadjoint]], and let $P$ be the physical projection of [[lem-qft-lattice-gauss-projection]]. For any scalar $\hbar>0$, the family
$$\mathcal U(t)=e^{-itH/\hbar},\qquad t\in\mathbb R,$$
is a strongly continuous unitary group on $\mathcal H_{\rm kin}$, preserves $D(H)$, and satisfies
$$\lim_{h\to0}\frac{\mathcal U(h)\psi-\psi}{h}=-\frac{i}{\hbar}H\psi\quad(\psi\in D(H)).$$
It commutes with every gauge transformation $U(\alpha)$ and with $P$. Hence $\mathcal H_{\rm phys}=\operatorname{ran}P$ is a reducing subspace and $\mathcal U(t)|_{\mathcal H_{\rm phys}}$ is a strongly continuous unitary group with skew-adjoint infinitesimal generator $-iH|_{D(H)\cap\mathcal H_{\rm phys}}/\hbar$; its self-adjoint Stone operator is $-H|_{D(H)\cap\mathcal H_{\rm phys}}/\hbar$. Equivalently, the restricted physical Hamiltonian $H|_{D(H)\cap\mathcal H_{\rm phys}}$ is self-adjoint. This is an exact fixed-graph result; no continuum dynamics are asserted.

items.reference: research/extended-frameworks-2026-10-03/quantum-field-theory/workers/qed/proofs.md#Q5; reserved proposed inventory, exact conditional statement authored in items/lem-qft-lattice-local-gauss-flux.md

items.statement:
Assume the data of [[def-qft-compact-lattice-gauge-data]] and let $R\subseteq V$. Define
$$\partial R=\{e\in E:\text{exactly one endpoint of }e\text{ lies in }R\},$$
with $\epsilon(e,R)=1$ when $s(e)\in R,t(e)\notin R$ and $\epsilon(e,R)=-1$ when $t(e)\in R,s(e)\notin R$. On the domain
$$\mathcal D_R=\mathcal H_{\rm phys}\cap\bigcap_{e\in\partial R}D(E_e),$$
the region number $N_R=\sum_{x\in R}(n_x-b_xI)$ obeys the exact identity
$$N_R\psi=\left(\sum_{e\in\partial R}\epsilon(e,R)E_e\right)\psi\qquad(\psi\in\mathcal D_R).$$
Thus for $R=V$, where $\partial R=\varnothing$, every physical vector has total occupation $\sum_x n_x=\sum_x b_x$. This finite-graph identity is exact and makes no continuum-limit claim.

items.title: Exact regulated gauge and infinitesimal Ward identities
items.reference: research/extended-frameworks-2026-10-03/quantum-field-theory/workers/qed/proofs.md#Q6; reserved proposed inventory, exact conditional statement authored in items/lem-qft-lattice-ward-identities.md
items.design_state: reserved claim; complete conditional argument authored; Step-1 readiness escalated pending batch-37 carrier
items.statement:
Assume the finite-graph model of [[def-qft-compact-lattice-gauge-data]] and the Axiom of Choice. Let $\psi\in\mathcal H_{\rm phys}$ be a normalized vector. A bounded operator $O$ has gauge charge $q=(q_x)_{x\in V}\in\mathbb Z^V$ when
$$U(\alpha)OU(\alpha)^\dagger=e^{i\sum_x q_x\alpha_x}O.$$
Then $\langle\psi,O\psi\rangle=0$ whenever $q\ne0$, and any finite product of bounded gauge-charge eigenoperators has zero expectation when the sum of its charge vectors is nonzero.

For each $x$, if $O$ maps $D(G_x)$ into itself and $[G_x,O]$ extends to a bounded operator, then
$$\langle\psi,[G_x,O]\psi\rangle=0.$$
The same assertions apply to $O(t)=\mathcal U(t)^\dagger O\mathcal U(t)$: the finite-regulator time evolution preserves the gauge charge and the domains $D(G_x)$. These are exact operator identities for the stated regulator; no trace or path-integral identity and no continuum Ward–Takahashi statement is asserted.

items.title: Gauss law and charged localization obstruction
items.reference: research/extended-frameworks-2026-10-03/quantum-field-theory/workers/qed/proofs.md#Q6; reserved proposed inventory, exact conditional statement authored in items/lem-qft-qed-gauss-localization.md
items.design_state: reserved claim; complete conditional argument authored; Step-1 readiness escalated pending batch-37 carrier
items.statement:
Assume the exact finite-graph model and let $R\subseteq V$. Set $Q_R=\sum_{x\in R}(n_x-b_xI)$ and let $\partial R$ and its orientation signs be as in [[lem-qft-lattice-local-gauss-flux]]. On $\mathcal H_{\rm phys}\cap\bigcap_{e\in\partial R}D(E_e)$, suppose a bounded operator $O$ preserves $\mathcal H_{\rm phys}$ and, for every boundary link $e$, maps $D(E_e)$ into itself and satisfies $E_eO\phi=OE_e\phi$ for every $\phi\in D(E_e)$. Then $[Q_R,O]\psi=0$ for every vector in that physical domain. Consequently, a charge-changing operator with $[Q_R,O]\psi=qO\psi$ for a fixed $q\ne0$ cannot both preserve the physical sector and commute with the boundary electric operators while acting nontrivially on any such physical vector.

There is also the following conditional continuum statement; it does not assert that a continuum representation exists. Let $D$ be a common invariant dense domain in a Hilbert space, and let $\rho(f)$ and $E_k(g_k)$ be linear assignments from real-valued test functions $f,g_k\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^3)$ to operators $D\to D$. For a real vector test function $\mathbf g=(g_1,g_2,g_3)\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb R^3)$ set $E(\mathbf g)=\sum_{k=1}^3E_k(g_k)$. Assume the assignments satisfy on $D$
$$\rho(f)=-\varepsilon_0\sum_{k=1}^3E_k(\partial_k f)\quad(f\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^3)),$$
for a fixed $\varepsilon_0>0$, and let $K\subset\mathbb R^3$ be compact. Suppose $O$ is bounded, maps $D$ into itself, and satisfies $E(\mathbf g)O\psi=OE(\mathbf g)\psi$ for every $\psi\in D$ whenever $\operatorname{supp}\mathbf g$ is disjoint from $K$. For each integer $R\ge R_0$, choose a real-valued $\chi_R\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^3)$ equal to $1$ on a neighborhood of $K$ and with $\operatorname{supp}\nabla\chi_R$ disjoint from $K$, and put $Q_R=\rho(\chi_R)=-\varepsilon_0 E(\nabla\chi_R)$. Assume there is an operator $Q:D\to D$ such that, for every $\psi\in D$, both $Q_R\psi\to Q\psi$ and $Q_RO\psi\to QO\psi$ as integer $R\to\infty$. Then $[Q,O]\psi=0$ on $D$. A bounded charge-changing operator satisfying $[Q,O]\psi=qO\psi$ for $q\ne0$ on $D$ must therefore be the zero operator. These continuum conclusions are conditional on the displayed domain, locality, convergence and commutator-passage assumptions.

items.title: Time-ordered Ward contact relation
items.reference: research/extended-frameworks-2026-10-03/quantum-field-theory/workers/qed/proofs.md#Q6; reserved proposed inventory, exact conditional statement authored in items/lem-qft-lattice-ward-contact.md
items.design_state: reserved claim; complete conditional argument authored; Step-1 readiness escalated pending batch-37 carrier
items.statement:
Assume the compact finite-graph model and the Axiom of Choice. Fix a vertex $x$, pairwise distinct real times $t_1,\ldots,t_n$ with $n\ge1$, bounded operators $O_j$, and a normalized physical vector $\psi$. Assume each $O_j$ maps $D(G_x)$ into itself and has a bounded commutator with $G_x$. Let
$$O_j(t_j)=\mathcal U(t_j)^\dagger O_j\mathcal U(t_j),\qquad G_x(t)=\mathcal U(t)^\dagger G_x\mathcal U(t),$$
where $\mathcal U(t)=e^{-itH/\hbar}$. Define ordinary time ordering by placing the factor with the larger time to the left; $G_x$ is bosonic, so moving it past an insertion introduces no grading sign. Then $G_x(t)=G_x$, and, as a distribution in $t$,
$$\frac{d}{dt}\left\langle\psi,\mathcal T\!\left[G_x(t)\prod_{j=1}^nO_j(t_j)\right]\psi\right\rangle=\sum_{j=1}^n\delta(t-t_j)\left\langle\psi,\mathcal T\!\left([G_x,O_j(t_j)]\prod_{i\ne j}O_i(t_i)\right)\psi\right\rangle.$$
The products and commutators are evaluated on the common domains just specified. This is a finite-regulator contact identity, not a claim about continuum renormalized time-ordered products.
