items.title: Specified bosonic scalar and CAR Dirac model adoption
items.design_state: Adopts the actual constructed scalar and Dirac branches and their species assignments; the QFT-MF04 action-to-equation carrier is present, its interface matches, and its current Step 1 record is ready. Its convention suppliers remain draft inputs used conditionally.
items.physical_scope: A selected, noninteracting real scalar and Dirac field model on four-dimensional affine Minkowski spacetime, with a chosen vacuum and bosonic symmetric-Fock and fermionic CAR-Fock representations. The assignments are model assumptions; no interacting continuum theory, empirical result, or general spin-statistics theorem is asserted.
items.statement:
Fix four-dimensional affine Minkowski spacetime with metric
$\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$, an inertial length-coordinate chart
$x=(x^0,\mathbf x)$, $x^0=ct$, and coordinates measured in metres, as specified
by [[def-qft-framework-units]]. Write
$\Box=\eta^{ab}\partial_a\partial_b$. The mass-shell parameter $\mu\ge0$ has
unit $\mathrm m^{-1}$ and
$\omega_\mu(\mathbf k)=\sqrt{|\mathbf k|^2+\mu^2}$ has the same unit. For a
massive species, $\mu=m_{\mathrm{rest,SI}}c/\hbar$; $\mu=0$ is the separately
admitted massless branch of the mathematical free-field construction. Thus
$\hbar c\omega_\mu$ is physical energy and $\hbar\mathbf k$ is physical
momentum. The natural-unit action is written $S/\hbar$.

The scalar one-particle space is
$\mathcal H_\mu=L^2(H_\mu^+,d\nu_\mu;\mathbb C)$, where
$H_\mu^+=\{(\omega_\mu(\mathbf k),\mathbf k):\mathbf k\in\mathbb R^3,\ \omega_\mu(\mathbf k)>0\}$ and
$d\nu_\mu=d^3\mathbf k/((2\pi)^3\,2\omega_\mu(\mathbf k))$; at $\mu=0$ the
measure-zero apex $\mathbf k=0$ is omitted. These are the shell conventions
of [[lem-qft-smeared-free-scalar]].

For a smooth real classical scalar $\phi_{\mathrm n}:\mathbb R^4\to\mathbb R$
with the canonical free-field length degree $-1$, adopt
$$\frac{S_\phi}{\hbar}=-\frac12\int_{\mathbb R^4}\left(\eta^{ab}\partial_a\phi_{\mathrm n}\partial_b\phi_{\mathrm n}+\mu^2\phi_{\mathrm n}^2\right)\,d^4x.$$
For a smooth commuting classical Dirac spinor
$\psi_{\mathrm n}:\mathbb R^4\to\mathbb C^4$ with canonical free-field length
degree $-3/2$, put $\bar\psi_{\mathrm n}=\psi_{\mathrm n}^\dagger\beta$ and
use the Clifford convention
$\{\gamma^a,\gamma^b\}=-2\eta^{ab}I_4$ from
[[def-qft-framework-units]]. Adopt
$$\frac{S_D}{\hbar}=\int_{\mathbb R^4}\bar\psi_{\mathrm n}(i\gamma^a\partial_a-\mu)\psi_{\mathrm n}\,d^4x.$$
The smooth classical variables in these functionals commute; no Grassmann
algebra or path-integral construction is being adopted. These formulas specify
local action densities: for arbitrary smooth global fields the total
integrals need not converge. Only compactly supported variations are used;
the action difference under such a variation is an integral over a compact
set and is finite for smooth fields. With these variations on the fixed
background, the intended Euler–Lagrange equations are
$(\Box-\mu^2)\phi_{\mathrm n}=0$ and
$(i\gamma^a\partial_a-\mu)\psi_{\mathrm n}=0$, conditional on the exact
mathematical supplier recorded as [L1] below.

As the physical interpretation of this selected free model, assign the real
scalar species to the bosonic symmetric Fock representation and assign the
Dirac field to the particle/antiparticle CAR representation on
$\mathcal H_+\oplus\overline{\mathcal H_-}$. Choose the zero-particle Fock
vectors as the scalar and Dirac vacuum states. This is an adopted species and
statistics assignment. The CCR/CAR and operator properties of the specified
representations are mathematical model consequences; they do not prove a
general spin-statistics theorem or establish that nature realizes this model.

The scalar construction is the Schwartz-smeared field
$\Phi_\mu(f)=a(K_\mu\overline f)+a^\dagger(K_\mu f)$ on the finite-particle
domain, with the future-shell phase
$p\circ x=\omega_\mu x^0-\mathbf k\cdot\mathbf x$, exactly as in
[[lem-qft-smeared-free-scalar]]. The Dirac construction is the bounded
spacetime-smeared CAR field of
[[lem-qft-free-dirac-car-locality]], using the positive and negative
projections of the specified free Dirac matrix. In that carrier,
$\mathcal H_D=L^2(\mathbb R^3,d^3\mathbf k/(2\pi)^3;\mathbb C^4)$,
$h_D(\mathbf k)=\boldsymbol\alpha\cdot\mathbf k+\beta\mu$, and
$P_\pm(\mathbf k)=(I_4\pm h_D(\mathbf k)/\omega_\mu(\mathbf k))/2$; the
particle and antiparticle one-particle spaces are the closed ranges
$\mathcal H_+$ and $\overline{\mathcal H_-}$. These carriers state their
mathematical hypotheses and construction domains; their draft status is not an
independent physics or proof approval.

Tong's lecture notes and Srednicki's book draft provide independent
presentations of the scalar and Dirac free-field formulations. Their formal
mode notation supplies context for this adoption, not a proof of the
operator-domain claims and not evidence that the adopted model describes
nature.

items.title: Specified free state and observable interpretation
items.design_state: Defines the selected smeared scalar and even Dirac observables, vacuum states, generator domains and Born reading. The current QFT-MF04 carrier omits the planned charged-number domain extension.
items.physical_scope: State and observable definitions for the selected flat, noninteracting scalar and Dirac free-field models. Fields are test-smeared; local Dirac observables are even CAR combinations. Measurements use only constructed instruments. The planned charged-number domain remains an explicit conditional input.
items.statement:
Use the fields, Fock spaces, vacua, coordinate conventions, and natural/SI
normalizations adopted in [[post-qft-free-field-model]]. For an open spacetime
region $O\subseteq\mathbb R^4$, a scalar test is a real
$f\in C_c^\infty(O;\mathbb R)$ and a Dirac test is a
$F\in C_c^\infty(O;\mathbb C^4)$. These are compactly supported smooth test
functions on the fixed inertial Minkowski chart.

For scalar tests use the bounded Weyl operators
$$W_\mu(f)=W_{\rm Segal}(\sqrt2 K_\mu f),$$
where $K_\mu$ is the future-shell restriction and
$W_{\rm Segal}$ is the unitary generated by the closed Segal field, with the
normalization and phase convention of
[[lem-qft-smeared-free-scalar]]. Define the scalar bounded observable algebra
$\mathfrak A_s(O)$ to be the norm closure of the unital $*$-algebra generated
by these $W_\mu(f)$. The real smeared field is symmetric on
$\mathcal D_{\rm fin}$ and its self-adjoint closure has the exact multiplier
domain supplied by [[lem-qft-free-domain-observables]] and
[[lem-qft-segal-weyl-domain]].

For Dirac tests, $\Psi(F)$ is the bounded smeared CAR field of
[[lem-qft-free-dirac-car-locality]]. Define $\mathfrak A_D(O)$ as the norm
closure of the unital algebra generated by products containing an even number
of these field operators and their adjoints, with all test supports in $O$.
“Even” here means even field parity, or equivalently an even number of odd
CAR field generators in each product. The even algebra is the selected local
Dirac observable algebra; an odd charged field is not included as a commuting
local observable.

The selected vacuum states on bounded operators are the vector states
$\omega_s(A)=\langle\Omega_s,A\Omega_s\rangle$ and
$\omega_D(B)=\langle\Omega_D,B\Omega_D\rangle$. For the scalar Fock space,
define the total number, Hamiltonian, and physical momentum components by
$$N_s=d\Gamma_s(1),\qquad H_s=\hbar c\,d\Gamma_s(\omega_\mu),\qquad P_{s,j}=\hbar\,d\Gamma_s(k_j).$$
Here $d\Gamma_s$ acts on the $n$-particle sector by summing the displayed
one-particle multiplier over its $n$ arguments. Their maximal domains are
the square-integrability domains of those sector sums; in particular,
$$D(N_s)=\left\{\Psi=(\Psi_n):\sum_{n\ge1}n^2\|\Psi_n\|^2<\infty\right\}.$$
These physical components have one-particle momentum $+\hbar k_j$, as in
[[def-qft-framework-units]]. The mathematical spatial generators in
[[lem-qft-smeared-free-scalar]] and [[lem-qft-free-domain-observables]] use
$G_{s,j}=d\Gamma_s(-k_j)$ with the positive-exponent convention;
thus $P_{s,j}=-\hbar G_{s,j}$. For a translation increment
$a=(a^0,\mathbf a)$ in length coordinates, the scalar translation unitary
is the sectorwise phase
$\exp(i(a^0H_s/(\hbar c)-\sum_j a^jP_{s,j}/\hbar))$.
Changing the sign does not change the maximal domain, since the squared
sector multiplier is unchanged. This also follows directly from
[[lem-qft-second-quantized-spectrum]] with multiplier $k_j$. For the Dirac Fock space, let $H$
and $P_j$ be the mathematical translation generators of
[[lem-qft-dirac-fermionic-translation-spectrum]]. Their one-particle
multipliers are respectively $(\omega_\mu,\mathbf k)$ for particles and
$(\omega_\mu,-\mathbf k)$ for antiparticles, and the sector multiplier is
their sum. Define the physical Dirac Hamiltonian and momentum by
$H_D=\hbar cH$ and $P_{D,j}=\hbar P_j$, using the positive SI constants from
[[def-qft-framework-units]]. Their exact domains are unchanged by these
nonzero scale factors; their multipliers have units joules and momentum,
respectively.

For any of these self-adjoint operators $A$, a normalized state
$\Psi\in D(A)$ has model mean $\langle\Psi,A\Psi\rangle$ and variance
$\operatorname{Var}_\Psi(A)=\|(A-\langle\Psi,A\Psi\rangle)\Psi\|^2$.
This requires the second spectral moment but does not require
$\Psi\in D(A^2)$. Products of unbounded operators use their composition
domains.

If a signed charge parameter $q_{\rm SI}\in\mathbb R$ measured in coulombs is supplied, the intended
Dirac charge-number operator is $Q_{\rm SI}=q_{\rm SI}(N_p-N_{\bar p})$.
Here $\Pi_p$ and $\Pi_{\bar p}$ are the orthogonal projections onto
$\mathcal H_+$ and $\overline{\mathcal H_-}$; on the $n$-particle sector,
$N_p$ and $N_{\bar p}$ are the sums of the corresponding projections over
the $n$ tensor factors. Its candidate maximal direct-sum domain is
$$D(Q_{\rm SI})=\left\{\Psi=(\Psi_n):\sum_{n\ge0}\left\|q_{\rm SI}\sum_{r=1}^n(\Pi_p-\Pi_{\bar p})^{(r)}\Psi_n\right\|^2<\infty\right\}.$$
This is a candidate definition only; no self-adjointness or proved-domain
claim is asserted here.

Measurements in this model are assigned only when a state and a normalized
finite bounded Kraus instrument have actually been constructed. For such an
instrument, the adopted outcome probabilities and positive-probability
conditional states are exactly those of
[[post-qft-constructed-model-and-measurement]]. They are model probabilities,
not observed outcomes. The field definitions are test-smeared: neither
$\Phi_\mu(x)$ nor $\Psi(x)$ is a pointwise operator supplied here, and the
smearing results do not define coincident products or a diagonal restriction.

items.title: CCR/CAR and particle occupations in adopted free models
items.design_state: Complete conditional CCR/CAR and normalized-mode occupation deduction. It does not prove a general spin-statistics theorem.
items.physical_scope: Conditional algebraic consequences of the adopted bosonic scalar symmetric-Fock and Dirac CAR-Fock free models. The result concerns normalizable one-particle wave-packet modes; it is not a general spin-statistics theorem, an interacting-field result, or an empirical claim.
items.statement:
Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. In the selected model of
[[post-qft-free-field-model]], let $H_\mu$ be the scalar one-particle Hilbert
space and let $\mathcal K=\mathcal H_+\oplus\overline{\mathcal H_-}$ be the
Dirac particle/antiparticle one-particle space. Let $\Omega_s$ and $\Omega_D$
be their zero-particle Fock vectors. The assignments of $H_\mu$ to bosonic
Fock space and $\mathcal K$ to CAR Fock space are the physical assumptions
of that postulate.

For every unit scalar wave-packet mode $h\in H_\mu$, define
$$|n\rangle_h=\frac{(a^\dagger(h))^n}{\sqrt{n!}}\Omega_s,\qquad n\ge0.$$
These vectors are normalized and mutually orthogonal, belong to the
finite-particle domain, and
$$a(h)|n\rangle_h=\sqrt n\,|n-1\rangle_h,\qquad a^\dagger(h)|n\rangle_h=\sqrt{n+1}\,|n+1\rangle_h,$$
where $a(h)|0\rangle_h=0$. The maximal operator domains supplied by
[[lem-qft-fock-ccr-car]] are
$$D(a(h))=\left\{\Psi=(\Psi_n)\in\mathcal F_s(H_\mu):\sum_{n\ge1}\|a_n(h)\Psi_n\|^2<\infty\right\},\qquad D(a^\dagger(h))=\left\{\Psi=(\Psi_n)\in\mathcal F_s(H_\mu):\sum_{n\ge0}\|a_n^\dagger(h)\Psi_n\|^2<\infty\right\}.$$
Define the one-mode number operator as the composition
$$N_h:=a^\dagger(h)a(h),\qquad D(N_h):=\{\Psi\in D(a(h)):a(h)\Psi\in D(a^\dagger(h))\},\qquad N_h\Psi:=a^\dagger(h)(a(h)\Psi).$$
The displayed finite-particle vectors $|n\rangle_h$ belong to $D(N_h)$ and
satisfy $N_h|n\rangle_h=n|n\rangle_h$.

For every unit Dirac particle mode $u\in\mathcal H_+$ or antiparticle mode
$u\in\overline{\mathcal H_-}$, regarded as a vector of $\mathcal K$, the
bounded operator $N_u=c^\dagger(u)c(u)$ is an orthogonal projection. The
one-mode subspace generated by $u$ is the closed span of
$\{(c^\dagger(u))^n\Omega_D:n\ge0\}$. It is spanned by $\Omega_D$ and
$c^\dagger(u)\Omega_D$; the latter is normalized and
$c^\dagger(u)^2=0$. Thus a single Dirac CAR mode has occupation $0$ or $1$.
All statements are conditional on the adopted representations and
$\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. They do not derive which statistics nature assigns to
all fields and do not assert an experimental observation.

items.statement:
Choose a unit scalar wave-packet mode $h$ and a unit Dirac particle or
antiparticle mode $u$. The states and operators below are those of the
conditional model theorem [[pthm-qft-free-fock-statistics]].

For the bosonic mode, let $|n\rangle_h$ be the normalized $n$-occupation
vector. We also construct a normalized Fock vector whose annihilation image
is not square-summable, so the maximal annihilation operator is not defined
on every Fock vector.

For the fermionic mode, the one-particle vector
$c^\dagger(u)\Omega_D$ has unit norm, while two creations in that same mode
vanish. This calculation concerns one normalized CAR mode in the adopted
representation; it is not a general spin-statistics argument.

items.design_state: Defines the SI and natural normalization dictionary for charge, potential, field strength and gauge functions.
items.physical_scope: Charge and gauge-field conversions for the selected flat-space QED model, in the stated SI and natural normalizations; no charge value, running law, regulator, boundary charge sector, or interacting continuum construction is inferred.
items.statement:
Use the oriented, time-oriented Minkowski model, length coordinates, metric,
and SI/natural dictionary of [[def-qft-framework-units]], with
$\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$ and $x^0=ct$. Use the gamma matrices,
Dirac adjoint, and effective Clifford metric of
[[def-qft-qed-gauge-data]]: $\gamma^0=\beta$, $\{\gamma^a,\gamma^b\}=-2\eta^{ab}I_4$,
and $\bar\psi=\psi^\dagger\beta$. Assume Countable Choice
[[def-countable-choice]] for the mathematical QFT gauge-data supplier; the
unit conversions below do not themselves spend a choice principle.

Identify the SI charge and mass symbols $q,m$ in
[[def-qft-qed-gauge-data]] with $q_{\rm SI},m_{\rm SI}$ here. Its natural
coupling $g$ is $q_{\rm n}$ below, and its inverse-length mass $\mu$ is the
same $m_{\rm SI}c/\hbar$.

Let $q_{\rm SI}\in\mathbb R$ be a selected charge parameter in coulombs and
$m_{\rm SI}>0$ a selected rest-mass parameter in kilograms. They are inputs
of the chosen model; neither is derived from Maxwell's equations. Set
$\mu=m_{\rm SI}c/\hbar$ in $\mathrm m^{-1}$ and
$q_{\rm n}=q_{\rm SI}\sqrt{\mu_0c/\hbar}$, which is dimensionless under the
framework units of [[def-qft-framework-units]]. For an electron use
$q_{\rm SI}=-e_{\rm SI}$ and
$e_{\rm n}=e_{\rm SI}\sqrt{\mu_0c/\hbar}>0$, so $q_{\rm n}=-e_{\rm n}$.
Use $\varepsilon_0=(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}$ with the measured current-SI
$\mu_0$ of [[def-qft-framework-units]]. These definitions therefore do not
assign an exact numerical value to $q_{\rm n}$, $e_{\rm n}$, or
$\varepsilon_0$.

In a named inertial chart, let $A^\mu_{\rm SI}=(\varphi/c,\mathbf A)$ be the
electromagnetic potential when one is supplied, with components in
$\mathrm{T\,m}$ under [[def-em-si-conventions]] and
[[def-em-electromagnetic-tensor]]. Define the canonical potential and
field-strength components by

$$a^\mu:=\frac{A^\mu_{\rm SI}}{\sqrt{\mu_0\hbar c}},\qquad f^{\mu\nu}:=\frac{F^{\mu\nu}_{\rm SI}}{\sqrt{\mu_0\hbar c}}.$$

They have engineering dimensions $\mathrm m^{-1}$ and $\mathrm m^{-2}$,
respectively. With the metric-lowered potential
$A_{{\rm SI},a}=\eta_{ab}A^b_{\rm SI}$, the potential component convention is
$A_{{\rm SI},0}=-\varphi/c$ and $A_{{\rm SI},i}=A_i$. The covariant derivative
in the selected QED model is

$$D_a:=\partial_a-iq_{\rm n}a_a =\partial_a-\frac{iq_{\rm SI}}{\hbar}A_{{\rm SI},a},$$

since $q_{\rm n}a_a=q_{\rm SI}A_{{\rm SI},a}/\hbar$. Both terms in $D_a$
have unit $\mathrm m^{-1}$. If the SI gauge function $\chi$ has unit
$\mathrm{Wb}=\mathrm{T\,m^2}$, then $q_{\rm SI}\chi/\hbar$ is dimensionless;
the corresponding natural gauge function
$\lambda=\chi/\sqrt{\mu_0\hbar c}$ is dimensionless and
$q_{\rm n}\lambda=q_{\rm SI}\chi/\hbar$. These conversions apply to smooth
local gauge transformations; they assert no boundary condition, asymptotic
charge sector, or global gauge-fixing result.

If a separately specified finite regulator introduces Hamiltonian
eigenvalues, they have unit joule; this definition introduces no regulator.
The field components and units refer to the selected inertial chart, not to a
new observer congruence or a cross-framework identification.

items.title: Positive transverse free photon model
items.design_state: Adopts the positive transverse free photon model conditionally on the actual QFT-MG01 carriers and current EM model conventions.
items.physical_scope: The selected source-free, flat Minkowski Maxwell photon model with a positive transverse one-particle Hilbert space, its constructed bosonic Fock representation and free dynamics, and actual smeared field-strength and bounded Weyl observables; no interacting continuum QED or empirical outcome is asserted.
items.statement:
Adopt the following specified free-photon model in the oriented,
time-oriented affine Minkowski spacetime and length coordinates of
[[def-qft-framework-units]], with metric $(-,+,+,+)$ and $x^0=ct$. The
classical electromagnetic input is the smooth source-free branch of
[[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]]; the electromagnetic two-form and its potential
components are those of [[def-em-electromagnetic-tensor]], and a supplied
potential is subject to [[def-em-gauge-transformation]]. These EM suppliers
are physical input and conventions: they do not by themselves construct a
quantum representation.

For almost every $\mathbf k\in\mathbb R^3\setminus\{0\}$, set
$\mathbf n=\mathbf k/|\mathbf k|$ and
$P_T(\mathbf k)=I_3-\mathbf n\mathbf n^{\mathsf T}$. The mathematical
definition [[def-qft-photon-transverse-space]] specifies the positive
one-photon Hilbert space

$$\mathcal H_T= \{u\in L^2(\mathbb R^3,d^3\mathbf k;\mathbb C^3): \mathbf k\cdot u(\mathbf k)=0\text{ for almost every }\mathbf k\},$$

with the inherited pairing
$\langle u,v\rangle_2=\int\overline{u(\mathbf k)}\cdot v(\mathbf k)\,d^3\mathbf k$,
linear in the second variable as in [[def-qft-fock-and-test-spaces]]. The
value assigned to $P_T$ at
$\mathbf k=0$ is immaterial because that point has Lebesgue measure zero; no
continuous polarization frame over all momentum directions is chosen. Adopt
the bosonic Fock representation $\mathcal F_s(\mathcal H_T)$ and the free
Hamiltonian

$$H_\gamma=\hbar c\,d\Gamma(|\mathbf k|),$$

where on the $n$-photon sector $d\Gamma(|\mathbf k|)$ is multiplication by
$\sum_{r=1}^n|\mathbf k_r|$ and is zero on the vacuum sector. Its exact
self-adjoint domain and the unitary mass-cone action are those in the
mathematical supplier [[lem-qft-photon-covariance-spectrum]]. The actual
smeared field-strength distributions and bounded Weyl operators are those
constructed in [[lem-qft-photon-local-weyl-observables]]; a pointwise
potential or field-strength operator is not asserted to exist. These
mathematical suppliers are draft carriers with mixed current Step 1 status: the
transverse-space, null-quotient, covariance-spectrum, framework-units, and
C01 measurement carriers have current ready records; the local-Weyl carrier is
escalated through its field-strength prerequisite. Readiness records are not
independent approval, and every use remains conditional on the exact statement
and proof supplied.

For the physical interpretation of an actually constructed state and a
supplied normalized measurement instrument, use
[[post-qft-constructed-model-and-measurement]]: Born probabilities are
assigned only to that specified model and instrument. This postulate records
the model's free Maxwell quanta as photons. It does not assert that the
model has been empirically confirmed, and it introduces no interacting
four-dimensional QED Hilbert space, scattering operator, LSZ limit,
asymptotic completeness, or nonperturbative continuum limit. In calculations
using an indefinite four-polarization auxiliary space, only the positive
transverse model or its separately constructed null quotient is physical;
four auxiliary components are not four positive photon states.

items.title: Explicit charged Dirac/Maxwell local coupling model
items.design_state: Adopts a smooth local classical Maxwell–Dirac coupling and its free-field correspondence; no interacting continuum QED construction is claimed.
items.physical_scope: A smooth local classical Maxwell–Dirac coupling in the stated SI/natural conventions, with electron charge q=-e as the selected QED species and the separately adopted free photon and Dirac representations; it asserts no interacting continuum Hilbert space, global PDE solution, pointwise quantum current, scattering operator, or nonperturbative QED construction.
items.statement:
Adopt a smooth local classical Maxwell–Dirac model on an open region of the
flat spacetime specified by [[def-qft-framework-units]]. Let $A_{{\rm SI},a}$
be a supplied real $C^\infty$ electromagnetic covector potential and let
$\psi:\!U\to\mathbb C^4$ be a $C^\infty$ commuting spinor field. The charge
$q_{\rm SI}$ and rest mass $m_{\rm SI}>0$ are model inputs; for the electron
take $q_{\rm SI}=-e_{\rm SI}$. Use the component, metric, Clifford, charge,
field-normalization, and unit conventions of
[[def-qft-qed-gauge-data]], [[def-qft-qed-physical-gauge-quantities]],
[[def-qft-framework-units]], and the electromagnetic suppliers of
[[post-qft-free-photon-model]]. In particular,
$D_a=\partial_a-iq_{\rm SI}A_{{\rm SI},a}/\hbar
=\partial_a-iq_{\rm n}a_a$ and $\mu=m_{\rm SI}c/\hbar$.

Adopt the local action density in natural normalization

$$\mathcal L_{\rm nat} =-\frac14 f_{ab}f^{ab} +\frac{i}{2}\bigl(\bar\psi\gamma^aD_a\psi -(D_a\bar\psi)\gamma^a\psi\bigr)-\mu\bar\psi\psi,$$

where $f_{ab}=\partial_a a_b-\partial_ba_a$ on the region where the
potential is supplied, $\bar\psi=\psi^\dagger\beta$, and
$D_a\bar\psi=\partial_a\bar\psi+iq_{\rm n}a_a\bar\psi$. The physical action
is $S_{\rm cl}=\hbar\int_U\mathcal L_{\rm nat}\,d^4x$ with $x^0=ct$. For
compactly supported local variations this is the adopted classical
Maxwell–Dirac formulation; its Euler–Lagrange consequences are not postulated
as a proof in this item.

For a smooth gauge function $\chi$ in webers, the adopted local
transformation is
$A_{{\rm SI},a}\mapsto A_{{\rm SI},a}+\partial_a\chi$ and
$\psi\mapsto e^{iq_{\rm SI}\chi/\hbar}\psi$. It leaves $F=dA$ invariant and
makes $D_a\psi$ transform by the same phase. This is the covector form of the
SI potential rule in [[def-em-gauge-transformation]]. Gauge functions in the
local variation argument are compactly supported; no assertion is made about
large gauge transformations, nontrivial bundles, boundary charges, or
asymptotic sectors.

The model adopts the separately specified free Dirac representation of
[[post-qft-free-field-model]] and the positive free photon representation of
[[post-qft-free-photon-model]] as the free-field correspondence used to
describe the selected species. This extra correspondence does not quantize
the interacting classical action. In particular, this postulate supplies no
interacting continuum four-dimensional QED Hilbert space, no globally
well-posed coupled PDE, no pointwise operator-valued composite current, no
scattering or LSZ construction, and no regulator-removal or
nonperturbative-existence result.

items.title: Two physical photon degrees and positive free dynamics
items.design_state: Proves the positive transverse fiber, auxiliary null quotient and nonnegative free spectrum conditionally on the named current draft suppliers.
items.physical_scope: The selected flat-space source-free photon model only: positive transverse one-photon states, the auxiliary null quotient, Lorentz-covariant free dynamics, and its exact Hamiltonian domain; no interacting gauge model or empirical photon state is asserted.
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice [[def-countable-choice]] for the selected Fock-space
construction, with the positive constants and physical energy units of
[[def-qft-framework-units]]. In the adopted model [[post-qft-free-photon-model]], for
$\mathbf k\ne0$ set $\mathbf n=\mathbf k/|\mathbf k|$ and
$P_T(\mathbf k)=I_3-\mathbf n\mathbf n^{\mathsf T}$. Then for almost every
nonzero momentum, $P_T(\mathbf k)$ is a positive orthogonal projection of
rank two, and the positive one-photon Hilbert space is its closed range
$\mathcal H_T\subset L^2(\mathbb R^3,d^3\mathbf k;\mathbb C^3)$. This
description chooses no global continuous polarization frame.

If an auxiliary four-polarization space
$\mathcal K=L^2(\mathbb R^3,d^3\mathbf k;\mathbb C^4)$ with indefinite form
$[\epsilon,\delta]=\int\epsilon^\dagger\eta\delta\,d^3\mathbf k$ is used,
the physical subsidiary space
$\mathcal K_0=\{\epsilon:-\epsilon^0+\mathbf n\cdot\boldsymbol\epsilon=0
\text{ a.e.}\}$ has null radical
$\mathcal N=\{b(\mathbf k)(1,\mathbf n):b\in L^2\}$. The quotient
$\mathcal K_0/\mathcal N$ is isometric to $\mathcal H_T$ with positive
inner product. The physical Fock Hamiltonian
$H_\gamma=\hbar c\,d\Gamma(|\mathbf k|)$ is self-adjoint, nonnegative, and
has the exact domain and strongly continuous Lorentz-covariant mass-cone
action in [[lem-qft-photon-covariance-spectrum]]. The vector-valued
auxiliary space is not a positive state space, and none of its negative
directions is assigned a negative Born probability.

references.title: David Tong, Quantum Field Theory, author-hosted full-text Chapter 6, §6.2
references.locator: §6.2.1 for transverse Coulomb-gauge modes and the two physical polarization components; §6.2.2 for the distinct indefinite auxiliary four-polarization construction and its subsidiary condition.

references.locator: §55, printed pp. 335–338, equations (55.3)–(55.25), for the transverse projection, two helicities, canonical commutator, and free photon Hamiltonian. Formal plane-wave expressions are replaced here by the conditional Hilbert-space suppliers.

items.title: Local covariant free field-strength and Weyl observables
items.design_state: Proves the conditional local field-strength and bounded Weyl-observable properties with the exact test-function normalization and domains.
items.physical_scope: Gauge-invariant observables of the specified positive transverse free-photon Fock model, smeared with compactly supported real tests; local commutativity applies to spacelike-separated supports, while the Coulomb-gauge potential is not claimed local.
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice [[def-countable-choice]] for the constructed Fock
representation. In the adopted model [[post-qft-free-photon-model]], let
$h^{ab}\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^{1,3};\mathbb R)$ be a real antisymmetric
two-tensor test. By the natural field-strength normalization of
[[def-qft-framework-units]], choose each component of $h^{ab}$ with unit
$\mathrm m^{-2}$. Since $f_{ab}$ has unit $\mathrm m^{-2}$ and $d^4x$ has
unit $\mathrm m^4$, $f(h)$ below is dimensionless. The corresponding
one-particle vector $g_h$ has profile unit $\mathrm m^{3/2}$ under the
coefficient formula of [[lem-qft-photon-smeared-potential]]: its effective
test $j^i=-\partial_a h^{ai}$ has unit $\mathrm m^{-3}$, the Fourier
integral contributes $\mathrm m^1$, and the factor $(2\omega)^{-1/2}$
contributes $\mathrm m^{1/2}$. Thus its Hilbert norm under $d^3\mathbf k$
of unit $\mathrm m^{-3}$ is dimensionless, as is the Weyl parameter
$\sqrt2\,g_h$. This is the test normalization adopted here, not a universal
test-function unit. Here $f_{ab}$ is the
natural-normalized field-strength
distribution of the selected free model, corresponding to $F_{ab}$ in the
mathematical free-photon suppliers and distinct from the SI tensor
$F_{{\rm SI},ab}$. Its smearing
$$f(h)=\frac12\int f_{ab}(x)h^{ab}(x)\,d^4x$$
is a well-defined operator-valued distribution on the common finite-particle
domain $\mathcal D_{\rm fin}$, not a pointwise field operator. It is gauge
invariant and covariant under the selected free mass-cone unitary action.
For two such tests with spacelike-separated supports,
$[f(h),f(\ell)]=0$ on $\mathcal D_{\rm fin}$. Let $g_h$ be the associated
one-particle test vector and define the Weyl observable
$W_h:=W_{\rm Segal}(\sqrt2\,g_h)$ as in
[[lem-qft-photon-local-weyl-observables]]. These are bounded unitaries of
norm one; their real and imaginary parts are bounded Hermitian operators
and commute for spacelike-separated supports. No locality claim is made for
a Coulomb-gauge potential.

references.title: David Tong, Quantum Field Theory, author-hosted full-text Chapter 6, §§6.2.1–6.2.2
references.locator: Coulomb-gauge transverse quantization and the separate Lorenz-gauge auxiliary construction in Chapter 6; these formal mode formulas motivate, but do not replace, the local domain proof.

references.title: Mark Srednicki, Quantum Field Theory, author-hosted 2006 prepublication book draft
references.locator: §55, printed pp. 335–338, for the transverse field and physical photon modes. The local smeared field-strength and bounded Weyl construction is supplied by the conditional local mathematical argument.

items.title: Conditional classical charged gauge equations and current
items.design_state: Derives the smooth classical Dirac and Maxwell equations and conserved charge current from compactly supported variations.
items.physical_scope: The smooth local classical Maxwell–Dirac branch on an open flat Minkowski domain, with compactly supported variations and the stated SI signs; it does not assert a global coupled PDE solution, an interacting quantum representation, or a pointwise quantum current.
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice [[def-countable-choice]] for the selected free-field
correspondence in [[post-qft-qed-local-coupling]]. Let $U$ be an open subset
of flat Minkowski spacetime with $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$ and
length coordinates $x^0=ct$. Let $A_{{\rm SI},a}:U\to\mathbb R$ be a supplied
$C^\infty$ covector potential, let
$\psi:U\to\mathbb C^4$ be a $C^\infty$ commuting spinor, and take a selected
real charge $q_{\rm SI}$ and mass $m_{\rm SI}>0$ with the conventions of
[[def-qft-qed-physical-gauge-quantities]] and
[[def-qft-qed-gauge-data]]. Use independent compactly supported smooth
variations of $A_{\rm SI}$ and of both real and imaginary components of $\psi$. If $(A_{\rm SI},\psi)$ is stationary
for the adopted classical action, then

$$\bigl(i\gamma^aD_a-\mu\bigr)\psi=0,\qquad \partial_aF_{\rm SI}^{ab}=-\mu_0j^b,\qquad \partial_aj^a=0,$$

where $D_a=\partial_a-iq_{\rm SI}A_{{\rm SI},a}/\hbar$,
$\mu=m_{\rm SI}c/\hbar$, and
$j^a=q_{\rm SI}c\,\bar\psi\gamma^a\psi$. In laboratory components this
current is $\rho_q=q_{\rm SI}\psi^\dagger\psi$ and
$\mathbf J_q=q_{\rm SI}c\,\psi^\dagger\boldsymbol\alpha\psi$, so
$j=(c\rho_q,\mathbf J_q)$. With $[\psi]=\mathrm m^{-3/2}$,
$[q_{\rm SI}]=\mathrm C$, and $[c]=\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$, the charge density
$\rho_q$ has unit $\mathrm{C\,m^{-3}}$, while $\mathbf J_q$ and every
component of $j^a$ have unit $\mathrm{A\,m^{-2}}$; here $x^0=ct$, so
$j^0=c\rho_q$ has the same component unit as $J_q^i$. Together with $F=dA$
on the supplied potential domain, the field equation and Bianchi identity
have exactly the smooth SI
Maxwell signs in [[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]]. The current and spinor here are
classical smooth commuting fields; this statement is not a construction of a
pointwise quantum composite operator.

references.locator: §6.3.1 for the local Dirac coupling, covariant derivative, gauge transformation, and charge current. Tong uses (+---) and natural units; the conversion below uses the explicitly declared (-+++) and SI conventions.

references.locator: §58, printed pp. 345–347, for the spinor-electrodynamics current, local U(1) transformation, covariant derivative, and Maxwell–Dirac formulation. The source uses Heaviside–Lorentz units and c=ℏ=1; signs and units are translated explicitly.

items.title: Periodic neutral classical Coulomb constraint model
items.design_state: Derives the periodic neutral Coulomb branch and the separate finite-mode classical first-order constraints conditionally.
items.physical_scope: The explicit smooth, periodic, neutral Gauss branch on a flat three-torus, with a zero-mean Coulomb potential, plus the separate finite-mode classical commuting-spinor primary-constraint calculation; no nonneutral periodic solution, continuum quantum density product, or CAR derivation is asserted.
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice [[def-countable-choice]] for the torus Fourier
construction. Let $L>0$, let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be an open time
interval, and let the spatial domain be the flat torus
$\mathbb T_L^3=(\mathbb R/L\mathbb Z)^3$, where $L$ is a positive length
in metres. Coordinates use $x^0=ct$ with $t$ in seconds under
[[def-qft-framework-units]]. Use the smooth classical branch of
[[post-qft-qed-local-coupling]] with smooth periodic electromagnetic
potentials and spinor. Here $\psi$ has the canonical length dimension
$\mathrm m^{-3/2}$ of [[def-qft-framework-units]], so the scalar-potential
source $\rho_q:=q_{\rm SI}\psi^\dagger\psi$ has unit $\mathrm{C,m^{-3}}$.
On stationary solutions it agrees
with the current density in [[pthm-qft-qed-classical-coupling]]. Use the
gamma-matrix and
$\alpha,\beta$ conventions of [[def-qft-qed-gauge-data]]. In Coulomb gauge
$\operatorname{div}\mathbf A=0$, the multiplier equation for any smooth
periodic configuration is
$\operatorname{div}\boldsymbol\pi_A+\rho_q=0$. On the explicitly neutral
branch
$\int_{\mathbb T_L^3}\rho_q(\mathbf x,t)\,d^3\mathbf x=0$ for every $t\in I$,
the zero-mean scalar potential is the unique smooth periodic solution of
$-\Delta\varphi=\rho_q/\varepsilon_0$. With
$\widehat\rho_q(\mathbf n,t)=L^{-3}\int_{\mathbb T_L^3}
\rho_q(\mathbf x,t)e^{-2\pi i\mathbf n\cdot\mathbf x/L}\,d^3\mathbf x$ and
$\boldsymbol\kappa_{\mathbf n}=2\pi\mathbf n/L$, the longitudinal energy is

$$\frac{\varepsilon_0}{2}\int_{\mathbb T_L^3}|\nabla\varphi|^2\,d^3\mathbf x =\frac12\int_{\mathbb T_L^3}\rho_q\varphi\,d^3\mathbf x =\frac{L^3}{2\varepsilon_0} \sum_{\mathbf n\in\mathbb Z^3\setminus\{0\}} \frac{|\widehat\rho_q(\mathbf n,t)|^2}{|\boldsymbol\kappa_{\mathbf n}|^2} \ge0.$$

The corresponding classical Hamiltonian, before imposing the Gauss
constraint, contains

$$H=\int_{\mathbb T_L^3}\left[ \frac{|\boldsymbol\pi_A|^2}{2\varepsilon_0} +\frac{|\mathbf B|^2}{2\mu_0} +\psi^\dagger\!\left(c\boldsymbol\alpha\cdot (-i\hbar\nabla-q_{\rm SI}\mathbf A)+\beta m_{\rm SI}c^2\right)\!\psi +\varphi(\operatorname{div}\boldsymbol\pi_A+\rho_q) \right]d^3\mathbf x,$$

with $\pi_\varphi=0$ the primary multiplier momentum. In a separate finite
mode truncation, fix $N\ge1$ time-independent modes
$u_1,\ldots,u_N\in C^\infty(\mathbb T_L^3;\mathbb C^4)$ satisfying
$$\int_{\mathbb T_L^3}u_j(\mathbf x)^\dagger u_k(\mathbf x)\,d^3\mathbf x=\delta_{jk}.$$
Restrict the commuting spinor field to
$\psi_N(\mathbf x,t)=\sum_{j=1}^Nz_j(t)u_j(\mathbf x)$, where
$z_j\in C^\infty(I;\mathbb C)$ and $\bar z_j=\overline{z_j}$. Under the
canonical field normalization $[\psi]=\mathrm m^{-3/2}$, these modes have
unit $\mathrm m^{-3/2}$ and the amplitudes $z_j$ are dimensionless. This is
only a kinematic restriction of field configurations; the mode subspace is
not asserted invariant under the field equations or to contain a solution
on the neutral branch.

For its finite-dimensional canonical phase space
$\mathcal P_N=\mathbb R^{4N}$, use real coordinates
$(x_j,y_j,P^x_j,P^y_j)_{j=1}^N$ and, for $F,G\in C^1(\mathcal P_N;\mathbb C)$,
the Poisson bracket
$$\{F,G\}=\sum_{j=1}^N\left(\frac{\partial F}{\partial x_j}\frac{\partial G}{\partial P^x_j}-\frac{\partial F}{\partial P^x_j}\frac{\partial G}{\partial x_j}+\frac{\partial F}{\partial y_j}\frac{\partial G}{\partial P^y_j}-\frac{\partial F}{\partial P^y_j}\frac{\partial G}{\partial y_j}\right),$$
extended complex-bilinearly. Define
$z_j=x_j+iy_j$, $\bar z_j=x_j-iy_j$,
$p_j=(P^x_j-iP^y_j)/2$, and
$\bar p_j=(P^x_j+iP^y_j)/2$. These definitions give
$\{z_j,p_k\}=\delta_{jk}$,
$\{\bar z_j,\bar p_k\}=\delta_{jk}$, and all other elementary brackets
zero. Substitution into the adopted action gives the velocity-dependent
part of the finite-mode physical Lagrangian
$$L_{\rm kin}=\frac{i\hbar}{2}\sum_{j=1}^N(\bar z_j\dot z_j-\dot{\bar z}_jz_j).$$
Its primary constraints are
$C_j=p_j-i\hbar\bar z_j/2$ and
$\bar C_j=\bar p_j+i\hbar z_j/2$. For $\hbar>0$ their constraint matrix is
$$M=\begin{pmatrix}0&-i\hbar I_N\\i\hbar I_N&0\end{pmatrix},$$
which is invertible; the reduced bracket satisfies
$\{z_j,\bar z_k\}_D=-i\delta_{jk}/\hbar$ and
$\{z_j,z_k\}_D=\{\bar z_j,\bar z_k\}_D=0$. This finite-dimensional
classical calculation does not derive fermionic CAR. The neutral torus
branch is an explicit hypothesis.
For the selected electron, $q_{\rm SI}=-e_{\rm SI}\ne0$, so a neutral
single-species commuting-spinor configuration has $\psi=0$; no nontrivial
neutral charged classical Dirac configuration is asserted. The finite-mode
constraint calculation is separate and does not claim to be a solution in
that branch.

items.title: Auxiliary negative vector versus physical quotient
items.design_state: Gives an explicit normalized negative-norm auxiliary wavepacket and a positive physical transverse comparison.
items.physical_scope: A hypothetical exact comparison between an indefinite auxiliary four-polarization vector and normalized states in the positive transverse free-photon model; no measurement, negative probability, or empirical event is asserted.
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice [[def-countable-choice]] and the positive transverse
free-photon model of [[pthm-qft-photon-physical-properties]]. Let
$\mathcal K=L^2(\mathbb R^3,d^3\mathbf k;\mathbb C^4)$ carry the indefinite
form $[\epsilon,\delta]=\int\epsilon^\dagger
\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)\delta\,d^3\mathbf k$. For nonzero
$\mathbf k$, put $\mathbf n=\mathbf k/|\mathbf k|$ and define the subsidiary
subspace by
$\mathcal K_0=\{\epsilon:-\epsilon^0+\mathbf n\cdot\boldsymbol\epsilon=0
\text{ almost everywhere}\}$. Fix a wave-number scale $\kappa>0$ in
$\mathrm m^{-1}$ under [[def-qft-framework-units]], and let $\Omega$ be the
momentum ball of radius $\kappa/4$ centered at $\kappa(0,0,1)$. By
[[lem-smooth-bump-between-concentric-euclidean-balls]], translate a smooth
bump $b$ that equals one on the concentric ball of radius $\kappa/8$ and
has support in $\Omega$. Set $g=b/\|b\|_2$, so
$g\in C_c^\infty(\Omega)$ and $\|g\|_2=1$. The auxiliary timelike wavepacket
$\epsilon_{\rm aux}(\mathbf k)=g(\mathbf k)(1,0,0,0)$ has
$[\epsilon_{\rm aux},\epsilon_{\rm aux}]=-1$ but is not in $\mathcal K_0$.
By contrast, a normalized transverse wavepacket in
$\mathcal H_T$ represents a positive physical one-photon state. Therefore
the negative auxiliary norm is not a negative Born probability.

items.title: Hypothetical charged periodic cell violates smooth Gauss
items.design_state: Uses the periodic Gauss constraint to refute a hypothetical nonzero net charge on a boundaryless torus.
items.physical_scope: A hypothetical smooth periodic Gauss-law branch on a flat three-torus with no boundary, puncture, or charge-compensating exterior; nonzero total charge is inconsistent with the stated periodic constraint. No real apparatus or observed charged cell is asserted.
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice [[def-countable-choice]] and adopt the local
classical Maxwell–Dirac action of [[post-qft-qed-local-coupling]]. Also use
the smooth periodic Gauss-constraint conclusion of
[[pthm-qft-qed-coulomb-constraints]] under its stated hypotheses. On
$\mathbb T_L^3$ with side length $L>0$ in metres, choose the electron charge
$q_{\rm SI}=-e_{\rm SI}<0$ and a constant nonzero smooth commuting spinor
$\psi(\mathbf x)=\psi_0\in\mathbb C^4$ in the canonical length normalization
of [[def-qft-framework-units]]. Its source
$\rho_q=q_{\rm SI}\psi_0^\dagger\psi_0$ is smooth and periodic, with SI
charge-density unit $\mathrm{C\,m^{-3}}$ under the stated field normalization,
and its total charge is
$Q=q_{\rm SI}\psi_0^\dagger\psi_0L^3\ne0$. In a hypothetical periodic
configuration with no boundary, puncture, or exterior compensating flux,
no smooth periodic electric momentum can satisfy the derived Gauss
constraint
$\operatorname{div}\boldsymbol\pi_A+\rho_q=0$. The neutral case
$Q=0$ is the separate branch supplied by
[[pthm-qft-qed-coulomb-constraints]] and
[[lem-qft-qed-coulomb-constraint]]. The setup is a thought experiment,
not a report of a physical measurement. The constant spinor is a
hypothetical field configuration; no Dirac stationarity or observed
charged cell is asserted.

items.title: Explicit formal QED vertex/free-line convention
items.statement:
Adopt the following coefficient convention for finite formal QED bookkeeping in
the Minkowski, units, and Clifford conventions of
[[def-qft-framework-units]]. In particular,
$\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$, $h=-\eta$,
$\{\gamma^a,\gamma^b\}=2h^{ab}I_4$, and
$\not p:=\gamma^a h_{ab}p^b$. The inverse-length mass is
$\mu=m_{\rm rest,SI}c/\hbar$ and a declared physical charge $q_{\rm SI}$ has
dimensionless value $q_{\rm n}=q_{\rm SI}\sqrt{\mu_0c/\hbar}$.

A **formal coefficient graph** here is a finite directed graph of interaction
vertices and internal lines with a momentum covector assigned to each line and
momentum conservation imposed at each vertex. It records a coefficient at a
fixed finite or formal order; it is not, by this definition, a convergent
amplitude or an operator on a continuum interacting Hilbert space. For a Dirac
species of dimensionless charge $g$, use $D_a=\partial_a-ig a_a$ and adopt the
vertex factor $ig\gamma^a$. For an electron, $g=-e_{\rm n}$, so the vertex is
$-ie_{\rm n}\gamma^a$.

For $\mu>0$ and off-shell momentum $p$ with $h(p,p)-\mu^2\ne0$, set
$$S_0(p)=\frac{\not p+\mu}{h(p,p)-\mu^2}.$$
The adopted fermion-line coefficient is $iS_0(p)$. In Feynman gauge the
auxiliary covariant photon-line coefficient is
$$D^F_{ab}(k)=-\frac{i h_{ab}}{h(k,k)+i0} =\frac{i\eta_{ab}}{h(k,k)+i0}.$$
The symbol $+i0$ denotes the selected Feynman boundary-value convention when a
distributional line is used; it does not define products of singular loop
distributions. The coefficient $D^F_{ab}$ is a calculational tensor factor,
not a declaration of four positive physical photon polarization states.

For the formal matrix realization, use the coefficientwise inverse specified
by the planned interface [[def-qft-qed-formal-ring]]: if $K_0$ is an invertible
finite matrix and $K(z)=K_0+zV$, the formal inverse is the power series in
$z$; no convergence in $z$ is claimed. The planned off-shell/tree identities
of [[lem-qft-qed-tree-ward]] fix the $h=-\eta$ slash and the nonzero-denominator
conditions. When a time-ordered free distribution is needed, use the actual
carrier $H_\mu$ of [[lem-qft-free-time-ordered-kernel]], for which
$(\Box-\mu^2)H_\mu=i\delta_0$ and whose definition has no extra prefactor
$i$. The distributional use of that carrier is conditional on
[[def-countable-choice]]; the formal coefficient factors above are adopted
independently of that optional distributional identification.

No convergence, loop renormalization, continuum scattering matrix, LSZ limit, or nonperturbative QED existence is asserted.

items.title: Specified finite spatial compact U(1) gauge regulator
items.statement:
Adopt as one selected regulated physical model the finite oriented-graph data
of [[def-qft-compact-lattice-gauge-data]], with finite nonempty vertex and link
sets, compact $U(1)$ rotor variables on links, finite CAR matter at vertices,
fixed integer background $b_x\in\{0,\ldots,s\}$, and the displayed Gauss
operators. The mathematical definition specifies
$\mathcal H_{\rm kin}=L^2(\mathbb T^E)\widehat\otimes\mathcal F_a(\mathbb C^{s|V|})$,
the integer-spectrum electric operators $E_e$, link unitaries $U_e$, and the
Hamiltonian $H=H_0+V_B+V_F$ on its stated maximal domain
$D(H_0)$. This physical adoption does not add an embedding of the graph into
space or alter the mathematical definition's operator domains.

For the physical-unit assignment, the link angles, $E_e$, $U_e$, and finite CAR
operators are dimensionless. Assign units joules to $\lambda_E$, every
$\lambda_p$, and every entry of $M_x$ and $T_e$ in the displayed Hamiltonian;
then $H$ has units joules and $tH/\hbar$ is dimensionless with $t$ in seconds
and $\hbar$ in joule-seconds, as in [[def-qft-framework-units]]. The graph is
finite regulator data, not a coordinate lattice with an assigned spacing.

items.title: Exact Ward/Gauss predictions in adopted regulator
items.statement:
Assume the finite-graph model of
[[post-qft-compact-lattice-gauge-model]] and the Axiom of Choice. Write
$\mathcal U(t)=e^{-itH/\hbar}$ for the unitary group of
[[pthm-qft-lattice-gauge-existence]], and let
$\mathcal H_{\rm phys}=\bigcap_x\ker G_x$ be its nonzero physical sector.

For a bounded operator $O$ on $\mathcal H_{\rm kin}$, define its gauge charge
$q=(q_x)_{x\in V}\in\mathbb Z^V$ by
$$U(\alpha)OU(\alpha)^\dagger=e^{i\sum_x q_x\alpha_x}O \quad(\alpha\in\mathbb T^V).$$
For each normalized $\psi\in\mathcal H_{\rm phys}$,
$\langle\psi,O\psi\rangle=0$ when $q\ne0$. A finite product of bounded
gauge-charge eigenoperators has zero expectation whenever the sum of its
charge vectors is nonzero. If $O$ maps $D(G_x)$ into itself and
$[G_x,O]$ extends to a bounded operator, then
$\langle\psi,[G_x,O]\psi\rangle=0$. These statements also hold for
$O(t)=\mathcal U(t)^\dagger O\mathcal U(t)$; the finite-regulator evolution
preserves gauge charge and the domains $D(G_x)$.

For a fixed vertex $x$, distinct real insertion times $t_1,\ldots,t_n$ with
$n\ge1$, bounded operators $O_j$ that map $D(G_x)$ into itself, and bounded
commutators $[G_x,O_j]$, define ordinary time ordering by placing the factor
with larger time to the left. With
$O_j(t_j)=\mathcal U(t_j)^\dagger O_j\mathcal U(t_j)$ and
$G_x(t)=\mathcal U(t)^\dagger G_x\mathcal U(t)$, the following identity holds
as a distribution in $t$ between normalized physical/domain vectors:
$$\frac{d}{dt}\left\langle\psi,\mathcal T\!\left[G_x(t)\prod_{j=1}^nO_j(t_j)\right]\psi\right\rangle =\sum_{j=1}^n\delta(t-t_j) \left\langle\psi,\mathcal T\!\left([G_x,O_j(t_j)]\prod_{i\ne j}O_i(t_i)\right)\psi\right\rangle.$$
The products are evaluated on the stated common domains and $G_x$ is
bosonic, so no grading sign is inserted.

For a region $R\subseteq V$, define its boundary links by
$$\partial R=\{e\in E:\text{exactly one endpoint of }e\text{ lies in }R\},$$
with $\epsilon(e,R)=1$ for a link directed out of $R$ and $-1$ for a link
directed into $R$. On
$\mathcal D_R=\mathcal H_{\rm phys}\cap\bigcap_{e\in\partial R}D(E_e)$, put
$Q_R^{\rm lat}=\sum_{x\in R}(n_x-b_xI)$. If bounded $O$ preserves
$\mathcal H_{\rm phys}$, maps each boundary $D(E_e)$ into itself, and
$E_eO\phi=OE_e\phi$ for every $\phi\in D(E_e)$ and every $e\in\partial R$,
then $[Q_R^{\rm lat},O]\psi=0$ for every $\psi\in\mathcal D_R$. Consequently,
an operator that changes $Q_R^{\rm lat}$ by a fixed nonzero charge cannot
satisfy all these preservation and boundary-commutation hypotheses while
acting nontrivially on that domain.

There is also a separate conditional continuum implication; it does not assert
that a continuum representation exists. Let $\mathcal H_c$ be a Hilbert space
and $D\subseteq\mathcal H_c$ a common invariant dense domain. For real
$f,g_k\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^3)$, let
$\rho(f),E_k(g_k):D\to D$ be linear assignments and put
$E(\mathbf g)=\sum_{k=1}^3E_k(g_k)$ for real
$\mathbf g=(g_1,g_2,g_3)\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb R^3)$. Fix
$\varepsilon_0>0$ and assume
$$\rho(f)=-\varepsilon_0\sum_{k=1}^3E_k(\partial_k f) \quad(f\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^3)).$$
Let $K\subset\mathbb R^3$ be compact. Suppose bounded $O$ maps $D$ into
itself and $E(\mathbf g)O\psi=OE(\mathbf g)\psi$ for every $\psi\in D$ whenever
$\operatorname{supp}\mathbf g$ is disjoint from $K$. For integers
$R\ge R_0$, suppose real $\chi_R\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^3)$ equals $1$ on a
neighborhood of $K$, $\operatorname{supp}\nabla\chi_R$ is disjoint from $K$,
and, with $Q_R^{\rm cont}:=\rho(\chi_R)
=-\varepsilon_0E(\nabla\chi_R)$, there is $Q:D\to D$ such that
$Q_R^{\rm cont}\psi\to Q\psi$ and
$Q_R^{\rm cont}O\psi\to QO\psi$ for every $\psi\in D$. Then
$[Q,O]\psi=0$ on $D$. If also $[Q,O]\psi=qO\psi$ on $D$ for a fixed
$q\ne0$, boundedness of $O$ implies $O=0$ on $\mathcal H_c$. This clause is
conditional on the displayed common-domain, Gauss, locality and limit
hypotheses only.

items.title: Qualified formal/tree gauge-current identities
items.statement:
Use the coefficient convention of [[post-qft-formal-qed-coefficients]] and
formal ring of [[def-qft-qed-formal-ring]]. Let $\zeta$ denote finite graph
link data, $z$ a formal indeterminate, and
$K(z;\zeta)=K_0(\zeta)+zV(\zeta)\in M_d(\mathbb C\llbracket z\rrbracket)$
with $d\ge1$ and $K_0(\zeta)\in GL_d(\mathbb C)$. For each vertex-angle
tuple $\theta$, let $\zeta^\theta$ and the invertible diagonal matrix
$D_\theta$ be the finite gauge action and phase matrix of
[[def-qft-qed-finite-graph-gauge-data]]. Assume the coefficient matrices
satisfy
$$K_0(\zeta^\theta)=D_\theta K_0(\zeta)D_\theta^{-1},\qquad V(\zeta^\theta)=D_\theta V(\zeta)D_\theta^{-1}.$$
Let $S(z;\zeta)$ be the coefficientwise formal inverse specified by
[[def-qft-qed-formal-ring]]. Then
$$S(z;\zeta^\theta)=D_\theta S(z;\zeta)D_\theta^{-1},\qquad \det K(z;\zeta^\theta)=\det K(z;\zeta).$$
For a real vertex tuple $\theta$, put
$\Theta=\operatorname{diag}_{x\in X}(\theta_xI_r)$,
$\zeta^s:=\zeta^{s\theta}$, and $D_s:=D_{s\theta}=e^{is\Theta}$.
For any coefficient family $A_s=A(z;\zeta^s)$, write
$\delta A:=\left.\frac{d}{ds}A_s\right|_{s=0}$ coefficientwise.
Assume also that
$K_0(\zeta^s)$ and $V(\zeta^s)$ vary differentiably along the gauge orbit
$\zeta^s$. Coefficientwise differentiation then gives
$$\delta S=i[\Theta,S]=-S(\delta K)S.$$
These are finite/formal identities only; the formal variable is not assigned
a numerical value and no convergence is asserted.

For the tree-current clause, take $\mu>0$ and four future-shell momenta
$p,p',q,q'$ with $h(p,p)=h(p',p')=h(q,q)=h(q',q')=\mu^2$, in inverse-length
units, and put $k=p-p'=q'-q$. Let
$$J_1^a=\bar u(p')\gamma^a u(p),\qquad J_2^b=\bar u(q')\gamma^b u(q),$$
where $\bar u=u^\dagger\beta$ and the spinors satisfy the corresponding
positive-energy Dirac equations
$(\not p-\mu)u(p)=0$, $(\not p'-\mu)u(p')=0$,
$(\not q-\mu)u(q)=0$, $(\not q'-\mu)u(q')=0$ and their Dirac-adjoint
left equations, in the $h=-\eta$ convention of
[[post-qft-formal-qed-coefficients]]. For a finite scalar $c(k)$, set
$\Delta D_{ab}(k)=c(k)k_a k_b$. Then
$$J_1^a\Delta D_{ab}(k)J_2^b=0.$$
For either displayed conserved current, the contraction with a covector
$\epsilon_a$ is unchanged by $\epsilon_a\mapsto\epsilon_a+\rho k_a$ for
finite $\rho\in\mathbb C$. If $c(k)$ is a rational coefficient containing
$1/h(k,k)$, require $h(k,k)\ne0$ at the selected momentum; a distributional
$+i0$ boundary value is not a pointwise finite $c(k)$. The adopted off-shell
fermion coefficient has denominator $h(p,p)-\mu^2$ and is used only when
that denominator is nonzero. No internal-line singular product is used here.
The tree clause is limited to these explicit finite contractions and does not
assert gauge independence for arbitrary diagrams.

items.title: Explicit soft-profile family has no strong Fock state limit
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice [[def-countable-choice]], the positive transverse
free-photon model [[post-qft-free-photon-model]], and the exact conditional
mathematical interface stated below. Use the one-particle space
$\mathcal H_T=\{u\in L^2(\mathbb R^3,d^3\mathbf k;\mathbb C^3):
\mathbf k\cdot u(\mathbf k)=0\text{ for almost every }\mathbf k\ne0\}$
of [[def-qft-photon-transverse-space]], with
$P_T(\mathbf k)=I_3-\mathbf n\mathbf n^T$ and
$\mathbf n=\mathbf k/|\mathbf k|$. Use the symmetric Fock sectors and
second-variable-linear pairing of [[def-qft-fock-and-test-spaces]]. Define
$E(f)=\bigoplus_{n\ge0}f^{\otimes n}/\sqrt{n!}$ and
$C(f)=e^{-\|f\|^2/2}E(f)$.

Fix a unit vector $\mathbf e\in\mathbb R^3$, a dimensionless
$\lambda\in\mathbb R\setminus\{0\}$, and inverse-length cutoffs
$0<\epsilon<\kappa$. Put
$$f_\epsilon(\mathbf k)= \lambda\,\mathbf1_{\{\epsilon<|\mathbf k|<\kappa\}} |\mathbf k|^{-3/2}P_T(\mathbf k)\mathbf e.$$
Here $\mathbf k,\epsilon,\kappa$ have units $\mathrm m^{-1}$,
$\hbar c$ has units joule-metres, and $f_\epsilon$ has momentum-wavefunction
units $\mathrm m^{3/2}$. Let $d\Omega$ be standard surface area measure on
$S^2$. On sector $n$, let $N$ multiply by $n$ and let
$H_\gamma=\hbar c\,d\Gamma(|\mathbf k|)$ act by the maximal multiplier
$\hbar c\sum_{j=1}^n|\mathbf k_j|$, with zero on the vacuum, as in the
planned free-photon model. With $C_\lambda=8\pi\lambda^2/3$, the conditional
coherent-family result gives
$$\langle C(f_\epsilon),NC(f_\epsilon)\rangle =C_\lambda\log(\kappa/\epsilon),\qquad \langle C(f_\epsilon),H_\gamma C(f_\epsilon)\rangle =\hbar c C_\lambda(\kappa-\epsilon).$$
Each $C(f_\epsilon)$ is a normalized vector in the number and energy
operator domains. As $\epsilon\downarrow0$, this family has no norm limit,
even after arbitrary phase choices, and converges weakly to zero; zero is not
a normalized state. This exact free-model family does not construct an
interacting charged sector or scattering limit and reports no observation of
photon emission.

finite-graph model of [[pthm-qft-lattice-gauge-ward]]. Let

boundary domain $D(E_e)$ into itself, and satisfies
$E_eO\phi=OE_e\phi$ for all $\phi\in D(E_e)$ and all

charge-changing insertion cannot act nontrivially on this domain while
preserving the physical sector and commuting with every boundary electric
operator. This is a fixed-regulator statement; it does not claim a continuum
charged-sector or general locality theorem.

items.title: Formal diagram coefficient-to-observable adoption
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice, $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ [[def-countable-choice]], as required by the cited mathematical phase-space map.

For a specifically named finite tree calculation, adopt its selected formal
diagram coefficient as a **leading perturbative coefficient** with a stated
phenomenological reading. For QED, use the vertex and free-line conventions
of the current draft supplier
[[post-qft-formal-qed-coefficients]]. A particle of natural charge $q_n$ has
vertex $iq_n\gamma^a$; the electron has $q_n=-e_n$ and vertex
$-ie_n\gamma^a$. The rational fermion line is
$$ i\frac{\not p+\mu}{h(p,p)-\mu^2}, $$
for $\mu>0$ and off-shell $p$ with $h(p,p)-\mu^2\ne0$. In Feynman gauge
the auxiliary photon line is
$$ -i\frac{h_{ab}}{h(k,k)+i0}=i\frac{\eta_{ab}}{h(k,k)+i0}. $$
For a finite matrix kernel the coefficientwise inverse in
[[post-qft-formal-qed-coefficients]] is part of the formal convention and
asserts no convergence. If a time-ordered distribution is used, use the
actual free carrier specified there; that identification is conditional on
[[def-countable-choice]]. The displayed pole notation does not define loop
products. In the pair-production channel below the selected muon also has
model charge $-e$, and only the photon line is internal.

For declared incoming spin probabilities, sum over declared final spin
labels, and a specified formal amplitude $\mathcal A$, adopt the
cross-section coefficient map of
[[lem-qft-example-two-body-phase-space]]. Its scattering inputs are
positive-shell energy vectors $p_i=(E_i,\mathbf p_i)$ with
$E_i=\sqrt{|\mathbf p_i|^2+\mathsf M_{i,\rm in}^2}>0$,
$\mathsf M_{i,\rm in}\ge0$, and common future-timelike total
$P=p_1+p_2=k_1+k_2$. The outgoing $k_j$ are on their specified positive
shells. Require $s=h(P,P)>(\mathsf M_1+\mathsf M_2)^2$ for the outgoing
rest energies and positive incoming flux $F>0$, precisely the supplier's
admissible scattering domain. In the center-of-momentum frame it
uses the invariant incoming flux $F$, the two-body measure $d\Phi_2$, and the
final-state factor $S_f=2$ for identical particles or $S_f=1$ for
distinguishable particles, integrated over the full labeled sphere. When
this coefficient is read phenomenologically, the initial preparation,
channel, threshold, and approximation are part of the model statement. No
universal error estimate for omitted terms is implied.

For the scalar examples, separately adopt the constant formal amplitudes
$\mathcal A=-\lambda$ for the quartic contact channel and $\mathcal G=G_E$
for the cubic parent decay, with the units and external normalization stated
at each use. The scalar scattering inputs lie on their stated positive
shells with a common total and the same strict threshold and positive-flux
conditions. For decay, the parent is $P_0=(\mathsf M_0,\mathbf0)$,
$\mathsf M_0>\mathsf M_1+\mathsf M_2$, and its two positive-shell daughters
sum to $P_0$. Their coefficient map is the one in
[[lem-qft-example-two-body-phase-space]]. If a rate $\Gamma$ is reported as
an energy width, the convention is explicitly $\Gamma_E:=\hbar\Gamma$; it
does not supply a survival law.

The readings above do not identify a formal coefficient with an exact
continuum cross section, probability, decay rate, or measured estimate. In
particular they do not construct an interacting continuum $S$-matrix or LSZ
limit, establish convergence of a perturbation series, bound loop or
soft-radiation effects, specify beam or detector cuts, resolve threshold
resummation, or reproduce the statistical analysis of an experiment. A
comparison with observations would require the actual apparatus, sampling,
calibration, uncertainty, and radiative-inclusiveness conditions. The
reported electron magnetic-moment measurements, including the Fan et al.
report listed in the source references, remain source-reported
empirical results and are not premises of this adoption.

items.title: Formal tree scattering and scalar-decay coefficients
items.statement:
Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ [[def-countable-choice]]. Use the fixed Cartesian
Minkowski chart $x=(ct,\mathbf x)$, the geometric metric
$\eta=(-,+,+,+)$, and the distinct algebraic contraction
$h=-\eta=(+,-,-,-)$ of [[def-qft-example-data]]. Let $m,M\geq0$ be the
electron and muon rest energies in joules. In this chart, a future energy
four-vector is
$q=(E,\mathbf q)\in\mathbb R^4$ with $E>0$; it has rest energy $\mathsf M\geq0$
when $h(q,q)=\mathsf M^2$. All four-vector components are in joules, and
$\mathbf q$ is $c$ times physical spatial momentum. Let $p_1,p_2$ be future electron
and positron energy four-vectors with rest energy $m$, and $k_1,k_2$ future
muon and antimuon energy four-vectors with rest energy $M$, satisfying
$p_1+p_2=k_1+k_2=P$ and
$$ s=h(P,P)>4\max(m^2,M^2). $$
By [[lem-qft-example-two-body-phase-space]], choose a proper orthochronous
$h$-Lorentz matrix $\Lambda\in GL(4,\mathbb R)$, meaning
$\Lambda^Th\Lambda=h$, $\det\Lambda=1$, and preservation of the future
causal cone $C_+:=\{(E,\mathbf q):E>0,\ h((E,\mathbf q),(E,\mathbf q))\geq0\}$,
with $\Lambda P=(\sqrt{s},\mathbf0)$.
Its boost construction supplies such a map because $P$ is future timelike.
The **center-of-momentum inertial chart** has coordinates
$x^{\rm CM}=\Lambda x$ on spacetime and corresponding four-vector components
$q^{\rm CM}=\Lambda q$; from here on, four-vector components are in that
chart, so $P=(\sqrt{s},\mathbf0)$. The strict threshold makes
$\mathbf p_1$ and $\mathbf k_1$ nonzero. Define the
scattering angle $\theta\in[0,\pi]$ by
$$\theta:=\arccos\!\left(\frac{\mathbf p_1\cdot\mathbf k_1}{|\mathbf p_1|\,|\mathbf k_1|}\right),$$
using the Euclidean inner product on $\mathbb R^3$.
Write $g=\sqrt{4\pi\alpha}>0$, as in
[[def-qft-example-data]], and
$$ \beta_e=\sqrt{1-\frac{4m^2}{s}},\qquad \beta_\mu=\sqrt{1-\frac{4M^2}{s}}. $$
For the selected formal one-photon tree coefficient, take equal incoherent
weight $1/4$ for the four initial spin-label pairs and sum over final spin
labels. Take the selected muon model charge to be $-e$ as well. Up to an
irrelevant common phase, its amplitude is
$$ \mathcal M_{\rm tree}=\frac{g^2}{s} [\bar v(p_2)\gamma^a u(p_1)] [\bar u(k_1)\gamma_a v(k_2)], $$
where the brackets denote the product of the two currents. This selected
formal amplitude adopts the current draft QFT-G02 line/vertex convention;
it is not an exact amplitude of a constructed continuum theory.

Conditional on this amplitude adoption and
[[post-qft-example-formal-observable-map]], the spin-averaged squared
coefficient is
$$ \overline{|\mathcal M_{\rm tree}|^2} =g^4[3-\beta_e^2-\beta_\mu^2 +\beta_e^2\beta_\mu^2\cos^2\theta], $$
The distinguishable-particle differential and total
cross-section coefficients are
$$ \frac{d\sigma_{\rm coeff}}{d\Omega} =\frac{\alpha^2(\hbar c)^2\beta_\mu}{4s\beta_e} [3-\beta_e^2-\beta_\mu^2+\beta_e^2\beta_\mu^2\cos^2\theta], $$
$$ \sigma_{\rm coeff} =\frac{\pi\alpha^2(\hbar c)^2}{s}\frac{\beta_\mu}{\beta_e} [3-\beta_e^2-\beta_\mu^2+\tfrac13\beta_e^2\beta_\mu^2]. $$
For $\delta=4m^2/s\leq1/2$, the ratio of this differential coefficient to
the coefficient at $m=0$ with the same $M,s,\theta$ belongs to
$[1,1+4\delta]$. This bound is only the incoming-electron-mass effect
within the selected tree coefficient.

The on-shell equations also give
$$ P_a\bar v(p_2)\gamma^a u(p_1)=0,\qquad P_a\bar u(k_1)\gamma^a v(k_2)=0. $$
These are the two current contractions for this finite external-spinor
calculation; they do not assert an all-orders or loop Ward theorem.

For the separate scalar conventions of
[[post-qft-example-formal-observable-map]], let $m_s\geq0$ be a scalar rest
energy, let the incoming $r_1,r_2$ and outgoing $l_1,l_2$ lie on the
positive $m_s$-shell, meaning each $(E,\mathbf q)$ has
$E=\sqrt{|\mathbf q|^2+m_s^2}>0$, and require
$r_1+r_2=l_1+l_2=P_s$ with $s=h(P_s,P_s)>4m_s^2$.
Evaluate in a proper orthochronous center-of-momentum chart taking $P_s$
to $(\sqrt{s},\mathbf0)$ as in [F4]. Let $\lambda\in\mathbb R$ be the dimensionless
constant quartic amplitude parameter. The identical-final full-sphere and
distinguishable total coefficients are respectively
$$ \sigma_{\rm coeff}^{\rm identical} =\frac{\lambda^2(\hbar c)^2}{32\pi s},\qquad \sigma_{\rm coeff}^{\rm distinguishable} =\frac{\lambda^2(\hbar c)^2}{16\pi s}. $$
For a parent at rest of energy $\mathsf M_0>2m_s$ and a constant identical
daughter amplitude $G_E$ in joules, take the daughters on the positive
$m_s$-shell with total $P_0=(\mathsf M_0,\mathbf0)$. The rate coefficient is
$$ \Gamma_{\rm coeff} =\frac{|G_E|^2}{32\pi\hbar\mathsf M_0} \sqrt{1-\frac{4m_s^2}{\mathsf M_0^2}}\quad[\mathrm{s}^{-1}]. $$
If an energy width is named, its convention is $\Gamma_E:=\hbar\Gamma_{\rm
coeff}$ in joules. None of these coefficient statements implies an exact
survival law. The QFT-G02 postulate is a current draft carrier; its use here
retains draft status and does not imply independent acceptance.

items.title: Minimal Dirac magnetic benchmark from the adopted action
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice, $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ [[def-countable-choice]], as in the mathematical Dirac-matrix supplier chain. Also assume the adopted local Maxwell–Dirac action of
[[post-qft-qed-local-coupling]] with electron charge $q=-e$, $e>0$, and
rest mass $m>0$, with $q,e$ in coulombs and $m$ in kilograms. Use the
oriented, time-oriented affine Minkowski spacetime
and inertial chart $x=(ct,\mathbf x)$ with
$\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$ of [[def-qft-framework-units]]. On
$\mathbb R^4$, the static lower potential is
$A_{{\rm SI},a}(x^0,\mathbf x)=(0,\mathbf A(\mathbf x))$: it is independent
of $x^0$, with $\phi=0$ and
$\mathbf A\in C^\infty(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb R^3)$ in SI units
$\mathrm{T\,m}$. Define $\mathbf B=\nabla\times\mathbf A$ in tesla,
$$ \pi_i=-i\hbar\partial_i-qA_i,\qquad H_D=c\sum_{i=1}^3\alpha_i\pi_i+\beta mc^2, $$
as spatial differential expressions on $C^\infty(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C^4)$.
Let $\mathcal D=C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C^4)$ be their common test
domain; smooth coefficients make $\pi_i$ and $H_D$ map $\mathcal D$ into
itself. Use the Dirac matrices and adjoint of
[[def-qft-dirac-projections]] and
$$ \Sigma_i=\operatorname{diag}(\sigma_i,\sigma_i),\qquad S_i=\frac{\hbar}{2}\Sigma_i. $$
The matrices $\alpha_i,\beta,\Sigma_i$ are dimensionless,
$S_i$ has units $\mathrm{J\,s}$, $\pi_i$ has units
$\mathrm{kg\,m\,s^{-1}}$, and $H_D$ has units joules. Let
$\psi:\mathbb R^4\to\mathbb C^4$ be a smooth spacetime spinor field. For a compactly supported direction
$\xi\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^4;\mathbb C^4)$, holding $A$ fixed and
using real $\varepsilon$, define
$$\delta_\xi S_{\rm cl}:=\left.\frac{d}{d\varepsilon}\right|_{\varepsilon=0}\hbar\int_{\mathbb R^4}\bigl(\mathcal L_{\rm nat}[\psi+\varepsilon\xi,A]-\mathcal L_{\rm nat}[\psi,A]\bigr)\,d^4x,$$
where $\mathcal L_{\rm nat}$ is the adopted density in
[[post-qft-qed-local-coupling]]. The integrand has compact support, so this
variation is finite. Assume $\delta_\xi S_{\rm cl}=0$ for every such $\xi$.
Then the compactly supported spinor-variation Euler–Lagrange equation of the
adopted action holds pointwise as a differential equation. In the natural
action normalization of [[def-qft-framework-units]], $\psi$ has engineering
length degree $-3/2$, and this equation is
$$ i\hbar\partial_t\psi=H_D\psi $$
for this pure magnetic specialization. Independently of this condition on
$\psi$, on $\mathcal D$ the spatial differential expression satisfies
$$ H_D^2=m^2c^4I_4+c^2(\boldsymbol\pi^2-q\hbar\boldsymbol\Sigma\cdot\mathbf B). $$
Writing the formal first-order square-root coefficient as
$mc^2+K/(2m)$, where
$K=\boldsymbol\pi^2-q\hbar\boldsymbol\Sigma\cdot\mathbf B$, the spin
term is $-(q/m)\mathbf S\cdot\mathbf B$. Under the explicitly chosen
magnetic-energy convention
$$ H_{\rm mag}=-\boldsymbol\mu_{\rm mag}\cdot\mathbf B,\qquad \boldsymbol\mu_{\rm mag}=g_s\frac{q}{2m}\mathbf S, $$
where $H_{\rm mag}$ is an energy-valued matrix coefficient in joules,
$\boldsymbol\mu_{\rm mag}$ is a $4\times4$ matrix-valued magnetic moment
coefficient with units $\mathrm{A\,m^2}$, and $g_s$ is dimensionless.
Comparing the coefficient of
$\mathbf S\cdot\mathbf B$ as a linear-form coefficient gives $g_s=2$ for
this minimal tree coefficient.
The Dirac equation is asserted only for fields satisfying the stated
stationarity condition. The square and coefficient are formal on the stated
test domain; no magnetic self-adjoint closure, full spectrum, radiative
correction, or empirical measurement is asserted.

items.title: Massless formal annihilation angular contrast
items.statement:
Use the massless $m=M=0$ case of the formal tree theorem
[[pthm-qft-example-formal-scattering-decay]], including its stated
$\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ hypothesis, with $s>0$. Explicitly take
incoming $p_1,p_2$ and outgoing $k_1,k_2$ on the positive massless shell,
so each $(E,\mathbf q)$ has $E=|\mathbf q|>0$, with
$p_1+p_2=k_1+k_2=P$ and $h(P,P)=s>0$. Use the theorem's proper
orthochronous center-of-momentum chart $\Lambda P=(\sqrt{s},\mathbf0)$;
$\theta$ is the Euclidean angle between the nonzero spatial parts of
$\Lambda p_1$ and $\Lambda k_1$. The differential
coefficient at $\theta=0$ is twice its value at $\theta=\pi/2$; integrating
over the full sphere gives
$$ \sigma_{\rm coeff}=\frac{4\pi\alpha^2(\hbar c)^2}{3s}. $$
All three quantities are formal coefficients in the adopted map, not event
counts or exact measured cross sections.

items.title: Scalar symmetry factor and conditional lifetime model
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice, $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ [[def-countable-choice]], as
required by the cited phase-space map and the Borel restriction of Lebesgue
measure.

Let $s>0$, dimensionless $\lambda\in\mathbb R$, parent energy
$\mathsf M_0>0$, and
$G_E\in\mathbb C\setminus\{0\}$ in joules. For scattering, take the incoming $p_1,p_2$ and outgoing $k_1,k_2$
on the positive massless scalar shell, each $(E,\mathbf q)$ having
$E=|\mathbf q|>0$, with common total
$p_1+p_2=k_1+k_2=P$, $h(P,P)=s>0$, and evaluate the coefficient in a
proper orthochronous center-of-momentum chart
$\Lambda P=(\sqrt{s},\mathbf0)$ as in the phase-space supplier.
For decay, take massless positive-shell daughters summing to the rest parent
$P_0=(\mathsf M_0,\mathbf0)$. With these data the identical
final-state quartic total coefficient is
$$ \sigma_{\rm coeff}^{\rm identical} =\frac{\lambda^2(\hbar c)^2}{32\pi s}, $$
and the distinguishable-final coefficient is twice this value. The
identical-daughter decay-rate coefficient is
$$ \Gamma_{\rm coeff}=\frac{|G_E|^2}{32\pi\hbar\mathsf M_0} \quad[\mathrm{s}^{-1}]. $$
Set $\Gamma:=\Gamma_{\rm coeff}>0$. For the lifetime calculation only, let
$(\Xi,\mathcal F,\mathbb P)$ be a probability space in the sense of
[[def-probability-measure]]: $\mathcal F$ is a sigma-algebra on $\Xi$, and
$\mathbb P$ is a countably additive measure with $\mathbb P(\Xi)=1$. Let
$\mathcal B([0,\infty))$ be the sigma-algebra generated by sets
$U\cap[0,\infty)$ for open $U\subseteq\mathbb R$, as in
[[def-borel-sigma-algebra]]. Let
$T:\Xi\to[0,\infty)$ be a parent lifetime measured in seconds and measurable
in the explicit sense that $T^{-1}(B)\in\mathcal F$ for every
$B\in\mathcal B([0,\infty))$. Define its law by
$\mu_T(B):=\mathbb P(T^{-1}(B))$ on those Borel sets. Let $\ell$ denote
one-dimensional Lebesgue measure from
[[def-lebesgue-measure-and-the-lebesgue-sigma-algebra]], restricted to
$\mathcal B([0,\infty))$; this restriction is a measure by
[[thm-borel-sets-are-lebesgue-measurable]] under the stated Countable Choice
assumption. Separately assume the exponential lifetime model, defined by
$$\mu_T(B)=\int_B\Gamma e^{-\Gamma t}\,d\ell(t)\quad\text{for every }B\in\mathcal B([0,\infty)).$$
It gives $P_{\rm surv}(t):=\mathbb P(T^{-1}((t,\infty)))=e^{-\Gamma t}$ for
$t\geq0$. Define the
mean lifetime as $\mathbb E[T]:=\int_{[0,\infty)}t\,d\mu_T(t)$, and define
the half-life $t_{1/2}$ by $P_{\rm surv}(t_{1/2})=1/2$. Then the mean
lifetime is $1/\Gamma$ and the half-life is $\ln 2/\Gamma$. The exponential
law is not a consequence of the formal coefficient calculation.

references.title: David Tong, Quantum Field Theory, Chapter 3 §§3.5.3 and 3.6

items.title: Minimal Dirac spin and orbital coefficient comparison
items.statement:
Take $q=-e$ with $e>0$, $m>0$, and a constant field
$\mathbf B=B_0\hat z$ with $B_0>0$. It is realized by the smooth SI
potential
$$ \mathbf A(x,y,z)=\frac{B_0}{2}(-y,x,0),\qquad \phi=0, $$
for which $\nabla\times\mathbf A=B_0\hat z$, where $\hat z=(0,0,1)$.
Under the Countable Choice and adopted-action hypotheses of
[[pthm-qft-example-dirac-magnetic-benchmark]], the formal spin term is
$-(q/m)\mathbf S\cdot\mathbf B=(e/m)S_zB_0$. Since
$\Sigma_z=\operatorname{diag}(1,-1,1,-1)$, its two spin eigenvalue
coefficients are
$$ \Delta E_{\uparrow,\downarrow}=\pm\frac{e\hbar B_0}{2m},\qquad \Delta E_{\rm gap}=\frac{e\hbar B_0}{m}. $$
Define the comparison orbital coefficient by
$\omega_{c,\rm orb}:=eB_0/m$ and
$\nu_{c,\rm orb}:=\omega_{c,\rm orb}/(2\pi)$. The cyclic coefficient
frequency of the spin gap is
$$ \nu_{s,\rm coeff}:=\frac{\Delta E_{\rm gap}}{2\pi\hbar} =\frac{eB_0}{2\pi m}=\nu_{c,\rm orb}. $$
This is a comparison of formal minimal coefficients. It is not the full
Landau spectrum, a radiative correction, a prediction of zero measured
anomaly, or a laboratory measurement.

items.title: Bosonic Fock number operator and counting PVM
items.statement:
Let $H$ be a complex Hilbert space and let
$$\mathcal F_s(H)=\bigoplus_{n=0}^{\infty}H_s^{(n)}$$
be its bosonic Fock Hilbert space under
[[def-qft-fock-and-test-spaces]]. A vector is a square-summable sequence
$\Psi=(\Psi_n)_{n\ge0}$ with $\Psi_n\in H_s^{(n)}$.

Define the number operator $N$ by
$$D(N)=\left\{\Psi\in\mathcal F_s(H): \sum_{n=0}^{\infty}n^2\|\Psi_n\|^2<\infty\right\},\qquad (N\Psi)_n=n\Psi_n.$$

For every Borel set $B\subseteq\mathbb R$, define the sector projection
$$E_N(B)\Psi=\bigl(\mathbf1_B(n)\Psi_n\bigr)_{n\ge0},\qquad P_n:=E_N(\{n\}).$$
The definitions specify a candidate number observable and its candidate
spectral projections. They assign no physical probability; well-definedness,
self-adjointness, and the projection-valued-measure property are established
by [[thm-qft-x03-photon-count-pvm]].

references.title: Mark Srednicki, Quantum Field Theory, author-hosted 2006 prepublication book draft, §55 “Electrodynamics in Coulomb Gauge,” printed pp. 335–338

items.title: The Fock number operator has its sector counting PVM
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice [[def-countable-choice]]. Let $H$ be a complex Hilbert
space, and let $N$, $E_N(B)$, and $P_n$ be as in
[[def-qft-x03-photon-count-pvm]]. Then $N$ is self-adjoint on its stated
domain and $E_N$ is a projection-valued measure on the Borel subsets of
$\mathbb R$. It is the sector counting resolution: $E_N(B)$ keeps exactly the
sectors whose integer label lies in $B$, and $N$ multiplies sector $n$ by $n$.
For any finite Borel partition $(B_a)_{a=1}^m$ of $\mathbb R$, the projections
$E_N(B_a)$ are mutually orthogonal and sum to the identity.

items.title: Regulated soft coherent photon-count prediction
items.statement:
Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ [[def-countable-choice]]. Use the SI/natural
normalizations of [[def-qft-framework-units]] and
[[def-qft-example-data]], in particular the spacetime metric
$\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$, the algebraic energy-momentum metric
$h=-\eta=\operatorname{diag}(1,-1,-1,-1)$, and the dimensionless coupling
$g_{\mathrm{em}}$ with $g_{\mathrm{em}}^2=4\pi\alpha$. For a finite nonempty
index set $i=1,\ldots,m$, take rest energies $M_i>0$ in joules and energy-momentum
vectors $p_i=(E_i,\mathbf p_i)\in\mathbb R^4$ with components in joules,
$E_i>0$, and $E_i^2-|\mathbf p_i|^2=M_i^2$. The sign $E_i>0$ selects the
future mass shell in the adopted $(-,+,+,+)$ spacetime convention. Put
$\mathbf v_i=\mathbf p_i/E_i$, so $|\mathbf v_i|<1$. Choose signs
$s_i\in\{-1,+1\}$ and real dimensionless charges
$Q_i$ satisfying $\sum_i s_iQ_i=0$. These are prescribed current data, not
dynamical charged-particle trajectories.

For $\mathbf n\in S^2$, let $q=(\omega,\omega\mathbf n)$ with photon energy
$\omega>0$ in joules and define
$$p_i\cdot q:=E_i\omega-\mathbf p_i\cdot(\omega\mathbf n),\qquad J^\mu(q):=\sum_{i=1}^m s_iQ_i\frac{p_i^\mu}{p_i\cdot q},\qquad K^\mu(\mathbf n):=\omega J^\mu(\omega,\omega\mathbf n).$$
The dot in this current formula is $h$-contraction; in particular
$p_i\cdot q=\omega E_i(1-\mathbf v_i\cdot\mathbf n)>0$. Choose measurable
real orthonormal spatial polarizations $\epsilon_1(\mathbf n),\epsilon_2(\mathbf n)$
with $\mathbf n\cdot\epsilon_r(\mathbf n)=0$ almost everywhere. Put
$\epsilon_r^\mu=(0,\epsilon_r)$ and
$K\cdot\epsilon_r:=-\mathbf K\cdot\epsilon_r$. Define the finite nonnegative
angular coefficient
$$C:=\frac{g_{\mathrm{em}}^2}{2(2\pi)^3} \int_{S^2}\sum_{r=1}^{2}|K(\mathbf n)\cdot\epsilon_r(\mathbf n)|^2\,d\Omega.$$

For fixed energy cutoffs $0<\lambda<\Lambda<\infty$ in joules, define
$\mathfrak h_E=L^2(\mathbb R^3,d^3\mathbf q/[(2\pi)^3 2\omega];\mathbb C^2)$,
where $\omega=|\mathbf q|$, and
$$h_{\lambda,\Lambda,r}(\mathbf q) =g_{\mathrm{em}}J(q)\cdot\epsilon_r(\mathbf q/|\mathbf q|) \,\mathbf1_{\{\lambda<|\mathbf q|<\Lambda\}}.$$
The current draft mathematical supplier
[[thm-qft-example-soft-current-angular-coherent]] supplies the $\mathbb C^3$
transverse energy-space norm and unitary conversion. The measurable
orthonormal polarization frame gives the pointwise unitary identification
$h\mapsto\sum_{r=1}^2h_r\epsilon_r$ proved in step 3.1; composing it with
that conversion identifies $\mathfrak h_E$ with the positive transverse
one-particle space $\mathfrak h_T$ of [[def-qft-photon-transverse-space]]
by the unitary map below, where for $\mathbf k\ne0$ the notation
$\epsilon_r(\mathbf k)$ denotes the homogeneous extension
$\epsilon_r(\mathbf k/|\mathbf k|)$ of the supplied sphere frame:
$$(U_Eh)(\mathbf k)= \sqrt{\frac{(\hbar c)^2}{(2\pi)^3\,2|\mathbf k|}} \sum_{r=1}^{2}h_r(\hbar c\,\mathbf k)\epsilon_r(\mathbf k), \qquad \mathbf k\in\mathbb R^3\setminus\{0\}.$$
Here $\mathbf k$ is a wave vector in $\mathrm m^{-1}$ and
$\hbar c\,\mathbf k$ is the corresponding energy-momentum vector in joules.
Set $N_\gamma:=C\log(\Lambda/\lambda)$ and prepare the normalized coherent
vector in the free photon Fock space
$$\Psi_{\lambda,\Lambda} =e^{-N_\gamma/2}\bigoplus_{n=0}^{\infty} \frac{(U_Eh_{\lambda,\Lambda})^{\otimes_s n}}{\sqrt{n!}} \in\mathcal F_s(\mathfrak h_T),$$
where the $n=0$ term is the vacuum sector. Let $P_n$ be the number-sector
projection from [[def-qft-x03-photon-count-pvm]] and define
$p_n$ as the model probability assigned to outcome $n$ by the finite
two-outcome projective partition $\{\{n\},\mathbb R\setminus\{n\}\}$.
Then
$$p_n=e^{-N_\gamma}\frac{N_\gamma^n}{n!},\qquad n\in\mathbb N_0,$$
with $0^0:=1$; these probabilities sum to one, the mean photon count is
$N_\gamma$, and the vacuum probability is $e^{-N_\gamma}$. The expected
photon energy is
$$\langle\Psi_{\lambda,\Lambda},H_\gamma\Psi_{\lambda,\Lambda}\rangle =C(\Lambda-\lambda)\ \mathrm J,$$
for $H_\gamma=\hbar c\,d\Gamma(|\mathbf k|)$ of
[[post-qft-free-photon-model]]. If $C>0$, the family has no Fock-norm or
projective-ray limit as $\lambda\downarrow0$ (projective-ray convergence means
norm convergence after allowing a unit-modulus phase for each cutoff), although
its mean energy tends to the finite value $C\Lambda$.

For the prescribed one-charge rest-to-velocity current with final velocity
$v\hat{\mathbf z}$, $0<v<1$, take
$s_{\rm in}=-1$, $Q_{\rm in}=1$, $p_{\rm in}=(M,\mathbf0)$ and
$s_{\rm out}=+1$, $Q_{\rm out}=1$,
$p_{\rm out}=(M\gamma_v,M\gamma_v v\hat{\mathbf z})$, where $M>0$ is the
rest energy and $\gamma_v=(1-v^2)^{-1/2}$. The same coefficient is
$$C(v)=\frac{\alpha}{\pi} \left(\frac1v\log\frac{1+v}{1-v}-2\right)>0.$$
If $C>0$, the cutoff family has no Fock-norm or projective-ray limit as
$\lambda\downarrow0$; the proof below derives this from adjacent-shell
overlaps and does not use the supplier's separate conditional infrared-limit
clause. Its required norm and coherent-state inputs remain conditional on
the inspected draft supplier until its upstream inputs are current. This
prediction concerns only the constructed positive free coherent state and
its count PVM under the adopted physical assumptions. It does not infer that
a full interacting-QED scattering event emits that state or that a detector
realizes this PVM.

Mark Srednicki, Quantum Field Theory, author-hosted 2006 complete prepublication book draft, §§54–56
Roy J. Glauber, “Coherent and Incoherent States of the Radiation Field,” Physical Review 131 (1963), 2766–2788, §§II–III and IX
