items.title: Regular polynomial field functional algebra
items.design_state: Finite symmetric compact coefficient families define the regular algebra and its smooth functional derivative kernels; local diagonal distributions are excluded.
items.statement:
Let $d\ge1$, $X=\mathbb R^d$, and $n\ge1$. Write
$\mathcal D(X^n)=C_c^\infty(X^n;\mathbb C)$ for the complex test-function
space of smooth compactly supported functions
([[def-test-function-space-d-of-an-open-set]]), with its LF topology
([[def-test-function-topology]]). The convergence criterion used below is
that convergent test sequences have one common compact support and converge
uniformly with every derivative
([[thm-sequential-convergence-in-test-function-space]]). Here $C^\infty$
means every coordinate derivative exists and is continuous
([[def-ck-and-multi-index-notation-in-several-variables]]). All integrals are
compact Riemann integrals: each integrand is continuous with compact support,
so restrict it to a compact rectangle and apply
[[thm-continuous-on-a-rectangle-is-riemann-integrable]]. Let
$\mathcal D_{\mathrm{sym}}(X^n)$ be the subspace of kernels invariant under
every permutation of their $n$ $X$-variables. Fields are real smooth
configurations $\phi\in C^\infty(X;\mathbb R)$. For an integer $N\ge0$
and a finite family
$f_0\in\mathbb C$, $f_n\in\mathcal D_{\mathrm{sym}}(X^n)$ for
$1\le n\le N$, define
$$ F_f(\phi)=f_0+\sum_{n=1}^{N}\int_{X^n}f_n(x_1,\ldots,x_n)\prod_{j=1}^{n}\phi(x_j)\,dx_1\cdots dx_n. $$
The pairing is complex-bilinear, with no conjugation on the kernel or field.
An element of $\mathcal P_{\mathrm{reg}}(X)$ is this finite symmetric
coefficient family, evaluated on fields by $F_f$. Pointwise sums, scalar
multiples, and products again have finite symmetric compactly supported
coefficient families: for products, expand the two finite sums and
symmetrize each tensor product $f_m\otimes g_n$. Thus these elements form
an algebra; the product-integral identity follows from Riemann Fubini on a
rectangle containing the compact supports
([[thm-riemann-fubini-on-product-rectangles]]).

For $k=0$, set $F_f^{(0)}(\phi)=F_f(\phi)$. For $1\le k\le N$,
the $k$-th functional derivative kernel assigned to this coefficient
family is
$$ F_f^{(k)}(\phi)(x_1,\ldots,x_k)=\sum_{n=k}^{N}\frac{n!}{(n-k)!}\int_{X^{n-k}}f_n(x_1,\ldots,x_n)\prod_{j=k+1}^{n}\phi(x_j)\,dx_{k+1}\cdots dx_n. $$
For $k>N$ it is zero. Each displayed kernel is smooth, symmetric and compactly supported in its $k$ remaining variables: compactness follows by projection of the finite union of coefficient-kernel supports, and derivatives pass through the finite-compact integrals by [[thm-differentiation-under-the-integral-sign-on-a-compact-rectangle]].
In the term $n=k$, the empty integral and empty product mean simply
$f_k(x_1,\ldots,x_k)$.

The scope is exactly smooth compact coefficient kernels. A local functional
whose higher derivative kernels are distributions on a thin diagonal is not
included merely because its field expression is polynomial.

references.title: Klaus Fredenhagen and Katarzyna Rejzner, Perturbative algebraic quantum field theory, complete lecture notes, section 4
references.locator: Complete 42-page notes, section 4, equation (23) and the discussion of regular polynomial and local functionals.

items.title: The diagonal delta is a distribution supported on the diagonal
items.design_state: Authorized local A-page prerequisite: defines the diagonal delta by its test pairing and proves continuity, exact support, symmetry, and the smooth-kernel obstruction used by the B remark.
items.statement:
Let $X=\mathbb R^4$ and let $\Delta_X=\{(x,y)\in X\times X:x=y\}$.
For $\Psi\in\mathcal D(X\times X)$, define
$$ \langle\delta_{\Delta_X},\Psi\rangle =\int_X\Psi(x,x)\,d^4x. $$
Then $\delta_{\Delta_X}\in\mathcal D'(X\times X)$ is a continuous
complex-linear distribution with support exactly $\Delta_X$, and it is
symmetric under exchanging $x$ and $y$. No nonzero smooth function on
$X\times X$ is supported on $\Delta_X$.

items.title: Bounded Dyson convergence and temporal factorization
items.design_state: Proves norm convergence, uniqueness, unitarity, composition, and separated-time factorization for bounded strongly continuous self-adjoint operators.
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice. Let $\mathcal H$ be a complex Hilbert space
([[def-hilbert-space]]), $I=[a,b]$ with $a\le b$,
and $V:I\to\mathcal B(\mathcal H)$ a strongly continuous family of
self-adjoint bounded operators (self-adjoint means $V(t)=V(t)^*$, using the
Hilbert adjoint of [[def-hilbert-space-adjoint]]) with
$M:=\sup_{t\in I}\|V(t)\|<\infty$. Strong continuity means that
$t\mapsto V(t)\psi$ is norm-continuous for every $\psi\in\mathcal H$.
Here a strongly continuous solution $U:I^2\to\mathcal B(\mathcal H)$ means
that, for each fixed $s\in I$ and $\psi\in\mathcal H$,
$t\mapsto U(t,s)\psi$ is norm-continuous.
Define $U_0(t,s)=I_{\mathcal H}$ and recursively
$$ U_{n+1}(t,s)\psi=-i\int_s^t V(r)U_n(r,s)\psi\,dr,\qquad a\le s,t\le b, $$
where the integral is the vector-valued Riemann integral and is oriented when
$t<s$. Then
$$ \|U_0(t,s)\|\le1,\qquad \|U_n(t,s)\|\le \frac{M^n|t-s|^n}{n!}\quad(n\ge1). $$
For every complex $z$, $U_z(t,s)=\sum_{n\ge0}z^nU_n(t,s)$ converges in
operator norm, uniformly on $I^2$, and is the unique strongly continuous
solution of
$$ U_z(t,s)=I_{\mathcal H}-iz\int_s^t V(r)U_z(r,s)\,dr . $$
For real $z$, $U_z(t,s)$ is unitary (that is, a surjective linear isometry
of $\mathcal H$) and obeys
$U_z(t,r)U_z(r,s)=U_z(t,s)$. If $V_2$ vanishes outside $[a,c]$ and
$V_1$ vanishes outside $[d,b]$, where $c<d$, then
$$ U_z^{V_1+V_2}(b,a)=U_z^{V_1}(b,a)U_z^{V_2}(b,a), $$
with the later-time factor on the left, provided $a\le c<d\le b$. This
identity also holds
coefficientwise as a formal power series in $z$.

references.title: David Tong, Quantum Field Theory, complete author-hosted Cambridge lecture notes, chapter 3
references.locator: Complete HTML chapter 3, section 3.1.1, equations (3.221)–(3.225), the time-ordered Dyson series. Its displayed argument is formal; the norm bounds and strong-continuity proof here are supplied locally.

items.title: Tensor-product tests are dense in smooth compact kernel topology
items.design_state: Proves tensor-test density in the LF topology and coefficient-representation uniqueness by periodic Fourier truncation and product cutoffs.
items.statement:
Let $d,n\ge1$, $X=\mathbb R^d$, and give
$\mathcal D(X^n)=C_c^\infty(X^n;\mathbb C)$ its LF test-function topology.
The finite linear span of elementary product tests
$$ (x_1,\ldots,x_n)\longmapsto\prod_{j=1}^{n}g_j(x_j),\qquad g_j\in\mathcal D(X), $$
is dense. More precisely, for each $\Phi\in\mathcal D(X^n)$, there is a
sequence of such finite sums whose supports lie in one fixed compact product
and whose derivatives of every multi-index converge uniformly to those of
$\Phi$. Symmetrized finite sums are dense in
$\mathcal D_{\mathrm{sym}}(X^n)$. Consequently the symmetric-kernel
representation in [[def-qft-regular-polynomial-functional-algebra]] is
unique: if a finite symmetric-kernel polynomial vanishes on every real smooth
field, every coefficient kernel vanishes.

references.title: Klaus Fredenhagen and Katarzyna Rejzner, Perturbative algebraic quantum field theory, complete lecture notes, section 4
references.locator: Complete 42-page notes, section 4, equation (23); the Fourier-density and uniqueness argument below is supplied locally.

items.title: Regular Wick-star contractions are well defined and associative
items.design_state: Defines distributional Wick contractions for continuous bidistributions and proves closure, associativity, the involution rule, and the generator commutator.
items.statement:
Let $X=\mathbb R^d$, $d\ge1$, and let $W\in\mathcal D'(X\times X)$ be
any continuous complex bidistribution. For a real formal parameter $\eta$
and $F,G\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{reg}}(X)$, define
$$ F\star_W G=\sum_{k\ge0}\frac{\eta^k}{k!}\left\langle W^{\otimes k},F^{(k)}(\phi)\otimes G^{(k)}(\phi)\right\rangle . $$
The pairing is over $k$ independent pairs of variables; $W^{\otimes k}$
is formed by iterated distributional tensor products, not by multiplying
distributions at coincident points. The sum is finite because the inputs are
polynomial. It defines an element of
$\mathcal P_{\mathrm{reg}}(X)[\eta]$, and $\star_W$ is associative.
If $W$ is Hermitian in the sense
$\overline{\langle W,\overline g\otimes\overline f\rangle}
=\langle W,f\otimes g\rangle$, then
$(F\star_W G)^*=G^*\star_W F^*$, where $F^*(\phi)=\overline{F(\phi)}$.
For $\ell_f(\phi)=\int_X f(x)\phi(x)\,dx$,
$$ [\ell_f,\ell_g]_{\star_W}=\eta\bigl(W(f,g)-W(g,f)\bigr), \qquad W(f,g):=\langle W,f\otimes g\rangle . $$

references.title: Klaus Fredenhagen and Katarzyna Rejzner, Perturbative algebraic quantum field theory, complete lecture notes, section 5
references.locator: Complete 42-page notes, section 5, equations (56)–(64), the regular-functional star product and the change-of-kernel normal-ordering map.

references.title: David Tong, Quantum Field Theory, complete author-hosted Cambridge lecture notes, chapter 3
references.locator: Complete HTML chapter 3, sections 3.3.1–3.3.2, equations (3.235)–(3.245), contraction and Wick expansion. The distributional and functional-domain arguments below are proved locally.

items.title: Regular normal-ordering change is an exact star isomorphism
items.design_state: Proves the finite second-derivative exponential gives an exact star-algebra isomorphism for a symmetric distributional kernel shift.
items.statement:
Let $W\in\mathcal D'(X\times X)$, $X=\mathbb R^d$, and let
$K\in\mathcal D'(X\times X)$ be symmetric under interchange of its
variables. Define
$$ \Gamma_KF(\phi)=\langle K,F^{(2)}(\phi)\rangle,\qquad \alpha_K=\exp\!\left(\frac{\eta}{2}\Gamma_K\right) =\sum_{j\ge0}\frac{(\eta/2)^j}{j!}\Gamma_K^j $$
on $\mathcal P_{\mathrm{reg}}(X)[\eta]$. Each sum is finite on each
polynomial because $\Gamma_K$ lowers degree by two. Then $\alpha_K$ is
invertible with inverse $\alpha_{-K}$, and
$$ \alpha_K(F\star_W G)=\alpha_K(F)\star_{W+K}\alpha_K(G) $$
for all regular polynomial functionals $F,G$. Thus the change from $W$
to $W+K$ is an exact algebra isomorphism on this regular class.

items.title: Regular time-ordered contraction coefficients
items.design_state: Defines the translation-invariant bidistribution lift, causal support order, finite time-ordered contractions, and the formal regular S-series. Countable Choice is adopted for the inherited construction of H_mu in lem-qft-free-time-ordered-kernel; the finite contractions need no additional choice assumption.
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice: for every sequence $(E_n)_{n\in\mathbb N}$
of nonempty sets there is a function $c$ with domain $\mathbb N$ such that
$c(n)\in E_n$ for all $n$ ([[def-countable-choice]]). This premise is inherited
from the construction of $H_\mu$ in [[lem-qft-free-time-ordered-kernel]];
the finite contractions below require no additional choice assumption.

Set $X=\mathbb R^4$. Fix $\mu\ge0$ and the $(-+++)$, shell, Fourier, and coordinate conventions
of [[lem-qft-free-time-ordered-kernel]]. That current supplier states that
its relative-coordinate tempered distribution $H_\mu$ is symmetric, agrees
with the ordered Wightman kernels on strictly ordered time supports and on
spacelike-separated supports, and has no prefactor $i$ in its definition.
Its current carrier is a draft with a supplied conditional proof; the formula
below uses that exact interface. Complex integrals of compactly supported
regular kernels use the componentwise Riemann convention in
[[def-qft-regular-polynomial-functional-algebra]]: write the integrand as its
real part plus $i$ times its imaginary part and integrate each real component.

For open $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^m$, $\mathcal D(\Omega)$ is the space
of smooth compactly supported complex tests with the LF topology, and
$\mathcal D'(\Omega)$ is its continuous complex-linear dual, paired
bilinearly with no conjugation
([[def-test-function-space-d-of-an-open-set]], [[def-test-function-topology]],
[[def-distribution]]). Schwartz space consists of smooth functions with all
polynomially weighted derivatives bounded; $\mathcal S'$ is its continuous
complex-linear dual with bilinear pairing
([[def-schwartz-space-and-its-seminorms]],
[[def-schwartz-topology-and-convergence]], [[def-tempered-distribution]]).

For any relative-coordinate distribution $K\in\mathcal S'(\mathbb R^4)$,
define its translation-invariant two-point bidistribution
$\widetilde K\in\mathcal D'(\mathbb R^4\times\mathbb R^4)$ by
$$ \langle\widetilde K,\Psi\rangle =\left\langle K,\ z\longmapsto\int_{\mathbb R^4}\Psi(y+z,y)\,dy\right\rangle, \qquad \Psi\in\mathcal D(\mathbb R^4\times\mathbb R^4). $$
The inner function is a test function: its support lies in the difference
of the two compact coordinate projections of $\operatorname{supp}\Psi$;
each derivative in $z$ is the Riemann integral of the corresponding
first-variable derivative of $\Psi$ over a compact rectangle containing
the fixed compact second-variable projection; iterate the real
single-coordinate differentiation rule over every derivative in $z$ and
apply it to both real components, using the compact parameter-integral
differentiation convention of
[[def-qft-regular-polynomial-functional-algebra]].
On each fixed compact support space, every output derivative seminorm is
bounded by the volume of a compact rectangle containing the second-variable
projection times the corresponding source derivative seminorm. The support
of the output lies in the compact difference of the two projections. Thus
this map is continuous on each fixed-support test space, and hence on the LF
test topology [[def-test-function-topology]].
Thus the displayed formula defines a distribution without multiplying
singular distributions. Write $\mathsf H_\mu=\widetilde H_\mu$.

For $F\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{reg}}(\mathbb R^4)$, define its support as the
finite union of the coordinate projections of the supports of its nonconstant
symmetric coefficient kernels. This is a compact set and is presentation
independent by [[lem-qft-tensor-test-function-density]]. For compact
$A,B\subset\mathbb R^4$, write $A\succcurlyeq_{\mathrm{out}} B$ when
$$ x-y\notin C_-:=\{(t,\mathbf x)\in\mathbb R^4:t\le-|\mathbf x|\} \quad\text{for every }x\in A,\ y\in B. $$
This means the first support has no point in the closed causal past of the
second, using the supplier's fixed inertial chart.

For $n\ge1$, let $\mathcal Q_n$ consist of finite coefficient families in
$n$ independent real smooth fields $\phi_i\in C^\infty(X;\mathbb R)$ of the form
$$Q(\phi_1,\ldots,\phi_n)=\sum_{\mathbf r}\int q_{\mathbf r}(\mathbf x^{(1)},\ldots,\mathbf x^{(n)})\prod_{i=1}^{n}\prod_{a=1}^{r_i}\phi_i(x_a^{(i)})\,d\mathbf x,$$
where $\mathbf r=(r_1,\ldots,r_n)\in\mathbb N_0^n$ ranges over a finite set,
$q_{\mathbf r}\in C_c^\infty(X^{r_1}\times\cdots\times X^{r_n};\mathbb C)$,
and each coefficient is symmetric within every block
$\mathbf x^{(i)}=(x_1^{(i)},\ldots,x_{r_i}^{(i)})$.
$X^0$ is a one-point space; an empty product and an integral over no variables
leave the scalar coefficient unchanged. Here $d\mathbf x$ is the product of
the $d^4x_a^{(i)}$ coordinate volume elements over all variables present.
The product
$\prod_iF_i(\phi_i)$ of regular polynomials is in $\mathcal Q_n$.

For $1\le i<j\le n$, define the one-pair contraction
$D_{\mathsf H}^{ij}:\mathcal Q_n\to\mathcal Q_n$ linearly and termwise on
each block coefficient $q_{\mathbf r}$. It is zero if $r_i=0$ or $r_j=0$;
otherwise it has multidegree $\mathbf r-\mathbf e_i-\mathbf e_j$ and
coefficient
$$q'_{\mathbf r-\mathbf e_i-\mathbf e_j}(\mathbf x')=r_i r_j\left\langle\mathsf H_\mu,(x,y)\longmapsto q_{\mathbf r}(\ldots,x,\ldots,y,\ldots)\right\rangle,$$
where $x$ occupies the first variable of block $i$, $y$ occupies the first
variable of block $j$, and the uncontracted variables $\mathbf x'$ are held
as parameters. The result remains symmetric within each remaining block.
The parameter-pairing theorem
[[lem-distribution-pairing-with-smooth-parameter-families]] makes this
coefficient smooth and compactly supported. The factor $r_i r_j$ counts the
choices of one variable from each symmetric block, so this is exactly one
functional derivative in each of the independent field slots followed by
pairing against $\mathsf H_\mu$.

For $r\ge1$, define full symmetrization by
$$\operatorname{Sym}_r h(x_1,\ldots,x_r)=\frac1{r!}\sum_{\pi\in S_r}h(x_{\pi(1)},\ldots,x_{\pi(r)}),$$
with $\operatorname{Sym}_0$ the identity. For $Q\in\mathcal Q_n$, define
$m_nQ$ by setting $\phi_1=\cdots=\phi_n=\phi$ and replacing each remaining
block coefficient by its full symmetrization across all variables. For a finite-degree $Q$, the
formal exponential is defined coefficientwise by
$$\exp\!\left(\eta\sum_{1\le i<j\le n}D_{\mathsf H}^{ij}\right)Q =\sum_{r\ge0}\frac{\eta^r}{r!}\left(\sum_{1\le i<j\le n}D_{\mathsf H}^{ij}\right)^rQ,$$
which terminates because each contraction lowers total degree by two. The
parameter $\eta$ is formal and fixed by complex conjugation. Define
$$ T_n^H(F_1,\ldots,F_n)(\phi) =m_n\exp\!\left(\eta\sum_{1\le i<j\le n}D_{\mathsf H}^{ij}\right) \prod_{i=1}^nF_i(\phi_i), \qquad T_0^H=1,\quad T_1^H(F)=F. $$
The tensor-product distribution theorem
[[thm-tensor-product-distributions-and-iterated-pairings]] and the
parameter-pairing theorem above make every contraction well defined; no
diagonal product occurs. Symmetry of $\mathsf H_\mu$ makes $T_n^H$ symmetric
in its inputs.

For any $V\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{reg}}(\mathbb R^4)$ and formal coupling $z$,
define
$$ S_z^H(V)=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}\frac{(iz/\eta)^n}{n!}\,T_n^H(V,\ldots,V) \quad\text{with coefficients in }\mathcal P_{\mathrm{reg}}(\mathbb R^4)[\eta,\eta^{-1}]. $$
This is a coefficientwise formal series; the definition asserts no
convergence in $z$, no time-ordered product for singular local functionals,
and no continuum interacting field.

items.title: All regular formal temporal causal-factorization coefficients
items.design_state: Proves all-order formal causal factorization conditionally on the inspected free scalar interfaces and regular contraction calculus.
items.statement:
Assume the current scalar suppliers
[[lem-qft-free-time-ordered-kernel]],
[[lem-qft-smeared-free-scalar]], and
[[lem-qft-scalar-causal-commutator]] at exactly their displayed draft
interfaces. Let $W_\mu$ be the relative-coordinate scalar Wightman
distribution from the smeared-field supplier, and let $H_\mu$ be the
time-ordered relative-coordinate distribution from the time-ordered-kernel
supplier. Form their translation-invariant bidistributions by the construction
in [[def-qft-regular-formal-time-ordering]].

Let $V,U\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{reg}}(\mathbb R^4)$ have compact supports
$A,B$, respectively. If $A\succcurlyeq_{\mathrm{out}}B$, as defined in
[[def-qft-regular-formal-time-ordering]], then
$$ S_z^H(V+U)=S_z^H(V)\star_{W_\mu}S_z^H(U) $$
coefficientwise in $z$. If every difference $x-y$, $x\in A$,
$y\in B$, is spacelike, then $F\star_{W_\mu}G=G\star_{W_\mu}F$ for
regular $F,G$ supported in $A,B$; the corresponding formal series commute
coefficientwise. These are formal identities for regular functionals only.
They assert neither convergence in the coupling nor a local Wick-product or
continuum-interaction construction.

items.title: Local Wick diagonal products need additional prerequisites
items.design_state: Verifies that a nonzero local quartic has a nonzero diagonal second-derivative distribution outside the regular class.
items.statement:
For a nonzero real $g\in\mathcal D(\mathbb R^4)$, the local quartic
functional $L_g(\phi)=\int g(x)\phi(x)^4\,dx$ is not in the regular
polynomial class of [[def-qft-regular-polynomial-functional-algebra]]. Write
$\delta(x-y)$ for the distribution
$\delta_{\Delta_X}$ defined in
[[thm-qft-diagonal-delta-distribution]], and define the diagonal kernel
$K_g$ by
$$ \langle K_g,\Psi\rangle =12\int_{\mathbb R^4}g(x)\Psi(x,x)\,d^4x. $$
The local quartic's second derivative at $\phi\equiv1$ has this kernel.
The verification below shows it is nonzero and cannot be a smooth compact
coefficient kernel, so no other regular presentation can represent $L_g$.
The regular star product in
[[thm-qft-regular-wick-star-associativity]] and the formal time-ordering
construction in [[def-qft-regular-formal-time-ordering]] take regular polynomial
functionals as inputs. Since $L_g$ is not in that class, neither construction
applies to it. Extending either operation across the diagonal requires a
separately stated and proved construction; no such extension or general
causal-renormalization theorem is asserted on this page.

The nonzero hypothesis matters: if $g=0$, then $L_g=0$ is the regular
constant family with all coefficient kernels zero.

references.title: Klaus Fredenhagen and Katarzyna Rejzner, Perturbative algebraic quantum field theory, complete lecture notes, sections 4–5

items.title: Explicit regular quadratic Wick star product
items.design_state: Computes each of the three finite quadratic Wick contraction orders exactly.
items.statement:
Let $f,g\in\mathcal D(\mathbb R^d)$, let
$\ell_f(\phi)=\int f(x)\phi(x)\,dx$, and let $W$ be any continuous
bidistribution. For the regular quadratic functionals
$F(\phi)=\ell_f(\phi)^2$ and $G(\phi)=\ell_g(\phi)^2$, the finite
contraction formula is
$$ F\star_W G =\ell_f^2\ell_g^2+4\eta W(f,g)\ell_f\ell_g+2\eta^2W(f,g)^2. $$
The formula is exact in the formal parameter $\eta$.

items.title: Scaling degree and local extension space

references.title: R. Brunetti and K. Fredenhagen, Microlocal Analysis and Interacting Quantum Field Theories: Renormalization on Physical Backgrounds, §5.1

Klaus Fredenhagen and Katarzyna Rejzner, “Perturbative Algebraic Quantum Field Theory,” in Mathematical Aspects of Quantum Field Theories, ed. Damien Calaque and Thomas Strobl, Springer (2015), Section 7
K. J. Keller, Dimensional Regularization in Position Space and a Forest Formula for Regularized Epstein-Glaser Renormalization, dissertation, §I.1

items.statement:
Fix an integer $n\ge1$, put $U=\mathbb R^n\setminus\{0\}$, and use the continuous complex-linear test-function pairing of [[def-distribution]]. For $t\in\mathcal D'(U)$ and $\rho>0$, define its dilation at the origin by

$$\langle t_\rho,\varphi\rangle:=\rho^{-n}\langle t,\varphi(\cdot/\rho)\rangle,\qquad \varphi\in\mathcal D(U).$$

Positive dilations preserve $U$, so the displayed pairing is defined for every test function in $\mathcal D(U)$. If $t$ is the regular distribution induced by a locally integrable function $g$, change of variables gives $\langle t_\rho,\varphi\rangle=\int_U g(\rho x)\varphi(x)\,dx$.

Convergence $s_\rho\to0$ in $\mathcal D'(U)$ as $\rho\downarrow0$ means $\langle s_\rho,\varphi\rangle\to0$ for every fixed $\varphi\in\mathcal D(U)$. The **scaling degree at the origin** is

$$\operatorname{sd}_0(t):=\inf\{\omega\in\mathbb R:\rho^\omega t_\rho\to0\text{ in }\mathcal D'(U)\}.$$

The infimum of the empty set is $+\infty$; if every real $\omega$ belongs to the set, the infimum is $-\infty$. A finite scaling degree means a real value $\delta\in\mathbb R$. For a distribution $T\in\mathcal D'(\mathbb R^n)$ use the same dilation formula on tests in $\mathcal D(\mathbb R^n)$. An **extension** of $t$ is a distribution $T$ on $\mathbb R^n$ whose restriction to $U$ equals $t$. The degree of divergence associated with a finite scaling degree $\delta$ in dimension $n$ is $\delta-n$. Exact homogeneity of scaling degree $\delta$ means $\rho^\delta T_\rho=T$ for every $\rho>0$.

The definitions use Euclidean dilations about the specified point only. They do not assert that a given distribution arises from a product of fields or that an extension is physically selected.

items.title: Complete test Frechet space and uniform scaling order

references.title: R. Brunetti and K. Fredenhagen, Microlocal Analysis and Interacting Quantum Field Theories: Renormalization on Physical Backgrounds, §5.1–§5.2

Klaus Fredenhagen and Katarzyna Rejzner, “Perturbative Algebraic Quantum Field Theory,” in Mathematical Aspects of Quantum Field Theories, ed. Damien Calaque and Thomas Strobl, Springer (2015), Section 7
K. J. Keller, Dimensional Regularization in Position Space and a Forest Formula for Regularized Epstein-Glaser Renormalization, dissertation, §I.1

items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $n\ge1$, $U=\mathbb R^n\setminus\{0\}$, and $t\in\mathcal D'(U)$ have finite real scaling degree $\delta$. For every compact $K\subset U$ and every real $\omega>\delta$, there are an integer $m\ge0$ and $C<\infty$ such that

$$|\langle t_\rho,\psi\rangle|\le C\rho^{-\omega}p_m(\psi)\qquad(0<\rho\le1,\ \psi\in\mathcal D_K),$$

where $\mathcal D_K$ and $p_m(\psi)=\max_{|\alpha|\le m}\sup_{x\in K}|\partial^\alpha\psi(x)|$ are the fixed-support test-function space and seminorms of [[def-fixed-support-test-function-frechet-space]]. The estimate is uniform over the entire moving-scale family, not merely over each fixed test separately.

items.title: Every finite-scaling-degree punctured distribution has an exact-degree extension

references.title: R. Brunetti and K. Fredenhagen, Microlocal Analysis and Interacting Quantum Field Theories: Renormalization on Physical Backgrounds, Theorem 5.2–5.3

Klaus Fredenhagen and Katarzyna Rejzner, “Perturbative Algebraic Quantum Field Theory,” in Mathematical Aspects of Quantum Field Theories, ed. Damien Calaque and Thomas Strobl, Springer (2015), Section 7
K. J. Keller, Dimensional Regularization in Position Space and a Forest Formula for Regularized Epstein-Glaser Renormalization, dissertation, Theorem I.6

items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $n\ge1$, $U=\mathbb R^n\setminus\{0\}$, and let $t\in\mathcal D'(U)$ have finite real scaling degree $\delta=\operatorname{sd}_0(t)$. Then there exists $T\in\mathcal D'(\mathbb R^n)$ such that $T|_U=t$ and $\operatorname{sd}_0(T)=\delta$. The result applies to arbitrary distributions with finite real scaling degree; it assumes no smooth kernel or pointwise product representation.

items.title: Point-extension counterterms form a finite delta-jet space

references.title: R. Brunetti and K. Fredenhagen, Microlocal Analysis and Interacting Quantum Field Theories: Renormalization on Physical Backgrounds, Theorems 5.2–5.3

Klaus Fredenhagen and Katarzyna Rejzner, “Perturbative Algebraic Quantum Field Theory,” in Mathematical Aspects of Quantum Field Theories, ed. Damien Calaque and Thomas Strobl, Springer (2015), Section 7
K. J. Keller, Dimensional Regularization in Position Space and a Forest Formula for Regularized Epstein-Glaser Renormalization, dissertation, Theorem I.6

items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $n\ge1$, let $t\in\mathcal D'(\mathbb R^n\setminus\{0\})$ have finite real scaling degree $\delta$, and let $\mathcal E_\delta(t)$ be the set of its extensions in $\mathcal D'(\mathbb R^n)$ having scaling degree exactly $\delta$. This set is nonempty by [[thm-qft-finite-scaling-degree-extension]]. If $\delta<n$, then $\mathcal E_\delta(t)$ has exactly one member. If $\delta\ge n$, let $k$ be the unique nonnegative integer with $k\le\delta-n<k+1$ (the floor of $\delta-n$). Then, for any $T_0\in\mathcal E_\delta(t)$,

$$\mathcal E_\delta(t)=T_0+\operatorname{span}_{\mathbb C}\{\partial^\alpha\delta_0:|\alpha|\le k\}.$$

Here a **point-local counterterm** means a distribution whose support, as defined in [[def-support-of-a-distribution]], is contained in $\{0\}$. Thus the same-degree freedom is finite dimensional, with precisely the displayed delta derivatives as its basis; at the threshold $\delta=n$, only a multiple of $\delta_0$ is allowed.

items.title: Exact four-dimensional Euclidean logarithmic scale anomaly

references.title: R. Brunetti and K. Fredenhagen, Microlocal Analysis and Interacting Quantum Field Theories: Renormalization on Physical Backgrounds, §5.1–§5.2

Klaus Fredenhagen and Katarzyna Rejzner, “Perturbative Algebraic Quantum Field Theory,” in Mathematical Aspects of Quantum Field Theories, ed. Damien Calaque and Thomas Strobl, Springer (2015), Section 7
K. J. Keller, Dimensional Regularization in Position Space and a Forest Formula for Regularized Epstein-Glaser Renormalization, dissertation, §I.1

items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. On $\mathbb R^4\setminus\{0\}$ let $u(x)=1/(16\pi^4|x|^4)$, equivalently the square of the displayed Euclidean kernel $C_0(x)=1/(4\pi^2|x|^2)$; interpret $u$ as its regular distribution there. Choose $\chi\in\mathcal D(\mathbb R^4)$ equal to one near $0$. For $\mu>0$ define

$$T_\mu(\varphi):=\int_{\mathbb R^4\setminus\{0\}}\frac{\varphi(x)-\chi(\mu x)\varphi(0)}{16\pi^4|x|^4}\,d^4x.$$

Then $T_\mu$ is a distribution extending $u$, has scaling degree $4$, and for every $\mu,\nu>0$,

$$T_\mu-T_\nu=\frac{1}{8\pi^2}\log(\mu/\nu)\,\delta_0.$$

In particular, no extension of $u$ with scaling degree $4$ is exactly homogeneous, where exact homogeneity means $\rho^4T_\rho=T$ for every $\rho>0$. Coordinates use one fixed Euclidean unit; if units are assigned, $\mu$ and $\nu$ have reciprocal coordinate units, so the logarithm's ratio is dimensionless. This is a Euclidean distribution identity and does not identify a measured coupling or physical beta function.

items.title: Subcritical singularity has a unique same-degree extension

references.title: R. Brunetti and K. Fredenhagen, Microlocal Analysis and Interacting Quantum Field Theories: Renormalization on Physical Backgrounds, §5.2

Klaus Fredenhagen and Katarzyna Rejzner, “Perturbative Algebraic Quantum Field Theory,” in Mathematical Aspects of Quantum Field Theories, ed. Damien Calaque and Thomas Strobl, Springer (2015), Section 7
K. J. Keller, Dimensional Regularization in Position Space and a Forest Formula for Regularized Epstein-Glaser Renormalization, dissertation, §I.1

items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Fix $n\ge1$ and a real $\delta\le n$. Define $g_\delta(x)=|x|^{-\delta}$ for $x\ne0$ and choose $g_\delta(0)=0$; this point value does not affect any integral. On $U=\mathbb R^n\setminus\{0\}$, let $t_\delta$ be the regular distribution induced by $g_\delta$. If $\delta<n$, then $g_\delta\in L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}(\mathbb R^n)$, and its regular extension

$$G_\delta(\varphi)=\int_{\mathbb R^n}|x|^{-\delta}\varphi(x)\,d^nx$$

has scaling degree $\delta$ and is the unique extension of $t_\delta$ with that same scaling degree. At the critical exponent $\delta=n$, $t_n$ still has scaling degree $n$ on $U$, but the regular integral diverges logarithmically at $0$; its same-degree extensions exist but form an affine line $T_0+\mathbb C\delta_0$.

items.statement:
Let $D\in\mathbb Z_{\ge1}$ be the number of Euclidean momentum coordinates. Use the finite undirected multigraph convention of [[def-multigraph-and-digraph-degrees-and-connectivity]]: loops are allowed, distinct edges with the same endpoints are parallel, and connectedness here means that the underlying simple graph obtained by deleting loops and identifying each parallel class is connected.

A **finite quartic graph** is data $\Gamma=(\mathcal V,\mathcal E_{\rm int},\eta,\mathcal H_{\rm ext},(S_v)_{v\in\mathcal V},a)$ with the following properties. The vertex set $\mathcal V$ is finite and nonempty, the internal-edge set $\mathcal E_{\rm int}$ and external-half-edge set $\mathcal H_{\rm ext}$ are finite, and $\eta:\mathcal E_{\rm int}\times\{0,1\}\to\mathcal V$ assigns the two (unoriented, but separately labelled) ends of each internal edge to vertices. Its endpoint set is $\{\eta(e,0),\eta(e,1)\}$, a singleton for a loop; distinct elements of $\mathcal E_{\rm int}$ with the same unordered endpoints remain distinct parallel edges. The internal multigraph $(\mathcal V,\mathcal E_{\rm int},\eta)$ is connected in the sense just specified.

For every $v\in\mathcal V$, the incidence-slot set $S_v$ has exactly four elements. Set $\mathcal S:=\bigsqcup_{v\in\mathcal V}(\{v\}\times S_v)$. The attachment map

$$a:(\mathcal E_{\rm int}\times\{0,1\})\sqcup\mathcal H_{\rm ext}\longrightarrow\mathcal S$$

is a bijection, and for each internal end $(e,j)$ its slot has vertex coordinate $\eta(e,j)$. Thus the two ends of a loop occupy distinct slots. Each external half-edge $h\in\mathcal H_{\rm ext}$ is attached by $a(h)$ to exactly one vertex slot and has no second endpoint. In particular, each vertex has exactly four slots and every slot is used exactly once by an internal-edge end or an external half-edge. Write $V:=|\mathcal V|$, $I:=|\mathcal E_{\rm int}|$, and $E:=|\mathcal H_{\rm ext}|$.

Define the cycle rank and loop count by $L:=I-V+1$. For this mathematical power-counting convention, a single formal loop-momentum integration has assigned degree $+D$: for $\ell\in\mathbb R^D$, Lebesgue measure $d^D\ell$ acquires the factor $\lambda^D$ under $\ell\mapsto\lambda\ell$ for $\lambda>0$. The total loop contribution is defined to be $DL$, the cycle rank multiplied by this one-loop degree; no momentum routing or actual graph integral is part of this definition. Assign degree $-2$ to each internal scalar-propagator factor and degree $0$ to each quartic-vertex factor. For $q=(q_1,\ldots,q_D)\in\mathbb R^D\setminus\{0\}$ use the Euclidean norm $|q|^2:=\sum_{j=1}^Dq_j^2$. For example, if $m\ge0$, then $(|q|^2+m^2)^{-1}$ has assigned ultraviolet degree $-2$, since

$$\lim_{\lambda\to\infty}\lambda^2(|\lambda q|^2+m^2)^{-1}=|q|^{-2}.$$

The **superficial degree** of $\Gamma$ under this assignment is

$$\omega_D(\Gamma):=DL-2I.$$

By convention, $\omega_D(\Gamma)=0$ is called a **logarithmic superficial degree**. This is finite graph bookkeeping under the stated assignment. It does not by itself establish convergence or divergence of an actual graph integral; proper subgraphs, numerator cancellations, exceptional infrared data, and distributional singularities require separate hypotheses and analysis.

items.statement: Let $D\in\mathbb Z_{\ge1}$ and let $\Gamma$ be a finite quartic graph in the sense of [[def-qft-quartic-graph-power-counting]]. With $V$ vertices, $I$ internal edges, $E$ external half-edges, and loop count $L$, the incidence and loop-count identities are $4V=2I+E$ and $L=I-V+1$. Its superficial degree under the stated Euclidean scalar power-counting convention is $\omega_D(\Gamma)=DL-2I=D+(D-4)V-\frac{D-2}{2}E$. In $D=4$ this reduces to $\omega_4(\Gamma)=4-E$. A zero value is a logarithmic **superficial** degree by the convention in the definition; these identities do not assert convergence or divergence of an actual graph integral.

items.title: Scalar engineering dimensions and tree-level dilation

references.title: Mark Srednicki, Quantum Field Theory, author-posted prepublication draft, §12, equations (12.5)–(12.11)
David Tong, Quantum Field Theory, §3 Interacting Fields, equations (3.202)–(3.204)

items.statement:
Let $D\in\mathbb Z_{\ge1}$, let $\phi\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^D;\mathbb R)$ (the smooth real-valued functions with compact support), let $r\ge3$ be an integer, and let $g_r\in\mathbb R\setminus\{0\}$. The Euclidean gradient is $\nabla_E\phi:=(\partial_1\phi,\ldots,\partial_D\phi)$ and its squared norm is $|\nabla_E\phi|^2:=\sum_{j=1}^D(\partial_j\phi)^2$. With Lebesgue measure $d^Dx$ on $\mathbb R^D$, define the real-valued functionals

$$S_{\mathrm{kin}}(\phi):=\frac12\int_{\mathbb R^D}|\nabla_E\phi(x)|^2\,d^Dx,\qquad S_r(\phi):=g_r\int_{\mathbb R^D}\phi(x)^r\,d^Dx.$$

They are finite because $\phi$ and its derivatives have compact support. Use the following formal natural-unit mass-degree convention: set $\hbar=c=1$, assign degree $-1$ to each coordinate $x^\mu$ ($1\le\mu\le D$), degree $1$ to each partial derivative, and degree $-D$ to $d^Dx$; degrees add under products. Normalize both displayed functionals as dimensionless action terms of degree $0$. The symbols $[\phi]$ and $[g_r]$ denote their formal mass degrees in this convention; these are the engineering dimensions. They are $[\phi]=(D-2)/2$ and $[g_r]=D-r(D-2)/2$. Under the dilation $\phi_b(x)=b^{-(D-2)/2}\phi(x/b)$ for $b>0$, $S_{\mathrm{kin}}(\phi_b)=S_{\mathrm{kin}}(\phi)$ and $S_r(\phi_b)=b^{D-r(D-2)/2}S_r(\phi)$. Call the monomial relevant, marginal, or irrelevant at tree level according as this dilation exponent is positive, zero, or negative. Thus a quartic monomial has exponent $4-D$: it is relevant for $D<4$, marginal by engineering dimension for $D=4$, and irrelevant for $D>4$. These labels concern only this classical engineering-dimension convention; no quantum correction, fixed point, or renormalization-group flow is asserted.

items.statement:
In Euclidean momentum dimension $D=4$, take the connected graph with two quartic vertices joined by two internal edges and with two external half-edges at each vertex. Its counts are $V=2$, $I=2$, $E=4$, and $L=1$. Its superficial degree is therefore zero, so it has logarithmic **superficial** degree under the stated power-counting convention.

Separately, on punctured Euclidean $\mathbb R^4$ let $C_0(x)=1/(4\pi^2|x|^2)$ and $u=C_0^2=1/(16\pi^4|x|^4)$. For any $\chi\in\mathcal D(\mathbb R^4)$ equal to one near $0$, and every $\mu>0$, define $T_\mu(\varphi)=\int_{\mathbb R^4\setminus\{0\}}[\varphi(x)-\chi(\mu x)\varphi(0)]/(16\pi^4|x|^4)\,d^4x$ for $\varphi\in\mathcal D(\mathbb R^4)$. Conditional on the current QFT-IR04 proposition [[prop-qft-four-dimensional-log-scale-anomaly]] with its explicit Axiom-of-Choice hypothesis, this family has the exact logarithmic scale-change identity stated below and no same-degree homogeneous extension. This is a separate Euclidean distribution-extension calculation; it is not identified with the integrated amplitude of the graph. The graph count alone does not establish convergence or divergence of an actual loop integral.

items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]) as in
[[def-qft-regulated-polynomial-hamiltonian]]; it supplies the stated
Hilbert-space construction and is not a physical measurement assumption. Fix
one finite nonempty label set $J$ with $N:=|J|\ge1$, an enumeration of $J$ by
$\{1,\ldots,N\}$, and dimensionless real coordinates
$q=(q_1,\ldots,q_N)\in\mathbb R^N$. Each label indexes one coordinate; no
spatial geometry or limit in $N$ is part of these data. The coordinate space,
Hilbert space, and polynomial differential expression are those of
[[def-qft-regulated-polynomial-hamiltonian]]:
$H_N=L^2(\mathbb R^N,dq;\mathbb C)$, with inner product linear in its first
variable, $D_0=C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^N;\mathbb C)$, and

$$h_0u=-\sum_{j=1}^N a_j\partial_j^2u+V(q)u,\qquad u\in D_0,$$

where $a_j>0$ and $V$ is a real polynomial. Require fixed constants $c>0$ and
$C_0\ge0$ such that

$$V(q)\ge c|q|^2-C_0\qquad(q\in\mathbb R^N).$$

For $j=1,\ldots,N$ define dimensionless linear maps
$Q_j,P_j:D_0\to D_0$ by
$$Q_ju(q):=q_ju(q),\qquad P_ju(q):=-i\partial_ju(q).$$
For maps preserving $D_0$, write $[A,B]u:=A(Bu)-B(Au)$. For every
$u\in D_0$ these maps obey
$$[Q_i,Q_j]u=0,\qquad [P_i,P_j]u=0,\qquad [Q_i,P_j]u=i\delta_{ij}u,$$
where $\delta_{ij}=1$ if $i=j$ and $0$ otherwise. In this finite-coordinate
model, the mixed identity follows from
$-iq_i\partial_j u+i\partial_j(q_i u)=i\delta_{ij}u$; the other two vanish
by commutativity of coordinate multiplication and mixed derivatives. A
**bosonic mode** means one such
coordinate-momentum pair with these commutation relations on $D_0$; this names
the algebraic commutation convention and adds no state-space construction
beyond $H_N$. A **polynomial interaction term** means a
monomial of total degree at least three in $V$; the model is interacting in
this finite-coordinate sense exactly when at least one such term has nonzero
coefficient. This terminology asserts no continuum field interaction or
scattering construction.

Define $V(Q):D_0\to D_0$ by $(V(Q)u)(q):=V(q)u(q)$. Then
$$h_0u=\sum_{j=1}^N a_jP_j^2u+V(Q)u\qquad(u\in D_0).$$
All terms here are dimensionless, and the physical energy unit enters only
through the scale $E_*$ below.

For this physical model, take $q_j$, $a_j$, $c$, $C_0$, and the coefficients
of $V$ to be dimensionless. Adopt a positive energy scale $E_*$ in joules as
primitive finite-regulator data, and use $\hbar$ in joule-seconds under
[[def-qft-framework-units]]. When the mathematical supplier
[[thm-qft-self-adjoint-regulated-interaction]] constructs its specified
self-adjoint form realization $h$ of $h_0$, the model Hamiltonian is
$H_{\rm phys}:=E_*h$ on that supplied domain. This postulate adopts the
finite-regulator polynomial data; it does not assert that the initial
differential expression is self-adjoint or choose an operator domain by
itself.

The finite label set and polynomial are held fixed. A finite spatial regulator
is not thereby Lorentz invariant, and this model asserts no continuum or
infinite-volume limit, no convergence of a perturbation series, and no
reported observation. Its parameters are selected model inputs, not measured
values.

For the fixed model of [[post-qft-regulated-polynomial-model]], use the SI
energy-unit convention of [[def-qft-framework-units]]. A declared temperature
input is a scalar $T>0$ with unit kelvin (K). Use the SI-defining Boltzmann
constant
$$k_B:=1.380649\times10^{-23}\,\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}}.$$
This exact value is the one stated by the BIPM SI Brochure, 9th edition,
version 4.01, §§2.2 and 2.3.1. Define the physical inverse-energy parameter

$$\beta_{\rm phys}:=\frac{1}{k_BT}\quad[\mathrm{J^{-1}}],$$

and its dimensionless form

$$\widehat\beta:=E_*\beta_{\rm phys}.$$

The product $k_BT$ has unit joule, and $\widehat\beta$ is dimensionless
because $E_*$ has unit joule. Since $k_B>0$ and $T>0$, both inverse parameters
are defined and positive. The temperature $T$ is a declared model input; this
definition does not infer it from a state or an experiment. It defines a
parameter convention only and asserts no dynamical thermalization.

items.design_state: Complete conditional proof and SI time conversion. The QFT-IR01 mathematical suppliers are current-ready, but the selected-model postulate and C01 constructed-model postulate lack Step 1 readiness records; this item is escalated.
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice. Use one fixed finite-regulator data set from
[[post-qft-regulated-polynomial-model]], and let $h$ be the self-adjoint form
realization supplied by
[[thm-qft-self-adjoint-regulated-interaction]], with domain $D(h)$ and
eigenpairs $(\psi_n,\lambda_n)$. Let $E_*>0$ joules and set
$H_{\rm phys}:=E_*h$ on $D(h)$. For physical time $\tau$ in seconds define

$$U_{\rm phys}(\tau):=U(E_*\tau/\hbar),$$

where $U(s)$ is the dimensionless-parameter group of
[[thm-qft-regulated-global-unitary-evolution]]. Then $U_{\rm phys}$ is a
strongly continuous unitary group, $U_{\rm phys}(0)=I$,
$U_{\rm phys}(\tau_1+\tau_2)=U_{\rm phys}(\tau_1)U_{\rm phys}(\tau_2)$,
and $\|U_{\rm phys}(\tau)\psi\|=\|\psi\|$ for every $\psi\in H_N$.
Its norm derivative exists exactly for $\psi\in D(h)$, and then

$$\frac{d}{d\tau}U_{\rm phys}(\tau)\psi=-\frac{i}{\hbar}H_{\rm phys}U_{\rm phys}(\tau)\psi.$$

The result is a conditional deduction for the selected finite-regulator
model. It is not an empirical observation or a continuum-limit theorem.
items.strategy:
**Proof technique:** direct.

1.1 Under Countable Choice [A1], the hypotheses of [F1] hold, so $h$ is self-adjoint on $D(h)$. Multiplication by the positive real scalar $E_*$ preserves self-adjointness and the domain, so $H_{\rm phys}=E_*h$ is self-adjoint on $D(h)$ with eigenvalues $E_*\lambda_n$. The units in [A2] make $E_*\tau/\hbar$ dimensionless. [A1, A2, F1, algebra]

2.1 Put $s=E_*\tau/\hbar$. Since this is a real linear change of parameter, Countable Choice [A1] discharges the hypothesis of [F2], which gives unitarity, strong continuity, the identity at zero, and the group law for $U_{\rm phys}(\tau)=U(s)$. Unitarity also gives $\|U_{\rm phys}(\tau)\psi\|=\|\psi\|$. [A1, F2, step 1.1, algebra]

3.1 If $\psi\in D(h)$, the chain rule and [F2] give $\frac{d}{d\tau}U(E_*\tau/\hbar)\psi =-i(E_*/\hbar)hU(E_*\tau/\hbar)\psi =-iH_{\rm phys}U_{\rm phys}(\tau)\psi/\hbar$. Conversely, because $E_*/\hbar>0$, the change $s=E_*\tau/\hbar$ is invertible, so norm differentiability in $\tau$ is equivalent to differentiability in $s$; [F2] makes its domain exactly $D(h)$. [A1, F1, F2, step 1.1, step 2.1, algebra]

4.1 [A3] supplies the physical reading of this already constructed self-adjoint Hamiltonian and group as the selected model's Schrödinger evolution. It adds no existence claim beyond [F1] and [F2], and no empirical premise is used. [A1, A3, F1, F2, step 1.1, step 2.1] ∎

Assume Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]) for the finite-regulator
spectral and trace construction. For the fixed model of
[[post-qft-regulated-polynomial-model]] and a declared
temperature input $T>0$, use
[[def-qft-regulated-thermal-parameter]] to set
$\beta_{\rm phys}=(k_BT)^{-1}$ and
$\widehat\beta=E_*\beta_{\rm phys}>0$. Let $h$ be the model's specified
self-adjoint form realization and $H_{\rm phys}=E_*h$. When the finite-mode
coercivity hypotheses hold, [[thm-qft-regulated-gibbs-trace]] proves that
$\rho_\gamma$ is positive trace class with finite positive trace for every
dimensionless $\gamma>0$. Make its spectral construction explicit: let
$(\psi_k,\lambda_k)_{k\ge0}$ be the complete orthonormal eigenbasis and
repeated eigenvalues used in that supplier. For $f\in H_N$, define

$$G_\gamma f:=\sum_{k\ge0}e^{-\gamma\lambda_k}\langle f,\psi_k\rangle\psi_k.$$

The vector series converges in $H_N$ for every $f$, and this is the action of
the supplier's operator $\rho_\gamma$, obtained there as the operator-norm
limit of its finite-rank truncations. In this item the notation
$e^{-\gamma h}$ means this explicitly defined operator $G_\gamma$. Since
$H_{\rm phys}\psi_k=E_*\lambda_k\psi_k$, define
$e^{-\beta_{\rm phys}H_{\rm phys}}$ on $H_N$ by the corresponding series
$e^{-\beta_{\rm phys}H_{\rm phys}}f:=\sum_{k\ge0}e^{-\beta_{\rm phys}E_*\lambda_k}\langle f,\psi_k\rangle\psi_k$.
Since $\widehat\beta=E_*\beta_{\rm phys}$, its coefficients equal those of
$G_{\widehat\beta}$ term by term, and both series converge in $H_N$.
Therefore, as operators on $H_N$,
$e^{-\beta_{\rm phys}H_{\rm phys}}=G_{\widehat\beta}=e^{-\widehat\beta h}$.
The Gibbs-trace supplier consequently applies to exactly the operator in the
state assignment below. Adopt the normalized operator

$$\rho_T:=\frac{e^{-\beta_{\rm phys}H_{\rm phys}}}{Z_T}=\frac{e^{-\widehat\beta h}}{Z_T},\qquad Z_T:=\operatorname{Tr}(e^{-\beta_{\rm phys}H_{\rm phys}})=\operatorname{Tr}(e^{-\widehat\beta h})$$

as this finite-regulator model's canonical equilibrium state. This is a
physical state assignment, not a deduction that the dynamics reach
equilibrium. It asserts no infinite-volume trace, no zero-temperature state,
and no empirical observation.

items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice and the finite-regulator coercivity hypotheses of
[[thm-qft-regulated-gibbs-trace]]. Use the model state of
[[post-qft-regulated-equilibrium-state]] and the inverse-energy parameters of
[[def-qft-regulated-thermal-parameter]]. Let
$\alpha_j:=\sqrt{a_jc}$, $j=1,\ldots,N$, for the dimensionless kinetic
coefficients and coercivity constant in the model, and let
$C_0\ge0$ be its potential lower-bound shift. Then

$$0<Z_T=\sum_{k\ge0}e^{-\widehat\beta\lambda_k}\le e^{\widehat\beta C_0}\prod_{j=1}^N\frac{e^{-\widehat\beta\alpha_j}}{1-e^{-2\widehat\beta\alpha_j}}<\infty,$$

where $\lambda_k$ are the eigenvalues of $h$. The adopted state
$\rho_T$ is a positive trace-class operator with trace one. For every
bounded linear operator $B:H_N\to H_N$,

$$\operatorname{Tr}(\rho_TB)=Z_T^{-1}\sum_{k\ge0}e^{-\widehat\beta\lambda_k}\langle B\psi_k,\psi_k\rangle,$$

and the series is absolutely convergent. If $E_a$ is an effect in a supplied
normalized finite instrument of
[[post-qft-constructed-model-and-measurement]], this trace is its adopted
canonical model probability. These are conditional finite-regulator
predictions, not measured outcomes or a continuum-limit claim.
items.strategy:
**Proof technique:** direct.

1.1 By [F2], $\widehat\beta=E_*\beta_{\rm phys}>0$ is dimensionless. For each $f\in H_N$, the series defining $e^{-\beta_{\rm phys}H_{\rm phys}}f$ has coefficients $e^{-\beta_{\rm phys}E_*\lambda_k}\langle f,\psi_k\rangle$, while the series defining $e^{-\widehat\beta h}f$ has coefficients $e^{-\widehat\beta\lambda_k}\langle f,\psi_k\rangle$. These coefficients are equal term by term, and both series converge in $H_N$; hence $e^{-\beta_{\rm phys}H_{\rm phys}}=e^{-\widehat\beta h}=G_{\widehat\beta}$ as operators. The trace supplied by [F1] is therefore $Z_T=\sum_ke^{-\widehat\beta\lambda_k}$. [A2, F1, F2, given, algebra]

2.1 Under Countable Choice [A1], apply [F1] at $\widehat\beta>0$. It gives $Z_T>0$, the stated finite upper bound, and trace-class positivity of $G_{\widehat\beta}=e^{-\widehat\beta h}$. Dividing by $Z_T$ yields $\operatorname{Tr}(\rho_T)=1$ and preserves positivity and trace class. [A1, A2, F1, step 1.1, algebra]

3.1 Under the same Countable Choice assumption [A1], for bounded $B$, [F1]
gives the absolutely convergent sum for $\operatorname{Tr}(G_{\widehat\beta}B)$. Since $\rho_T=Z_T^{-1}G_{\widehat\beta}$, linearity of the trace and $Z_T>0$ give the displayed normalized formula. If $B=E_a$ is an effect in the instrument of [A3], that postulate supplies its physical model probability interpretation; the finite trace calculation supplies its value. [A1, A2, A3, F1, step 2.1, algebra] ∎

items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice and use one fixed one-mode regulator of
[[post-qft-regulated-polynomial-model]] with
dimensionless $a>0$, $r>0$, and $\lambda\ge0$. Here $r$ is a polynomial
coefficient, not an SI rest mass. Take
$V_\lambda(q)=\frac{r^2}{2}q^2+\lambda q^4$ on
$H_1=L^2(\mathbb R,dq;\mathbb C)$, with the form realization from
[[thm-qft-self-adjoint-regulated-interaction]]. Let $\epsilon_g(\lambda)$
be its least eigenvalue. The physical ground-energy prediction for the
adopted scale $E_*>0$ joules is
$E_g^{\rm phys}(\lambda):=E_*\epsilon_g(\lambda)$. Then

$$0\le E_g^{\rm phys}(\lambda)-E_g^{\rm phys}(0)\le \frac{3E_*a\lambda}{2r^2}.$$

For $\lambda>0$, the potential has a nonzero degree-four term and is
interacting in the finite-coordinate sense defined by
[[post-qft-regulated-polynomial-model]]. This conclusion makes no claim about
field scattering or a continuum field theory. The inequality is an exact fixed-regulator model

items.strategy:
**Proof technique:** direct.

1.1 Since $V_\lambda(q)=r^2q^2/2+\lambda q^4\ge (r^2/2)q^2$, the coercivity hypotheses of [F1] and [F4] hold with $c=r^2/2$ and $C_0=0$. Countable Choice [A1] therefore gives the form domains of [F1] and the self-adjoint compact-resolvent form realizations with attained least eigenvalues from [F4], for both $q_\lambda$ and $q_0$. If $\lambda>0$, the term $\lambda q^4$ is an interaction term by the finite-coordinate definition in [A2]. [A1, A2, F1, F4, given, algebra]

2.1 On $C_c^\infty$, the shifted form norms obey $\|u\|_{Q_0}^2\le\|u\|_{Q_\lambda}^2$ because their difference is $\lambda\int q^4|u|^2dq\ge0$. Hence the identity extends continuously $Q_\lambda\to Q_0$, and the two continuous injections into $L^2$ identify the same representative. On the core, $q_\lambda(u)=q_0(u)+\lambda\int q^4|u|^2dq\ge q_0(u)$; approximating any $u\in Q_\lambda$ by core elements and using continuity of both forms passes this inequality to $u$. For a normalized $u$, [F3] gives $q_0(u)\ge\epsilon_g(0)$, so taking the infimum on $Q_\lambda$ yields $\epsilon_g(\lambda)\ge\epsilon_g(0)$. [A1, F1, F3, F4, step 1.1, algebra]

2.2 Let $g_b(q)=(b/\pi)^{1/4}e^{-bq^2/2}$ with $b=r/\sqrt{2a}$, the normalized ground function in [F2] for $c=r^2/2$. Choose the smooth cutoff $\chi_R(q)=\chi(q/R)$ from [F2], with $\chi=1$ on $[-1,1]$, $\chi=0$ outside $[-2,2]$, and $|\chi_R'|\le C/R$. Then $u_R=\chi_Rg_b\in C_c^\infty$. For $S>R$, $u_R-u_S$ is supported where $|q|\ge R$, and $\|(u_R-u_S)'\|_2\le\|1_{|q|\ge R}g_b'\|_2 +C(R^{-1}+S^{-1})\|1_{|q|\ge R}g_b\|_2\to0$. The weighted part of its $Q_\lambda$ norm is bounded in square by $\int_{|q|\ge R}(r^2q^2/2+\lambda q^4+2)|g_b(q)|^2dq\to0$. These tails vanish because each polynomial times $e^{-bq^2}$ is integrable: for large $|q|$, its product with $|q|^2$ is bounded. Thus $(u_R)$ is $Q_\lambda$-Cauchy. Its $L^2$ limit is $g_b$, so injectivity in [F1] gives $g_b\in Q_\lambda$. [A1, F1, F2, F4, step 1.1, construct, algebra]

3.1 From $g_b'=-bqg_b$ and $\|g_b\|_2=1$, integrate the derivatives of $q e^{-bq^2}$ and $q^3e^{-bq^2}$ over $\mathbb R$. Their boundary terms vanish by Gaussian decay, giving $\int q^2|g_b|^2dq=1/(2b)$ and $\int q^4|g_b|^2dq=3/(4b^2)$. Hence $q_\lambda(g_b)=ab/2+r^2/(4b)+3\lambda/(4b^2)$. At $b=r/\sqrt{2a}$, the first two terms equal $\epsilon_g(0)=r\sqrt{a/2}$ by [F2], and the last term is $3a\lambda/(2r^2)$. [A1, F2, step 2.2, algebra]

4.1 Since $g_b\in Q_\lambda$ is normalized, [F3] gives $\epsilon_g(\lambda)\le q_\lambda(g_b)$. Combining this with step 2.1 and step 3.1 yields $0\le\epsilon_g(\lambda)-\epsilon_g(0)\le3a\lambda/(2r^2)$. [A1, F3, step 2.1, step 3.1, algebra]

5.1 Multiplication by $E_*>0$ preserves both inequalities and gives the stated joule-valued bound. By [A3], this is a selected-model energy prediction and not a reported measurement. [A2, A3, step 4.1, algebra] ∎

items.statement:
Choose $N=1$, $a=1$, $r=1$, and $\lambda=1$, all dimensionless. The
potential is $V(q)=q^2/2+q^4$, and the physical Hamiltonian is $H_{\rm phys}
=E_*h$ with $E_*>0$ joules. The coordinate-space Hilbert space is the full
$H_1=L^2(\mathbb R,dq;\mathbb C)$ of
[[def-qft-regulated-polynomial-hamiltonian]], not a finite matrix truncation.
The positive $q^4$ term is present in the potential of the full form-selected
operator. This is a one-coordinate model; no field-scattering, continuum, or
empirical conclusion is asserted.
items.strategy:
1.1 The parameters satisfy $a>0$, $r>0$, and $\lambda>0$, and $V(q)=q^2/2+q^4\ge q^2/2$, so the coercivity hypotheses hold with $c=1/2$ and $C_0=0$. The coordinate variable $q$ ranges over $\mathbb R$; vectors in $H_1$ are square-integrable complex functions of $q$, identified up to equality almost everywhere by [F3]. The characteristic functions $\mathbf 1_{[3n,3n+1)}$, $n\in\mathbb N$, are nonzero pairwise orthogonal vectors, so this Hilbert space is infinite-dimensional. [F3, algebra]

2.1 By [A1], the Countable Choice hypothesis of [F2] holds. Substituting $a=r=\lambda=1$ into it gives $0\le E_g^{\rm phys}(1)-E_g^{\rm phys}(0)\le3E_*/2$. This is an exact bound for the selected model, not an exact value of either ground energy. [A1, F2, step 1.1, algebra]

3.1 By [A1], the Countable Choice hypothesis of [F1] holds. Applying [F1]
to the same selected model gives a global unitary group $U_{\rm phys}(\tau)$ for every $\tau\in\mathbb R$, norm preservation for all states, and differentiability precisely on the stated Hamiltonian domain. The quartic coefficient is positive, and the Hilbert space is infinite-dimensional by step 1.1; thus this is a one-coordinate polynomial operator model on the full Hilbert space, not a finite matrix replacement. No observation or continuum extrapolation is asserted. [A1, F1, step 1.1, algebra] ∎

[[prop-qft-four-dimensional-log-scale-anomaly]]. That proposition gives an
exact Euclidean distribution-extension identity for the specified punctured
kernel $u(x)=1/(16\pi^4|x|^4)$: changing its cutoff scale changes the
extension by $(8\pi^2)^{-1}\log(\mu/\nu)\delta_0$. Its statement

does not say that an experimentally measured parameter changes with energy
scale, choose which extension a physical model uses, or define a measurement
procedure. It constructs no Lorentzian field theory. This remark asserts
neither existence nor nonexistence of a field theory obtained by taking a
continuum limit and supplies no empirical claim.
